quest:1001.text: Buzzbox 411. Along Darkshore, Buzzbox 411 waits for thresher eyes to bring it back into service. Wizbang Cranktoggle, an eccentric and intoxicated gnome inventor, reaches it through a mechanical relay network. After you repair Buzzbox 827 farther south, Wizbang Cranktoggle's voice crackles through the transmitter again. Hidden from sight, the gnome inventor directs you north along Darkshore's beach to the damaged Buzzbox 411. His words break with hiccups and praise for crawler wine. He says local aquatic predators carry what his coastal apparatus needs to work. Thresher eyes must go into Buzzbox 411's hatch to restore the machine. Darkshore threshers prowl the shallows off Auberdine, and Wizbang says their eyes can recalibrate the device. Feed the eyes to the apparatus, and it jolts back to life. Then the line opens for another assignment, delivered in an even slurrier voice.

quest:1002.text: Buzzbox 323. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s fieldwork now reaches the third Buzzbox along Darkshore’s coast. You gather six Moonstalker fangs and feed them to the machine north of Auberdine. After you operate Buzzbox 411 farther south, Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the speaker. Drink has muddled his directions, but he points you north of Auberdine, to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research calls for six Moonstalker fangs from the fierce hunters roaming Darkshore’s forests. Before you begin, Buzzbox 323 chatters with static and faint muttering. Place the requested fangs in its intake hopper, and the machine rattles as it grinds the teeth to dust. Then Wizbang’s boozy voice returns through the transceiver, pleased with your delivery. He points you toward the next machine in his scattered network.

quest:1003.text: Buzzbox 525. Along Darkshore's coast, Wizbang Cranktoggle's scattered machines await the last of his strange requests. Buzzbox 525 calls for animal remnants and stranger materials. Once Buzzbox 323 is serviced, its rattling speakers carry Wizbang Cranktoggle's garbled instructions. His words slur through drunken chuckles and rambling directions. He sends his helpers far south along Darkshore's main road. There, he asks them to hunt grizzled thistle bears and place four thick scalps in Buzzbox 525's compartment. The machine is concealed behind a fence in the brush beside the road.

quest:1008.text: The Zoram Strand. Naga now threaten Ashenvale at The Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar sends Alliance champions to scour the northwestern coast, where an ancient city lies in ruins. Stopping the naga guards the forest against a haunting echo of the night elves’ distant past. At Ashenvale’s northwestern edge, the Zoram Strand meets the Veiled Sea. The shore lies northwest of Astranaar, where forest canopy gives way to coast. For ages, the beach lay quiet, its stones left by a civilization shattered ten millennia ago. Now Wrathtail naga surge from the dark tides. They have made a hostile beachhead on night elven borders and threaten to press inland. The city of Zoram lies shattered beneath the surf, submerged during the Great Sundering. For ages, the kaldorei left it abandoned and nearly forgotten. Now the naga’s arrival among its ruins stirs bitter memories among Astranaar’s defenders. Sentinels such as Shindrell Swiftfire know the invaders as twisted cousins, born of their own ancient catastrophe. They will not let the depths claim the shore again.

quest:102.text:
Patrolling Westfall. Gnoll packs threaten the people still living on Westfall’s grasslands. From Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin calls on volunteers to hunt them, fearing they work with thieves in the Deadmines. Sentinel Hill is Westfall’s main defense, held by local volunteers instead of royal troops. With Stormwind sending no soldiers to protect the outer farmlands, the people formed the People’s Militia. Captain Danuvin once farmed in Westfall. Now he leads the militia and refuses to abandon his homeland.

The militia depends on travelers passing through to help hold its perimeter against dangers gathering across the plains. Gnolls threaten the refugees and squatters struggling to survive in Westfall. Danuvin’s scouts believe the packs work with bandits based in the Deadmines. So he sends hunters to collect gnoll paws. He hopes to curb the packs’ growing patrols and break any cooperation between the beasts and the outlaws.

quest:103.text: Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. He seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, guiding ships safely past the reefs. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off Westfall’s southwest shore. Its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson died in the waters by these rocks and now watches over the tower as a ghost. He could not stop the slaughter in life, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark. No living keeper remains to tend the flame, so Captain Grayson needs an unusual fuel. Harvest Watchers roam Westfall’s abandoned farmlands, carrying flasks of machinery oil inside their rusted bodies. Grayson sends you ashore to recover the oil from these broken constructs. With it, the beacon can keep burning and guide captains past the reefs.

quest:1061.text: The Spirits of Stonetalon. Unrest stirs among the spirits of Stonetalon, and Zor Lonetree sends Horde champions west to learn why. From Orgrimmar, you pass the Crossroads and report to Seereth Stonebreak near Greatwood Vale. In Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree listens to the natural world and feels deep distress from the Stonetalon Mountains. The elemental spirits of its rocky peaks rage as logging cuts into their forests. Horde shamans hear their unrest and fear that the devastation in the western highlands will upset Kalimdor's spiritual balance. The Venture Company is an unscrupulous goblin syndicate cutting timber in Greatwood Vale. Its crews use aggressive machinery, saws, and muscle to butcher the ancient woodland instead of harvesting it sustainably. So the Horde sent Seereth Stonebreak, a young shaman, to watch the forest from the frontier and rally defenders against the ravagers.

quest:1062.text:
Goblin Invaders. At the Barrens and Stonetalon border, Goblin Invaders strike at the mountains' ancient woodlands. Seereth Stonebreak sends the Horde against Venture Company loggers in Windshear Crag. Venture Company loggers cut deep into the Stonetalon Mountains. They strip the hillsides and burn the underbrush, leaving scorched ground behind. For tauren and their allies, the harm reaches beyond the forests. The primal spirits bound to Stonetalon howl in torment.

Seereth Stonebreak watches from the mountain border. She sees the goblins' assault has left the spirits blind with agony and fury. Profit is all the Venture Company's executives and hirelings heed. Reason will not sway them. So Seereth sends you past Greatwood Vale and into Windshear Crag to kill fifteen loggers.

The Horde meets the company's greed with force. The blow is meant to halt the deforestation and give tauren elders time to soothe the land's agitated spirits.

quest:1063.text: The Elder Crone. Seereth Stonebreak sends word from Stonetalon to Thunder Bluff. Goblin deforestation and mining have enraged the mountain's elements, and Seereth seeks spiritual guidance from Magatha Grimtotem on Elder Rise. In Stonetalon Mountains, goblin deforestation and mining have enraged the elemental spirits. Seereth Stonebreak sees that force alone cannot ease the land's anguish. So Seereth turns to elder shamans for wisdom. Few tribal leaders are known to Seereth by name, but Magatha Grimtotem is known for her wisdom and commanding presence. Magatha Grimtotem holds court atop Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, where shamanic and spiritual affairs gather. Her tribe's ties with Cairne Bloodhoof's leadership are tense and often confrontational. Even so, Magatha is a formidable elder whose counsel carries great weight across the Horde. You bring her Stonetalon's troubles and seek her guidance.

quest:1064.text: Forsaken Aid. In Thunder Bluff, Magatha Grimtotem seeks Forsaken Aid for the blighted spirits of Stonetalon. She turns to Apothecary Zamah in the Pools of Vision, hoping tauren and undead knowledge can help the suffering land. Magatha Grimtotem sees practical value in the Forsaken alliance. Word reaches Thunder Bluff of corrupted elemental spirits and suffering land in the Stonetalon Mountains, so she turns to the undead for help. She believes those who understand disease may help cure it. Rather than seek traditional druidic remedies, she sends you to the Royal Apothecary Society. Apothecary Zamah represents Undercity interests on Kalimdor from the Pools of Vision beneath Spirit Rise. Tauren shamans, priests, and seers use the cavern as a sacred retreat. Zamah's presence brings Forsaken work into their midst. Magatha sends a serpent messenger ahead of you to alert Zamah, opening a direct line to the Forsaken's alchemical researchers.

quest:1065.text: Journey to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Zamah seeks a way to drive the Venture Company from Stonetalon Mountains without open war. She sends you across the sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, where the Royal Apothecary Society works in Lordaeron. In Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah links the Forsaken with the Earth Mother's children. The Venture Company cuts timber and mines the sacred lands of Stonetalon Mountains, and ordinary means have failed to stop them. So Zamah turns to her peers in the Royal Apothecary Society for a chemical deterrent. She hopes their alchemy can drive the company away without a drawn-out war. You cross the sea from Kalimdor by zeppelin toward Lordaeron and the Undercity. From Tirisfal Glades, the road runs south through Silverpine Forest and into the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill lies near human farmsteads and ruins. Once a human hamlet, it is now a Forsaken stronghold where the Royal Apothecary Society carries out its research.

quest:109.text: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle gathers Westfall's defenders against threats to the farms. Guards along the Elwynn border and farmers driven west both send capable travelers toward Sentinel Hill. Those who answer join a defense built from local volunteers. No royal battalions come to their aid. From the stone tower atop Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle organizes farmers, retired veterans, and mercenaries into the People's Militia. You join their bitter guerrilla war to keep Westfall's farmlands from falling into lawlessness.

quest:1097.text: Elmore's Task. Smith Argus sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind, where Grimand Elmore awaits help with a delivery. The weaponsmith needs it carried to his kin in Khaz Modan, and Argus trusts you with the road ahead. Smith Argus watches for travelers he can trust with work beyond wolves and kobolds. Grimand Elmore has sent word from Stormwind and asks for help carrying a delivery to his kin in Khaz Modan. The city gates open the way to Elmore's call. Stormwind and Ironforge rely on open trade and goodwill to keep both realms supplied and united. Argus says Elwynn Forest needs defenders, yet promises to the dwarves matter too. In northeastern Stormwind, the Dwarven District leads you to Elmore's shop. There, a journey beyond the forest begins.

quest:1099.text: Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, the goblin race decides who wins a goblin prize box. Goblins Win! names the result for whoever holds the winning ticket. You hold the goblin race ticket while the goblins' side is decided. If they win, the ticket earns you a goblin prize box. The gnome ticket counts for the other side.

quest:11.text: Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty. In western Elwynn, Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty calls for help against gnolls pressing the border. Deputy Rainer offers a reward at Westbrook Garrison for painted armbands taken from Riverpaw packs in the woods and by the water. Westbrook Garrison guards Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Its depleted forces struggle to contain the growing Riverpaw presence. The gnolls camp south of the guard tower and farther east around Stone Cairn Lake. From those camps, they threaten travelers and nearby homesteads. Deputy Rainer cannot spare regular infantry to sweep the woods, so he offers a bounty on the raiders. He requires painted armbands from slain gnolls as proof of each kill. Wandering adventurers and recruits are hired to thin the pack before the Riverpaws overrun the western marches.

quest:111.text: Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield asks Gramma Stonefield for a way to reach Maybell Maclure. Their families keep them apart, and he hopes to meet her without drawing their kin into conflict. Tommy Joe and Maybell hide their love from their families. He turns to Gramma Stonefield, hoping she can find them a chance to meet in secret. Their kin must not discover the romance and turn old hostility into violence. Gramma Stonefield knows the families cannot truly unite while their bad blood remains. Still, she will not let that end the young couple's hopes. She begins seeking small chances to bring Tommy Joe and Maybell together.

quest:112.text: Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew her an invisibility liquor. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see the one she loves without bringing their kin into an armed clash. So she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor, but its rare ingredients are not in the inn's cupboards. William Pestle needs crystal kelp as the catalyst for his brew. Its fronds usually grow far out in saltwater oceans, but tribal murlocs have carried stashes inland to their crude camps along Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Their peculiar instincts draw them to haul the marine plants to the freshwater shore. You need to recover enough fronds from the murlocs before returning to Goldshire with them.

quest:1138.text: Fruit of the Sea. Along Darkshore, Auberdine fisherman Gubber Blump asks you to gather crab meat. He keeps to the docks and dreams of dishes for his catch. Gubber Blump fishes from Auberdine's long wooden piers, thinking of crab meat. He calls crabs the ocean's true bounty and imagines them baked, barbecued, or boiled. His recipes include whipper root crab and Ironforge surprise crab. Gubber cannot leave his fishing rod, so he asks you to gather ingredients from Darkshore's beaches. Reef crawlers and encrusted tide crawlers move among the breakers, offering meat for a coastal cook. Mind their claws as you gather the fine crab chunks.

quest:114.text: The Escape. Maybell Maclure seeks a way to leave her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed with crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield asks William Pestle, an alchemist at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, for help. Crystal kelp from nearby lakes gives Pestle what he needs to brew Invisibility Liquor. The brew can hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

quest:1141.text: The Family and the Fishing Pole. On Auberdine's docks, Gubber Blump waits with his heirloom Fishing Pole for a catch. Hostile murlocs keep the town's small fishing boats ashore, so he seeks help catching native Darkshore grouper from the coast. Gubber Blump takes pride in his family's skill with a fishing line. Night elves make up most of Auberdine, though dwarves and gnomes have settled around its docks and port. Gubber spends his days gazing over the Veiled Sea instead of digging into stone. He hopes to bring in the local catch. Darkshore grouper thrive along the coast and make versatile food. They put up a lively fight on the line. Local fishermen usually row small boats into deeper waters to catch them, but aggressive murlocs now prowl the coast. The boats stay ashore, and Gubber fears the creatures are eating the local fish. So he asks travelers to fish from shore. Gubber gives a Blump Family Fishing Pole to anyone who brings him a hearty catch. He believes that landing a batch of feisty groupers proves an angler worthy of his family's legendary fishers, including his cousin Graun Blump. For Gubber, handing over a family rod is the highest mark of respect.

quest:116.text: Dry Times. Lakeshire's inn is running short of drink as Blackrock orcs keep the town under siege. The roads are unsafe, and the usual supplies have stopped coming. Blackrock orcs descend from Stonewatch Keep and press Lakeshire hard. With supply lines cut and roads unsafe, the inn is running low on drink. Barkeep Daniels turns to travelers who can cross the blocked roads and bring supplies back for frightened villagers and the town guards. Daniels needs drink from across Stormwind's lands. You can find Merlot in the capital and Sweet Rum at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Moonshine comes from Darkshire in Duskwood, and Grimbooze Thunderbrew brews Thunderbrew Lager in the hills of Westfall.

quest:117.text: Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew gathers fresh hops for his next batch. Without them, his ale may turn thick as stew, so he shares kegs with those who bring what he needs. Far from Dun Morogh, Grimbooze keeps his family's brewing tradition alive. He insists on proper hops for his current brew, or it may turn to thick stew instead of refreshing ale. Grimbooze praises hops, barley, yeast, and malt in cheerful rhymes. Fresh hops let him finish fermentation on the spot. In return, he shares whole kegs of Thunderbrew Lager, known for its forceful taste.

quest:1174.text: Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, the gnomes' victory decides which ticket pays out. The holder of the winning ticket gets a prize box. When the gnomes win, the holder of the Gnome Race Ticket gets the prize box. The goblin ticket counts for the other side of the race.

quest:118.text: The Price of Shoes. Verner Osgood has no iron left in Lakeshire, and the guards need constant repairs. He sends you west through Elwynn Forest to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for horseshoes. Lakeshire faces gnolls, orcs, and murlocs, while Stormwind sends little help. The garrison fights each day to keep the town standing, and battle wears down its gear. Verner Osgood spends nearly every waking hour repairing dented breastplates, reshaping dulled swords, and keeping the guards clad in iron. Now his raw materials are gone. Without iron, even ordinary work in a frontier town can stop. Horses without shoes cannot carry messengers swiftly or haul supplies along Redridge's rocky paths. Verner swallows his pride and sends you west along the Three Corners road to Goldshire. Smith Argus there has regular access to the kingdom's mineral stores.

quest:119.text: Return to Verner. Smith Argus has finished fifty horseshoes, and you carry them from Goldshire to Verner Osgood in Lakeshire. Redridge needs them for its hard-pressed mounts. You carry the crate east across the border into Redridge. There, supply shortages and gnoll attacks threaten the town. The fifty iron shoes keep horses and draft animals working on rugged mountain roads, which Redridge needs to face those dangers. Verner Osgood is relieved when the horseshoes arrive. Then he finds the bill Smith Argus attached to the crate. Verner is annoyed that the Goldshire smith expects payment. With dangers pressing around Redridge, there is little time to argue over the charge.

quest:12.text: The People's Militia. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle puts the People's Militia to the test against outlaws in Westfall's northern fields and mines. Local volunteers defend the region from the Defias Brotherhood while Stormwind's throne is distracted and its army absent. Gryan Stoutmantle founded the People's Militia, and he does not take just anyone. Anyone seeking its badge must prove they can fight and protect innocent settlers. He calls for decisive action to reclaim Westfall from the outlaws, vagrants, and thieves overrunning the region. Before Gryan Stoutmantle trusts new recruits with deeper operations, he sends them against Defias forces near the northern homesteads. Defias Trappers and Smugglers work openly near Jangolode Mine, Molsen Farm, and Furlbrow's Pumpkin Patch. They pillage stores and ambush travelers. Driving them out disrupts their foraging and shows Stoutmantle's scouts you have the grit for a long fight against crime.

quest:120.text: Messenger to Stormwind. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Stormwind. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs press around the town, and he cannot spare garrison troops for the journey. He entrusts you with The State of Lakeshire for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City. Gnolls contest every road from Lakeshire, while Blackrock orcs raid from the north. The town's guardsmen are stretched thin. Magistrate Solomon cannot spare fighting men for the days-long ride to the capital, so you carry his official plea for regular troops to the city gates. General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's defense. Solomon's report reaches him, and he respects the magistrate's leadership and sees the urgency. Yet army protocol bars him from mobilizing troops without a royal directive. Redridge's defense must wait while he consults the young King Anduin and the regency council.

quest:1205.text: Deadmire. In Dustwallow Marsh, hunters seek Deadmire in the waterways north of the Stonemaul Ruins. Melor Stonehoof asks you to bring back a tooth from the ancient crocolisk. The hunt teaches tracking and mercy. From Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof sends you east to Dustwallow Marsh. He teaches promising trackers the spiritual traditions of the hunt. Tauren hunters seek reverence and a bond with the natural world, not slaughter or trophies. There, you are to find Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk whose long life has become a burden. North of the Stonemaul Ruins, Deadmire prowls the waterways as a massive, pale crocolisk. His strength and fury still flare in sudden bursts, but age has worn down his body. Grinding bones bring unrelenting pain. Melor asks you to grant him a swift, honorable end and bring back one tooth as a token of his release.

quest:121.text: Messenger to Stormwind. In Stormwind, you carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital sends no troops while its leaders delay, leaving the settlement exposed. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his first reply back to Redridge while he waits for the throne's approval. Without royal permission, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens still have no city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling to the Blackrock clan.

quest:122.text: Underbelly Scales. In Redridge, Verner Osgood needs black dragon whelp scales to pay his debt to Smith Argus of Goldshire. You gather them from young drakes south of Lakeshire, and the scales settle Verner’s account with raw hide left for a piece of gear. Verner Osgood runs a forge outside Lakeshire and trades with craftsmen beyond the Redridge Mountains. Smith Argus of Goldshire sent him horseshoes, but Verner lacks the coin to pay. Argus asks for dragonhide instead: the softer underbelly scales of the black dragon whelps in the region. Without them, collectors may come from Elwynn Forest to claim the debt. Black dragon whelps trouble the defenders of the Redridge Mountains. Gnolls and orcs contest the roads, while the Black Dragonflight nests in the high peaks. Its brood wanders the skies south of Lake Everstill. The young predators’ underbelly scales are tough yet pliable, prized by armorers, smiths, and leatherworkers across the kingdom who dare to harvest them.

quest:123.text: The Collector. In Elwynn Forest, gold shipments leave the abandoned mines under cover of gnoll raids. An intercepted dispatch names their overseer as 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnolls in western Elwynn Forest carry a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule. It sets dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer known only as 'The Collector.' At the Lion's Pride Inn, Marshal Dughan learns that gold is still being mined and moved. Official mines across Elwynn have been closed for months because of gnoll attacks, kobold infestations, and roaming bandits. Gnolls with shipping schedules point to an organized criminal network stealing the kingdom's wealth.

quest:125.text: The Lost Tools. Blackrock fire has sunk Foreman Oslow's tools in Lake Everstill. Lakeshire is under pressure, and its builders need the shipment from Goldshire to repair the Great Bridge. The Great Bridge no longer joins Lakeshire to Elwynn Forest. A replacement shipment of stonework and carpentry tools came overland from Goldshire, but the wagons could not reach town. So the crew loaded the supplies into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. A Blackrock orc catapult struck the boat. It broke apart, and Oslow's heavy ironbound toolbox sank to the lake floor. Lake Everstill is dangerous below the surface. Aggressive murloc tribes prowl the shallows, while predatory threshers hunt in the murky depths. Foreman Oslow needs his tools to resume repairs on the bridge. Without them, Lakeshire risks falling further into ruin.

quest:129.text: A Free Lunch. Darcy has a meal ready for Guard Parker on the southern road from Lakeshire. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the approaches, while the town's guards are stretched thin. Darcy, the cook in Lakeshire, has packed a meal for Guard Parker. She cannot carry it beyond town herself. Redridge gnolls and roaming orc warbands make the roads outside the gates too dangerous for a civilian. So she asks passing travelers to carry the food toward Darkshire, where Parker keeps watch. Guard Parker watches the southern road from Lakeshire toward Duskwood. Redridge has too few reinforcements from the Stormwind army to face the growing gnoll packs and the Blackrock clan in the mountains. Sentries like Parker keep watch alone in hostile country. A hot meal from town can lift their spirits.

quest:13.text: The People's Militia. Westfall's volunteers face a growing Defias threat. Led by Gryan Stoutmantle, The People's Militia now confronts thieves who have moved beyond highway robbery to ransack Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry. The Militia calls for harsher retaliation. Defias attacks have spread from the roads to Westfall's economic centers. Defias Looters and Pillagers, who hurl fire, occupy Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry. They strip the Alexston Farmstead as well. Gryan Stoutmantle sees what their hold on these places could mean: Westfall may become impossible to reclaim without a formal royal army. Stormwind has sent Gryan Stoutmantle neither soldiers nor supplies. So he calls on the Holy Light and the resolve of Westfall's remaining farmers. Volunteers carry the fight into Defias strongholds, wearing down the Brotherhood. Driving out the looters will deny them resources and show fearful residents that defenders still fight for Westfall's peace and prosperity.

quest:130.text: Visit the Herbalist. Guard Parker asks you to buy flowers for Darcy in Lakeshire. He wants the gift kept secret before you return to the inn. Guard Parker watches Lakeshire's southern approach for blackrock orcs and gnolls. You bring him a warm meal from Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn. Grateful for her kindness, he asks you to buy flowers for her at the herbalist shop on the west end of town. Parker asks you to keep the order private when you visit Martie Jainrose, Lakeshire's herbalist. The town is small, and he does not want Martie to know who sent the flowers or who will receive them. At the shop, Martie teases you, guessing you have already found a sweetheart in town. Orc incursions and brigands trouble Redridge, so a small gesture of romance brings welcome relief.

quest:131.text: Delivering Daffodils. In Lakeshire, Delivering Daffodils brings you from Guard Parker's thanks to an uneasy exchange at the inn. First you take Parker his lunch, then carry flowers from Martie Jainrose to Darcy. Guard Parker thanks you for bringing his lunch. Darcy, the cook who prepared it, is owed a kindness, so Parker asks you to fetch flowers from Martie Jainrose. Martie arranges a bouquet of daffodils, her own favorite flowers. She does not know who will receive them.

quest:132.text: The Defias Brotherhood. At the edges of Redridge and Westfall, Wiley the Black warns Gryan Stoutmantle. His intelligence shows the Defias threat reaches beyond banditry, and Gryan needs to learn how far it extends. Wiley the Black says sharing what he knows could cost him his life. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups across the countryside, though those groups are usually hostile to one another. Wiley warns that the Defias has drawn an alarming network around itself. The red-masked outlaws have enlisted gnoll packs, kobold diggers, and goblin engineers instead of working alone. Their brutal muscle, burrowing labor, and mechanical cunning point to an enterprise beyond what the People's Militia first expected. Gryan Stoutmantle has little love for Wiley. He openly laments that he did not leave the rogue to rot when he had the chance. Yet Westfall cannot afford pride. The People's Militia must take useful intelligence wherever it can find it.

quest:1338.text:
Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike sends a shield order south to Stormwind City. He asks you to carry it to Furen Longbeard, the armorsmith he trusts. Stormpike trusts no other smith with his shield. He offers good pay to place the commission in Furen Longbeard’s hands, though Stormwind City lies far south of Loch Modan. Stormpike wonders why Furen works so far from Ironforge and the Great Forge, where many dwarves make their home. He suspects Stormwind’s humans pay the smith a king’s ransom.

When the order reaches Furen at his anvil, he takes pride in hearing from the prestigious Stormpike clan. He eagerly prepares to forge the shield.

quest:1339.text: Mountaineer Stormpike's Task. At his post in Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike needs a runner for urgent business beyond the valley. Mountaineer Kadrell sends you to find him, since Stormpike cannot leave his watch. The northern guard tower is Stormpike’s post, and his watch keeps him from leaving Loch Modan. The Mountaineers are stretched thin by troggs and roaming wildlife. So Kadrell directs capable travelers to guards who cannot abandon their duties. Stormpike needs a messenger for business far beyond the region’s borders. You find Stormpike atop the northern guard tower, looking out over the valley. He belongs to the prominent Stormpike clan and has affairs beyond Thelsamar’s frontier defenses. Carrying his message and supplies takes you across regional borders on his behalf. Your road leads from the loch onto the highways of Khaz Modan.

quest:135.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle suspects the Defias Brotherhood has ties to Stormwind's old Stonemasons Guild. He sends you there with Wiley's Note. Wiley's mention of the Stonemasons catches Gryan's attention. The guild rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but many believe it scattered or dissolved. If the Defias are linked to the guild, Westfall's rural insurgency may be more than a band of outlaws. Gryan cannot test his suspicions from Sentinel Hill, so he sends you to Master Mathias Shaw, head of Stormwind's covert intelligence wing, SI:7. Shaw works from the Barracks in Old Town, gathering whispers and secrets from across the realm. He may untangle the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:1358.text: Sample for Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim waits for a wolf heart sent from across the sea. Apothecary Zinge has sent it from the Undercity to support the Forsaken's research in central Kalimdor. Apothecary Zinge sends a Wolf Heart Sample from the Undercity to Apothecary Helbrim in the Barrens. The Royal Apothecary Society's experiments now reach beyond Lordaeron's ruins. Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine sent tainted organs before Zinge sought to carry their research across the world. Now a courier bears the sample over the sea to Helbrim, an alchemist stationed in the Barrens' dry savanna. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies how Kalimdor's native beasts react to compounds from the Plaguelands. The wolf heart may show how those toxins affect local creatures. Helbrim believes that dissecting and testing it alongside them will help the Forsaken master poisons and unnatural afflictions.

quest:1359.text: Zinge's Delivery. From the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel sends strange wolf hearts to the Undercity. Their toxins should have killed the beasts, and Apothecary Zinge receives them for the Royal Apothecary Society to study. In Silverpine Forest's ruined woods, Apothecary Renferrel found wolves with a deadly trait. Toxins in their hearts were so powerful they should have killed them. He preserved several tissue samples and packed them for his colleagues at the Apothecarium in the Undercity. At the Undercity's underground headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Zinge receives the preserved organs. The society seeks potent plagues and new alchemical compounds, so poisons that leave their hosts alive draw its notice. Zinge welcomes the samples for further trials in laboratories across the Forsaken alchemical network.

quest:136.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. Along Westfall's shore, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure begins with a battered parchment map. It sends you searching for his personal footlocker, then onward toward his hidden plunder across the region. Captain Sanders was an old seafarer who met a watery grave off Westfall's western coast. He left cryptic instructions so his hard-won fortune would not be lost to the Great Sea or taken by scavengers. You can retrace the trail he left behind. Shipwrecks and the restless spirits of drowned sailors mark the western shore.

quest:138.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. Along Westfall's shore, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure sends you inland. You leave the coast and follow the next mark in his scattered trail. Captain Sanders left riddles across the countryside instead of marking one cache by the beach. The solved cipher points beyond rocky bluffs toward Westfall's main roads. Among the roadside ruins, an old chimney marks the next stop. A discarded, weathered barrel nearby holds another message, and the ruined farmstead gives Sanders a landmark for his trail.

quest:139.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A broken barrel on Westfall's western shore begins Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure trail. Its clue points north to an old jug beside a coastal windmill, one step closer to the late pirate's riches. Captain Sanders left clues that point only to the next hiding place. No single parchment shows where his plunder lies, so the trail stays unresolved until you find each message. The parchment sends you due north from the barrel to the sea cliffs. An isolated windmill stands on the bluffs, with another clue in an abandoned jug beside it. Murlocs and Defias scavengers roam the coast, making the way perilous.

quest:14.text: The People's Militia. In southern Westfall, volunteers of The People's Militia press their fight against the Defias. The seasoned brigands hold the Dagger Hills, and Gryan Stoutmantle leads a campaign to clear the roads and farms. Complete the patrols, and you earn full induction at Sentinel Hill. The Defias Brotherhood has brought great hardship to Westfall's northern farmlands. Those who escaped Gryan Stoutmantle's first sweeps fled south to the rocky Dagger Hills. From there, Defias Highwaymen, Pathstalkers, and Knuckledusters still raid homesteads and waylay travelers. You join hardened recruits sent into the hills to break the brigands' hold over southern Westfall. After returning from the fight against the Scourge in Lordaeron, Gryan Stoutmantle found Westfall abandoned by Stormwind's royal garrison. A criminal syndicate went unchecked, and hunger drove farmers from their land. So he rallied local volunteers to take up arms. Complete this final patrol, and Stoutmantle blesses you in the Light as he formally inducts you into the militia. The fight against the Brotherhood deepens.

quest:140.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A whiskey-soaked clue sends you west from Westfall's shore and out across the Great Sea. Captain Sanders' trail ends at a remote islet, where his hidden prize waits. Captain Sanders left clues along Westfall's coast for you to piece together. The last parchment came from the dregs of his favorite whiskey jug. It gives the final bearing: head west to the water's edge, then swim into the waves.

quest:141.text: The Defias Brotherhood. From Stormwind, Mathias Shaw sends Gryan Stoutmantle a confidential report at Sentinel Hill. Shaw investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:142.text: The Defias Brotherhood. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you after an elusive Defias courier, hoping to learn how the Brotherhood directs its forces. Gryan Stoutmantle's scouts have seen an elusive Defias Messenger traveling between Moonbrook, the Gold Coast Quarry, and the Jangolode Mine. Unlike the thugs who hold the countryside, this courier carries written orders across the region. Stoutmantle wants him captured or killed so the People's Militia can read his satchel and learn where the brotherhood directs its forces.

quest:143.text: Messenger to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends word west for help against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls. With Stormwind's forces absent, he hopes Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia can aid Redridge. Blackrock orcs and gnolls besiege Lakeshire, but the Stormwind Army has not arrived in force. Magistrate Solomon knows the town guards and irregulars cannot hold the Redridge Mountains alone. No royal reserves are in sight, so he writes a formal plea for help. Word has reached him of a citizen defense group forming west of Elwynn Forest, and he sends his appeal there. Gryan Stoutmantle is a veteran commander rallying volunteer fighters under the People's Militia banner. Solomon sends his dispatch across the kingdom, hoping Westfall's volunteers can reinforce Lakeshire's borders until the Crown's armies mobilize. Yet Westfall is fighting its own desperate struggle against the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:144.text: Messenger to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon receives a hard answer from Westfall. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall faces troubles of its own. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. So he writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall, and asks the southern frontier for help. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are. Gryan Stoutmantle refuses, though the answer weighs heavily on him. Westfall fights the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned the kingdom's breadbasket. The People's Militia formed to help the people survive. Its ranks lose good men each day, and Stoutmantle cannot spare a single fighter for Redridge.

quest:145.text: Messenger to Darkshire. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Darkshire for aid. Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten Redridge, and Solomon seeks military support from his neighbor. A courier must cross Duskwood to deliver the letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke, Darkshire's mayor. Blackrock orcs and gnoll packs press Redridge, while Lakeshire's guards are stretched thin. Stormwind's royal court has ignored Magistrate Solomon's pleas, and Westfall is caught in its own insurrection. With little help nearby, Solomon writes to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Duskwood. He hopes Darkshire can lend or hire its Night Watch to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. Solomon's letter travels south through Duskwood, a forest under supernatural gloom. He warns you to keep to the roads because the wilderness between Lakeshire and Darkshire is perilous. The letter is bound for Town Hall, where Lord Ebonlocke can receive it. Whether Duskwood can spare any forces remains uncertain.

quest:1453.text: Reclaimers' Business in Desolace. Roetten Stonehammer sends travelers from Ironforge across the sea to Desolace for paid work with the Reclaimers. At Nijel's Point, Kreldig Ungor needs help recovering lost treasures and relics. Beyond the sea, Desolace is a harsh stretch of Kalimdor ruled by warring centaur clans. The Reclaimers seek profit among its forgotten ruins and barren lands. For those willing to face the danger, the journey may pay well. The route runs west through the Stonetalon Mountains and into northern Desolace. High among the cliffs, Nijel's Point is an Alliance outpost where Kreldig Ungor welcomes new hands. The Reclaimers recover heirlooms, magical artifacts, and family treasures lost across the war-torn world. For the right price, Kreldig and his associates retrieve those valuables from the wild.

quest:146.text: Messenger to Darkshire. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers a plea for help from Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls press against the town, but the plea cannot be granted. Magistrate Solomon of Redridge asks his old peer in Duskwood for troops. Blackrock orcs and gnolls are closing in on his town. Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers in anger. Darkshire struggles against the living dead, ravenous beasts, and cursed magic on every side. Ebonlocke says the Night Watch exists because Stormwind abandoned Duskwood. Without its defenders, Darkshire would fall before a patrol could cross the forest.

quest:1462.text: Earth Sapta. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather prepares another Earth Sapta for a young shaman whose brew was lost before the rite was complete. The draught opens a novice’s sight to the spirits of stone, so the trial can continue. Young shaman begin by learning to sense forces beyond ordinary sight. To meet Mulgore’s earth elementals, an initiate drinks a sapta made from natural essences of stone and soil. The Earth Sapta lifts the veil between the physical and spiritual realms. Then a novice can see and commune with the spirits of the land. A novice may lose or spill the brew before reaching the stone monument for communion. Seer Ravenfeather waits at Camp Narache and prepares another vessel when a pupil needs one. With the draught restored, the novice can continue the rite and face the spirits.

quest:1463.text: Earth Sapta. In the Valley of Trials, Earth Sapta is lost, and an initiate can ask Canaga Earthcaller for another. The replacement lets the young shaman commune with the spirits of the land, with a warning to guard sacred draughts carefully. An initiate who loses the Earth Sapta may lose the chance to commune with the spirits of stone and soil. Rituals prepare the elemental brew, which thins the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. If the draught is lost or spilled while traveling through Durotar, Canaga Earthcaller prepares another in good faith. He warns the novice to guard sacred gifts with greater care. Canaga Earthcaller watches over fledgling shamans emerging from the Den in the Valley of Trials. Young orcs and trolls can stumble amid their early trials, but elemental spirits do not take kindly to negligence. Accepting a second sapta brings a small lesson in humility. Power granted by the earth must be guarded and respected.

quest:147.text: Manhunt. In Elwynn Forest, Marshal Dughan sends you to find the Collector, a Defias bagman. He works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines to the Brotherhood. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

quest:1470.text: Piercing the Veil. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand tests a novice warlock's resolve. Newly risen Forsaken gather skulls from nearby mindless skeletons to earn the knowledge to summon and bind an imp. Venya Marthand teaches newly awakened Forsaken warlocks in Deathknell that strength comes through knowledge and mastery of chaotic powers. She sends them to gather skulls from Rattlecage Skeletons near Deathknell's abandoned smithy. The trial tests whether they can focus enough to command powers beyond this world and subdue nether beings. Venya accepts the skulls as proof that a novice can overcome mindless undead and face the bleak truths of warlock craft. Then she teaches the rituals to summon and bind an imp. Small as it is, the demon brings cunning and fire, and makes a dangerous ally.

quest:1471.text: The Binding. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks seek power over a voidwalker they can summon and command forever. Carendin Halgar oversees the rite that grants them this power. Forsaken warlocks must prove they can master a voidwalker before they may summon one. Minor imps are easily drawn into pacts by dark magic. Creatures of the Void despise reality and wield formidable physical might. In the Magic Quarter, mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes that tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm. Beneath Carendin Halgar's dais, a glowing summoning circle is etched into the floor. Activate the runes, and an unbound voidwalker appears in fury. Diplomacy cannot subdue it; arcane force and raw will must break it. Only when the creature is thoroughly crushed does Carendin reveal the true summoning formula, binding its essence to you indefinitely.

quest:1473.text: Creature of the Void. In the Undercity, Forsaken warlocks seek the grimoire needed to summon a voidwalker. They must recover Egalin's Grimoire from the Scarlet Crusade in western Tirisfal Glades to learn how to summon and bind one. Carendin Halgar guides Forsaken summoners in the Temple of the Damned. When an acolyte can wield more than the power of petty imps, Halgar points them toward a voidwalker. The creature is forged from pure shadow and chaos. Forsaken warlocks depend on the careful research of Egalin, Halgar's former master, who wrote the rituals for subduing such beings. Egalin's Grimoire holds the methods for channeling the volatile magic needed to master a voidwalker. Perrine, a Scarlet Crusade zealot, stole the book and keeps it in an outpost tower to the west. The Crusade may regard it only as blasphemous contraband to seize and hoard. Recovering it gives the Forsaken the ritual secrets they need before they try to tear open the veil.

quest:1478.text: Halgar's Summons. In Undercity, Halgar's Summons calls promising Forsaken warlocks to advanced training. Carendin Halgar awaits those who have mastered the first fel arts in the Magic Quarter, where dangerous beings from the Nether test their skill. A warlock's command of basic fel energies earns notice in Brill or the Tirisfal wilderness. Ageron Kargal, a senior practitioner who recognizes talent, sends word to those who show promise. Carendin Halgar's summons is a rare privilege and a perilous step in a warlock's training. Basic imps and petty curses no longer suffice. Carendin Halgar oversees warlock rites in Undercity's Magic Quarter, near the Temple of the Damned. Forsaken darkcasters lack the moral restraint of the living, but summoning across the planes still demands discipline. Halgar tolerates neither hesitation nor sentiment. Those called to him are expected to show deference and face the hostile horrors of the Twisting Nether.

quest:1485.text: Vile Familiars. Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten warlocks who seek the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength by bringing back their heads. This is the first dangerous step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes. Warlocks have an uneasy place in Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Durotar tolerates fel magic, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live apart and practice in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength before he teaches you the dangerous rites for bending an imp to your will. Vile Familiars lurk near a cave northeast of the Den and hurl bolts of flame at those who approach. Slay these lesser demons and bring their heads back to Ruzan. They will show him you can overcome the fiery creatures you hope to control. Only then can you face the danger of the magic you seek to command.

quest:1486.text: Deviate Hides. At the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak seeks a use for the strange properties of deviate hides. A disciple of Naralex, he keeps watch above the entrance while his teacher lies trapped in a twisted nightmare. Beneath the Barrens, mutated beasts roam, and Nalpak hopes their skins can serve a practical purpose. Naralex sought to awaken the springs beneath the Barrens and restore life to the dry plains. Instead, the Wailing Caverns became dangerous. The night elf druid's mind slipped into a terrifying nightmare, and that nightmare reached the waking world. Raptors, crocolisks, vipers, and shambling horrors turned vicious and misshapen, warped by emerald corruption leaking from their dreaming master. From the rock above the cavern mouth, Nalpak watches the disaster with dread and practical curiosity. He knows the deviate beasts are malignant and unnatural, yet their corrupted forms may yield useful materials. Their tough, warped pelts could help skilled leatherworkers. Nalpak hopes to make durable equipment from the fruits of a tragic nightmare.

quest:1489.text: Hamuul Runetotem. Tonga Runetotem sends you to Thunder Bluff as a strange taint spreads through the Barrens. He suspects the Wailing Caverns lie at its heart and seeks Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem’s counsel. Near the Barrens’ oases, Tonga Runetotem found creatures marked by a strange affliction. An unnatural taint covered their shells, and Tonga came to believe the land itself was caught in a troubled dream. He suspects the waters flowing from the Wailing Caverns are to blame. Entering those caverns calls for more wisdom than one naturalist can offer. Tonga sends you to Thunder Bluff for counsel from his kin, Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. Hamuul is the highest-ranking tauren druid and a revered spiritual leader of the Cenarion Circle in Mulgore. From Elder Rise, he watches for disturbances across Kalimdor. He confirms the nightmare spreading through the Barrens is a dire threat, calling for the full might of Horde champions.

quest:1490.text:
Nara Wildmane. In Thunder Bluff, Nara Wildmane helps the Horde grasp the danger in the Wailing Caverns. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem saw corruption in the Emerald Dream but could not endure it, so he sent travelers to his young disciple. Nara saw the nightmare taking hold of their kin. Unnatural signs spread across the Barrens, and Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem entered the Emerald Dream to find their cause. There he found a druidic cult that had once hoped to restore life to the dry savannah. A vile taint had driven its members mad.

Age kept Hamuul from enduring the nightmare’s assault, so he fled to the waking world. His younger disciple, Nara Wildmane, refused to leave so soon. Her fierce resolve kept her in the dreamscape, where she saw the transformed cult for herself.

quest:1491.text: Smart Drinks. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix seeks a new formula for his drink. His brew of powdered Sunscale raptor horns disappointed him, so he now wants ectoplasmic residue from the Wailing Caverns. Mebok Mizzyrix sells goods in Ratchet and hopes to make a fortune with a drink that sharpens the mind. His first formula used powdered Sunscale raptor horns, but the brew disappointed him. Now he has turned to the strange essence seeping from the Wailing Caverns, hoping it will make his drink succeed. Strange changes have come to the Barrens. New oases have appeared, and local wildlife has grown aggressive and warped. Mebok suspects a substance he calls Wailing Essence is behind them. He sends you into the cavern labyrinth to destroy its oozing ectoplasms and gather their glowing fluid in bottles for his formula.

quest:1492.text: Wharfmaster Dizzywig. At Ratchet's pier, Wharfmaster Dizzywig finds passage for a crate of alchemy supplies. It is bound for the Old World aboard a ship sailing to Blackwater Cove. A crate of potions and reagents waits at the Barrens port for colleagues in the Old World. The caravans that could have carried it have already left. So you are asked to bring the secure shipment to Ratchet's water's edge. From there, ships cross the Great Sea between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Cargo passes through Wharfmaster Dizzywig's hands on Ratchet's wooden piers. He records each shipment in ledgers and manifests, then finds room aboard vessels sailing east across the Great Sea. This crate is booked for a ship bound for Blackwater Cove.

quest:1498.text: Path of Defense. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek teaches young Horde warriors to defend those who cannot defend themselves. He sends them to Thunder Ridge to test their endurance against its electric beasts. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek teaches young warriors that the Horde has a duty to defend. The post lies on the border between the Barrens and Durotar. He says a warrior’s highest calling is to stand between danger and those unable to defend themselves. They take the blows so the Horde can endure. Uzzek sends the novices to Thunder Ridge, north across the Southfury River in Durotar, to test their stamina and resolve. Thunder lizards and lightning hides roam the canyon. The initiates must endure the beasts’ jolts and gather their singed scales. That trial shows they have the fortitude to hold the front line.

quest:1499.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Ruzan tests warlock initiates against vile familiars. After you slay them, you report to Zureetha Fargaze, who directs the effort against the Burning Blade. Warriors and scouts in the Valley of Trials answer to Zureetha Fargaze. She sends them to curb the Burning Blade Coven. Warlock initiates answer first to Ruzan, their shadowy mentor. He demands proof that you can master lesser demons before sending you back to aid the Horde's defense. Your work helps the warlocks and keeps the Den safe. Zureetha Fargaze watches the northern cavern above the Valley of Trials. Vile familiars hide within, the weakest pets of the Burning Blade cultists. Their presence insults the orcs and threatens the sacred training grounds. When you report your success, you show that those who practice fel magic are ready to defend Durotar from corruption.

quest:15.text: Investigate Echo Ridge. Kobolds gather in force at Echo Ridge Mine, so Marshal McBride sends you north. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard stationed there. Scattered vermin have troubled the valley's forested edge near Northshire. Now the scouts report a more organized gathering. At the entrance, you face kobold workers and see how deeply they have settled into the mine. The kobolds have seized the tunnels and stopped the digging. Their presence strains the Northshire brotherhood's defenses. McBride asks you to cull ten workers, but the infestation reaches farther into the shafts than a surface patrol can reach.

quest:1501.text: Creature of the Void. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends a young warlock to recover the stolen Tablet of Verga. Burning Blade cultists have carried it to their cavern at Skull Rock, where its runes are needed to summon a voidwalker. Gan'rul Bloodeye trains Horde warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow. Thrall's new realm distrusts fel magic because of the orcish clans' dark history. Few true warlocks remain in the Horde, Gan'rul says, yet their perilous skills are needed for its survival. To serve the Warchief, an initiate must master more than an imp's chaotic fire. They must command beings of pure shadow and endurance. The runes for summoning a voidwalker are carved on the Tablet of Verga. The Burning Blade, a fanatical shadow cult, stole the relic and hides in a cavern at Skull Rock, beneath the Warchief's nose. Gan'rul sends you into their den to recover it and strike a bloody blow against renegades who stain the name of every warlock.

quest:1502.text: Thun'grim Firegaze. Atop Thorn Hill, a lone forge draws warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze. After their first lessons in defense, Horde warriors cross the Barrens seeking steel suited to their growing skill. After you demonstrate skill in the defensive arts under veteran trainers such as Uzzek, you are sent to sharpen your fighting with suitable steel. Ordinary armories can carry a frontline fighter only so far. True mastery calls for a personal weapon from a smith of renown. In the Barrens, that smith is Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc who left settlement life behind for an isolated forge high above the plains. Thun'grim Firegaze lives atop Thorn Hill, a jagged rise east of the Crossroads. Wild raptors and hostile quilboar roam there, far from the protection of town walls. He spends his solitary hours shaping metal. Decades gazing into blistering forge flames have ruined his eyesight, though his instincts remain sharp. When you climb the heights and disturb his solitude, he knows why: a warrior has come seeking forged steel.

quest:1503.text: Forged Steel. In the eastern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze waits for the steel stolen from his camp. He will forge a weapon for the warrior who brings it back. Thun'grim Firegaze keeps a smithy in the eastern Barrens, far from Orgrimmar. Years at the forge have dimmed his sight. The nearby Razormane quilboar used that weakness to steal an iron chest from his camp. Some snorted and made noise on one side to draw his gaze while others slipped in from the other and carried off his forged steel bars. Thun'grim is angry at the theft, but doubts the Razormanes can use the steel. Quilboar craft with stone, tusks and thorny roots, not refined metal. The heavy chest remains near a broken wagon in their camp, untouched and useless to them. For Thun'grim, its steel is the stock he needs to forge weapons for young Horde warriors.

quest:1504.text: The Binding. In Orgrimmar, The Binding marks young Horde warlocks' final initiation ritual. Gan'rul Bloodeye directs each petitioner to use glyphs from the Tablet of Verga in Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle. You face your first true test of will when you summon a voidwalker. An imp is child's play by comparison. Warlocks do not make pacts with these creatures or commune with them. You pull them across dimensions by force and bind them to serve. Gan'rul Bloodeye directs you to use glyphs from the Tablet of Verga and call the voidwalker into Neeru Fireblade's ritual circle, to break it there in single combat. Defeating the voidwalker in physical and magical combat is only half the struggle. Gan'rul Bloodeye warns that a bound voidwalker never truly accepts its enslavement. Even while it guards its master in battle as a durable, shadowy bulwark, it waits for a lapse in your concentration. If your hold over your servant ever falters, it will consume the soul of the one who bound it.

quest:1506.text: Gan'rul's Summons. Ophek brings Gan'rul's Summons to young Horde warlocks in Razor Hill. Gan'rul Bloodeye calls them to the Cleft of Shadow to advance their training. There, they take the first step toward summoning a voidwalker. In Durotar, novice warlocks do not go unnoticed for long. When a practitioner shows enough mastery over an initial imp, word reaches the deep caverns beneath Orgrimmar. Ophek carries messages for the senior dark casters from his post in Durotar. He finds warlocks with an urgent demand to leave their work and report to the Cleft of Shadow. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the training of young orc warlocks within the Horde. From the hidden caverns beneath Orgrimmar, he hones their lethal fel power while keeping these dangerous arts from the Warchief's disapproving gaze. A call to his circle means simple fire spells and imps are no longer enough. The apprentice is ready to bind a creature from the Twisting Nether.

quest:151.text: Poor Old Blanchy. On Westfall's road, Poor Old Blanchy waits with the stranded Furlbrows, worn out and hungry. Their wagon broke as they fled, and Verna asks you to find oats at nearby abandoned farms to feed the mare. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. The Furlbrows tried to carry their belongings to safety, but their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country. Old Blanchy has plowed and hauled for the Furlbrow family through many seasons. Now the delay has left the gentle mare exhausted and starving. Verna asks you to search nearby overrun farmsteads for sacks of oats. Hostile threshers and gnoll scavengers threaten there, but the grain could give the faithful mare a decent meal.

quest:1516.text: Call of Earth. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller tests novice Horde shamans through endurance and patience. Their hunt for felstalkers prepares a ritual sapta. A shaman first learns to bond with each element. For orcs and trolls, that path begins with earth, the bedrock of life, endurance, and patience. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new shamans. He teaches them that earth demands respect and steadfastness before it grants protection. North of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade cult works dark magic in the ravines. Its spells summon felstalkers, corrupt hounds from beyond this plane. Hunting them tests whether a shaman can defend the land from unnatural decay. Canaga uses their hooves to brew an Earth Sapta, a sacred draft that opens mortal eyes to the elemental plane.

quest:1517.text: Call of Earth. At Spirit Rock, Canaga Earthcaller guides young shaman through their first communion with the elements. An Earth Sapta lets them see the Minor Manifestation of Earth on sacred ground. A sapta is a rare draught known to only a few shaman masters. Elemental magic lets it bridge mortal sight and the spiritual plane, granting Sapta Sight to the strong-willed. Since it binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition forbids drinking it outside consecrated holy ground. To commune with earth, you leave the Valley of Trials and climb the Hidden Path into Durotar's southern crags. Spirit Rock waits at the trail's end, an elevated sanctuary above the rugged wasteland. Drink the sapta there, and you can see what ordinary eyes cannot: an elemental presence among the stone. The Minor Manifestation of Earth asks for neither bloodshed nor submission. It asks only that you stand humbly before the world. Fire, water, and air bear turbulent, volatile, often chaotic spirits, while earth teaches steadiness. Mountains endure, and plains teach boundless patience.

quest:1518.text:
Call of Earth. In Durotar, you seek the earth spirit’s favor and return to Canaga Earthcaller with rough quartz. He shapes it into your first elemental totem. A novice shaman seeks the earth through patience and humility. Brute strength will not win the spirit’s favor. The Minor Manifestation of Earth gives you rough quartz. That small stone proves the spirit has accepted your pledge, and it holds the seed of power. You complete the trial when you bring the quartz to Canaga Earthcaller in the Valley of Trials. Canaga shapes it into an Earth Totem, the focus through which you channel the ground’s steadfast protection and strength.

Earth begins your path through the four elemental disciplines. The rite lays the foundation for a lifetime of communion with the natural world.

quest:152.text: The Coast Isn't Clear. Shipwrecked sailors struggle to reach Westfall's western shore as murlocs close in. Captain Grayson calls on you to clear the beaches so survivors can land safely. Reefs, squalls, and jagged rocks drive ships onto Westfall's shoals. Survivors cling to wreckage and crawl onto the sand, hoping help will come. They find murloc tribes along the shore instead, and the murlocs show no mercy to castaways. Captain Grayson watches from a lonely outcropping southwest of the mainland. Though dead, he remains bound to the lighthouse and to his duty toward passing ships and lost sailors. Coastrunners hold the northern shore. Farther south, Tidehunters, Warriors, and Oracles gather.

quest:1520.text: Call of Earth. At Kodo Rock, you seek communion with earth through a sacred tauren rite. Drink an Earth Sapta to see a Minor Manifestation of Earth. Shamanic elders brew a sapta to join an initiate’s mortal spirit to a primal element. Ancestral magic guards the recipe, known to only a few tauren. Drink the draught at a sacred site, and your mind opens beyond the physical world. The veil parts, revealing the elements in their raw form. East of Camp Narache, Kodo Rock rises as a stone pillar and holy sanctuary. Drink the sapta there, and a Minor Manifestation of Earth appears before you. Other aspects of nature along the shaman’s path are volatile, fiery, or raging. Earth asks for quiet humility. Honor the land, and its spirit grants you the mountain’s enduring strength and the plains’ calm patience.

quest:1521.text: Call of Earth. In Mulgore, a young tauren shaman returns to Camp Narache bearing a gift from the earth. The Earth Sapta lets the initiate speak with a spirit and receive raw stone, beginning the path through the four elements. After drinking the Earth Sapta, you meet the Minor Manifestation of Earth on the crags near Red Cloud Mesa. The spirit gives you Rough Quartz, a plain stone that marks your pact with the element and its endurance. Patience and strength are the virtues earth demands. Through mutual respect, the spirit promises harmony with the land. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather shapes the gifted quartz into your first Earth Totem. More than a mark of status, it is a lasting anchor for body and spirit. Through this carved focus, you channel the earth’s grounding and protective magic. It is your first true step along the fourfold elemental path.

quest:1524.text: Call of Fire. In the Barrens, Kranal Fiss sends an aspiring shaman toward the next trial for communion with fire. The initiate crosses the Southfury River to a secluded mountaintop shrine in Durotar, carrying an unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame. Kranal Fiss entrusts you with the Torch of the Dormant Flame. Raw mystical strength cannot meet fire’s demands; the trial calls for temperance, focus, and respect. The torch is both a ritual instrument and proof to the shrine’s keeper that you are judged ready to attempt the trial. The shrine lies across the Southfury River, among Durotar’s southern crags. A weathered stone carved with a fire rune marks an obscure path climbing toward one of the region’s highest peaks. At the summit, Telf Joolam, a troll hermit, watches over the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. He turns away curious travelers and treasure hunters, keeping the sacred brazier from ordinary eyes until a petitioner arrives with the unlit torch.

quest:1525.text: Call of Fire. Telf Joolam sends you through Durotar and the eastern Barrens to gather what he needs for a Fire Sapta. The draught prepares an initiate to see and speak with fire spirits. A Fire Sapta opens a shaman’s senses to the Eternal Flame. Like the draught for earth, it lets you see and speak with spirits hidden from mortal sight. Telf Joolam sends you across Durotar and into the eastern Barrens for ingredients bound to heat and flame. Razormane quilboar spellcasters in the eastern Barrens carry fire tar, made in their earthy rituals. Burning Blade cultists carry the other ingredient in Dustwind Cave, in the ravines northeast of Razor Hill. They use fire for destruction and demonic chaos, yet the reagents in their pouches have a natural tie to the element.

quest:1526.text: Call of Fire. On Durotar's peaks, Call of Fire puts a shaman to a trial of flame. Telf Joolam sends the initiate to drink fire sapta, face a Minor Manifestation of Fire, and claim its ember. On Durotar's summit, fire spirits remain hidden from untrained eyes. Drink fire sapta, a draught made from reagents gathered across the barrens and coast, and your senses sharpen to the unseen. Minor spirits and manifestations appear among the summit crags. A Minor Manifestation of Fire waits atop the mountain. Once the sapta takes hold, it knows you can see it and awaits your challenge. Fire answers strength and decisive action, so strike without delay. The longer the fight lasts, the more fiercely the elemental fire burns.

quest:153.text: Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the Defias fight. Scout Galiaan seeks the red masks worn by outlaws as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, a red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life join the gang, then rally beneath the same crimson sign. At Sentinel Hill, Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia collect the cloth as proof that bandits have fallen. The bandanas also help them follow the Defias as its fronts shift across the countryside. Stormwind has denied Westfall proper military support, leaving the People's Militia to chart Defias activity with seasoned observers like Scout Galiaan. From Sentinel Hill, Galiaan watches outlaw patrols and tracks their movements. Passing adventurers and militia volunteers take on the dangerous work of bringing down the highwaymen who drove honest farmers from their land.

quest:155.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A captured brigand will guide you there in exchange for protection, leading through Moonbrook to Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum. The Defias Traitor fears execution or assassination by his former brothers. So he bargains with the People's Militia: escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

quest:1578.text: Supplying the Front. In Loch Modan, Mountaineers need fresh arms as trogg attacks threaten their defenses. Tormus Deepforge sends apprentice smiths east to supply them. Excavations have opened ruins and caverns across the border. Troggs now strike the Mountaineers without warning. Their lines need fresh blades, belts, and fittings to hold against the attacks. Tormus sends apprentices east while veteran smiths stay at Ironforge’s city forges. His colleague Thorvald Deepforge keeps a field armory in the southern guard tower. There, sturdy copper axes and copper chain belts prove a smith’s reliability and earn advanced smithing techniques.

quest:1579.text: Gaffer Jacks. Near Auberdine, Wizbang Cranktoggle needs his lost gaffer jacks. He lost a box of hardware overboard on his voyage from Ironforge, and the parts lie somewhere along Darkshore's coast. Wizbang Cranktoggle crossed the Great Sea from Ironforge seeking quiet in Darkshore. The gnome inventor drank too much on the voyage. In a drunken haze, he leaned over the rail and lost a crate of specialized metal parts called gaffer jacks in the water near Auberdine. Wizbang says gaffer jacks are essential precision tools. Without them, he cannot tune his stintle pegs or continue his delicate tinkering. He will not wade into the cold surf himself, so he asks local anglers to cast along Darkshore's shore and fish up the scattered parts.

quest:1580.text: Electropellers. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle wants his lost electropellers back. A mishap with an explosive duck decoy scattered the prototype parts in freshwater streams. Wizbang Cranktoggle went inland one evening to find a place to test his latest invention. The gnome tinkerer, based in Auberdine, had built a self-propelled duck decoy that explodes. He drank too much and blacked out. Hours later, he woke in town with singed hair and an empty pack; his bag of electropellers had fallen into one of the coastal rivers. Wizbang asks local fishermen to dredge Darkshore's freshwater streams, for he will not brave the wilds himself. Anglers on the Wildbend River and Cliffspring River can snag the buoyant metal parts along with local fish. Once the components are back, Wizbang can resume his erratic waterfowl experiments.

quest:1581.text: Elixirs for the Bladeleafs. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf seeks help supplying her family's busy trade. Her husband spends nearly all his time brewing, and fresh elixirs could ease his burden while bringing him uncommon herbs. Dolanaar sees travelers, sentinels, and druids crossing Teldrassil. Syral Bladeleaf and her husband have built a thriving herb and alchemy trade to serve them. Demand keeps him at vials and cauldrons for nearly all his waking hours. The work leaves little time for the two of them. Syral asks passing herbalists and brewers to ease her husband's workload. She seeks Elixirs of Lion's Strength and Minor Defense, and offers freshly gathered, uncommon herbs in exchange. For a budding alchemist beneath the Great Tree, the trade brings a bundle of herbs and a chance to turn common forest plants into prized local wares.

quest:1582.text: Moonglow Vest. In Darnassus, Lotherias prepares leather gear for young adventurers setting out across Kalimdor. She offers a night elf pattern in return for shipments of embossed leather goods. Darnassus leatherworkers outfit sentinels and young scouts. Night elves and allied wanderers leave Teldrassil for Kalimdor's wilds, where sturdy armor is in demand. Lotherias is a master leatherworker who supplies them with gear. Lotherias asks apprentices to bring matching embossed gloves, boots, and cloaks to show their skill. Those who fulfill her order earn her trust. She teaches them a night elf pattern for a vest that protects while allowing free movement.

quest:1598.text: The Stolen Tome. At Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle seeks a stolen tome from the Defias camp in the vineyards. Powers of the Void could aid her teaching, and bringing it back will prove your skill. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands keep their craft and their research from prying eyes. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the protected wing herself. She covets Powers of the Void and needs another to retrieve it. An abbey novice joined the Defias Brotherhood and stole several valuable texts as he left. He fled to the Northshire Vineyards and took refuge near the Defias campsite. The thieves keep their prize in a field tent, unaware of the danger in the book's dark arts. Recovering Powers of the Void tests your nerve and opens the way to darker knowledge. Returning the tome satisfies Drusilla's ambition and proves you are ready to practice the dark arts. She rewards you with the rites to summon and bind an imp, the first demon an apprentice learns to command.

quest:1599.text: Beginnings. In Dun Morogh, Alamar Grimm tests Alliance warlock novices before teaching them to summon an imp. First, they must take feather charms from Frostmane troll novices. Influential voices have noticed a recruit with promise, and their attention draws Alamar Grimm from his occult research. Though reluctant, the warlock comes to assess the novice. Before teaching a novice to enslave lesser demons, Grimm demands proof of endurance and magical affinity. Frostmane troll novices carry feather charms in a cave southwest of Anvilmar. Subtle primal magic runs through the charms, and taking them proves the novice can overcome a magical foe. The curious specimens also serve Grimm's research. The charms persuade Grimm that the novice has the will to survive. He teaches the summoning of an imp, a warlock's most basic minion. Its chaotic fire magic can overpower a master who lacks discipline.

quest:16.text: Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. Passing travelers bring water and trade it for apples. Elwynn's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. The work is hot beneath the open sky. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller tends the crops, keeps pests away, and manages the harvest. With little time to reach the town wells, he depends on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working. Gerard trades provisions for water instead of coin. Travelers with extra flasks of Refreshing Spring Water can exchange them for fresh apples from his orchard. The kingdom stretches its resources to keep order and feed its army. So barter between smallholders and recruits remains a practical way to get by in rural Elwynn.

quest:161.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh suspects sabotage and sends a powder sample north for examination. A courier must carry it through the Wetlands to demolition expert Ashlan Stonesmirk at Dun Modr. A suspicious barrel near the dam’s eastern ramp held a strange-smelling powder. Hinderweir had seen Dark Iron sappers nearby, and suspects the powder is a refined explosive meant to shatter dwarven masonry. The dam has no specialized equipment to test it. Before he can be certain, he needs a military demolitionist to examine the sample. The road runs through the Algaz Gate and down into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. Hostile wildlife, aggressive dragonkin, and Dark Iron infiltrators make the way dangerous. Hinderweir urges couriers to keep to the cobbled road to Dun Modr. The pillaged dwarven town stands at the southern approach to the Thandol Span, where an Ironforge regiment still keeps watch.

quest:1618.text: Gearing Redridge. In Lakeshire, a hard pressed garrison needs sturdy copper gear from Ironforge. Tormus Deepforge asks aspiring Alliance smiths to forge it and aid Verner Osgood as he helps defend the region from hostile orcs and gnolls. The Great Forge sends help beyond Dun Morogh, where the Alliance's front line is under strain. In the Redridge Mountains, Lakeshire faces repeated attacks from Blackrock orcs marching from Stonewatch Keep and gnolls roaming the northern ridges. Stormwind's royal reinforcements are slow to arrive, and local supplies are dangerously low. Verner Osgood, Lakeshire's resident blacksmith, works nearly alone at his outdoor forge. He mends shattered armor and replaces broken weapons.
