Seeing his human counterpart under strain, Tormus Deepforge asks developing smiths to bring four Runed Copper Belts and four Heavy Copper Mauls to Lakeshire. The gear strengthens the militia's reserves, and Verner teaches traveling craftsmen finer trade techniques.

quest:1638.text: A Warrior's Training. Lyria Du Lac sends young warriors from Goldshire to Stormwind for lessons in battlefield endurance. At the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Old Town, veteran Harry Burlguard puts them through seasoned instruction. When you have shown your skill against threats across Elwynn Forest, Goldshire's trainers have little more to teach. So Lyria Du Lac sends you to Stormwind and the rough district of Old Town. Veteran fighters gather there to share what combat has taught them, far from the royal garrison's rigid ways. Harry Burlguard is an aged battle veteran who keeps his quarters at the Pig and Whistle Tavern. He tests your mettle with drink and practical trials of stamina, not parade-ground drills. Before teaching defensive moves for dangerous campaigns, Harry expects you to match his appetite for drink and face the tavern's local brawlers.

quest:1639.text: Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces Harry Burlguard’s test. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby’s prized mug before Harry teaches deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks you to prove your backbone before he teaches deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man’s mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge tests your resolve. Soldiers, laborers, and rough locals fill the Pig and Whistle, where polished manners count for little. Bartleby mocks newcomers as too prissy for a tavern scuffle instead of answering politely. The exchange leads to a brawl on the floorboards. In Stormwind, a warrior’s training begins with a test of basic barroom fighting.

quest:1640.text: Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Beat Bartleby keeps a prized mug from the warrior instructors. He will not give it up, so a recruit must win it in a brawl. The warrior instructors make no claim that combat is noble or grand. Bartleby swears no one will take his prized mug without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. So you settle the matter with your fists. For a fledgling warrior, words give way to a brawl. Bartleby boasts that he will fight to the death, but a thorough thrashing sobers him. Bruised admiration replaces his bravado when he sees your strength, and he yields peacefully. You can take the mug to the training hall and complete your trial.

quest:1641.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides you through a solemn rite for young paladins. Its teachings test your virtue and devotion to the Holy Light. Your training now reaches beyond arms and the order's rites. Duthorian's trials ask you to weigh a paladin's moral duties and grasp the deeper promise your calling demands. Those who depend on the Holy Light need defenders who understand what that duty means. The Book of Divinity binds you to service and self-sacrifice. Duthorian asks you to study its holy text and learn what the Light demands of its defenders. Its lessons prepare you to oppose the Scourge's creeping horrors and protect common folk. Virtue and compassion must guide your power.

quest:1645.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge puts the Tome of Divinity into a dwarven paladin's hands. Its teachings begin trials of devotion to the Light and readiness to defend Azeroth from dark forces such as the Scourge. From across the eastern kingdoms, promising paladin initiates come to Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries after mastering the martial and spiritual basics. There, young dwarven paladins learn what sets a champion of the Holy Light apart from an ordinary warrior. Taking up this calling means pledging a life to duty, self-sacrifice, and spiritual discipline. The novice receives the Book of Divinity as a guide to its duties, virtues, and spiritual teachings. Its words show how sacred power can be wielded against wicked threats. Yet study is only the first step. The initiate must carry those lessons into acts of faith across Khaz Modan and beyond.

quest:1665.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind's Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby faces a young warrior's trial. After you best him, you take his drinking mug to your trainer, Harry Burlguard. In Old Town, Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl. He sends you to face Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug. First, he takes one last swig to drain the dregs. When you return the mug, Harry Burlguard accepts it as proof of your novice trial. He sees that you can win another's compliance through force and judges you ready to learn defense. Then he points you toward Marshal Haggard, a seasoned veteran in Elwynn Forest, for further instruction on the battlefield.

quest:1666.text: Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to meet Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Over a lifetime in the field, Haggard gathered a personal armory. His home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms. Marshal Haggard lives in a secluded manor near the Eastvale Logging Camp. Years of service have weakened his sight, and he sometimes mistakes approaching travelers for prowling riverpaw gnolls. Age keeps him in this quiet corner of eastern Elwynn. Even so, Stormwind's guards and trainers still respect the old marshal.

quest:1667.text: Dead-tooth Jack. In eastern Elwynn Forest, retired Marshal Haggard needs your help: Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into giving up his badge. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard and pretended to be Marshal Dughan. Haggard fears the Defias Brotherhood will use the badge to impersonate Stormwind officials. At night, a figure wearing a Stormwind tabard came to Haggard's isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. The stranger claimed to have official business and asked for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Haggard believed he was handing it to a fellow officer, so he gave it over. The figure laughed and vanished into the woods. He was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack. Marshal Haggard has retired, but his badge still carries Stormwind's legal authority. Defias bandits are creeping across Elwynn, Westfall, and Redridge. With the badge, they could pass guard checkpoints, redirect patrols, or take command of supplies. Jack retreated to a camp to the south and locked the badge in a strongbox. Haggard needs it back before the Defias cause serious harm.

quest:1679.text: Muren Stormpike. In Ironforge, Muren Stormpike awaits warriors sent from Kharanos for formal training. Granis Swiftaxe sends recruits who have proved their mettle in Dun Morogh to the city's Military Ward. Granis Swiftaxe sends promising warriors from Kharanos to Ironforge after they face local threats in Dun Morogh. He knows rough skirmishes can teach only so much. In the Military Ward, senior fighters oversee formal training for those bound for battle. At the Hall of Arms, you meet Muren Stormpike, a veteran of a storied dwarven clan. He wants proof that his new charges can endure real combat, not tavern tales. Reporting to him opens the way to learn defensive arts, control an enemy's aggression, and earn iron arms for the front line.

quest:168.text: Collecting Memories. In Stormwind City, Wilder Thistlenettle asks you to remember the miners lost beneath Moonbrook. He wants their Miners' Union Cards returned to their grieving families. Before the Defias Brotherhood brought lawlessness to Moonbrook, Westfall's mines supported many working-class families. Wilder Thistlenettle survived when a cave-in buried one wing of the tunnels. Many friends and fellow miners died underground, beyond the reach of rescue. Their families in Stormwind never learned for certain what became of them. The miners killed in the collapse now wander the tunnels outside the main iron works as undead. You search those haunted passages for their Miners' Union Cards and face the remains of the men Wilder worked beside. Bring the cards back to Stormwind so their families can learn what happened and Wilder can honor his fallen companions.

quest:1681.text: Ironband's Compound. At Ironband's Compound, Tormus Deepforge seeks vengeance for his slain mentor, Sturgy Ironband. Rare umbral ore drew the Dark Iron dwarves to the outpost and brought it down. South of Helm's Bed Lake, Sturgy Ironband taught smithing at a compound away from the Great Forge's crowded anvils. Promising pupils came there to train under a master revered across Ironforge as an unmatched instructor. Then one student acquired an unfamiliar mineral called umbral ore, and Sturgy chose to experiment with it. He did not know that its presence had marked his school for ruin. Soon after the umbral ore arrived, Dark Iron dwarves attacked the compound. They killed Sturgy Ironband and every apprentice in his care, then took over the grounds. Tormus Deepforge, one of Ironband's surviving protégés in the capital, refuses to let the massacre go unanswered. He sends Alliance travelers to avenge his teacher and recover the ore that brought destruction to the outpost.

quest:1683.text: Vorlus Vilehoof. In Darnassus, Elanaria sets young night elf warriors a trial. They must hunt a satyr defiling a hidden moonwell near the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Elanaria asks you to prove your dedication and discipline before she teaches advanced martial techniques. Those who defend Kalimdor must offer more than words. A guardian must face corruption and cleanse the sacred boughs of Teldrassil. Your trial leads to a moonwell in the mountains southeast of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. There, Vorlus Vilehoof hides. Satyrs were ancient betrayers, twisted by demonic influence, and they hate sacred Kaldorei relics. Vorlus bathes in the moonwell, fouling its blessed waters and mocking Elune's grace.

quest:1685.text: Gakin's Summons. In Stormwind, Gakin's Summons draws promising warlocks beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. Remen Marcot brings Gakin the Darkbinder's message, sending fledgling practitioners to the crypts under the tavern in the Mage Quarter for further occult training. Demonology is forbidden in Stormwind's settled districts, yet its practitioners work near the city guard. When a warlock shows skill with introductory imps, word reaches senior warlocks in secret. Remen Marcot carries their message quietly and urges new practitioners to keep the meeting place private as they make their way beneath the Mage Quarter. Cellars and hidden catacombs lie behind the Slaughtered Lamb's modest front. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches Stormwind's warlocks there, beyond the reach of Kirin Tor mages and the Cathedral's inquisitors. Under his guidance, warlocks learn to command a voidwalker. The rite demands dangerous stolen reagents and perilous summoning circles.

quest:1686.text: The Shade of Elura. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors beneath Auberdine's waves to lay Elura to rest. They seek her medallion and Elunite ore for a weapon Smith Mathiel will forge. Long ago, a ship laden with rare Elunite ore struck rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse and sank. Its captain, Elura, cursed her own soul in despair and from unwavering duty. Bound to the wreck beneath the waves, her shade guards the lost cargo from anyone who would disturb it. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into Darkshore's surf to defeat Elura and recover her medallion and ore. Both are needed to put the captain to rest, and the metal goes to Smith Mathiel's forge. The trial tests their martial skill and respect for the fallen. It also provides ore for a crafted weapon.

quest:1688.text: Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and the bloodstone choker she carries. He sends a new apprentice after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him and joined the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. Once, he took Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. But Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:1689.text: The Binding. Beneath Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder sets you a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Below the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter lie catacombs beyond the watch of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin teaches that dark magic takes more than power. It demands mastery over beings from beyond this world. You recovered his stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to summon a voidwalker beneath the tavern. A voidwalker will not bargain with you. The Bloodstone Choker opens a rift and draws the shadow creature into the mortal world. You batter it with magic and force until its will breaks. Then its essence binds to you, giving you a durable shadowy protector that can endure punishment in the battles ahead.

quest:1692.text: Smith Mathiel. In Darnassus, sacred elunite ore is on its way to the forge. After you recover it from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine, Elanaria sends you to Mathiel to shape it into a weapon for the Kaldorei. Elanaria sends you across Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace with the elunite ore you recovered from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine. The warrior trainer packs the ore in a sturdy case and directs you to Mathiel, one of the capital's finest smiths. He can shape the metal into a weapon worthy of your calling. Mathiel treats smithing as an act of devotion. Elunite bears the sacred blessing of Elune, the Moon Goddess, and he accepts the case as an honor. He will shape the holy metal into arms to defend the young boughs of Teldrassil.

quest:1693.text: Weapons of Elunite. In Darnassus, Weapons of Elunite brings a young warrior's rite of passage to its end. You carry ore blessed by Elune to Mathiel, who forges it into arms for a defender of Kalimdor. Night elf warriors defend Teldrassil and the kaldorei people. Promising young warriors gather elunite, a mineral blessed by the Moon Goddess, to arm themselves beyond ordinary steel. Its ore needs a smith skilled in metalcraft and mindful of Elune's gift. Mathiel works in Darnassus, shaping blessed elunite into weapons of war. He considers the work an honor, not routine metalcraft. Bring him the ore, and he forges arms to suit your style. For your service, he gives you weapons blessed by your goddess.

quest:170.text: A New Threat. Balir Frosthammer calls for aid as Rockjaw troggs surge through Coldridge Valley and threaten its settlements and camps. Rockjaw troggs claw up from below in growing numbers. Reports reach Anvilmar of troggs swarming the frozen lake and nearby foothills. They disrupt patrols and cut supply routes through the valley pass. For young dwarven warriors and mountaineers, this valley has long been a place to train. Now the threat reaches it. A coordinated trogg attack has overrun a dwarven camp west of the valley. The mountaineers retreated and left their posts. Ironforge cannot spare full battle regiments, so Balir Frosthammer calls on newly recruited adventurers to fight through the Rockjaw ranks. The hills must be secured before the creatures reach Anvilmar.

quest:1715.text: The Slaughtered Lamb. Gnome warlocks from Ironforge now seek their training in Stormwind. The Slaughtered Lamb gives them a place to learn from human warlocks, while King Magni Bronzebeard keeps watch over dark practitioners at home. Before Gnomeregan fell, Khaz Modan's aspiring warlocks studied with tinker-mages and demonic scholars in the techno-city. Then disaster scattered those schools and drove the gnomes into exile. The survivors crowded into Ironforge's underground caverns, where King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarven guard watch them. They cannot openly practice demonic arts or perform dangerous rituals, so senior instructors like Lago Blackwrench send students away. From Ironforge, gnome students travel south to the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Twisting stone passages and stairs descend from the tavern's taproom to a hidden sanctum where human warlocks gather. Gakin the Darkbinder oversees them there. In its shadowed rooms, instructors can teach novices to summon and bind minor demons without drawing the city marshals' immediate anger. Stormwind's coven welcomes capable hands, though refugee novices bring new strain. Human mentors already risk discovery by the city's paladins and authorities. As more practitioners arrive from Khaz Modan, Gakin and his colleagues find their sanctuary growing crowded. The steady flow from the dwarven mountain could expose their hidden gathering. Yet neither the gnomes nor the human warlocks have an easier choice.

quest:176.text: Wanted: "Hogger". In southwestern Elwynn, Hogger has turned back every local attempt to bring him down. The Alliance bounty posted outside Goldshire seeks the head of this massive, savage gnoll chieftain. Banditry and kobold infestations trouble Elwynn Forest, while gnolls in the south grow bolder and more organized under Hogger's brutal leadership. Taller than typical Riverpaw gnolls, he has made camp near the Forest's Edge. From there, he ambushes travelers and overpowers the local militia patrols sent to subdue him. The Stormwind Army is stretched thin and cannot spare regular forces to police the capital's outskirts. So Marshal Dughan has taken the unusual step of posting an open bounty on Hogger. Hunting him means venturing into deeply hostile gnoll territory. His ferocity has earned him a fearsome reputation among novice adventurers in Elwynn.

quest:179.text: Dwarven Outfitters. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm offers new recruits a bargain. Hunt wolves for their tough meat, and he provides sturdy gloves against Dun Morogh's cold. Cold reaches every path through Coldridge Valley. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm asks new recruits to hunt wolves in the snowy drifts and bring their tough meat to the outpost. In return, he gives them gloves to guard their hands from the cold. Wolves threaten the dwarven scouts and young gnomes training in the valley. Yet they also feed the garrison at Anvilmar. Hunting them makes the paths between local encampments somewhat safer. Stoutarm's bargain tests recruits against local wildlife and adds food for the bitter nights ahead.

quest:18.text:
Brotherhood of Thieves. Across Northshire's eastern river, the Defias Brotherhood has begun to trouble the valley. Deputy Willem sends recruits to face the brigands, whose red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first clear sign of their organized presence. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest. Stormwind guards it, and recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light train there. Lately, though, the valley's watch has grown thin. Vagrants and thieves cross the eastern river and hide near the woods. They make small camps close to the abbey.

Deputy Willem keeps order, but the guards cannot watch every corner of the valley. He needs volunteers to help hold the line. The outlaws move together and wear matching red burlap bandanas. They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and the cloth marks their allegiance. Deputy Willem sends recruits to drive back the brigands and recover their masks. He hopes to slow their advance and learn how far the Defias have reached into the kingdom's heartland.

quest:1818.text: Speak with Dillinger. At Brill's Gallows' End Tavern, Austil de Mon sends fighters on a hazardous mission for Lady Sylvanas. The order sends able-bodied recruits to Deathguard Dillinger at the village's west end. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, warrior trainer Austil de Mon seeks fighters willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards need capable hands, he sends untested recruits into the field. Deathguard Dillinger oversees security on Brill's western edge and has requested someone with martial skill for an urgent task. The Forsaken must constantly prove their martial dominance on Tirisfal Glades' front line. Near Brill's graveyard, Dillinger manages local incursions. Reporting to him tests your combat skill and loyalty to the newly forged Forsaken nation.

quest:1819.text: Ulag the Cleaver. Beneath a mausoleum north of Brill, Ulag the Cleaver awaits a trial for young Forsaken. Deathguard Dillinger sends you to free the captive and meet him in combat. After the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the Forsaken captured an unusual undead warrior who named himself Ulag the Cleaver. His mind stayed clear, but the Lich King still held his spirit in psychic thrall. Beneath a mausoleum north of Brill, the Forsaken bound him with a magical seal. They hoped to learn how the Scourge chained a mind and to break its hold over Ulag. The Forsaken could not free Ulag from the Lich King's command. Now Deathguard Dillinger sets the captive as a combat trial for rising Forsaken warriors. Disturb the skull stone outside the crypt, and the wards break, freeing Ulag from his prison. A warrior must face him with an axe. Death will release him at last.

quest:182.text: The Troll Cave. In southern Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard sends you against Frostmane whelps settling in a cave. Their growing camp threatens nearby dwarven homesteads. Grelin watches the frozen valley from a bluff as Ironforge's soldiers fight troggs across the snowfields. He and his brother Senir came on the mountain authorities' orders to learn whether the native ice trolls threatened the heartland. Now Grelin keeps watch alone, tracking their movements along the southern approaches. Grelin found the local Frostmane clan settling in a deep cave along Coldridge Valley's southern ridge. He judges a full mobilization a waste of dwarven manpower, so he hires capable local volunteers to cull the aggressive whelps. Thinning the young fighters could disrupt the camp before the Frostmane launch coordinated raids against nearby dwarven homesteads.

quest:1820.text: Speak with Coleman. In Brill, Deathguard Dillinger sends proven fighters to Coleman Farthing for help. Their meeting in the tavern opens the way to a private matter tied to the old Agamand lands. You have helped contain grave threats near Brill, including Ulag the Cleaver. So Deathguard Dillinger trusts your strength. He watches the roads into town and chooses who can take on work beyond the usual patrols. Seeing you are ready, he points you toward people who need specialized help. Not every fight in Tirisfal Glades begins with orders from the Undercity. The surviving undead of Lordaeron still bear grudges over the lands, families, and fortunes they left behind. Coleman Farthing waits in the Gallow's End Tavern for a fighter willing to strike at threats near former settlements such as the Agamand Mills.

quest:1821.text: Agamand Heirlooms. At Agamand Mills, Coleman Farthing sends you after heirlooms in the family crypt. He blames the Agamands for his death and seeks their ancestral weapons. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Coleman Farthing served the wealthy Agamand family at their mills in Tirisfal Glades. Farthing blames his former lords for his death. Now raised into undeath among the Forsaken, he takes spiteful satisfaction in the Agamands' downfall. The once-proud family has become mindless minions enslaved to the Lich King. Farthing sends you to the Agamand Family Crypt beneath the northern bluffs of the mills. Restless dead and lingering Scourge wander its stone halls. He wants you to take four relics: the Agamand family sword, axe, dagger, and mace. Their loss would strip the bloodline of its remaining honor.

quest:183.text: The Boar Hunter. In Coldridge Valley, Talin Keeneye asks young recruits to thin the crag boars threatening the trails. Then seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley gives young mountaineers and Ironforge scholars a quiet, protected place to train. Through the harsh winter, small crag boars have multiplied across the valley. Their attacks now threaten everyone on the snowy trails. Hunting gives dwarves meat, hide, and practice in the field. When game grows numerous and attacks on sight, culling restores balance. Thin the crag boars across the valley slopes, and young adventurers prove their readiness for combat. Local hunters gain room to track without being overwhelmed.

quest:184.text: Furlbrow's Deed. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna stand driven from their farm, while Defias bandits carry their land grant through Elwynn Forest. Return it to Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border, and the couple keeps its claim to the stolen homestead. A deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow turns up among Defias bandits in Elwynn. On its back, a crude note says the bandits drove the elderly farmer from his property. They carried the deed across the river into Elwynn to copy it and forge claims to other seized land. The note places the stranded Furlbrows just over the border, beside the road, after their wagon broke. The Defias have driven dozens of Westfall families from their ancestral land. They use force and false claims to seize more farms for the Brotherhood, while Theodore and Verna leave their own farm for safety. Their lawful deed preserves their claim if order ever returns to the province.

quest:1858.text: The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues who seek a place in the Shattered Hand. He wants Tazan's recovered satchel opened with a key taken from an unwitting accomplice. You have Tazan's locked satchel, but it is no use without its key. Therzok expects a rogue to master the lock through skill, not brute force. So he sends you to Gamon, a tauren drunkard who frequents Orgrimmar's tavern. Gamon is easily distracted, and he once helped Tazan. That makes him a fitting mark for quiet theft. Take the key from Gamon without alerting the tavern. Then open the satchel and bring Tazan's logbook to Therzok in the Cleft of Shadow. A clean job meets the Shattered Hand's standards. Therzok gives you formal recognition as one of its operatives.

quest:1859.text: Therzok. In Orgrimmar, Therzok awaits a promising rogue sent from Durotar. Kaplak has seen your skill in violence and stealth, and sends you to the Cleft of Shadow to meet a Shattered Hand operative. The new Horde honors Thrall, yet not all its servants fight openly beneath his banner. Word reaches Orgrimmar of a fighter skilled in violence and stealth, one willing to bend the rules of open warfare. The underground guild takes notice. Kaplak sends you beneath Orgrimmar's red stone cliffs to the Cleft of Shadow. Therzok waits there, hidden from the city's grunts. Lone cutpurses and ambushers are brought into the Shattered Hand, the Horde's covert network of daggers in the dark.

quest:1860.text: Speak with Jennea. In Stormwind, novice mages from Goldshire come to Jennea Cannon after advancing beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends them to her. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum gathers the kingdom's senior mages for study and instruction in the arcane arts. They coordinate magical matters across the realm, and your training now has a place within that wider work. Jennea Cannon oversees local assignments, including reports on the security of Elwynn Forest and Stormwind, as well as your studies. Cautious about sharing grand secrets with a newly arrived apprentice, she receives your report as the beginning of your service to the wizarding order.

quest:1861.text:
Mirror Lake. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, novice Alliance mages are sent to test Mirror Lake for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to sample the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts that began with the opening of the Dark Portal and continued through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels.

In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems. Beneath the cliffs southwest of Stormwind's gates, Mirror Lake is a natural reservoir fed by mountain falls. The surrounding countryside depends on its waters.

Jennea sends novice mages with a glass flask to the waterfall's base, where they collect fresh spray. The Sanctum can then use scrying and reagent tests to learn whether wild magic is seeping into the public water supply.

quest:1879.text: Speak with Bink. Magis Sparkmantle sends you to Bink in Ironforge, where her studies need an arcane specialist. Bink seeks someone who can wield magic and aid her work. Near Kharanos, Magis Sparkmantle sends apprentices who have outgrown their early exercises to answer Bink's call. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Bink studies in the Hall of Mysteries. Scholars, priests, and arcanists gather there. She watches each arriving apprentice closely, for raw potential without discipline can make a spellcaster dangerous in arcane work.

quest:1881.text: Speak with Anastasia. In the Undercity, Cain Firesong sends a promising Forsaken mage to Anastasia Hartwell. Her summons calls you to the Magic Quarter for practical work among the Forsaken magi, with field investigations in Tirisfal Glades ahead. Cain Firesong trains young Forsaken mages in Brill. When he sees promise in a student, he sends them to the Undercity. There, the Forsaken magi study the arcane arts and plan defenses across Lordaeron. Cain decides which students are ready to serve more experienced practitioners. Those with real talent go to Anastasia Hartwell, who needs capable hands in the field. Anastasia Hartwell is one of the Undercity’s prominent mage instructors. She sends promising students into practical work for the Forsaken’s interests and territory, rather than letting them study incantations in safety. Answering her call begins your service among the Forsaken mages and their practical magical work in the years after the Scourge.

quest:1882.text: The Balnir Farmstead. In eastern Tirisfal, snapdragons at the Balnir Farmstead may reveal how far the Scourge's corruption has spread. Anastasia Hartwell sends young Forsaken mages to gather the flowers for study in the Undercity. Forsaken mages watch the borderlands for magical corruption. Anastasia Hartwell sends novice spellcasters to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from its gardens. The flowers absorb magical energies from the soil and air. Arcane scholars in the Undercity examine them to learn whether corruption from the Lich King's domain has reached Tirisfal. The Balnir Farmstead lies near the edge of the glades, close to the blighted wilderness of the Western Plaguelands. The Forsaken know the Lich King's plague rots the land, and Scourge corruption threatens their borders and security. Though the Forsaken wield dark arts of their own, Anastasia plans to pass the snapdragons to the apothecaries for study. Together, mages and alchemists can examine the danger and help defend Lordaeron's reclaimed heartland.

quest:1885.text: Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, Marion Call sends you to report to Mennet Carkad. Deep in the Rogues' Quarter, he tests promising operatives for the Deathstalkers. Marion Call brings you a summons from Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, higher leaders notice covert operatives, and Marion carries word when a scout or assassin is called to report. The Forsaken's intelligence arm is feared for its deadly work. Ignoring its orders is no real choice. Mennet Carkad waits in the Rogues' Quarter, where he watches recruits and judges their readiness. Those who answer his call face tests for entry into the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken's feared arm of espionage and assassination. To serve the Dark Lady from the shadows, obedience comes first.

quest:1886.text: The Deathstalkers. Mennet Carkad tests hopeful Deathstalkers in the Undercity by sending them after a traveling messenger. Only the ruthless will find a place in Lord Varimathras's covert order. In the Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad sets a trial for anyone seeking a place among the Deathstalkers. They serve Varimathras as the Forsaken's secret police and elite assassins. A hopeful agent must show cunning and discretion, then prove the will to eliminate a target. Carkad means to turn away the weak and anyone troubled by too many scruples.

quest:1898.text: The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers hunt suspected treachery within Forsaken ranks. At Lord Varimathras’s urging, you pose as an expected messenger and question a merchant who may aid an outside faction. At Lord Varimathras’s urging, Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration in motion. The Deathstalkers watch Forsaken citizens as closely as they guard against outside threats. With Astor Hadren’s letter of introduction, forged or acquired, you approach the local merchant Andron Gant. You try to pass as the courier he expects.

quest:1899.text: The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers turn Andron Gant's trust against him. Believing you are the courier he expected, Gant gives you a ledger for his secret contacts. You take it to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, opening the way to deeper covert work for the Forsaken state. Andron Gant keeps names and information in a personal ledger in the Undercity. Believing you are the courier he expected, he gives you the ledger to deliver to his secret contacts. Gant asks for the same courier to carry future messages. He does not know the ledger is bound for the Deathstalkers.

quest:1918.text: The Befouled Element. At Mystral Lake, its water spirits leave glowing globes of tainted water among the slain. You carry one to Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post to learn what has poisoned the lake and its spirits. In south-central Ashenvale, Mystral Lake's water elementals have grown violent and visibly corrupted. When slain, they leave strange, glowing spheres of putrid fluid instead of pure elemental essence. The globes hold the corruption that has settled over the lake. Something beyond natural territorial aggression is at work.

quest:1941.text: Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents her finished Manaweave Robe with pride as a showcase for her family’s shop. She wove it from fine materials for a commission now complete. In Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Larson Clothiers makes garments for spellcasters facing volatile energies. Fine magical robes need rare materials, careful needlework, and thread that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in every piece from her shop. Each robe worn into the field carries the Larson name. The manaweave robe offers comfort, freedom of movement, and practical resilience for travel through contested lands. Once you deliver the needed components, Wynne Larson weaves the final stitch herself and presents the finished garment. It is a fine example of Larson tailoring, meant to draw admiration and spread the shop’s name across the kingdom.

quest:1959.text: Report to Anastasia. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, Horde mages are called to the Undercity. Anastasia Hartwell has sensed an unknown magical disturbance there and needs capable spellcasters to investigate. Horde mages across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms hear the same call. It reaches those studying atop Thunder Bluff, in Durotar's dusty heat, and among Lordaeron's ruins. The Undercity's mages have sensed an unexplained disturbance within their domain. They need help learning what it means. Anastasia Hartwell oversees arcane matters in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Mages there have detected strange energies within the city, but no one knows if the magic is harmless or hostile. Anastasia needs a capable mage to investigate quietly. The inquiry begins in the Apothecarium.

quest:1960.text: Investigate the Alchemist Shop. In Algernon's shop, invisible creatures wander among the alchemy. Anastasia Hartwell sends Horde mages to reveal and contain them before they cause harm. Anastasia Hartwell sends arcane initiates to investigate a disturbance in the Apothecarium. Invisible magical creatures wander through Algernon's alchemy shop among its cauldrons and reagents. The Undercity's mage instructor suspects a breach in the flow of magic. The creatures must be contained before they cause serious damage. Anastasia gives her students a Cantation of Manifestation to reveal the invisible creatures and sturdy containment coffers to hold them. Ordinary tracking cannot find beings made entirely of raw arcane force. Once visible, the rift spawns must be weakened and sealed in the coffers before they can unravel further or harm the alchemists at work.

quest:1961.text: Gathering Materials. In the Undercity, Gathering Materials sends new Horde mages to Silverpine Forest for Dalaran mana gems. They need linen as well to make their first true mage's robes. Undercity initiates gather a bolt of simple linen and potent Dalaran mana gems for their first true robes. Those robes mark their station and personal worth. Anastasia Hartwell directs the novices to gather the raw materials for an enchanted weave. The mana gems cannot be bought or conjured. Dalaran mages are stationed across Silverpine Forest, especially near Ambermill, and the gems must be taken from them. Anastasia Hartwell says Dalaran's arcane philosophies mirror those of the Forsaken. Yet sentiment has no place in the Undercity. To the Forsaken, wizards too weak to defend their relics forfeit their treasures and their lives. Josef Gregorian is a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where the gathered cloth and gems are brought. He lacks the magical talent to judge the pristine quality of Dalaran's enchanted stones. But he has the rare artisan skill to weave their raw power into the robes.

quest:1962.text: Spellfire Robes. In the Undercity, Spellfire Robes mark a young Horde mage's passage toward mastery. Josef Gregorian finishes them after the apprentice brings rare components from across the realm. In Lordaeron, you need more than ordinary cloth to channel and shield your growing magic. Josef Gregorian is a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. He makes magical garments from specialized materials gathered by promising Horde spellcasters. The final stitching marks your passage beyond basic incantations toward arcane and fire magic. Josef Gregorian needs alchemical and arcane components to make robes that focus powerful magic. You gather the supplies through dangerous trials and bring them to his sanctum in the Undercity. There, Gregorian weaves them together. The robes mark your growing status and offer protection as an aspiring mage.

quest:1963.text: The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues who seek entry to the secretive Shattered Hand. Their trial sends them after Tazan, a troll smuggler, and his locked satchel. The Shattered Hand works from the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. This order of assassins and thieves keeps to old orcish traditions. Warchief Thrall rules the young Horde with honor, diplomacy, and caution. Yet the Shattered Hand's leaders believe restraint weakens their people, so they seek to restore martial supremacy through covert violence. They use knives and poison when a battlefield charge may fail.

quest:1978.text: The Deathstalkers. In Undercity, the Deathstalkers welcome a new operative into their ranks. You carry Andron's Ledger to Varimathras as proof of the Syndicate's covert work. Mennet Carkad welcomes you into the Deathstalkers after you uncover Andron Gant's records. The order serves Lady Sylvanas across Lordaeron as her eyes, ears, and daggers. Its agents use intelligence, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to remove threats before they rise. Recognition by the order marks your first step in service to the Forsaken. You deliver the sensitive ledger to Varimathras in Undercity's Royal Quarter. The nathrezim commander oversees Forsaken tactical intelligence under Sylvanas Windrunner. Pleased by the Deathstalkers' initiative, Varimathras welcomes your ability and says his intelligence division can use someone who delivers results.

quest:199.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, sabotage threatens the barrier that holds back Loch Modan's waters. You find a barrel near the shore and bring its strange smelling powder to Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh. Whispers of sabotage have reached the shore around the Stonewrought Dam. Near the water's edge, a barrel lies where it does not belong. Inside is strange, pungent powder, far from the dam's maintenance supplies.

quest:1998.text: Fenwick Thatros. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad sends promising rogues to kill Fenwick Thatros on Lord Varimathras's orders. Thatros is suspected of gathering independent undead along Silverpine Forest's shores. His death proves an operative's mettle to the Deathstalkers and earns access to advanced trade training. In the Undercity's Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad handles Deathstalker contracts and trains rogues. The Deathstalkers are the Forsaken's secretive intelligence wing. Lord Varimathras has named Fenwick Thatros a priority target, a charge too serious for novice recruits. Thatros has established a foothold among rogue undead in Silverpine Forest. Left alone, their independent leaders could threaten Forsaken control across Lordaeron's old holdings. Deathstalker scouts place Fenwick Thatros near a decrepit dock on Lake Lordamere in Silverpine Forest. To reach him, you must cross wilderness claimed by feral beasts, Rot Hide gnolls, and Scourge remnants. Varimathras demands proof of the kill: Thatros's severed head. Bring it back, and you may earn entry into deeper covert operations.

quest:2038.text: Bingles' Missing Supplies. On Loch Modan’s southeastern shore, Bingles Blastenheimer is stranded after troggs steal his gear. You can recover his tools and Blastencapper explosives so he can repair his gyrocopter and return to the fight for Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer crashes his gyrocopter into Loch Modan’s cold waters. He drags himself ashore, dazed, and troggs from the lake’s central islands swarm him. They steal his most valuable belongings. Troggs scatter Bingles’ gear among their island camps. The stolen things include a wrench, screwdriver, and hammer, along with his volatile, high-yield invention, the Blastenheimer Blastencapper. Left among troggs, the explosives put travelers in immediate danger. Bingles fights to free Gnomeregan, his homeland, from subterranean troggs and irradiated leper gnomes. He imagines a decisive aerial assault, but without his tools and Blastencappers he cannot rebuild his flying machine. His campaign remains grounded in the reeds.

quest:2039.text: Find Bingles. In Ironforge, Gnoarn starts a search for Find Bingles after more than a week without word. Bingles Blastenheimer vanished during a flight toward fallen Gnomeregan, and searchers are sent to Loch Modan's shores. There, Bingles is alive and needs mechanical salvage. Gnome aviator Bingles Blastenheimer was sent from Tinker Town in Ironforge to scout the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan from the air. More than a week has passed without word. Gnoarn fears Bingles may have blown himself out of the sky, a danger of gnome engineering. His last report placed him somewhere above Loch Modan's waters. Searchers find Bingles alive along the Loch Modan shoreline, far from a tragic pile of wreckage. He is unfazed by his long absence and takes slight offense that anyone doubted his piloting. Rather than return promptly to report to Gnoarn, he asks his rescuer to recover tools and Blastencapper explosives stolen by troggs. He wants them so he can resume his duties for the gnomish movement.

quest:2041.text: Speak with Shoni. In Ironforge, Alliance travelers are sent to Stormwind to find Shoni the Shilent, whose unit prepares for Gnomeregan. After Gnomeregan fell to radiation, surviving gnomes made an exile quarter in Ironforge. Its engineers, tinkers, and strategists keep seeking a way back into their lost home. Tinkertown directs the effort, but the preparations reach beyond Khaz Modan. Now adventurers are sent south to Stormwind, where military gear for fighting underground is being prepared. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent commands an elite crew trained for underground assault. Her sappers need gyrodrillmatic excavationators to burrow toward the sectors held by troggs. The Deeprun Tram runs beneath the mountains between Ironforge and Stormwind, making the journey to Shoni straightforward.

quest:21.text: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. At Echo Ridge, Marshal McBride sends you into a mine overrun by kobolds. Left alone, the garrison fears, they will tighten their hold. Kobolds dig deep in Echo Ridge Mine, hoarding what they steal and growing in number. Thin their ranks now, before they spread through Northshire Valley, its farms, and its spiritual retreat. McBride has few soldiers to spare. The garrison guards the southern borders, while unrest is rumored across Elwynn. Prove reliable at Echo Ridge, and you earn the army’s respect and readiness for harder work elsewhere in the kingdom.

quest:2118.text: Plagued Lands. Darkshore's wildlife is falling to a creeping sickness, and Tharnariun Treetender seeks a way to save it. He asks you to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive. A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, violent creatures. Thistle bears suffer most, and their frenzy threatens travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause. Tharnariun Treetender will not kill the corrupted beasts before trying to save them. He made a trap called Tharnariun’s Hope. Set on the forest floor, its soothing light briefly calms a raging thistle bear. Pacified, the bear follows you back to Tharnariun’s outpost for study.

quest:2138.text: Cleansing of the Infected. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender asks you to stop the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cleanse one failed, and he fears the rabid beasts will harm other creatures and spread the sickness. Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness in Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. So he asks you to put them down before they maul other creatures or carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

quest:2139.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turn. Travelers have put down infected beasts across Darkshore, and now he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of town. Since the Third War, an unnatural sickness has made Darkshore's wild creatures rabid. Tharnariun Treetender is stationed in Auberdine, where he has asked travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. Yet killing rabid thistle bears treats only a symptom. Tharnariun decides the source among the local bears must be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother. Tharnariun gives profound thanks after the Den Mother's death, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agony. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. Auberdine's defenders accept the heavy burden of protecting their wilderness.

quest:214.text: Red Silk Bandanas. In the Deadmines, Scout Riell sends the People's Militia after Red Silk Bandanas. Their fine weave marks the Defias leaders directing the uprising in Westfall. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have learned that cloth marks rank in the Defias Brotherhood. Across Westfall, common cutpurses and highwaymen tie coarse red cloth over their faces. Senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives wear fine red silk. Recovering their bandanas strikes at the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising. The senior outlaws gather deep in the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook. Sentinels and scouts outside Sentinel Hill depend on freelance champions to enter the contested tunnels. Each silk bandana recovered means one fewer lieutenant organizing ambushes, guarding weapon caches, or enforcing VanCleef's rule across Westfall.

quest:2159.text: Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, travelers carry herbs south to Dolanaar. Porthannius is busy with the druids, and the road beyond the sheltered glade opens before young adventurers. Porthannius asks travelers bound south from Shadowglen to carry freshly gathered herbs along the forest path. Pressing business with the druids tending the glade keeps him from making the journey himself. The bundle goes south as young adventurers leave the training grounds and set out into the wider reaches of Teldrassil. The southern road from Shadowglen reaches Dolanaar, a foremost night elf settlement on Teldrassil's great boughs. Innkeeper Keldamyr looks after rest, hospitality, and supplies for wanderers, sentinels, and druids. When he receives Porthannius's herbs, he urges young adventurers to rest their minds and spirits before facing the corruption spreading across the world tree.

quest:2160.text: Supplies to Tannok. Hands Springsprocket has inn supplies for Tannok Frosthammer, but troggs have made the pass unsafe. He asks you to carry the crate from Coldridge Valley to the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass, making the route out of Coldridge Valley dangerous. Mountaineers are stretched thin guarding settlements and defenses, so supply escorts can be delayed for days. The inn's crate has no safe way through. Hands Springsprocket is a gnome tinkerer waiting at the pass, but he cannot carry the crate safely himself. You can take the supplies to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the Thunderbrew inn in Kharanos. Tannok Frosthammer receives the supplies in Kharanos. He says word from Anvilmar has been scarce since troggs disrupted travel. Without the delivery, communication and trade between the two isolated dwarf communities remain fragile.

quest:2161.text:
A Peon's Burden. Ukor waits outside the Valley of Trials with provisions he cannot carry home. The recruits in the red canyon refused his food, so he asks travelers to take it back to Razor Hill. Ukor left Razor Hill carrying provisions for the fresh recruits training in the red canyon. He thought they needed the food, but the taskmasters sent him away. They keep rations meager, believing hardship teaches young Horde warriors discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk later explains that hunger is part of their training. Ukor reached the pass, but fears crossing Durotar on the way back. Scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars haunt the rocky trail. He has no weapons or armor, and lacks the fighting spirit expected of an orcish grunt.

So Ukor waits along the path and asks travelers leaving the proving grounds to carry his heavy provisions back to the inn in Razor Hill.

quest:217.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. Captain Rugelfuss sends you into Stonesplinter Valley to stop the attacks on the King’s Lands. Scouts have traced them to Grawmug, chieftain of the Stonesplinter troggs. His death may break the pack’s resolve and help reclaim southern Loch Modan. Captain Rugelfuss’s scouts have found that the Stonesplinter troggs follow Chieftain Grawmug. Their attacks threaten the King’s Lands in southern Loch Modan. You are sent into their lair to kill Grawmug and his personal bruisers. Breaking the pack’s cohesion may stop its advance. Grawmug holds a cavern in the southeastern cliffs of Stonesplinter Valley. His trusted brutes, Gnasher and Brawler, stand beside him, making the three a danger to a lone soldier. Defeating them could throw the remaining troggs into disarray. That would give the beleaguered Mountaineers time to fortify the roads and drive the beasts back underground.

quest:2178.text: Easy Strider Living. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong offers hunters her own recipe for strider stew if they bring her foreststrider meat. Auberdine's coastal folk make use of the wildlife around them. Alanndarian Nightsong has her own recipe for hearty strider stew, made from the tall foreststriders that range through Darkshore's woods. She asks you to hunt the birds and bring back their meat before she shares her cooking. Foreststriders range through the woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. Their sharp beaks and quick tempers make them dangerous when provoked, but their meat makes a rich stew. Bring fresh meat to Alanndarian, and she will share her recipe.

quest:218.text: The Stolen Journal. Grelin Whitebeard needs his stolen journal to finish judging the troll threat in Coldridge Valley. Grik'nir the Cold, leader of the Frostmane, carried it into the troll cave, leaving Grelin without most of his reconnaissance. The Frostmane trolls have pressed into Coldridge Valley, and Grelin Whitebeard's notes track them. They record the trolls' habits and their sudden aggression. During the unrest, an imposing troll stole Grelin's personal journal and fled into the depths of the den. The journal holds most of his reconnaissance, so Grelin cannot finish his assessment until it is recovered. Grik'nir the Cold holds court in the heart of the valley's troll cave. Distinctive paint marks his body and face. Defeating this powerful Frostmane troll breaks the cave trolls' immediate leadership and secures Grelin's journal. With it returned, Grelin can finish his findings, judge the local troll situation manageable, and send his report to his brother Senir.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean is making pie through hard times. Bandits have ravaged the kingdom’s breadbasket, and homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall once fed Stormwind as its fertile breadbasket. Now neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make life hard for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few comforts to homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. Goretusks roam Westfall’s plains in great numbers. Their tough hides and vicious tusks make them dangerous to farmhands alone, yet their meat feeds families cut off from regular trade. Salma’s recipe calls for crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy. Prepared with care, the beasts’ pungent organs become a rich, savory meal.

quest:2205.text: Seek out SI: 7. From Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends new rogues with a sealed package to Stormwind City. The delivery brings them before Master Mathias Shaw, who leads the crown's covert intelligence network. Rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius doubts that fresh initiates look like covert agents. She gives them a sealed delivery for the capital, testing their reliability as couriers. In doing so, she quietly judges whether they might serve the realm as scouts. SI: 7, or Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7, works from southeastern Old Town in Stormwind City. In this worn district, Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert operations. He receives the package with dry skepticism, then judges whether you have the grit for real espionage.

quest:2206.text: Snatch and Grab. At Jerod's Landing, Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to learn how the Defias move their supplies. The Brotherhood uses the river dock to ship goods in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests those who seek a place among Stormwind's covert agents. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents quietly take down key figures and recover important papers. They do this without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen. Jerod's Landing sits on the river in southern Elwynn, south of Goldshire and just east of the Maclure Vineyards. The Defias Brotherhood seized the once-quiet dock and turned it into an illicit route. Arms, supplies, and contraband cross the water from Redridge toward Westfall. Royal road patrols cannot reach them there. Master Mathias Shaw warns agents that capture, compromise, or death leaves them without the Crown's support. Stormwind and its spymasters will deny they ever existed. The Defias Dockmaster's schedule gives SI:7 proof of the Brotherhood's supply lines. Recovering it keeps Stormwind's official involvement hidden.

quest:224.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the southern watchtower, Mountaineer Cobbleflint calls for help as Stonesplinter troggs press toward the Valley of Kings. Ironforge’s forces serve on distant fronts. Cobbleflint and the guards are too few to stop the growing trogg invasion beneath the great dwarven monuments. King Magni Bronzebeard has sent much of his regular army abroad to support the Alliance. Local patrols and hired blades must keep the province from being overrun. Stonesplinter Valley cuts through Loch Modan’s southern peaks, where troggs have burrowed up from the depths. Their scouts reconnoiter the roads while warriors build camps along the valley floor. If left unchecked, their parties threaten the roads to the southern passes. The Mountaineers must fight them without pause.

quest:2242.text: Destiny Calls. Near the Oracle Glade, Syurna asks you to learn what Sethir the Ancient knows of Teldrassil's corruption. The satyr has turned away force and diplomacy alike. Teldrassil's growing sickness troubles the night elf leaders in Darnassus. Syurna, the rogue trainer, needs someone quiet, since armed patrols have died trying to reach Sethir the Ancient. The satyr roosts on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade. He has turned away force and diplomacy alike. To learn what he knows, you must enter his lair and take his personal possessions.

quest:2259.text: Erion Shadewhisper. From the forests of Teldrassil, promising rogues are sent to Darnassus. At the Cenarion Enclave, Erion Shadewhisper points them toward work beyond the forests. Jannok Breezesong sends you from Teldrassil to find Erion Shadewhisper in Darnassus. There is no need to fear a summons to Syurna, the exacting trainer. Erion waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he handles work that calls for a quieter touch. For rogues in night elf lands, Teldrassil's forests can no longer contain their duties. Erion Shadewhisper sends capable hands into a wider, more dangerous world. Their work lies across the sea.

quest:2260.text: Erion's Behest. In Darnassus, Erion Shadewhisper sends promising night elf rogues across the Great Sea. He sees their growing skill in stealth and directs them to Stormwind City to report to Stormwind Intelligence. Night elf rogues train in Teldrassil's shadow under mentors such as Erion Shadewhisper. When one shows exceptional talent, word travels beyond the World Tree. Through Erion, Stormwind Intelligence, also called SI:7, invites you across the Great Sea to the human capital. From northern Kalimdor, you travel by way of the docks at Darkshore or the Wetlands to Stormwind City. In the capital, you make your way to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town and report to Renzik "The Shiv." He assesses newcomers and opens the way to advanced espionage, poison mastery, and covert operations for the Alliance.

quest:2281.text: Redridge Rendezvous. In Lakeshire, promising Alliance rogues train for dangerous work under seasoned operatives. SI:7 sends them east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to prepare for the field. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, knows that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. So SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains. There, Lucius trains them among Lakeshire’s docks. Lakeshire gives Lucius good ground for clandestine training. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the frontier town. Its piers let him test a rogue’s stealth, reflexes, and lockpicking without drawing the notice of townspeople or guards.

quest:2300.text:
SI:7. From Goldshire, promising young rogues are sent to report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Stormwind. There, you enter Master Mathias Shaw's service, where covert work awaits. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius watches Goldshire's local recruits. You prove cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, and Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. Report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. You leave Elwynn's fields for Stormwind's covert ranks. Behind an unassuming barracks in Old Town, Stormwind's hidden agency keeps its headquarters. Master Mathias Shaw commands its work across the kingdom and beyond. The agency handles covert operations, reconnaissance, and assassination.

Renzik "The Shiv" is Shaw's sharp-tongued second-in-command. He assesses promising agents, then sends them into dangerous work beyond the reach of the kingdom's formal military.

quest:233.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. At Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm sends you west with mail for scouts beyond the frozen lake. Snow and nearby troggs can cut off the valley's defenders, leaving important news undelivered. Mail from across Dun Morogh reaches Anvilmar by mountain pass, where winter couriers leave it to gather. Sten Stoutarm tends supplies and security, so recruits carry the bundles down the western road. Without your help, important messages remain in the hall. Talin Keeneye watches the frozen lake west of Anvilmar for trogg movements and dangerous wildlife. Even at a cold outpost, news from Ironforge and the surrounding camps matters. Harsh mountain conditions make sorting mail difficult, so letters for different scouts can end up together in one bundle.

quest:234.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. In Coldridge Valley, a dispatch travels from Talin Keeneye's post to Grelin Whitebeard's camp. You carry it down the southeastern road, keeping the mountaineers in touch with Ironforge. Anvilmar is Coldridge Valley's center of rule. From there, field scouts and sentries carry dispatches along the trails between the high passes and Ironforge. Grelin Whitebeard keeps a small camp southeast of Talin Keeneye's post. Veteran mountaineers at these remote watchpoints face freezing drifts and steady trogg harassment. Regular letters keep them abreast of affairs across Dun Morogh and the kingdom beyond.

quest:237.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. In southern Loch Modan, Mountaineer Gravelgaw calls for help against the Stonesplinter troggs. With dwarven forces committed to the Alliance front, local outposts rely on volunteers to hold the line. The Mountaineers guarding the southern pass into Dun Morogh are stretched thin. King Magni Bronzebeard has sent much of Ironforge's strength to the wider Alliance front, leaving the Valley of Kings towers short of regular infantry. So Mountaineer Gravelgaw calls on volunteers to strike Stonesplinter Valley and keep the troggs at bay. Reinforcements may never come. The Stonesplinter troggs are neither mindless nor aimless. Their war bands fight with brute force and crude elemental magic. Gravelgaw wants their veteran Skullthumpers and their Seers, who lead with mystic power, driven from the fight. Without those leaders, the tribe's southern camps lose their order and cannot mass against the Ironforge road.

quest:2378.text: Find the Shattered Hand. A Forsaken rogue from Tirisfal Glades is bound for Orgrimmar, where the Shattered Hand awaits. The Deathstalkers send the promising initiate across the sea to Durotar to learn the clan’s specialized arts. Mennet Carkad has seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken train their own covert order, the Deathstalkers. Their alliance with the Horde opens a path to darker arts. So Mennet directs promising rogues to the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, joining Lordaeron’s undead operatives with Kalimdor’s orcish assassins. The journey ends beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow. Warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders work out of sight there. Shenthul, a Shattered Hand trainer, awaits the newly arrived undead agent. The gruff troll greets the envoy with harsh skepticism. Reputation alone will not satisfy him; he wants to see whether the envoy has real cunning or has wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

quest:2379.text: Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul sends a promising rogue to meet Zando'zan. There, training begins for the Shattered Hand's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know strength alone cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow is home to the Shattered Hand, a covert guild serving the Horde through espionage, sabotage, and theft. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to Zando'zan for training as an operative. Zando'zan tests each inexperienced rogue who enters the cavern before granting respect. Meeting him begins formal training in stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. His lessons bridge the gap between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives. From there, rogues prepare for fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

quest:2380.text: To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill north to Orgrimmar. You are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your growing skill has drawn the notice of handlers with greater standing, though your craft is still rough. You leave Durotar's red crags behind and make for the capital.

quest:2381.text: Plundering the Plunderers. Near Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives in Ratchet. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor. Southsea Freebooters crew the ship. Rogues must board unseen and enter the pirates’ den, where cutpurses train. Then they pick the strongboxes in the hold and bring back the plunder.

quest:2382.text: Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends you to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In the Cleft of Shadow, Orgrimmar's rogue guild works from winding crevices, mostly unseen. Zando'zan is a troll who greets operatives with wild ramblings and dark portents. He speaks of Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. Then he gives no reason for the vision and sends agents south to Ratchet, a port town in the Barrens. Ratchet lies on the Barrens coast, east of the Crossroads. Scoundrels, mercenaries, and tinkerers gather in this neutral port, where Wrenix the Wretched makes his home. Wrenix has little patience for Zando'zan's strange ways. He says the troll's earlier recruits met grim ends in the bay, among its hungry predators.

quest:239.text: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure with few soldiers to spare. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to the outpost on Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, leaving the garrison to contend with Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards Elwynn Forest's western edge, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, so the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers. Deputy Rainer and his men face Riverpaw gnolls who harass travelers and nearby homesteads. The pack ranges through the borderlands between Elwynn and Westfall. Stormwind is distracted by political and military troubles, and the gnolls press deeper into inhabited lands. Westbrook Garrison guards against their unchecked advance into the heart of the forest.

quest:2399.text: The Sprouted Fronds. At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Its new growth now shows among the garden beds. You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth. There the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready for gathering and study. Young Teldrassil is vast, and its plants grow quickly. Night elf herbalists find that growth fascinating and troubling. The shimmering fronds and their offshoots show how quickly life takes hold on the World Tree's boughs. Yet its vitality can be hard to predict.

quest:2438.text: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot asks you to retrieve the Emerald Dreamcatcher from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. Gaerolas Talvethren gave him the heirloom, but corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs drove him from the village before he could take it. Its gentle magic still waits there. Gaerolas Talvethren gave Tallonkai a rare druidic talisman. The warden watches over the sleeping druids in Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The amulet channels the serene currents of the Emerald Dream, bringing peace and fortune to its bearer. Such gifts go only to a trusted few whose lives are bound to the forest's care. Starbreeze Village was peaceful until the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to violent madness. They drove the villagers from their ancestral homes. In the fearful flight, Tallonkai left his most treasured possession hidden in his dresser in the village's southeastern quarter. Alone, he could not reclaim it.

quest:244.text: Encroaching Gnolls. Gnolls press toward Redridge’s western road, and Lakeshire fears being cut off. Guard Parker spots camps near the border and sends word to Deputy Feldon. The warning confirms the town’s fear that the beastmen may isolate Redridge. Guard Parker watches the western border trail, where the road leads from Elwynn Forest into Redridge Mountains. Stormwind’s forces have thinned, leaving few defenders along the route. Parker keeps the gravel road open for supply wagons, but his scouts report gnoll warbands advancing from the crags to the north and east. Their camps lie alarmingly close to the road. Near the Lakeshire bridge, Deputy Feldon receives the warning and sees the danger facing the town. Redridge gnolls raid near Lakeshire, while their camps near the Elwynn border could let them encircle the town and push into the kingdom’s heartland. Stormwind has ignored pleas for reinforcements, leaving Lakeshire’s watch unready for threats from both sides.

quest:2459.text:
Ferocitas the Dream Eater. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot sends you north to recover an emerald stolen by Gnarlpine furbolgs. Their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater, wears it around his neck. Tallonkai Swiftroot was relieved when his dreamcatcher returned from the corrupted wilds. Then he saw its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, and its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame.

Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the sway of their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. The gem was useless and perverse in Ferocitas's clutches, so Tallonkai sent defenders to reclaim it. The Gnarlpine furbolgs in northern Teldrassil were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption from the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but now draw on distorted magical energies. You can reach Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. Return the jewel to Tallonkai, so he can make his dreamcatcher whole and restore balance to the woods.

quest:246.text: Assessing the Threat. Near Lakeshire, Deputy Feldon needs to learn how great the gnoll threat has grown. With the garrison stretched thin and Stormwind withholding reinforcements, he pays travelers to thin the packs and gauge their strength. Blackrock orc warbands threaten Lakeshire from the heights, while aggressive gnolls roam the valleys. The town has too few defenders for ordinary scouting patrols. When reports showed gnolls pressing toward the border, Deputy Feldon called on travelers. He pays them to test the enemy in the wild, sparing guards the town cannot afford to send. You scout along Redridge's southern road and strike the camps of Redridge Mongrels and Poachers. Each fight thins the gnolls' forward scouts and disrupts their supply lines. The clashes reveal whether the packs are scattered scavengers or an organized force threatening Lakeshire. Feldon can use what you learn to plan the town's strained defense.

quest:2498.text: Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, you carry Rellian Greenspyre's alarming news to Denalan, the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word comes from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian sees the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

quest:2499.text: Oakenscowl. At Lake Al'Ameth, blight spreads from Oakenscowl, once a guardian of Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to end the threat. The maddened timberling dwells in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Timberlings tend Teldrassil's boughs, and Oakenscowl once led them. Now corruption reaches the world tree's humble wildlife and ancient protectors alike. A massive growth swells across Oakenscowl's bark and drives the timberling mad. Its old duty was to guard the forest. Now blight takes hold. Oakenscowl hides in a cavern on Lake Al'Ameth's southern shore. From there, it poisons nearby water and woodland beasts. Denalan cannot face the creature alone, so he seeks its destruction. He hopes to cut off the corruption and study the strange growth afflicting the lake's spirits.

quest:250.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh fears Dark Iron sappers near the eastern ramp threaten the Stonewrought Dam. With much of its garrison sent to the Alliance Front, you investigate the danger. The Stonewrought Dam holds back Loch Modan's waters. Ironforge engineers raised it as a great work, yet much of its security detail has gone to the Alliance Front. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh and his small crew now have little protection if an attack comes. Dark Iron dwarves struck the Thandol Span and pillaged Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Now known sappers lurk near the dam's eastern ramp. Hinderweir fears the clan has turned to Loch Modan's lifeline, and means to demolish it.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Once blessed by Elune, the spider now brings danger, and the Sisterhood seeks to ease her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Elune once blessed the spider. Beneath the night sky, Sathrah wove silver webs across Teldrassil's boughs, and evening mist gathered on them. The Sisterhood of Elune collected the shimmering dew for its healing power in sacred rites.

quest:2519.text: The Temple of the Moon. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne calls for aid to a suffering ancient creature in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune cannot tend to it alone, and the call begins a solemn ritual of mercy. In Darnassus's Temple Gardens, Sister Aquinne asks you to help a venerable forest creature in pain. She serves Elune and speaks for her order. The Sisters cannot tend to the creature alone. Sister Aquinne sends you southeast to the Temple of the Moon. There, Priestess A'moora coordinates rituals and practical duties for Teldrassil's troubled wildlife. She prepares allies for a sorrowful act of mercy.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah a final rite. You bring her spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite for Lady Sathrah after she is slain. The dark madness spreading across Teldrassil twisted the great spider's peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

quest:2541.text: The Sleeping Druid. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw lies asleep while his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den. Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans have breached Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and drawn his living spirit from his sleeping body.

quest:255.text:
Mercenaries. In Thelsamar, Magistrate Bluntnose hires passing fighters as Mo'grosh ogres press into northeastern Loch Modan. Ironforge has promised soldiers for the valley's defense, but they are months away. Settlements, excavations, and the Stonewrought Dam remain exposed. Ironforge took two months to promise a handful of soldiers for Loch Modan's local defense. Another two months will pass before they arrive. Thelsamar's guards are stretched thin as hostile forces gather beyond the valley. Magistrate Bluntnose cannot wait for reinforcements. Mo'grosh ogres have fortified a camp in the hills northeast of the loch. Their growing presence threatens Thelsamar, the Ironband Excavation Site, and the Stonewrought Dam. If the dam is attacked or damaged, destruction downstream would be catastrophic.

Without official mountaineer detachments, Bluntnose hires independent fighters to thin the ogre ranks. He hopes to buy the valley time against both ogres and troggs.

quest:2561.text: Druid of the Claw. Beneath Teldrassil, Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits for release. The corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs bound his body with dark enchantment, and you can free him by destroying its soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw slept in the barrows beneath Teldrassil. Then the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream.
