Now Oben’s spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

quest:257.text: A Hunter's Boast. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling sets you a timed hunt in Loch Modan: bring down six mountain buzzards within fifteen minutes. Daryl calls himself Daryl the Bold and dismisses travelers as greenhorns who cannot match his hunting skill. Then he points you toward the mountain buzzards scavenging around the lodge's nearby crags and hillsides. The hunt tests your speed, patience, and aim against the buzzards' quick flight. Bring down all six before time runs out, and Daryl grudgingly gives up one of his ranged weapons. He offers you further hunting dares, too.

quest:258.text: A Hunter's Challenge. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling dares you to kill five elder mountain boars within twelve minutes. He expects Loch Modan's rough highlands and dangerous wildlife to make you fail. Daryl the Youngling lives among Farstrider Lodge's seasoned huntsmen, but he lacks their quiet patience. He covers his youth with bluster and long hunting tales, including rambling accounts of how he earned his “famous” scar. He refuses to admit that anyone else is skilled. He also keeps getting his fellow hunters' names wrong and sets strict trials for newcomers, hoping to humble them and restore his standing among the lodge's residents. Elder mountain boars roam Loch Modan's crags and hillsides. They are massive and thick-skinned, and grow dangerous when provoked. Daryl gives you twelve minutes to find and kill five. If you finish in time, the loudmouthed youngster retreats awkwardly and pretends he knows nothing of the extravagant wager he made so casually.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, an elder of the Cenarion Circle guides their first steps toward aquatic form. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and is ready for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them to master the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus. To cross the depths without drowning, young druids need the guidance of the Cenarion Circle’s elders. You leave Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:263.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the Southern Guard Tower, Mountaineer Wallbang calls travelers to defend Loch Modan from the Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's reserves sent to distant fronts, the southern pass is thinly held. Wallbang sends seasoned recruits into Stonesplinter Valley against the clan's shamans and bonesnappers. Loch Modan's defenses are stretched thin. Ironforge's regular reserves have been summoned to distant fronts across Azeroth, leaving the Southern Guard Tower short-handed. Mountaineer Wallbang and his few comrades face constant pressure from the Stonesplinter clan. They depend on Alliance travelers passing through to help hold the southern pass. The fight reaches beyond stray scouts to the Stonesplinter clan's strength. Its bonesnappers bring brutal force, while its shamans use earthen magic to rally their kin. Slaying twenty of these foes weakens the clan's incursions into the lowlands. It also serves King Magni Bronzebeard's defense of the realm.

quest:264.text: Until Death Do Us Part. In Silverpine Forest, Clarice Foster sends her keepsake to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to lay it on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children. Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage with bitterness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead. He declared service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away. Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands. No grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs. The old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people remain.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. At Loch Modan’s Southern Gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a growing trogg threat with too few defenders. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to Alliance battlefronts, leaving him to hold the pass while troggs threaten the nearby hills. Dwarven mountaineers and the Ironforge Reserve have gone to reinforce Alliance battlefronts. Captain Rugelfuss now has only a small garrison. Strict orders keep him at the gate, unable to lead an attack into the highlands. Settlers and travelers there remain exposed to ambushes. Troggs in the nearby crags threaten Khaz Modan. Left unchecked, their numbers grow quickly, and they could overrun dwarven outposts. Rugelfuss calls for help to buy time and thin their ranks. Strike at the troggs in their hillside warrens, then bring back their stone teeth as proof.

quest:27.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids north to study the waters. Their road leads to Nighthaven in Moonglade, where the Cenarion Circle guides their training. You have learned the bear form and its strength. Now Turak Runetotem turns his students toward adaptability. Azeroth's waterways hold hazards that are hard for travelers bound to land. So he sends those devoted to nature north to learn the aquatic form. Turak Runetotem sends you beyond Mulgore to learn how to shape yourself for the waters. You travel to Moonglade, the sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal, and reach Nighthaven. There, night elf mentors of the Cenarion Circle welcome tauren students. They set factional strife aside to preserve the shared teachings of Cenarius. Dendrite Starblaze waits for you in Nighthaven, where your training begins. The night elf elder says mastery over the waters must be earned. Two trials await. One tests your endurance and composure beneath the water. The other calls for deep spiritual understanding of the aquatic aspect.

quest:273.text: Resupplying the Excavation. Jern Hornhelm sends you from Thelsamar after a slow wagon carrying blastpowder to Ironband's Excavation Site. Its three dwarven haulers travel south along the Loch's shore. In southern Loch Modan, Ironband's Excavation Site needs blastpowder to break through hard rock. The powder comes first to Thelsamar, where Jern Hornhelm arranges for Huldar, Miran, and Saean to haul three volatile barrels south. The heavy load slows their pack team along the lakeside road, giving you time to catch them and help on the way.

quest:274.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At Stonewrought Dam, strange powder puts Loch Modan and Ironforge at risk. Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies it as unstable Seaforium, which can explode when it touches water. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the silver crystals and sharp odor in samples from Stonewrought Dam. The powder is Seaforium. It stays inert while dry, but moisture makes it react violently. An unchecked blast could blow Ironforge out of the mountain, Ashlan warns.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks an apprentice to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks a budding smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar beneath the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, so he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury. Its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meet his demands, and he may believe an apprentice can keep the Omosh legacy alive and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh tests smiths with hard work. Green iron armor puts their endurance to the proof and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, while the Omosh bloodline's techniques hang in the balance. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar with trials of hard physical labor. To him, metalworking is more than heating ore and shaping it. It honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and making tempered green iron armor again and again builds muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear win rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. For the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots. Horde warriors wear them to crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After your great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith wipes his tears away as soot, then dances for joy to pass on an unusual piece of family heritage. At Orgrimmar's forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. Your great help has touched the burly blacksmith deeply. Yet he stubbornly blames a fleck of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk Omosh says he must share one last family secret. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice. Then he teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:278.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron explosives threaten the Stonewrought Dam, and Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs your help. He asks you to gather rare reagents from Loch Modan so he can make a mixture to neutralize them. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs three ingredients for his mixture. Forest Lurker venom, a tear from a crocolisk in the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal each bring a different reaction. Together, they can render the dwarven charges inert. The ingredients lie in dangerous parts of Loch Modan. Forest Lurker spiders and crocolisks threaten travelers, while Mo'grosh ogres guard their mined crystals in a stronghold to the northeast. Reaching the crystals means facing the ogres in their encampments.

quest:280.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron saboteurs threaten the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs the charge disarmed before the loch floods the lowlands. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh saw Dark Iron Insurgents swim toward the Stonewrought Dam with a keg of explosive Seaforium. No Mountaineers were nearby to stop them. The infiltrators fastened the keg against the dam’s underwater foundation. If the dam breaks, the loch will flood the lowlands and cripple dwarven trade and travel.

quest:282.text: Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard sends you east to Kharanos with his report for his brother Senir. Troggs have overrun the tunnel from Coldridge Valley, where Mountaineer Thalos guards the way. Grelin Whitebeard's report tells of Frostmane troll activity around Coldridge Valley. The trolls stole his journal, and you recovered it. Grelin judged the findings too important for an inexperienced apprentice to carry. So he entrusts the report to you, to deliver directly to his brother Senir in Kharanos. Troggs have overrun the eastern tunnel from Coldridge Valley into the rest of Dun Morogh. Mountaineer Thalos guards the entrance to keep civilians from danger. He lets travelers through only when they carry urgent official business.

quest:287.text: Frostmane Hold. Above Iceflow Lake, Frostmane trolls guard a cavern stronghold in the western peaks. Senir Whitebeard, a mountaineer and scout in Kharanos, sends you to scout its depths and bring back intelligence for his reports. Senir tracked the aggressive tribes to their main cavern southwest of Brewnall Village. Armed trolls crowd the entrance. Behind on his official reports, Senir will not enter alone, so he hires you to scout the icy cavern in his place. Above Iceflow Lake, the stronghold is carved into the western peaks and packed with hostile ice trolls. You fight through underground tunnels, kill the Frostmane Headhunters stationed along the ledges, and map the interior. Your findings give Senir the intelligence he needs to complete his report for Ironforge's military commanders.

quest:291.text: The Reports. From Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard sends word to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge about the Frostmane threat to Dun Morogh. He asks you to leave his scout unnamed. The report carries news from deep inside Frostmane Hold, where the trolls threaten Dun Morogh. Senir wants you to take it straight to Barin Redstone and keep the scout from the snowy crags unnamed.

quest:2948.text: Gnome Improvement. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel offers to improve a ring he made in Gnomeregan. He needs silver and moss agate for a delicate lattice over its old band. Talvash del Kissel fled Gnomeregan after the trogg invasion and radiation brought the city down. Now the gnome refugee lives in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The jeweler and tinkerer is short on coin and out of stock, but determined to prove his skills remain sharp in exile. Talvash is glad to see his simple ring design again, cleaned by the Sparklematic 5200. Yet he considers the old band dated. He offers to improve it with silver and moss agate lattice work, showing his skill with metal and gemstones.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg seeks to improve a ring brought from Gnomeregan. He wants rare materials and word of the Dark Iron dwarves, hoping to prove goblin craft finer than gnomish design. You carry a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer studies its plain gnomish work and offers a bargain. Bring him raw materials and a small fee, and he will frame the band with silver and moss agate. The lattice is meant to strengthen the magic within.

quest:298.text: Excavation Progress Report. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband needs you to carry his dispatches and powder orders to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar. Ironband's dispatches tell of his dig and renew its supply requests. The work needs picks, workers, and blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband relies on runners to keep Jern Hornhelm informed.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. Azar Stronghammer sends promising dwarven paladins from Dun Morogh to Ironforge for deeper instruction. There, Tiza Battleforge awaits in the Hall of Mysteries, where the trials begin in service to the Holy Light. Dwarven initiates guard Dun Morogh's snowbound villages and roads. When Azar sees that a defender is ready for deeper spiritual instruction, he sends that candidate from field duties to Ironforge. There, the city's holy elders can guide them. The summons takes you through the Mystic Ward to the Hall of Mysteries. Sacred relics and solemn study fill its halls. Tiza Battleforge tests your readiness for self-sacrifice, mercy, and the moral duties of your calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons now calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Brother Wilhelm sends for them, and the Tome of Divinity begins the sacred trials that teach mastery of resurrection through the Holy Light. In Elwynn Forest, novice paladins spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows discipline in battle and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. The paladin leaders mark promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind. Their report is due at the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the kingdom's foremost sanctuary for its priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall lives there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set the formal trials of the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The trials test compassion, fortitude, and willingness to sacrifice.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, young dwarven paladins are sent to Tiza Battleforge to learn the Holy Light's deeper duties. Their rite of passage reaches beyond martial training and toward sacred vows. You have defended Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, proving your discipline in battle. Now Brandur Ironhammer, your trainer, sends you upstairs in the Hall of Mysteries. Senior paladins there prepare initiates for the order's spiritual duties. Tiza Battleforge teaches that the Light asks more than swordplay and hammer blows. It asks for compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her begins your formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred path toward the power to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, dwarf paladins return for deeper training in the Holy Light. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker sends them home, and Tiza Battleforge guides them toward the sacred trials of the Tome of Divinity. Dwarf paladins keep their spiritual and martial roots in Khaz Modan, even when they serve Stormwind or travel through human lands. When Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker judges that a dwarf has gained enough field training, he sends them home. There they learn the duties expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. In Ironforge, you are directed to the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Mysteries. Tiza Battleforge waits upstairs, where she mentors young dwarven paladins. She prepares them to bear the burden of the Holy Light through sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:301.text:
Report to Ironforge. Jern Hornhelm sends Ironband’s report to Prospector Stormpike in Ironforge. The dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies, and the Explorers’ League must attend to it. The Explorers’ League funds and oversees archaeological expeditions across Khaz Modan, and supplies them. Ironband’s dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies. Its overseers cannot simply requisition more nearby.

At the Thelsamar inn, Jern Hornhelm entrusts you with Ironband’s written report. You carry it over the mountain passes to Prospector Stormpike at the League’s headquarters in Ironforge.

quest:302.text: Powder to Ironband. In Ironforge, the Explorer's League sends blasting powder south to Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan. Prospector Stormpike approves the request, and the shipment goes to Thelsamar before continuing to Ironband's Excavation. The Explorer's League sends blasting powder from Ironforge to Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan. When the dig runs short, word reaches the League's leaders. Prospector Stormpike approves the request and sends the runner to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the valley's main supply hub.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove yourself against the Mottled Boars, Gornek gives you a parchment marked for you alone. Durotar is harsh, so the Horde gives its fighters guidance quickly. The parchment sends you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den. Frang shelters in the shade outside the Den and watches recruits come from the red scrubland. He judges each arrival with a seasoned eye, then teaches the fundamentals with a heavy axe or a spear. He prepares each recruit to defend the young Horde's fragile settlements.

quest:307.text: Filthy Paws. In Silver Stream Mine, Filthy Paws supplies wait in danger. The Miners' League stored its equipment there after the ore ran dry, but kobolds now fill the tunnels. Mountaineer Stormpike wants the tools recovered before his warriors attack. Silver Stream Mine lies in northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station. Its silver ran out long ago, so the dwarven Miners' League turned the empty shafts into a depot for spare excavation gear, picks, and staging materials. Across Khaz Modan, sturdy tunnels make good storehouses, provided they stay guarded and locked against the wilderness. As dwarven watchfulness across Loch Modan has thinned, kobolds have slipped into the mine. Dark shafts and gleaming iron tools drew the scavengers, and soon the depot became their warren. Mountaineer Stormpike is ready to lead warriors inside and drive them out, but their heavy boots and sweeping blows could smash the crates. You can slip or fight your way in to recover the League's supplies before the assault begins.

quest:308.text: Distracting Jarven. At Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Jarven Thunderbrew watches the cellar stores. His family forbids him to drink from the barrels while on duty, so he asks you to bring him Thunder Ale from upstairs. He hopes a mug will sharpen his wits. Jarven watches the deep stores, with Dun Morogh’s finest stout all around him. His family forbids him to drink from the stock while he is on guard. Yet temptation gets the better of him, and he asks you to fetch a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs. Jarven says a good drink will sharpen his senses and strengthen his watch. Whether a guard ought to drink on duty is another matter. Still, few hardy dwarves can fault a Thunderbrew for wanting a taste of the ale his own kin make.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends a carved tablet to young hunters. Jen'shan's mark calls them to train in the wild. After young hunters prove themselves against the boars near the Den, Gornek brings them a carved tablet. Jen'shan's mark is cut into the stone. She is a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby, and her message shows that seasoned hunters have noticed the recruit's grit. Now the lesson turns from surviving local dangers to disciplined training in the wild. Jen'shan teaches that orcs and trolls have a long history within the Horde. Orcs brought renowned traditions of warriors and shamans. The Darkspear trolls carried ancient skills in stalking, tracking, and survival, which helped orcs endure life on Azeroth. As Jen'shan trains new hunters, the two peoples share what they know, bound by respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new rogues to Rwag with a coded message. The summons leads them into the Den, where rogue training is bound to the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives the Encrypted Tablet to initiates who prove their mettle against the local wildlife. Its message is written in cipher, a test and safeguard for those trained in stealth, poison, and subterfuge. The summons sends each recruit into the Den to meet Rwag, trainer of the Horde’s rogues, thieves, and cutpurses. Inside the Den, Rwag trains new rogues as an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. He says the guild will not dictate every breath, yet the Hand holds him to account if an apprentice fails to perform. The fledgling Horde is surrounded by foes, so it depends on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and strike from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Shikrik calls promising initiates to formal shaman training. The tablet's runes carry the summons to study the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air. After showing early discipline in the Valley of Trials' dusty grounds, fledgling shamans receive a carved stone tablet from Gornek. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons says each initiate is ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Hallowed Tablet carries Ken'jai's call to young priests after their first test. It points them toward the Darkspear way of communing with spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone: the Hallowed Tablet. Ken'jai's mark is on its message. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic. Darkspear priests among the Horde seek communion with spirits and loa. Across the sea, human and dwarven priests follow the Holy Light. Ken'jai welcomes you to Durotar and teaches that spiritual discipline makes your power grow. He will guide you in greater rites as your bond with the spirits matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet calls young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek gives it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife. Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet sent by Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer. When you are ready to begin your arcane studies, she asks you to meet her by the Den's entrance. Mai'ah speaks plainly about a mage's power and its danger. Magic's unseen pull toward corruption, she warns, is a greater threat than rival warriors or enemy races. Humility and patience matter. Without them, unchecked sorcery can make a mage believe they have mastered more than they have.

quest:3087.text:
Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek delivers Jen'shan's summons to a young hunter. It comes after the initiate's first blooding and opens the way to wilderness training in Durotar. After proving themselves against mottled boars, hunters in the Valley of Trials receive a parchment from Gornek. Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter, sent it after watching new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. Her note welcomes the initiate to formal training and recognizes the instincts needed to master Durotar's untamed beasts and harsh land. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the move from recruit to dedicated stalker. She warns that hunting is no easier than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, keeping ranged weapons in good order, and surviving on unforgiving land all demand discipline.

Jen'shan sends her apprentices to aid the valley's other inhabitants and test their abilities. Then they return to learn more advanced ways to survive.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment calls proven novice orc rogues toward the Den. Its cipher leads them to Rwag, an agent of the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives the coded parchment to novice orcs who have proved themselves against the local wildlife. Other trainers recruit pupils openly in the clearing, but rogue instructor Rwag sends his summons by cipher. The message leads you past the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern called the Den. You find Rwag watching among the rocks inside the Den. Warlocks lurk deeper in the cave, and Rwag tells you he watches recruits for the Shattered Hand. Orcish society prizes open honor and glory in battle. The Shattered Hand works in secret as the Horde's network of spies, cutthroats, and gatherers of intelligence.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives new shamans Rune-Inscribed Parchment, a summons from Shikrik. It begins their training in communion with spirits and the elements. New orc shamans prove they can survive against local wildlife. Then Gornek, who oversees the Valley of Trials, gives them a rune-inscribed summons. Shikrik, the valley's shaman trainer, wrote its mystical message and asks to meet each newly arrived initiate. Meeting Shikrik begins a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. She teaches that shamans serve as conduits for ancestral spirits and wield the wrath of the elements. Under her guidance, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call on Kalimdor's natural forces.

quest:309.text: Protecting the Shipment. In southern Loch Modan, Miran carries blasting powder toward Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband needs it for his dig, but failed supply lines and threats to the courier wagons have left Miran stranded. Prospector Ironband needs blasting powder to cut through stone at his dig. Miran is stranded on the road under threat, carrying a heavy load. You guide him along the uneven roads to the excavation site so the powder can reach the dig.

quest:3092.text: Etched Note. At Camp Narache, Etched Note calls a young tauren hunter to train with Lanka Farshot. The message begins their study of the wild. Grull Hawkwind gives the etched message to a young tauren skilled in marksmanship and tracking. The novice has trained among the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa. Lanka Farshot has noticed the youth's bloodline and raw ability, and calls them to study under his watch. Among the Shu'halo, hunters scout and fight, but they serve the tribes in other ways too. They provide food with their quarry, guard nomadic camps, and keep close to Kalimdor's beasts. Lanka begins with weapons and Mulgore's creatures. In time, the novice may learn the ancient art of taming wild companions.

quest:3094.text: Verdant Note. At Camp Narache, the Verdant Note calls young tauren to seek Gart Mistrunner. Grull Hawkwind carries the summons on Gart’s behalf. On the Red Cloud Mesa, Grull Hawkwind gives young tauren a message from a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The summons calls those with natural gifts to accept their responsibilities. It invites them into the ancient practice of tauren druidism and asks them to leave simple village errands behind for the balance of the plains. Gart Mistrunner warns that ancestral and natural spirits have grown restless across Mulgore. Tauren druids act as living avatars of nature and keep harmony with the Earthmother’s will despite rivalries far away. Night elves also practice druidic arts, but Gart says their pride blinds them to the tauren’s deep bond with the natural realm.

quest:3096.text: Encrypted Scroll. At Deathknell, a sealed message reaches a newly awakened Forsaken rogue. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends the recruit to David Trias after they prove ready. Newly raised Forsaken fight mindless zombies in the cemetery while Deathknell's leaders watch for those drawn to stealth and subterfuge. Once you prove ready, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives you a sealed parchment. David Trias's discreet seal marks an early link to the covert network beneath Forsaken leadership. David Trias watches Deathknell's crossroads and inn for prospects in future covert operations. The Forsaken need disciplined agents for their fledgling kingdom, not common thieves or reckless cutpurses. Trias says capable rogues may draw the notice of the Shadowstalkers, a Forsaken cadre that prizes cunning, precision, and absolute loyalty to the Dark Lady.

quest:3097.text: Hallowed Scroll. In Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis calls newly risen Forsaken priests to the chapel. He sends each novice to Dark Cleric Duesten to learn how the Forsaken wield faith after death. Newly awakened undead stagger from Deathknell’s graves, their minds shaken by plague, death, and freedom from the Lich King's grip. Those who followed the Holy Light in life find death hard to understand. As fledgling undead fight the mindless Scourge at the settlement’s edge, Shadow Priest Sarvis receives a message from Dark Cleric Duesten. It calls newly risen priests away from their wandering and into the desecrated town chapel. At the chapel, Dark Cleric Duesten teaches a harsh faith. He says the Holy Light abandoned the Forsaken in death, ancestral spirits are hollow tales, and demons do not care about their plight. Forsaken clergy teach that willpower and self-reliance are their only sources of salvation. Under Duesten’s guidance, newly risen priests learn divine discipline and shadow through faith in their own survival, not devotion to distant gods.

quest:3098.text: Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, Isabella calls newly awakened Forsaken mages to the ruined church. Her sealed scroll bids them to hone their volatile arcane powers. Isabella calls newly awakened Forsaken mages to the ruined church in Deathknell. Nearby, you show an affinity for arcane magic while fighting the mindless Scourge. Then a scroll bearing her arcane sigil bids you to report to her. Isabella trains local mages and knows untrained magic can endanger the Forsaken as much as their enemies. In Deathknell’s ruined chapel, Isabella teaches new Forsaken mages that undeath has not ended the dangers of arcane magic. Their bodies have lost life’s frailties, yet magic remains volatile and corrupting. Mastering the arcane takes more than study. It can help the Forsaken survive, seek vengeance, reclaim their destiny, and destroy those who threaten their fragile return to Lordaeron.

quest:31.text: Aquatic Form. In Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to be recognized among the keepers of nature. The druid has proved worthy in Moonglade and taken on the sea lion aspect; now formal recognition brings Aquatic Form. Dendrite Starblaze sends you back to Mulgore after your trials in Moonglade. The Pendant of the Sea Lion bears proof of your balance and dedication across Kalimdor's waters. By carrying it home, you show that you have honored the ancient traditions needed to take an aquatic aspect. At Thunder Bluff's heights, you bring the pendant to Turak Runetotem, your mentor. He is pleased that you have honored your ancestors and kept nature in balance. Then Turak teaches you the secret of aquatic form. You can swim beneath rivers and oceans, breathe freely, and find your way through the depths as a sea creature.

quest:310.text: Bitter Rivals. Marleth Barleybrew asks you to replace a cask of Thunder Ale at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos with her family's brew. The Barleybrews have long begrudged the Thunderbrews the fame of their distillery. Marleth respects its ale, but she cannot abide Dun Morogh knowing only Thunderbrew. She means to change local tastes with her family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder. Beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, aging casks fill a basement storeroom. A guard watches near the Thunderbrews' prized reserve. Draw him away, then secretly switch the barrels.

quest:3103.text: Hallowed Letter. In Northshire, Marshal McBride gives promising young priests a letter from Priestess Anetta. It calls them to begin formal training in the Holy Light at Northshire Abbey, while trouble still shadows the realm. After proving themselves against the kobold camps around Northshire, novice priests receive a letter sealed by Priestess Anetta. Marshal McBride delivers it as an invitation to study the Holy Light in the abbey's quiet halls. When you bring the letter, Priestess Anetta tells you the realm remains troubled. The Burning Legion's lingering threats still shadow Azeroth, and the continents bear fresh wounds and unrest. To Anetta, becoming a priest means more than study. It is a duty to bring healing and comfort to a suffering world.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley from Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, the mage trainer at Northshire, wrote it. He watches new recruits arrive at the abbey, looking for magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long sheltered the Holy Light. Yet Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen, who offers no easy praise. He warns that mastering arcane power means defying nature's limits. Such power earns profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. In Northshire, Tainted Letter draws novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards to learn the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle gives it to Marshal McBride, who carries it to her recruits. After proving themselves against the kobolds, novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride. Priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, but warlocks must keep to quieter paths. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter. It directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that Stormwind's guards watch warlocks closely. She calls them 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons both risk corruption. So she urges patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies. Caution, she says, must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:3106.text: Simple Rune. At Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm brings new dwarven warriors a summons from Thran Khorman. The rune calls them from Coldridge Valley's snowy paths to begin training. Veteran scouts watch recruits clear pests around Coldridge Valley, seeking promising fighters. Sten brings an inscribed stone from Thran Khorman. Its simple rune calls them from the snowy paths into Anvilmar's warm forge-hall, where they can pledge themselves to the warrior's trade. Thran speaks plainly about Dun Morogh's troubles. Gnomes displaced by the explosions that destroyed Gnomeregan seek refuge, while some dwarves take up foreign arcane arts or follow the human faith in the Holy Light. Troggs claw at the mountain borders after being disturbed deep underground. Thran believes firm martial discipline is needed to withstand these threats.

quest:3107.text: Consecrated Rune. At Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner calls fledgling dwarven paladins to join the Knights of the Silver Hand. Sten Stoutarm summons them there. Your rune marks the start of a formal induction, where raw potential must meet discipline. Around Coldridge Valley, local leaders watch for those gifted in divine martial prowess. Bromos Grummner awaits inside Anvilmar to guide new initiates. The Knights of the Silver Hand began among the humans of Lordaeron, yet Ironforge dwarves embraced the Holy Light with fierce devotion. Bromos welcomes you into the brotherhood and reminds you that dwarven paladins share the solemn duty of protecting Azeroth. The order is grounded in sacrifice, tradition, and martial virtue, and asks recruits to take up hammer and faith in equal measure.

quest:3108.text: Etched Rune. In Coldridge Valley, novice dwarf hunters receive a carved summons from Sten Stoutarm. It sends them to Thorgas Grimson inside Anvilmar to learn the hunt. As you help Sten Stoutarm face threats around Coldridge Valley, he gives you the Etched Rune. Dwarven mentors favor carved runes for formal messages, not spoken orders or plain parchment. The stone asks you to take stock of your early work, then report indoors at Anvilmar for deeper instruction in the hunt. At Anvilmar, the Etched Rune marks a hunter's entry into formal discipline. Thorgas Grimson teaches that mountaineering and survival in Khaz Modan demand respect for the harsh land. You learn to read tracks in bitter snowdrifts, care for your weapons and ammunition, and understand the wild beasts roaming the crags. The rune marks your first step from a lone wanderer with a gun to an apprentice among Anvilmar's veteran pathfinders.

quest:3109.text: Encrypted Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm gives young rogues a coded rune and calls them into Anvilmar to meet Solm Hargrin. Sten says someone slipped him the etched stone to deliver. He suspects Solm Hargrin sent it. The rune tests whether a novice can keep a confidence, calling them inside without Solm announcing his need for scouts and scoundrels across the courtyard. Inside Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin welcomes the new rogues to their craft. He offers to teach the maneuvers, strikes, and subtle arts that keep them alive and earn them coin. He also reminds dwarf rogues to look after their displaced gnomish allies, still recovering from Gnomeregan's catastrophic fall.

quest:311.text: Return to Marleth. Marleth waits in Brewnall Village for the Thunder Ale you bring from Kharanos. The barrel will prove her Scalder reached the Thunderbrew cellar. The barrel comes from the Thunderbrew cellar, taken under the distillers’ noses. It proves the switch worked and gives Marleth a trophy from her rival. You carry the heavy keg over snowy ridges to Brewnall Village. Marleth delights in outsmarting Kharanos’s guards and cellar masters. Her caper shows how fiercely dwarven families prize their signature recipes.

quest:3110.text: Hallowed Rune. In Coldridge Valley, a young dwarf priest is called to Anvilmar by Sten Stoutarm. He carries Branstock Khalder’s inscribed prayers and guidance to the novice, who is summoned inside to deepen their bond with the Holy Light. A young priest earns Sten Stoutarm’s notice while helping clear threats outside Anvilmar. Branstock Khalder, the settlement’s spiritual guide, gives Sten a rune inscribed with prayers and guidance for the novice. Then the young priest is called inside Anvilmar’s sturdy halls to begin sacred studies. Dwarven life prizes martial strength and heavy plate, yet the Holy Light remains central to Ironforge society. In Coldridge Valley, holy casters stand with warriors and hunters to protect the enclave from trogg incursions and dangerous wildlife moving through the snow.

quest:3112.text: Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, gnome warriors receive a call to Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm carries Thran Khorman’s summons to trained fighters, who are invited to learn the arts of war and prepare to reclaim Gnomeregan. You help Sten Stoutarm drive off troggs and boars in Coldridge Valley. Thran Khorman, a veteran trainer in Anvilmar, sees promise in the refugee recruit. He calls the recruit to the central hall for martial instruction. Dwarven trainers may tease gnome warriors about their size, but Thran Khorman takes their loss seriously. He asks them to imagine how dwarves would feel if Ironforge fell to the Dark Irons. Thran has pledged to help the exiled gnomes. He teaches them the arts of war until they are ready to reclaim their home.

quest:3113.text: Encrypted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm gives new gnome rogues a folded note for Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. As you help the mountaineers face trogg threats, Sten gives you a parchment entrusted to him. It looks like an official memorandum. The note invites you to meet Solm Hargrin, the rogue trainer stationed inside Anvilmar. Gnome survivors share close quarters with their dwarven hosts after Gnomeregan's sudden fall drove them from their underground home. Solm Hargrin knows rogues draw suspicion when items go missing. So he urges them to stand together quietly and help each other survive.

quest:3114.text: Glyphic Memorandum. In Anvilmar, Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm gives you a memorandum from mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, who invites you to meet him. The summons is for you, a novice mage Sten assists in Coldridge Valley. Read it, then go inside Anvilmar to meet the gnome who wrote it. Your spellcraft studies begin there. Inside Anvilmar, gnome mage trainer Marryk Nurribit offers plain advice before your lessons. Keep out of serious trouble and save coin for training and tavern drinks. Stay clear of fallen Gnomeregan and its radioactive danger. Marryk is ready to teach you the arcane arts.

quest:3115.text: Tainted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm quietly sends you to Alamar Grimm in Anvilmar. Grimm urges you to trust dark power over your dwarven hosts. Warlocks face deep suspicion in Coldridge Valley. As you help Sten Stoutarm with local threats, he reluctantly slips you a note. His warning makes plain how little your kind is trusted here, even under the uneasy truce that allows warlocks to practice in Alliance lands. In Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm speaks of the gnomes’ plight. He believes ordinary magic and tinkering failed Gnomeregan, bringing their people near extinction and leaving them as second-class refugees dependent on dwarven goodwill. He urges you to trust neither the Holy Light nor dwarven politics. Instead, summon fiends and master them, for their obedience is unconditional.

quest:3116.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine bears her summons as the Kaldorei face change across Teldrassil and beyond. You have proved your skill at surviving Shadowglen's restless wildlife. Now Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil. It marks the beginning of your combat training. Alyissia asks you to dedicate your strength to defending your people. Alyissia begins your training while the night elves face swift change and danger. In only a few years, they have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, watched a taint spread through forest beasts near and far, and reconnected with ancient lands once thought lost, including Feralas. The Kaldorei need capable defenders against these perils. Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for more than combat. She asks you not to judge visitors to Teldrassil by their race. Some may not act from pure generosity, yet allies are vital to the Kaldorei's defense. As you take up the work of protecting your people, she asks you to offer visitors reasonable trust.

quest:3117.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil sends young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride calls them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft. After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy. Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and face the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

quest:3118.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, a coded summons brings new night elf rogues to their trainer. Conservator Ilthalaine carries the message for Frahun Shadewhisper, who warns that peace across Kalimdor remains fragile. While young night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those drawn to stealth receive a quieter summons. A runner brings the Encrypted Sigil from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Its ciphers are meant for initiates of the trade. They are to decipher the message and find Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to begin instruction. Frahun's message warns that peace across Kalimdor remains uncertain. The Third War has ended, but the truce between the Alliance and the emerging Horde is fragile. So rogue scouts and informers in Shadowglen are urged to sharpen their eyes and ears early. They watch for threats and covert provocations that could renew war across the borders.

quest:3119.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Hallowed Sigil carries Shanda's call to young night elf priests beginning their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine delivers her message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training. Shanda tells the young acolyte that unusual change has reached Teldrassil's sheltered sanctuary. Travelers fill the World Tree's boughs, including members of the wider Alliance who have leave to meet with the kaldorei. The wider world calls, but Shanda urges novices to first attend to Shadowglen's troubles before turning to conflicts beyond it.

quest:312.text: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. Tundra MacGrann needs his winter stores back from Old Icebeard. The yeti carried off the thorium-reinforced meat locker, and MacGrann's injured leg keeps him from reaching the cave. For the cold season, MacGrann had salted away a month's worth of dried meat. He sealed it in a thorium-reinforced locker to keep hungry bears out. Old Icebeard carried off the whole chest instead of trying to open it. While MacGrann was away hunting deer, Old Icebeard dragged the chest to a cave in the jagged hills. MacGrann believes the yeti cannot break through solid thorium, but his injured leg keeps him from retrieving the stores. You can face the beast or slip inside while it prowls the snowdrifts.

quest:3120.text: Verdant Sigil. In Shadowglen, newly awakened night elf druids receive a summons to begin their training. Conservator Ilthalaine gives them the Verdant Sigil for Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil, where their study of nature and the Emerald Dream begins. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine. She entrusts it to the initiate, showing that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and inviting the young druid to begin formal training. Present the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil, and the initiate is welcomed into the fold. Deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastery of animal forms lie ahead. For now, Mardant becomes their first guide, teaching them to read nature's spirits and channel the raw power of the woods.

quest:313.text: The Grizzled Den. At Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, Pilot Stonegear sends you west to hunt wendigos in the Grizzled Den. Their thick pelts will warm his siege engine, Trollplow. Stonegear tests newcomers before he trusts them with the work. A massive siege tank is hard to operate in freezing mountain air. It takes nerves of iron and a steady constitution. Face the native beasts in the frozen hills to prove you have both. Dun Morogh's bitter cold bites through Trollplow's cramped, iron-plated cabin. Stonegear wants thick wendigo manes for a warm, durable rug on the engine's deck. The hunt also helps keep the local beasts in check.

quest:314.text: Protecting the Herd. At Amberstill Ranch, Rudra Amberstill fears Vagash will take more prized mountain rams. He asks passing fighters to protect the herd and bring proof of the predator’s death. Vagash has taken two prized mountain rams from Amberstill Ranch. The ranch supplies the Bronzebeard dwarves with riding and working beasts, and the herd supports Dun Morogh’s rustic economy. Vagash hunts local livestock in the crags above the ranch. Ironforge’s forces are spread thin across the realm, supporting the Alliance on distant frontiers. With no military patrol on the ridgelines, Rudra Amberstill asks independent fighters to hunt Vagash. He wants one of the beast’s deadly fangs as proof.

quest:315.text: The Perfect Stout. In Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew still pursues The Perfect Stout. He draws on family brewing tradition and exotic local ingredients, and now seeks shimmerweed, a pungent plant cultivated only by the hostile Frostmane trolls atop Shimmer Ridge. He sends daring travelers into their encampment to take the herb from tribal baskets. Brewing is a way of life in Brewnall Village, especially for the Barleybrew family. Rejold Barleybrew believes greatness runs in his blood, but the perfect stout calls for new ideas. He looks beyond hops, malt and mountain spring water to Dun Morogh's untamed plants, hoping they will give his ale an unmistakable bite. East of Brewnall Village, the Frostmane trolls cultivate shimmerweed on Shimmer Ridge. They gather it for tribal and mystic rituals, while dwarves know it for its sharp, distinct flavor. The herb is kept in baskets in the troll village, where Rejold's latest and boldest brewing experiment awaits it.

quest:317.text: Stocking Jetsteam. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam for a long deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade. Its crew needs boar meat and bear pelts for the journey. Master engineer Beldin Steelgrill tunes the siege tank at Steelgrill's Depot, just outside Kharanos. Jetsteam is being readied for an operation on behalf of the Siege Brigade. The crew needs a month's provisions to endure Dun Morogh's sub-zero temperatures. Beldin Steelgrill works beneath Jetsteam's hood, so Bellowfiz cannot leave the vehicle to gather food and insulation. The snowy plains south of the Grizzled Den hold boars for meat and bears whose pelts can line the tank's bedding and keep it warm.

quest:318.text: Evershine. At Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, Pilot Bellowfiz needs Evershine from Rejold Barleybrew in Brewnall Village. The strong brew warms him and can fuel his siege engine, Jetsteam. Rejold Barleybrew's brewing experiments go beyond ordinary dwarven ales. Evershine can knock all but the hardiest dwarves flat, yet its heat is prized in Dun Morogh's bitter cold. At Steelgrill's Depot outside Kharanos, Pilot Bellowfiz takes a warming sip of Evershine against the freezing winds. The volatile brew can also feed Jetsteam's furnace. When Bellowfiz is in a tight spot, it gives his siege engine an explosive burst of emergency power.

quest:319.text: A Favor for Evershine. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz needs Evershine for his siege engine, Jetsteam. Rejold Barleybrew will give up a cask only after you drive the predators away from Brewnall Village. Rejold offers his brew if you thin the wild beasts of western Dun Morogh. Ice Claw Bears, Elder Crag Boars, and Snow Leopards roam near Brewnall Village. Their presence endangers the locals and keeps Rejold from freely giving up the cask. Rejold says no self-respecting dwarf cowers before wild animals. Yet watching for predators around the village takes the craftsmen valuable hours. Once the beasts are driven off, villagers can focus on distilling and smithing without keeping watch on the tree line.

quest:3221.text: Speak with Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel awaits your findings about the tainted wolf hearts. High Executor Hadrec has sent you to speak with the Royal Apothecary Society researcher. After you help the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec gives you an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has studied discolored wolf hearts gathered from local wildlife and needs you at once. Apothecary Renferrel works for the Royal Apothecary Society in a laboratory inside the Sepulcher crypt. He studies how dark magic and disease are changing Silverpine's beasts. His alchemical research draws on military reports from the front.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, Jorn Skyseer guides Horde hunters seeking deeper knowledge of the wilds. After your hunts for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker teaches you more. You have hunted sunscale and scytheclaw raptors across the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows a hunter needs more than skill with weapons; the land's great beasts demand understanding. Her teaching here is done, so she sends you south. The Gold Road leads south across rougher plains to Camp Taurajo, a tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker with lessons for hunters who seek elusive and legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, Gazrog sends you after silver stolen from the guards’ payroll by raptors. Their cunning has led you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and raptors have taken their wages. He sends you to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. At first, he wanted vengeance for the ambush on the payroll shipment. But killing the pack would not bring the money back. The Horde needs to learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory and guard it beside their eggs and fresh kills. Gazrog's tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. In Northshire Valley, Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where daily needs remain even as guards focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls, angry at the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have little strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits. Tradesfolk still have daily needs, so Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and lacks leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Mura Runetotem hopes a shell from the Barrens can help the Forsaken. Around the Barrens oases, Tonga Runetotem studies wildlife changed by magic. The altered snapjaws catch his eye. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. So he asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. At the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest, Mura Runetotem aids her allies. She made the arduous journey to help them cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. The shell holds an inner glow and an enduring spark of life. Mura hopes it may reveal how to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop in Stormwind. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine at their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the rebuilt capital. In Stormwind's Trade District, commerce fills the cobbled streets. Renato Gallina walks among them, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals. Each offers a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. In Stormwind, merchant Harlan Bagley cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. Demand surges, so he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves empty fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers buy reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if they are preparing for a harsh season or winter. The rush leaves his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom. Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. Rema Schneider needs help getting her son’s shears and needles to Larson Clothiers in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter. Thurman is apprenticing there and may fall behind without them. Thurman hurried out of home without his tools. Rema fears he will fall behind at his apprenticeship, so she asks you to carry the shears and needles across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:3361.text: A Refugee's Quandary. Gnomeregan's displaced gnomes flee into Dun Morogh after troggs and radiation drive them from their home. Near Anvilmar, engineer Felix Whindlebolt has lost his tools and belongings to Frostmane scavengers. Troggs overran Gnomeregan, the high-tech city beneath the earth. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors released radioactive gas to kill the invaders. The gas brought disaster instead. Thousands of innocents died, survivors became mindless leper gnomes, and the rest fled across Dun Morogh. Gnome engineers and tinkerers carried away the tools and blueprints they could save. Frostmane trolls prowl the icy mountain passes between Gnomeregan and Coldridge Valley. As Felix Whindlebolt hurried toward shelter at Anvilmar, Frostmane raiders took his tool chest, lockbox, and bucket of bolts. They carried his belongings to camps southwest of town.

quest:3364.text: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery. Nori Pridedrift sends you across Coldridge Valley with hot mornbrew for Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. The mountain cold can steal its heat before it arrives. After you deliver to Grelin Whitebeard, Nori has another cup to send. He cannot carry it himself before the mornbrew freezes into slush. So he asks you to brave the snow and keep his customer from waiting. Durnan Furcutter waits inside Anvilmar's warm mountain hall and is particular about his refreshments. He will not take chilled mornbrew. A hot cup gives the weary dwarf a needed break from his duties. Nori expects his favorite mug back in one piece.

quest:3365.text: Bring Back the Mug. Durnan Furcutter sends you back across Coldridge Valley with Nori Pridedrift's empty mug. Its return closes the Mornbrew delivery. After warming himself with the Mornbrew, Durnan leaves the tankard in your care. Cold bites hard in Dun Morogh, where hospitality depends on mutual respect. Good dishware should make it back too. Nori Pridedrift values sturdy drinkware. Mugs do not grow on trees, especially among the subzero crags of the dwarven homeland. Bring his mug back in one piece, and you show the local community that you can be trusted.

quest:3376.text: Break Sharptusk!. At Red Cloud Mesa, Brave Windfeather sends you east to end the raids on Mulgore. Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine, and his death may weaken their attacks. Young tauren learn to hunt and follow the ways of the Earth Mother at Red Cloud Mesa. East of the mesa, Bristleback quilboar hold Brambleblade Ravine. They see the tauren as invaders on sacred ground, and their skirmishes threaten the tribes trying to make a home in Mulgore. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle commands the Bristleback attacks on Red Cloud Mesa. From a fortified, makeshift village deep in Brambleblade Ravine, he directs warriors and geomancers against the Shu'halo. Brave Windfeather knows the raids will continue while Sharptusk lives. She sends you into the ravine to kill him and bring back his severed head as proof. Brave Windfeather teaches that hunting an enemy who hunts back tests more than skill. For young tauren and their allies, the hunt for Sharptusk calls for courage, awareness, and discipline. His death brings justice for fallen kin and marks a hunter's readiness to travel across Mulgore's wider plains.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. East of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan sends you to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas at the river crossing toward Redridge. Marshal Dughan commands Goldshire's garrison and takes reports of hostile creatures along Elwynn's riverbanks seriously. Bandits and vermin already trouble the forest's center, so he cannot spare guards from town. He sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen the danger for himself. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along eastern Elwynn's waterways. Stormwind's army is absent, and local garrisons guard town walls and supply lines. Rural bridge posts like Thomas's are left isolated as the danger grows.

quest:3519.text: A Friend in Need. In Shadowglen, Iverron lies bitten and in danger. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened from a bite by Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and ventured too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Now dizziness and failing strength keep him from reaching safety alone. Iverron sends passersby to Aldrassil's central tree to find Dirania Silvershine. She watches over him and knows the dangers of Shadowglen. His life may depend on her preparing an antidote before the venom proves fatal.

quest:3521.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must be brewed before a scout's poison takes hold. Dirania Silvershine needs wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor to make the remedy. Young Iverron was scouting the boughs of Shadowglen when Webwood spiders struck him with their poisonous fangs. Now collapsed and dying, he depends on Dirania Silvershine's herbal knowledge at Aldrassil. His venom spreads fast, so she must prepare a remedy before it takes hold. Dirania balances Teldrassil's restorative plants against the spiders' venom. Hyacinth mushrooms, which thieving grell favor in the south, make an earthy base. Moonpetal lilies from tranquil forest pools bring purifying qualities. She also needs Webwood ichor from spiders near Shadowthread Cave, to tailor the cure to their poison.

quest:3522.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for a cure before the poison takes hold. Webwood spiders have poisoned the night elf scout, and Dirania Silvershine's brew must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine makes the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. Once distilled, the unstable brew holds its strength for only five minutes. Carry the vial straight from the glade toward the northern heights, without delay. Webwood spiders near Shadowglen's barrows and caves poisoned Iverron. He admits he often stumbles into danger and relies on Dirania's herbal skill to save him. Even after he drinks the antidote, he remains frail. Hostile spiders still guard his way home, and he fears them.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, sea creatures are washing ashore in growing numbers. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde studies the deaths from Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Great sea creatures have sometimes beached themselves on Darkshore. It is a tragic sight, but it has been occasional. Now they wash ashore in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon fear these deaths may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts come ashore. Based there, she gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains. Without armed protection, researchers cannot reach the bones.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. From Stormwind's Dwarven District, the road reaches an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. In Ironforge, the Stormpike clan is respected for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore entrusts travelers with carrying the weapon north, across the distance from Stormwind to the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. Rumors of unrest and banditry reach the southern human kingdoms, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:354.text: Deaths in the Family. In Brill, Coleman Farthing seeks vengeance on the Agamand family. He once worked at their mills and stayed to defend their estate during the Third War. His fellow workers and their stubborn masters died there, then rose as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or leave its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east. Coleman Farthing and the other workers trusted their lords' assurances and stayed to defend the estate. The Scourge overwhelmed them. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, then raised into undeath where they fell. Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation. The Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries. Coleman Farthing now lives in Brill, still bitter toward the masters whose pride cost him his mortal life. Seeking vengeance and closure, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. He hopes his former masters kept enough awareness behind their rotting faces to feel terror as their unlife came to an end.

quest:355.text: Speak with Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren calls you north after Coleman Farthing's reckoning at Agamand Mills. The undead there threaten Brill's northern border. Coleman Farthing sought revenge on his former neighbors, the Agamands, and sent travelers north to kill the undead around their flour mills. When you brought back their remains, Coleman saw that his grudge had uncovered a greater danger. The Agamand estate still crawls with aggressive Scourge minions, close to Brill. Magistrate Sevren oversees Brill's civic and military security for the Dark Lady. Reports say you survived deep incursions into the haunted farmlands. Now Sevren directs you toward the source of the infestation: the ancient Agamand family crypt.

quest:356.text: Rear Guard Patrol. At the Bulwark, Deathguard Linnea sends you to guard Tirisfal's eastern flank. Scourge horrors and lingering spirits threaten Balnir Farmstead, the road, and the supply lines that keep the front supplied. The Bulwark guards Tirisfal Glades from the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands. Deathguard Linnea watches over the defenders behind the frontier. They cannot spare troops to guard against attacks from the rear. So any undead that slip past the choke point must be destroyed before they cut the supply lines feeding the front. Balnir Farmstead once worked as a farm in eastern Tirisfal, but fell to ruin during the Third War. Blight covers its fields, and Bleeding Horrors and restless Wandering Spirits shelter in its crumbling stables. Clearing the farmstead denies the Lich King a place to gather forces inside Tirisfal. It also keeps the road open for Horde reinforcements.

quest:357.text: The Lich's Identity. Bethor Iceshard seeks the name of the lone lich on Brightwater Lake. He sends an emissary to take the lich's spellbook and learn his power and allegiance. A lone lich lives in exile on a small island in Brightwater Lake, north of the Undercity. Unlike the Lich King's mindless pawns, he has free will, but paranoia rules him. He believes any undead who come near are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude. So he sends summoned minions against anyone who sets foot on his shore. Word of the rogue lich reaches Bethor Iceshard, the archmage who oversees the Undercity's mages. Bethor knows Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks every scrap of magical mastery and every capable will to strengthen the Forsaken against their many foes. To learn whether the recluse can be recruited, Bethor needs proof of his identity and necromantic skill.

quest:358.text:
Graverobbers. At the Mass Grave southwest of Garren's Haunt, Rot Hide gnolls dig among the dead. Magistrate Sevren sends you to stop them and bring back their embalming ichor for the Royal Apothecary Society. The Plague of Undeath swept through Tirisfal Glades, leaving more dead than the living could bury. Across the north, people dug immense mass graves for the countless victims. For a time, those buried there escaped resurrection.

Now the Scourge sends Rot Hide gnolls to the trenches southwest of Garren's Haunt. They exhume the remains to swell the Lich King's armies. Embalming ichor preserves and animates the Rot Hides' rotting frames. Magistrate Sevren sends you to kill the graverobbers and recover the fluid. This keeps the Scourge from harvesting more bodies and gives Brill's apothecaries specimens to study.

They hope to turn the Lich King's own alchemy against him.

quest:36.text: Westfall Stew. Westfall homesteaders are driven from their farms by banditry. As the Furlbrows prepare to leave, Verna entrusts her cherished recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before they go, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew. She hopes the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on. Salma Saldean and her husband, Farmer Saldean, still hold their homestead just down the road. Verna's recipe keeps a local farm tradition alive as another family leaves. Salma sets out to gather ingredients to feed those still struggling on the frontier.

quest:360.text: Return to the Magistrate. At Brill, Magistrate Sevren receives word that the Lich King's servants still press against the Forsaken frontier. Deathguard Linnea sends the warning from the east. East of Tirisfal Glades, the road runs to the blighted ruins of the Western Plaguelands, where the Scourge holds sway. The Forsaken built the Bulwark to bar the undead from their homeland. Deathguard Linnea watches from a waystation behind the line and gathers reports from the eastern gate. Then she sends messengers west along the King's Road to Brill, before enemy infiltrators can find gaps in the defenses. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren hears that Scourge scouts are finding paths around or through the frontline. Each creeping ghoul and mindless skeleton recalls the Forsaken's enslavement, ended when Lordaeron fell. Sevren vows that no matter how ceaseless the Lich King's assault, the free undead will not surrender their new autonomy.

quest:361.text: A Letter Undelivered. Among Agamand Mills' skeletal ruins, A Letter Undelivered lies bloodstained and faded. It recalls two lovers parted as the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, and the life Forsaken left behind. Thurman Agamand, eldest son of patriarch Gregor Agamand, wrote a message that never reached Yvette Farthing. When the Plague of Undeath consumed Tirisfal Glades, Thurman refused to leave his ancestral home or his kin. As the Scourge struck, he took up his quill for Yvette. He had loved her before the kingdom turned to ash.

quest:362.text: The Haunted Mills. Coleman Farthing sends you north from Brill to Agamand Mills, seeking vengeance on the family who once owned his land. First, he wants Devlin's remains gathered. Their feud began when the Agamands failed to protect Tirisfal's common folk from the Plague. Before the Third War, the wealthy Agamand family ruled the mills and fed northern Tirisfal. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the common folk turned to the nobles for safety, but found no shelter. Coleman Farthing survived as undead, yet hatred for the family he served still consumes him. He wants their bones gathered so he can desecrate them beneath his heel. Devlin Agamand was the younger brother of Thurman Agamand. People remembered Devlin as weak, spiteful, and sharp-tongued, unlike his gentle elder brother. When the Plague of Undeath reached the mill estate, Devlin quickly fell to its corruption. Now his mindless corpse chatters without cease along the northern road into the family mills.

quest:363.text: Rude Awakening. Newly awakened Forsaken leave Deathknell's crypts and face an unfamiliar life. Freed from the Lich King's grip, you are sent down the hill, away from the incinerators, to learn what comes next from Shadow Priest Sarvis. In Deathknell's crypt, you wake to undeath among damp stone and cold air. Undertaker Mordo watches the newly buried, sorting those who regain free will from those bound for the burning pits. Many rise confused, surrounded by rot and stone. By chance, they have slipped the Scourge's grasp. Before you reach the chapel, you face a grim truth: once, you were a mindless tool of the Lich King. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke that psychic enslavement, freeing remnants of your former humanity to reclaim independent thought. You leave the tomb and head down into Deathknell, beginning life in a world where the living and the Scourge alike see you as an abomination to be destroyed.

quest:364.text: The Mindless Ones. At Deathknell's northern edge, newly risen Forsaken face The Mindless Ones. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them against Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies, Scourge thralls bound to the Lich King's command. Many who rise from Lordaeron's soil never recover their minds. The Forsaken broke free of Ner'zhul's rule as his power waned, but countless dead remain chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies roam, driven to violence. For you, newly risen among the undead, laying them to rest is your first hard trial. You prove your freedom by ending the thrall of those who never escaped. Shadow Priest Sarvis grieves that these legions of dead cannot strengthen the Forsaken's desperate struggle. There is no cure for them. Their minds are broken, and they remain instruments of slaughter. Left to roam, they bring chaos to Deathknell's doorstep and give the Lich King easy fodder. Destroying them is necessary for the settlement and brings a grim end to some of Lordaeron's fallen.

quest:365.text: Fields of Grief. Pumpkins from a human farm north of Deathknell are bound for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill. Deathguard Simmer sends the newly risen Forsaken to gather them. Deathguard Simmer sends you from Deathknell's crypts into hostile land. He serves Sylvanas Windrunner's forces. There, survival means taking what the living have and putting it to use for the Undercity's darker aims. The farm lies west of the road and north of Deathknell.
