Human peasants work its blighted soil, and Simmer says they infest the realm like mold on a corpse. They hold their homesteads under the uneasy protection of nearby Scarlet Crusade towers. Taking their crops strikes at their supplies and gives the Royal Apothecary Society produce for research.

quest:366.text:
Return the Book. Bethor Iceshard sends an enchanted message to Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. The stolen spellbook may draw his old Kirin Tor companion toward the Forsaken. The spellbook you took from Gunther Arcanus goes back to him, but it is no longer plain. Learning that the necromancer on Brightwater Lake is his old companion, Bethor enchants its pages. His magic leaves a mark on the tome. It shows Gunther that Bethor is active in Lordaeron and free of the Lich King's control. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw studied together in the Kirin Tor of Dalaran and became friends. When the Lich King rose, Thule betrayed them and joined the Scourge willingly. Bethor and Gunther fell to the Plague. Bethor later broke free alongside Queen Sylvanas.

Bethor believed Gunther dead or enslaved. Now he learns his old friend has won his freedom too, and seeks to bring him into the Forsaken fold.

quest:367.text:
A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan gathers blood from darkhounds for a new plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works at Lady Sylvanas Windrunner’s command. Apothecary Johaan serves the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill, under orders from the Dark Lady. Sylvanas Windrunner has charged her alchemists with making a disease unlike any Azeroth has known.

The Lich King's Plague of Undeath slaughtered humanity and bound their souls. This new plague is meant to annihilate Arthas Menethil and lay waste to his Scourge legions. Johaan seeks grim experiments for a weapon against the undead. He believes the blood of native beasts may hold useful chemical properties, and begins with darkhounds roaming Tirisfal Glades.

You gather vials of their tainted blood. Johaan can isolate its elements and test whether the beasts' resilience and predatory nature might help make a lethal contagion.

quest:368.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan gathers Vile Fin scales for the Royal Apothecary Society's work on a plague. He hopes it will spread beyond isolated victims and reach larger populations. Apothecary Johaan's work in Brill calls for more than a poison that harms one target. He seeks a disease that can spread on its own and endure in the wild. So he studies the shoreline wildlife of Tirisfal Glades. The resilient Vile Fin murlocs offer promising material. Aggressive Vile Fin murloc tribes trouble Tirisfal Glades' northern and western shores. Their scales hold organic compounds adapted to damp, harsh conditions. Johaan hopes these slick, resilient scales will strengthen the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague and help it endure in the wild.

quest:3681.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Master Brandur Ironhammer sends promising human paladins south for deeper training. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Master Duthorian Rall guides their study of the sacred Tomes of Divinity. Stormwind calls promising holy warriors south to the Cathedral of Light. Senior priests and paladin mentors await them there, keeping the Silver Hand's traditions alive in the Church of the Holy Light among human lands. Master Brandur Ironhammer knows when a student is ready for deeper study of the faith. You can reach Stormwind's Cathedral District by the Deeprun Tram or across the mountain passes. There, Duthorian Rall prepares initiates to study the sacred Tomes and learn the rites of redemption.

quest:369.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan searches old records for a plague that endured in spider venom. He hopes to give the Forsaken a potent new biological agent. Apothecary Johaan studies old texts in Brill for the Royal Apothecary Society. There he finds records of an ancient pestilence that killed thousands. The writings say its pathogen endured across generations in the venom of spiders native to Tirisfal Glades. Johaan needs that venom as a biological reagent. Apothecary Johaan sends agents to eastern Tirisfal Glades in search of a living sample. Venomweb Vale lies south of the Scarlet Monastery, and vicious night web spiders fill its hollow. To gather fresh venom glands for Johaan's experimental brew, harvesters must enter the spiders' dens.

quest:37.text: Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas waits at Elwynn's eastern bridge, needing news of two missing Stormwind guards. At the crossing where the King's road nears Redridge, the riverbanks have grown more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent Rolf and Malakai north along the river to scout the murloc threat and clear their nests. Now he fears violence has stopped their patrol.

quest:370.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken strike at Scarlet Crusade forces threatening their borders. Executor Zygand sends champions against Captain Perrine and his garrison at a ruined tower southwest of Brill, guided by intelligence taken in Deathknell. Executor Arren recovered Scarlet Crusade documents in Deathknell. They revealed troop movements across Tirisfal Glades. So Executor Zygand uses that intelligence to strike the field commanders first, before the fanatics can attack newly fortified Brill. At a ruined watchtower southwest of Brill, Captain Perrine commands Scarlet Zealots and Missionaries. The Crusade watches Forsaken movements from there and reaches farther into Tirisfal. Perrine's death matters to the defense of the Dark Lady's young kingdom.

quest:371.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Near Balnir Farmstead, Executor Zygand sends Forsaken fighters against the Scarlet Crusade. They target Captain Vachon and his friars in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, where Crusader raids threaten the Dark Lady's lands. Brill and the Undercity are guarded by the Forsaken, while the Scarlet Crusade holds fortified sites across the countryside. From a crumbling guard tower in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, Executor Arren reports active Crusader incursions. The tower stands close to the abandoned Balnir Farmstead. Executor Zygand strikes at the Crusade's field leaders, for coordinated squads are more dangerous than scattered zealots. You attack Captain Vachon and the Scarlet Friars who strengthen his men with holy magic. Without their leaders and support, the cell may lose its unity, and its raids into Forsaken lands may falter.

quest:372.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, Executor Zygand sends Forsaken agents from Brill against the Scarlet Crusade. Captain Melrache and his sworn guards hold a ruined watchtower beyond Faol's Rest. The Forsaken are securing Lordaeron's ruins, but the Scarlet Crusade keeps testing Tirisfal's borders. From a tower in the north, past Faol's Rest, crusaders lead raids against Forsaken patrols and lands. Executor Zygand means to strike the officers directing those raids before another attack comes. Captain Melrache commands the northern camp with two sworn bodyguards always at his side. From the tower, the Scarlet Crusade watches the coastal roads and nearby woods. Kill Melrache, and the raiders near Brill lose their order. His fall removes a direct threat to Lady Sylvanas's young kingdom and drives the zealots toward stronger fortifications farther east.

quest:374.text:
Proof of Demise. In Brill, Proof of Demise sends soldiers against the Scarlet Crusade across Tirisfal Glades. Varimathras, Sylvanas Windrunner's dreadlord lieutenant, orders the campaign to thin their ranks and test loyalty to the Forsaken cause. Recruits must take signet rings from fallen crusaders as proof. Across northern Tirisfal Glades, the Forsaken wage a coordinated war against the living. Varimathras surrendered and pledged his blade to Sylvanas Windrunner. He oversees many of the Forsaken's aggressive military maneuvers.

His orders pass to commanders such as Executor Zygand, then to frontline officers like Deathguard Burgess. Burgess makes the order plain: humans are vermin to be purged from Lordaeron, and nearby crusaders are the immediate target. In Brill, words alone do not satisfy the commanders. Soldiers must take Scarlet Insignia Rings from the fingers of slain zealots to prove obedience to the Dark Lady and her lieutenant. The rings bear the Scarlet Crusade's mark, identifying their bearers as sworn enemies of the Forsaken.

Bring back these trophies, and the dead crusaders are proved. The rings also show a soldier's allegiance to the Forsaken leadership.

quest:3741.text: Hilary's Necklace. At Lakeshire's docks, Hilary loses the necklace her father gave her. Shawn asks you to find it in Lake Everstill, where their parents forbid them to swim. Hilary and Shawn fish from Lakeshire's docks, seeking an ordinary day amid the threats around the Redridge Mountains. Then Hilary's treasured necklace slips into Lake Everstill. They search the piers and shore, but find nothing. Shawn asks you to help. Their parents forbid Hilary and Shawn to swim in Lake Everstill. Aggressive murlocs and hungry threshedons lurk below the surface. The necklace lies in glinting mud at the lake bottom, beyond the children's reach. So Shawn asks you to recover the gift.

quest:375.text: The Chill of Death. In Brill, The Chill of Death weighs on Gretchen Dedmar as she fights the cold of undeath. The Forsaken tailor fears losing her mind and her service to Lady Sylvanas, so she asks for materials to sew a warm blanket. Gretchen Dedmar feels the Plague of Undeath like an icy serpent moving through her body. The chill drains warmth from her limbs and threatens to leave her mindless, like the wandering corpses in Tirisfal Glades. Her shaking hands make even ordinary work difficult. Gretchen will not abandon her duty to the Forsaken kingdom. When Sylvanas Windrunner first rallied the liberated dead, Gretchen sewed burial shrouds and body bags for fallen soldiers. Sturdy duskbat pelts and coarse thread can help her make a blanket. Its warmth may steady her hands enough to keep serving the Forsaken cause.

quest:376.text: The Damned. New Forsaken in Deathknell seek clothing and battlefield wraps from Novice Elreth. She trades salvaged armor for the materials to make them. Novice Elreth tends the newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell. She aids Shadow Priest Sarvis, cares for battered soldiers, and mends their garments. When supplies run short, she sends you into the surrounding glades to hunt duskbats and scavenger wolves. Their pelts, wings, and sinew help supply the camp, and Elreth offers salvaged armor in return. Elreth's armor belonged to Forsaken who did not survive their awakening. She hopes it serves you better than it served its former owner. In Tirisfal Glades, every piece of leather and rusted chain finds a use.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. On her farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers face bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a meal that sustains her farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. Such fare may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:380.text: Night Web's Hollow. Northwest of Deathknell, spiders overrun a gold mine the Forsaken need. Executor Arren sends newly risen recruits into the cavern to thin their ranks. Raw materials are scarce, and the mine's wealth could sustain the Forsaken settlement and war effort. In Deathknell, Executor Arren oversees the newly risen Forsaken as they struggle to survive. The Scourge and Scarlet crusaders threaten them, but defense is only part of the work. A fledgling society needs raw materials too. Precious metals such as gold were scarce in northern Lordaeron even when the Alliance was strong. Arren knows the Forsaken need wealth to arm and equip themselves and establish their society. Northwest of Deathknell's cemetery, a gold vein runs through the natural cavern called Night Web's Hollow. Monstrous spiders have overrun its tunnels, laying thick webs and deadly venom in the depths. Arren has too few seasoned troops for a full purge, so fresh recruits thin the young and adult spiders. Once the danger is reduced, mining crews can burn away the webs and extract the ore.

quest:381.text: The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, a Scarlet Crusade camp threatens Deathknell from the southeast. Executor Arren sends the newly awakened Forsaken to strike its zealots, among their most fanatical and persistent enemies. After the Night Web spiders are dealt with, Executor Arren turns his attention to a danger drawing near Deathknell. A Scarlet Crusade detachment has made a foothold just southeast of the settlement. Its zealots see no difference between mindless Scourge and free-willed Forsaken. Their presence on Deathknell's border threatens the newly risen dead. Executor Arren orders a strike before the camp can grow into an organized attack on Deathknell. You cut down Scarlet Converts and Scarlet Initiates, then return with their crimson armbands as proof. The holy fanatics see all dead flesh as an abomination, so the Forsaken must claim survival by force.

quest:382.text: The Red Messenger. Executor Arren sends you after a courier bound for the camp outside Deathknell. Sent from the Scarlet Monastery, the courier carries the crusade's word to its camp. This offensive move secures intelligence before the zealots can strengthen their hold in the valley, as the Forsaken defend their fledgling sanctuary. Executor Arren learns of the Scarlet courier from his superiors in Brill. The Scarlet Crusade sent an emissary west from its stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery to Deathknell. Crusaders press across Lordaeron. A courier sent to the edge of the Forsaken's waking grounds signals an organized effort to destroy the newly risen before they can prepare a defense. Meven Korgal, the courier, has blended into the small Scarlet camp east of Deathknell without distinctive heraldry. Executor Arren orders a targeted strike to kill Korgal and seize his dispatch. Taking the missives cuts off the local zealots from further tactical coordination with their eastern headquarters.

quest:383.text: Vital Intelligence. In Tirisfal Glades, a newly risen Forsaken bears captured Scarlet Crusade documents from Deathknell to Brill. Executor Zygand awaits the courier there. Executor Arren sends you from Deathknell with captured Scarlet Crusade documents. You have dealt with local threats and intercepted a Scarlet Crusade courier, and now wider service awaits. Leave through Deathknell's sheltered canyon and follow the road east toward Brill, passing Cold Hearth Manor.

quest:384.text: Beer Basted Boar Ribs. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, patrons hunger for Ragnar Thunderbrew's famed ribs. His regular supplier has joined the King's Army, so Ragnar needs fresh crag boar ribs and Rhapsody Malt to keep them on the menu. Tavern keeper Ragnar Thunderbrew has eager customers, but his pantry is bare. The local hunter who supplied fresh meat enlisted in the King's Army to reinforce the Alliance front. Now Ragnar has no fresh ribs for the patrons who favor them. Crag boars roam the snowy foothills around Kharanos, and their meat is tough. Ragnar's recipe also calls for fresh Rhapsody Malt, drawn straight from the distillery's taps. The malt softens the game meat and makes a savory feast fit for a dwarf's praise.

quest:385.text: Crocolisk Hunting. At Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart seeks trackers to hunt Loch Modan's crocolisks. Their hides and meat bring steady trade, though hunting along the lake's shores and rocky islets is dangerous. Crocolisks haunt the shallows and muddy banks, making crossings and fishing perilous. Across Khaz Modan, craftsmen and tailors seek their hides for rugged armor and leather goods. Rustic taverns pay well for the lean tail meat. Loch Modan's crocolisks gather mainly around the rocky islets. Their crushing jaws and sharp teeth make them dangerous quarry. Dwarven veterans like Marek Ironheart carry scars from wrestling them into submission. He warns that one misstep in the water can cost a limb. Skinning and butchering one takes patience, sturdy steel, and a willingness to enter its hunting ground.

quest:3861.text: CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Across Azeroth, ordinary chickens wander farmsteads, though most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and cluck, and one may stop pecking to regard you. In that brief moment, it scratches letters in the dirt, pointing you toward the farmer who can provide the food it wants. The bird asks for Special Chicken Feed, which the Saldean family keeps for its flock in Westfall. Offer the grain and cheer the chicken on as it eats. In return, it lays a warm egg, ready to be nurtured into a feathered companion.

quest:39.text: Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where few hands remain to defend the roads. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Aggressive murloc tribes have killed Guards Malakai and Rolf. Thomas has too few guards left to contain them, so he sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report. Marshal Dughan receives Thomas' report in Goldshire, where he already struggles to keep patrols on the roads. Kobolds infest the area, Defias bandits threaten travelers, and Stormwind City has sent no reinforcements. The deaths of two experienced guards deepen his burden. Murlocs may soon threaten Goldshire itself, while the region's defenses grow ever thinner.

quest:3901.text: Rattling the Rattlecages. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken face the Rattlecage Skeletons and a test of their freedom. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to destroy twelve skeletons and prove they can defend what they won. After culling the mindless zombies in Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken face a harder trial. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends recruits against the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the settlement’s outskirts. The animated bones have no sapience or self-control, yet strike harder and fight more fiercely than the nearby decaying corpses. Surviving their clattering ambushes shows Sarvis a recruit can withstand immediate pressure. Destroying the skeletons protects Deathknell from the lingering grip of the Lich King and tests which recruits can endure the fight. Those who fail or hesitate risk becoming like the mindless wretches wandering the woods. Overcoming the Rattlecages proves to Sarvis you have the mettle to face a world that despises your existence.

quest:3902.text: Scavenging Deathknell. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken gather supplies for recruits rising from nearby graves. Deathguard Saltain sends them through the blighted settlement to search abandoned boxes and crates for what they need to survive. Newly raised Forsaken wake in Deathknell with little to call their own. Deathguard Saltain sends them to gather clothing and arms for recruits still climbing from their graves. Every usable piece helps outfit the newly risen. Deathknell holds remnants of its former human inhabitants and supplies abandoned during the kingdom’s fall to the Scourge. Deathguards send newly awakened Forsaken to search boxes and crates scattered through town. The living offer no charity, so the Forsaken must rely on their own effort to survive.

quest:3903.text: Milly Osworth. Deputy Willem sends you across Northshire Abbey to help his friend Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in danger, and Willem's guards cannot leave the abbey grounds to help. After you drive back the Defias thieves pressing into Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem trusts you with a personal favor. His friend Milly Osworth is a civilian caught in the valley's unrest, and helping her falls beyond his guard duties. Milly waits beside her wagon near the stables on the far side of Northshire Abbey. Deputy Willem stays at his post to defend the abbey. With the guard garrison stretched thin, Milly's troubles in the valley go without help.

quest:3904.text: Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her gathered grapes remain in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, at risk of theft or ruin. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. The grapes she had gathered remain in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind. Defias bandits now occupy working vineyards, a sign of how little safety Northshire can offer. Stormwind's attention lies elsewhere, and the valley has too few guards. So farmers like Milly depend on recruits and wanderers to protect their property and secure the food and wine that supply the abbey.

quest:3905.text: Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth needs you to bring her manifest to Brother Neals at Northshire Abbey. It will help the brotherhood replenish its wine stores. Defias thieves and other brigands took the eastern fields. The abbey lost its food and its grapes. Milly has recovered the crop and recorded every bushel in her manifest, including what the occupied fields had yielded. Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. In the quiet of the bell tower, he is known to sample Northshire's vintages. Brigands still threaten the gates, yet fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

quest:3921.text: Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Sputtervalve needs Wenikee Boltbucket to mend a broken samophlange. He damaged it after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now his claims to his colleagues in Undermine hang on its repair. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine rest on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen. Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off, and his tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. Now he needs someone with sharper skill to find the fault and repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket camps beside the road just south of the Mor'shan Rampart, which divides the northern Barrens from Ashenvale. Her curious mind is drawn to intricate machinery, and the broken samophlange quickly catches her attention. Its inner gears fascinate her, so she sets to work figuring out how to rebuild it.

quest:3922.text: Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket seeks parts for a samophlange she has recovered. She sends you to the nearby Venture Company crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has recovered a samophlange and wants to learn how its intricate workings fit together. The goblin machine needs exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

quest:3923.text: Rilli Greasygob. Wenikee Boltbucket sends a damaged samophlange to Rilli Greasygob in Orgrimmar. She hopes his knowledge of its Venture Company origins will explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed it was close to collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone who knew its design. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Wenikee sends you to Nogg's Machine Shop. Rilli Greasygob works there as an engineer and once learned his trade within the Venture Company. He recognizes the machine at once and marvels that anyone survived exploring the company's contested operations in the Barrens.

quest:3924.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob needs help with a broken samophlange. The goblin engineer sends you back into the Barrens for the operating instructions, held by his former Venture Company rival. Rilli Greasygob once worked beside Boss Copperplug in the Venture Company. Copperplug oversaw the samophlange’s inner workings and guarded their secrets closely. He gave Rilli no manual. Instead, Copperplug handed separate pages only to underlings he trusted, leaving his fellow engineer without the knowledge to understand the device.

quest:398.text: Wanted: Maggot Eye. In Brill, the Forsaken have set a death bounty on Maggot Eye. The notorious gnoll robs nearby graveyards and farms, supplying bodies to the Lich King's Scourge. Executor Zygand demands proof of the kill to secure the lands around Garren's Haunt. In Tirisfal Glades, the dead do not rest in peace. Maggot Eye faces a severe sentence for aiding the Lich King. Gnolls are usually savage brutes driven by hunger. Yet Maggot Eye digs up corpses and gathers remains to strengthen the Scourge army. The Forsaken fight to break free of the Lich King's control. Feeding their dead kin to the Scourge is among the gravest offenses. Executor Zygand oversees local military enforcement in Brill. He ordered the bounty to end grave robberies near Garren's Haunt. To claim the reward, bring Maggot Eye's paw as proof that the beast can trouble Tirisfal no longer.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. In Cathedral Square, Baros Alexston asks you to search his family's burned farm in Westfall. Thieves hold the ruins, and he hopes to recover the compass he treasured as a boy. Baros Alexston once worked the fields of Westfall. Now he is Stormwind City's accomplished architect, advising on stonework and city buildings. Few in the kingdom have made such a journey from farm to city. Yet Baros remains bound to the humble beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall and reached the Alexston Farmstead. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, driving Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms remained behind amid the fire and occupation. Now Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:40.text: A Fishy Peril. In eastern Elwynn, Remy "Two Times" fears a danger is spreading. Fishing has suffered and travelers face attacks, but he doubts the guard understands the trouble. In Goldshire seeking business, Remy grows uneasy as murlocs swim up streams and into inland shallows. He asks passersby to warn the township before the threat spreads further. Marshal Dughan hears the report but doubts it. His garrison is stretched thin, and without confirmed intelligence, he will not send scarce men after rumors of fish-men in the eastern streams.

quest:400.text: Tools for Steelgrill. At Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone sends you northeast with tools for Beldin Steelgrill at the depot. The road leads from town to the mechanics and war machines gathered there. Across Dun Morogh, Beldin Steelgrill is known as the sharpest siege engine mechanic in the mountains. His rough work breaks arclight spanners and other tools faster than Kharanos suppliers can replace them. Tharek Blackstone has a fresh batch of durable gear ready, so a traveler bound northeast carries the heavy crate to the depot. Steelgrill's Depot is crowded with idle war machines and military repairs. Beldin's backlog includes urgent work on Pilot Stonegear's siege engine. He broke his last fang-ratchet only hours before you arrive. The crate is needed to keep Ironforge's tracked armor fleet running.

quest:403.text: Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel. In Kharanos, the Thunderbrew family’s ale waits under guard in the distillery cellar. Jarven watches over the stock. Jarven Thunderbrew keeps watch over the aging casks beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Sentries stand beside the barrels, guarding the brew from tampering or theft. The Thunderbrews keep their recipes close, especially the potent Thunder Ale. Dwarves give brewing the care they give smithing and mining. Troggs creep nearby, and brewing rivals compete across the Alliance. So Jarven watches until the family’s ale is ready to be tapped.

quest:404.text: A Putrid Task. Deathguard Dillinger sends you west from Brill to guard the old bridge against the Scourge. Bring back proof that the dead are destroyed, and Tirisfal's defenders can keep the road clear. Brill guards a crossroads in eastern Tirisfal Glades, where the Scourge threaten the Forsaken stronghold. The dead wander west across the waterways and gather around the broken old stone bridge. Without patrols to drive them back, they could block travel between Brill and the western farmsteads. For the Forsaken, the Scourge at their borders are more than a threat to face. Every mindless ghoul and rotting corpse recalls the servitude and torment they escaped under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Deathguards like Dillinger take grim satisfaction in crushing their former captors. Severed claws prove the mindless dead have been put to rest for good.

quest:405.text: The Prodigal Lich. In the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard seeks an agent for a matter involving a wayward lich. After your work against Scourge remnants and Rot Hide gnolls in Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends you south with orders. Your service in Brill has earned Magistrate Sevren's trust for greater Forsaken work. He sends you to Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Bethor wants an agent tested against the Scourge, and Sevren gives you official orders to carry beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the corridors of the Forsaken capital. Magistrate Sevren does not know the full details, but the orders concern finding and recruiting a rogue lich. Liches are among the Scourge's deadliest spellcasters, so dealing with one is perilous. You bring the orders to Bethor atop his arcane sanctum. The icy mage is ready to see whether Brill's magistrate has sent someone strong enough to track such dangerous quarry.

quest:407.text: Fields of Grief. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan tests a weapon made from pumpkins. He laces them with his latest alchemical concoction and sends you to feed one to a captive Scarlet Crusader. The Forsaken face the Scourge to the north and human incursions to the south, so Apothecary Johaan believes they must use every advantage. The Royal Apothecary Society looks beyond blades and dark sorcery. It seeks weapons among the land’s ordinary produce. Johaan has tainted pumpkins gathered from the mortal farmers at Solliden Farmstead. He means to prove that common crops can be made deadly in service of the Dark Lady.

quest:408.text: The Family Crypt. Scourge forces press the Forsaken at Agamand Mills. From Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends agents to strike the undead in the family crypt. The Forsaken hold Tirisfal Glades, though the Scourge still commands much of its countryside. The Agamand Mills once ground flour for Lordaeron. Now the mills shelter the Scourge. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren watches the enemy gather with grave concern. Every stretch of land lost to the undead weakens the Forsaken's independence. Captain Dargol, a skeletal commander, has made the Agamand Family Crypt his headquarters. He uses necromancy to raise generations of the Agamand dead as Rotting and Wailing Ancestors, swelling his ranks. Magistrate Sevren sends Forsaken agents to purge the crypt and lay its disturbed dead to rest. He also wants Dargol's head, to disrupt Scourge forces in northern Tirisfal.

quest:409.text: Proving Allegiance. Gunther Arcanus tests whether you serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. He sends you to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a Scourge operative near his island. Gunther Arcanus has lived on an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath. He guards his freedom fiercely. Bethor Iceshard enchanted Gunther's spellbook and found no Scourge taint on the emissary. Yet neither words nor charms can quiet Gunther's suspicions. He needs an outsider to prove hostility toward the Lich King's minions through decisive violence before he will trust them.

quest:410.text: The Dormant Shade. At Gunther's Retreat in Brightwater Lake, a dark rite calls to Lillith Nefara. Set a mystic candle on the old blood-soaked table to summon the Scourge agent and prove to Gunther Arcanus that you oppose the Lich King. On Gunther's Retreat, an island in Brightwater Lake, a battered dinner table lies stained with blood. It is no abandoned piece of furniture. Dark conjuring gathers around the rough slab, where dried gore marks the place of death and magic.

quest:411.text: The Prodigal Lich Returns. In the Undercity, you carry a Nether Gem to Bethor Iceshard after winning Gunther Arcanus's trust and restoring his grimoire. Gunther Arcanus spent years alone on an island in Brightwater Lake. By will alone, he escaped the Lich King's control, not knowing Sylvanas Windrunner had freed Lordaeron. Bitter and wary, he distrusted the Undercity's emissaries. An adventurer returned his spellbook and showed him their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied the visitor was no enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to contact his former colleague.

quest:412.text: Operation Recombobulation. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt search for a cure for their kin. Their experimental Recombobulator needs parts taken from hostile leper gnomes outside Gnomeregan. Razzle and Ozzie are building a machine to restore their afflicted kin to health and sanity. Radiation changed most of Gnomeregan's gnomes into sickly, deranged leper gnomes. The inventors hope their Recombobulator can reverse that change. Razzle needs Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears for the delicate prototype. The parts must come from hostile leper gnomes outside Gnomeregan's sealed gates. Debris from their altered kin may help undo the tragedy they share.

quest:413.text: Shimmer Stout. At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew is sending Shimmer Stout to his brother Wellart. The guard watches the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink welcome. Rejold Barleybrew perfected Shimmer Stout with shimmering fronds gathered from Dun Morogh’s icy crags. His family tends the vats and kegs at Brewnall Village, while his brother Wellart chose life as a Mountaineer. Knowing how lonely frontier guard duty can be, Rejold sends a fresh barrel with passing travelers. It is a kindness between brothers and a chance to test the brew. Wellart Barleybrew guards the South Gate Pass into Loch Modan from the southern tower. High in the pass, Mountaineers face bitter winds and occasional beast attacks as they watch over travelers on the mountain road. Wellart is running low on drink and restless for excitement. Shimmer Stout packs quite a punch, he finds, and seems to brighten his vision in the dim mountain night.

quest:414.text: Stout to Kadrell. A cask of Rejold Barleybrew’s new Shimmer Stout is headed east to Mountaineer Kadrell in Loch Modan. You carry it from Dun Morogh’s frozen heights to the warmer valley. From Dun Morogh’s eastern border post, Mountaineer Barleybrew watches the mountain passes and the kin guarding neighboring lands. The Mountaineers’ patrols can be cold and grueling, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Rejold’s new Shimmer Stout is too good to keep in Dun Morogh. Barleybrew wants an honest opinion from a fellow patrolman, so he sends a cask east with travelers bound for Loch Modan. For young dwarven and gnomish adventurers, the road to Loch Modan is a rite of passage after their early days in Dun Morogh’s snowbound crags. You pass southeast through the South Gate Outpost, then follow long tunnels cut through the mountain bedrock. Beyond them lies Loch Modan’s warmer, wooded basin. Mountaineer Kadrell patrols the road through Thelsamar. He pauses to tap the cask and finds that Barleybrew’s new recipe has an astonishing kick.

quest:415.text: Rejold's New Brew. Back at Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew has perfected his new recipe. He wants you, the trusted friend who secured the Shimmerweed, to taste it. Tharek Blackstone and Pilot Bellowfiz send you back to Brewnall Village. Rejold has finished fermenting his experimental batches and is ready to share them with you. You secured Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes, and now he can offer you the fruits of that effort. Rejold Barleybrew has blended local herbs into his mash to make Shimmer Stout. Before he ships barrels to neighboring outposts and thirsty patrons in Loch Modan, he gives you the honor of the first sip. You risked life and limb for the herbs, and the first taste is yours.

quest:4161.text: Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, Zarrin teaches young cooks to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. His lesson begins with food and the forest, not the battlefield. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. Night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins with their bond to food and Teldrassil's boughs, and leaves the battlefield aside. Outside Shadowglen, Zarrin asks you to gather exactly seven small spider legs from woodland arachnids. The kaldorei seek harmony with nature by taking only what they need and treating the wild with kindness. Even in troubled times, that balance matters. A spider kabob makes the lesson plain.

quest:417.text: A Pilot's Revenge. Hildelve’s search ends in the crags of Dun Morogh, where Pilot Hammerfoot’s searchers find him frozen beside his journal. His last words call for vengeance. Hildelve’s journal tells of his savage fight with Mangeclaw, the huge Ice Claw bear. He drove the beast away at first, but his wounds were grave. Mangeclaw returned and killed him. Hildelve’s final plea calls for vengeance against Mangeclaw. Bring his journal and a claw torn from the beast to Pilot Hammerfoot. The grim news gives the Ironforge Siege Brigade closure and honors its lost comrade.

quest:418.text: Thelsamar Blood Sausages. At Thelsamar's Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove keeps Thelsamar Blood Sausages on the table. A favorite across Loch Modan, they need fresh ingredients from the valley. Hungry children and miners returning from the Ironband Excavation fill Thelsamar's tavern. Vidra Hearthstove tends the stove, making sausages known across Loch Modan. Her recipe draws on wildlife from the rugged mountain pass. Vidra uses boar intestines for casings and bear meat for the filling. Spider ichor gives the sausages their sharp, pungent bite. Gathering the entrails and venomous fluid takes a steady stomach, though travelers come to appreciate this regional favorite.

quest:419.text: The Lost Pilot. At the wreck, Pilot Hammerfoot fears for Mori Hildelve in Dun Morogh's crags. Hildelve went on foot to seek rare ore for potent blastpowder, but days have passed and roars echo through the peaks. Pilot Mori Hildelve drove his siege engine up Dun Morogh's steep ridges in search of rare ore for high-grade blastpowder. The machine broke on the slope. He left Pilot Hammerfoot at the camp to guard the wreck, then climbed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot. Days passed, and Hildelve did not return to camp. At night, vicious growls echoed from the rocky crags. Hammerfoot's impatience gave way to dread. Hildelve was tough, but the frigid heights offered little shelter from prowling predators without his engine or heavy support.

quest:420.text:
Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard's report reaches his brother Senir in Kharanos, carrying news from Coldridge Valley. Its arrival sends Senir back to watching hostile forces across the snowfields. Mountaineer Thalos guards the gate out of Coldridge Valley. He entrusts passing travelers with Grelin's dispatch. Beyond the gate, violent troggs ambush those crossing the tunnel and make the passage to Kharanos dangerous. Past the tunnel, the main road runs through central Dun Morogh to town. At the Thunderbrew Distillery, Senir Whitebeard warms himself over drinks when Grelin's report arrives. He chuckles at his brother's forceful words. Grelin invokes King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, Senir says, and that will agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate.

The bitter cold has kept Senir from filing his own observations. Grelin's dispatch sends him back to watching hostile forces across the snowfields.

quest:421.text: Prove Your Worth. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver's campaign against Silverpine's worgen is underway. The Forsaken seek a path south through human and dwarven lands, but feral worgen threaten the road. Their presence leads back to Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to secure the lands south of Tirisfal Glades. Human and dwarven enclaves lie among them. Silverpine Forest is in their path, but the route is dangerous. Feral Moonrage worgen prowl its pine-covered hills, threatening Forsaken supply lines and forward bases. Dalar Dawnweaver says Arugal brought the worgen to Silverpine. Once a mage of Dalaran, Arugal was disgraced. During the Scourge invasion, he unleashed otherworldly worgen upon the forest. Now he has claimed Shadowfang Keep, while his feral creations roam the woods. Before Dalar trusts soldiers to investigate Arugal's sorcery further, recruits must prove their fighting skill against the nearest Moonrage Whitescalps.

quest:422.text: Arugal's Folly. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sends Forsaken agents to a nearby farmstead for Arugal's earliest spellbooks. The Forsaken need to understand the magic behind the worgen curse if they are to turn it against Arugal and secure Silverpine Forest. The Remedy of Arugal is the first step in unraveling the threat from Shadowfang Keep. In the Sepulcher's crypts, ambitious Forsaken mage Dalar Dawnweaver holds Archmage Arugal in contempt. He sees him as an ordinary practitioner whose place in the Kirin Tor makes no sense, and whose grasp of magic seems amateurish. Yet the monstrous beasts roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver means to take apart the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

quest:423.text: Arugal's Folly. In Silverpine, Forsaken agents seek shackles worn by Moonrage worgen. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's notes to learn how the renegade mage strengthened his unstable magic. The bindings may help the Forsaken break the worgen threat. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's recovered research and speaks of his former peer with open contempt. He says Arugal was unfit to serve Dalaran, let alone wield high sorcery in the kingdom's darkest hour. Short on talent, Arugal turned to enchanted relics and devices to strengthen and bind the worgen he summoned. Dalar needs samples to study the magic that tethers the beasts. Moonrage worgen roam Silverpine wearing shackles marked by Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls prowl north and east of the Sepulcher. Their heavy metal shackles hold residual arcane energy. Dawnweaver hopes that energy will help him find a way to counter Shadowfang Keep.

quest:424.text: Arugal's Folly. Worgen hold Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills, keeping the Forsaken from ore needed by Varimathras's forces. Dalar Dawnweaver sends you to slay their corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, and carry his head to the Sepulcher. Dalar Dawnweaver learns from the Forsaken Darkstalkers that worgen have reached Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills. Their feral sorcery spread from Shadowfang Keep, where Archmage Arugal unleashed dark enchantments across the forest. Ore from the mine is needed to arm the Undercity. But worgen now make their lair in its shafts, and the mine lies unusable. Grimson the Pale leads the worgen through the mine's infested shafts. Dalar Dawnweaver orders you to slay the corrupted foreman and bring his head to the Sepulcher. With Grimson gone, the worgen will lose their leader, and Forsaken laborers can claim the mine for Lord Varimathras.

quest:425.text: Ivar the Foul. At the Ivar Patch in northern Silverpine, Rane is guarding her badly mauled brother while Ivar the Foul prowls nearby. She asks Horde travelers to kill the savage ghoul so Quinn can recover and they can finish their report to High Executor Hadrec. In northern Silverpine Forest, Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were sent to survey the forest for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their work ended in violence at a farmstead, where Ivar the Foul ambushed them. Rane and Quinn escaped, but Quinn was badly mauled. An alchemical remedy made from forest beasts has helped, though he is still too weak to travel. Ivar prowls the nearby barn, waiting for Rane's guard to fail. She asks Horde travelers to enter and kill him, so the homestead can be secured.

quest:426.text: The Mills Overrun. The Scourge mass at Agamand Mills in Tirisfal, close to Forsaken settlements. Deathguard Dillinger sends soldiers from Brill to break their ranks before the ruined mills become a base for attacks deeper into the glades. The Agamand Mills once anchored Tirisfal Glades' agriculture. Since the Third War, Scourge forces have gathered beneath their windmills, held in thrall by the Lich King. These mindless undead threaten the young Forsaken holdings. If they seize the mills, they will have a base for attacks deeper into Tirisfal and against its settlements. Deathguard Dillinger helps fortify Brill and patrols the territory. He sends recruits after Rattlecage and Cracked Skull Soldiers, along with Darkeye Bonecasters. Dillinger asks for notched ribs and blackened skulls as proof that the skeletal ranks have broken and been driven back toward the Plaguelands before their offensive begins.

quest:427.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand sends you against the Scarlet Crusade. Executor Arren has recovered intelligence, and your first target is Scarlet Warriors at a tower west of Solliden Farmstead. The strike begins the Forsaken campaign to drive the crusaders from their borders. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken face threats on several fronts. The Deathguard watches the Lich King's growing armies, while the Scarlet Crusade challenges Forsaken rule over their former homeland. The Crusade calls all undead abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Its zealots do not see that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge's control. At Deathknell, Executor Arren secured documents showing where Scarlet encampments and outposts lie across Tirisfal Glades. The Deathguard is busy containing the Scourge, so independent Forsaken champions strike the zealots directly. Their first target is a guard tower west of Solliden Farmstead. Scarlet Warriors gather there and threaten the western approaches to Brill.

quest:428.text: Lost Deathstalkers. In northern Silverpine, two Forsaken scouts have been missing for weeks. High Executor Hadrec sent Rane and Quinn Yorick to watch the abandoned farms, and now you seek word of them. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec has heard nothing from Rane and Quinn Yorick for weeks. He sent the pair into northern Silverpine Forest to watch the abandoned farms and track enemy movements. Deathstalkers are the Forsaken’s hidden scouts and killers. They serve Lady Sylvanas, and Hadrec fears the Scourge or another threat has cut them down. Northern Silverpine lies between Lordaeron’s ruined estates and the shadowed borders of Tirisfal Glades. Undead roam there, beasts prowl, and feral worgen make travel perilous even for seasoned rogues. Search the decaying farmsteads where Rane and Quinn Yorick began their survey. Any intelligence they gathered may be vital, if danger has not overtaken them first.

quest:429.text: Wild Hearts. In Silverpine, Rane Yorick seeks help while her brother Quinn lies badly wounded. She needs discolored worg hearts for Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher, whose alchemy may help Quinn recover. Rane Yorick stays beside her brother Quinn, badly wounded after the Deathstalkers' disastrous mission left them pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul mauled him, and he is failing to recover. Ordinary rest cannot mend an undead body torn by such savagery. So Rane turns to the Royal Apothecary Society and its grim arts for a way to put her brother back together. Silverpine's worgs carry the corruption spreading through northern Lordaeron. Their hearts are discolored and hold potent essences. The Royal Apothecaries can distill these blighted organs into concoctions that restore withered Forsaken flesh.

quest:430.text: Return to Quinn. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick waits for a draught that may let him travel again. Apothecary Renferrel sends you from the Sepulcher with the mixture, while Quinn remains wounded in dangerous country. After you gather wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel brews a restorative draught for Quinn Yorick at the Sepulcher. He hands it to you, then returns to his secret alchemical research. You carry the mixture back into the wilderness. At the ruined Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick shelters beside his sister, Deathstalker Rane Yorick. The ghoul Ivar the Foul wounded him so badly he cannot cross hostile ground. Quinn drinks the draught as soon as you arrive. It restores enough strength for him to travel in time, though danger still surrounds the farmstead and Ivar lurks nearby.

quest:431.text: Candles of Beckoning. In Tirisfal Glades, candles from Gunther's island are bound for a grim test. Gunther Arcanus keeps them for a trial of allegiance. Gunther asks you to carry a candle from the crate on Gunther's Retreat to the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast. Light it there, and Lillith Nefara, the Scourge agent, will face you. On Gunther's Retreat, the island in Brightwater Lake where Gunther Arcanus dwells, a crate holds the candles. For his test in Proving Allegiance, one candle is enough. Lit on the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast, it awakens Lillith Nefara, the Scourge agent.

quest:432.text: Those Blasted Troggs!. In Gol'Bolar Quarry, troggs wreck the workings while Foreman Stonebrow calls for help. They have broken his equipment and powder barrels. His fading aim keeps him from fighting them himself, so he asks willing fighters to thin the Skullthumpers. Troggs have overrun the lower terraces of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. They broke through the bedrock and flooded the tunnels, ending the dwarven excavation's productive days. Now they smash scaffolding and blow apart powder barrels, leaving the quarry in ruin. From the ridge, Foreman Stonebrow watches his life's work crumble. Age has weakened his hands and spoiled his aim, so he relies on passing wanderers and Alliance recruits to fight in his place. He wants the burly Rockjaw Skullthumpers thinned. Only their complete destruction would satisfy his anger.

quest:433.text: The Public Servant. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow calls for aid against troggs that have halted mining in Dun Morogh. He wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers driven out so miners can return to work. Mehr Stonehallow serves in Ironforge's Senate and belongs to the Explorers' League. He has come to Gol'Bolar Quarry to direct the response himself. There, he hires travelers and mercenaries to drive the invaders from the mine. Deep digging at Gol'Bolar Quarry broke into sealed hollows underground. Rockjaw troggs poured into the pits, smashed mining equipment, and drove out the workers. Stonehallow wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers cleared away so Mountaineers can secure the quarry and mining can resume.

quest:435.text: Escorting Erland. In Silverpine, Deathstalker Erland is trying to reach his partner, Rane Yorick. Wolves have trapped him in a shelter, and the way to Rane crosses their hunting ground. Deathstalker Erland is trapped in a shelter by hungry wolves. Even a seasoned Forsaken scout can be overcome by Silverpine's wilds. Wolves circle the ruined refuge, drawn to the little flesh left on Erland's withered frame. Alone, he cannot break through their pack. Deathstalker Erland needs to reach his partner, Rane Yorick, near the Ivar Patch. Wolves prowl the ground between them. Once you guide Erland past the pack, he runs the last stretch to Rane Yorick's outpost. There, the scouts can bring their intelligence together for the Undercity.

quest:436.text: Ironband's Excavation. Jern Hornhelm has sent you from Thelsamar to find out why Ironband's Excavation is making so little progress. Supplies reach Prospector Ironband's team, and Jern trusts his diligence, but the work remains slow. Jern Hornhelm watches from Thelsamar as provisions and tools cross Loch Modan to the Explorers' League. They arrive steadily, yet the dig makes little progress. Jern suspects something is disrupting the work. He needs you to find out what is holding the team back.

quest:437.text: The Dead Fields. In northern Silverpine, Forsaken forces face a Scourge threat at the Dead Fields. High Executor Hadrec sends champions from the Sepulcher against the Rot Hide gnolls and the banshee who shields them. North of the Sepulcher, Rot Hide gnolls overrun an abandoned farmstead. Ordinary farms once stood in these fields. Now plague-ridden scavengers infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec sent small raiding parties to drive them out, but each attack stalled against a strange magical resistance. Nightlash, a Scourge banshee, directs the Rot Hide gnolls. When the gnolls face defeat, she scatters Forsaken skirmishers with dark sorcery. Hadrec sends Horde champions to cut down the gnolls and draw Nightlash into the open. He asks for her spectral essence as proof of her destruction.

quest:438.text: The Decrepit Ferry. At the Decrepit Ferry, the Scourge gathers along Lordamere Lake’s shore. High Executor Hadrec sends Forsaken champions east to learn what draws them there. After the Scourge presence in the Dead Fields is suppressed, High Executor Hadrec turns his attention east. The Decrepit Ferry lies among Silverpine Forest’s eastern waterways, where mainland Lordaeron once connected to the island estates of Lordamere Lake. Now undead gather around its rotted piers. Hadrec sends scouts to discover what draws the Lich King’s servants there.

quest:439.text: Rot Hide Clues. At Lordamere Lake, Rot Hide Clues come to light with an engraved ring on a recently deceased woman's hand. When you report the grim find to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher, he sees that Rot Hide gnolls are taking bodies from Tirisfal's mass graves and carrying them to Fenris Isle. Forsaken scouts find a ferry laden with corpses on the shore of Lordamere Lake. Among the dead is the unwrapped, plague-marked hand of a recently slain woman. A plain band on it bears the words “For Deliah.” The ferry points to an organized effort to move the dead, not scavengers feeding at random.

quest:440.text: The Engraved Ring. High Executor Hadrec sends you across the border to Brill with a ring bearing Deliah's name. Magistrate Sevren searches the town records to learn who she was and where the ring came from. Scouts searching for the Rot Hide gnolls in northern Silverpine Forest found Deliah's ring. Magistrate Sevren keeps Tirisfal's civic records and burial registers, though Hadrec doubts any Forsaken still cares for such keepsakes.

quest:441.text: Raleigh and the Undercity. In Brill and the Undercity, a ring draws Raleigh into an old tragedy. Magistrate Sevren sends you to return Deliah's ring to her widowed husband, found after her stolen corpse was bound for Fenris Isle. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren has pieced together clues about a stolen corpse and an engraved ring. The ring belonged to Deliah, and Sevren hopes to learn where it came from and return it to her family. He sends you into the Undercity to find Raleigh, Deliah's surviving husband.

quest:443.text: Rot Hide Ichor. In Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec seeks Rot Hide Ichor before the Forsaken attack Fenris Isle. He wants the fluid studied to understand the gnolls infesting the island. Rot Hide gnolls on Fenris Isle decay and fight with a fury unlike ordinary wild humanoids. They hold strategic ground across Lordamere Lake. High Executor Hadrec believes the strange fluid in their veins may explain their unnatural resilience. He needs samples before the Forsaken commit soldiers to a costly assault. The Royal Apothecary Society works from the Sepulcher, where Apothecary Renferrel studies biological and chemical anomalies. Bring him samples of the putrid fluid. The Forsaken hope to learn where the gnolls came from, who is engineering them, and what weaknesses they have in battle.

quest:444.text: Rot Hide Origins. In Silverpine Forest, the Rot Hides carry a magic Renferrel cannot explain by alchemy alone. He sends a sample to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, where arcane knowledge may reveal its origin. Apothecary Renferrel has reduced fluid from the Rot Hides of Silverpine Forest to its basic elements. His first tests show the ichor bears both necromancy and warlock magic. Alchemy cannot explain the sorcery behind it, so he prepares a sample for an expert in the Undercity.

quest:445.text: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. You carry Apothecary Johaan’s findings from Brill to Renferrel at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. The Royal Apothecary Society needs them for its work on the New Plague. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner commands the Royal Apothecary Society, which seeks a New Plague that can wipe out the living and the Scourge. Its laboratories lie across Forsaken territory, so researchers share their findings to keep the work moving. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results for other field researchers. You carry them south to Renferrel at the Sepulcher. Silverpine Forest is the next frontier of Forsaken expansion and research. Apothecary Renferrel works from the Sepulcher, overseeing biochemical tests amid threats from Moonrage worgen, rogue humans, and the lingering Scourge. He receives Johaan’s notes from Tirisfal Glades and adds their alchemical findings to his own experiments, advancing the Society’s design.

quest:446.text: Thule Ravenclaw. At the Undercity, a courier brings Bethor Iceshard strange Rot Hide ichor. Bethor recognizes the work of Thule Ravenclaw, his traitorous former colleague, and prepares counter-incantations to help the Forsaken resist the gnolls. Bethor Iceshard studies the courier’s sample in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter and finds an arcane mark. Thule Ravenclaw made the distillation. Before the Third War, Thule was a bright young mage and Bethor’s colleague. When the Lich King rose to power, Thule betrayed his peers and swore himself to the Scourge. As Lordaeron fell, he abandoned his humanity.

quest:447.text:
A Recipe For Death. In Silverpine, A Recipe For Death gathers reagents for the Forsaken's New Plague. From the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel sends bear hearts and spider blood to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. In Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel sees two foes closing on Sylvanas's people. Arthas's legions press them, while remnants of humanity remain enemies. The Forsaken have little hope in conventional warfare. They seek a New Plague that can rot living humans and undead Scourge alike.

Renferrel's field research found a virulent foundation for the plague. Arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark, joined with toxins in the hearts of native bears, forms that base. Bear hearts and spider blood gathered in Silverpine's wilderness travel beneath Lordaeron's ruins to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the Royal Apothecary Society's design.

Faranell takes Renferrel's samples to test their contaminable properties and refine formulas. The work may secure Forsaken supremacy across the continent.

quest:448.text: Report to Hadrec. In Silverpine, Renferrel sends you to Hadrec as the Scourge threat grows. Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have investigated the Scourge presence in Lake Lordamere, and High Executor Hadrec now directs preparations against Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have studied the danger posed by Thule Ravenclaw, a renegade necromancer. Yet study alone cannot break the Scourge stronghold rising on Fenris Isle. Ravenclaw binds the restless dead there, and Renferrel sees that alchemy and magic will not be enough. The Forsaken military must bring its steel and discipline to bear, so Renferrel sends you to its commander. High Executor Hadrec directs Silverpine Forest's strategic operations for the Dark Lady from the Sepulcher's crypts. Bethor's warnings about Ravenclaw reach him, and Hadrec knows a necromancer entrenched on Lordamere's western shore threatens Undercity's flank. He opens the local garrison's armory to equip the vanguard before sending them against the island fortress.

quest:449.text:
The Deathstalkers' Report. Near the northern wilds, the Deathstalkers have found Scourge forces where the Forsaken did not expect them. You carry their report from the wounded scouts to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher, bringing word that Silverpine Forest holds a greater threat than command believed. The Deathstalkers scout ahead for the Dark Lady, slipping into wild country before the main forces. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, one patrol met fierce resistance while tracking enemy movements.

Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his wounds, while Erland fought his way to safety. Their patrol still gathered intelligence the Forsaken need to hold Silverpine Forest. High Executor Hadrec reads the sealed report and learns that the Scourge hold a stronger presence in Silverpine than Undercity strategists expected. Their forces are more active and aggressive than command believed.

The Forsaken had planned to secure abandoned human hamlets and drive off rogue beasts. Now the Sepulcher's command must prepare for organized Scourge opposition as it fights to claim the region.

quest:4495.text: A Good Friend. At Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine grows anxious when Iverron misses his daily visit. She asks travelers to search the hills near Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Beneath Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine waits for Iverron, her friend who visits every day. Hours pass, and he does not come. So she asks travelers bound for Shadowglen to look for him. Iverron often wanders the hills in northern Shadowglen, close to the webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. The spiders make those slopes dangerous for travelers. Search west of the cave entrance, where Iverron is hiding and needs help.

quest:45.text: Discover Rolf's Fate. Guard Thomas waits for news of Rolf and Malakai, missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks point toward a murloc village. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints mark the mud and lead east along the water's edge. They run straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

quest:450.text: A Recipe For Death. From the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell sends you to Pyrewood Village in A Recipe For Death. You seek Apothecary Berard's notes on the ancient blight that wiped out Lake Lordamere's aquatic life. Apothecary Berard once stood among the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising researchers. He worked in Pyrewood Village, studying past ecological disasters for the Forsaken's alchemical pursuits. Then Archmage Arugal unleashed shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, and Berard fell under its curse. His mind gave way, binding him as a servant to the mage.

quest:451.text: A Recipe For Death. Across Lake Lordamere, Apothecary Renferrel sends you to gather rare reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. Berard's journal describes mosses and a strange tumor, bound for Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity and his work on a New Plague. Apothecary Berard's death under Arugal's curse cost the Royal Apothecary Society a skilled researcher. His field journal survived, preserving what he learned about blighted life in Silverpine Forest and Lake Lordamere. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel studied the recovered notes and found Berard's account of promising properties in local freshwater organisms. Now Renferrel asks you to carry forward the work his colleague began. Berard's reagents lie among the Dawning Isles, mist-shrouded islands in the eastern waters of Lake Lordamere. Lake skulkers and lake creepers on the isles carry peculiar moss strains that live in tainted water. Berard also noted a hardened tumor among the fierce Vile Fin murloc tribes that nest along the islets and the lake's southern shoreline near Ambermill.

quest:4512.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle seeks ooze samples from Felwood for his studies. He hopes to learn why the Royal Apothecary Society gathers them and what interests the Undercity's alchemists. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes with the Explorers' League. Most of its scholars seek titan relics or dwarven genealogies, but these living puddles resist ordinary classification. They appear in wetlands, cursed woods, and damp ruins. Laris has seen Forsaken apothecaries collecting slime across Lordaeron, and wants to know what draws them to it. Laris believes oozes may be primordial secretions tied to Azeroth's creation. He thinks they are neither vermin nor magical byproducts. To test his theory, you travel across the ocean to Felwood's blighted canopy. There, you gather Cursed and Tainted Oozes in specially made jars. For Laris and many displaced gnomes, these studies carry personal weight. Since Gnomeregan fell to troggs and radiation, thousands have taken refuge in Ironforge's Great Forge. A discovery for the Explorers' League could answer dwarven skeptics. It could show that welcoming gnomes into the mountain city has become an enduring asset to Alliance science.

quest:4513.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Laris Geardawdle seeks pure oozes across Kalimdor. His Felwood-tainted samples showed that oozes absorb and reflect their surroundings. Clean specimens may show him how they adapt to the places they inhabit. Laris Geardawdle needs clean samples for his study. The tainted ones showed how oozes take on the traits of their surroundings, but left him without a clear comparison. He seeks samples untouched by demonic taint or urban filth, so he can study ooze life on its own.

quest:452.text: Pyrewood Ambush. In Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia waits while Arugal's council keeps the afflicted in line. The Forsaken aim to break his hold on the town and weaken his position in Shadowfang Keep. Deathstalker Faerleia waits in Pyrewood Village's town hall for the local leaders. Archmage Arugal tends his dark sorceries in Shadowfang Keep, leaving the Pyrewood Council to keep order among the afflicted villagers. Faerleia plans to ambush the council. Without its mediation, the Forsaken hope the worgen in the woods and village streets will break free of Arugal's control.

quest:454.text: After the Ambush. Miran needs an escort to carry blasting powder to Loch Modan’s southern excavation site. Dark Iron dwarves ambushed the supply run, and the road is still dangerous. Saean and his conspirators attacked the supply run. Barrels were scattered, and the road became perilous. Huldar remains behind to guard the powder left there. Miran prepares to move ahead with the next load, so the supply line is split. The southern excavation site needs blasting powder to break stone and uncover titan relics. Miran fears another ambush from the ridges. He seeks a companion before loading his cargo and setting out past any traps the Dark Irons may have prepared.

quest:456.text: The Balance of Nature. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine calls newly awakened night elves to tend Teldrassil’s wildlife. Young nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too numerous, and keeping nature in balance calls for stewardship and difficult choices. Heavy spring rains have disturbed Teldrassil’s young and fragile forest cycle in Shadowglen, beneath the Great Tree’s boughs. Some wildlife populations have grown beyond what the land can sustain. They threaten to strip the glen of resources and bring famine to the ecosystem. Preserving the forest calls for active care. Conservator Ilthalaine watches over Shadowglen’s woods so no part overtakes the others. To prevent mass starvation among the animals, he sends young night elves into the grove to thin thistle boars and predatory nightsabers. The work is unglamorous but vital. Kaldorei stewardship seeks harmony with nature through active balance and difficult decisions.

quest:457.text: The Balance of Nature. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance. Adult animals now threaten Shadowglen and the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game. North of Aldrassil, younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars rooting through the soil. For kaldorei, controlled hunting is a grim duty. It protects the whole forest from collapse.

quest:458.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm hears troubling whispers from the forest spirits. He asks you to seek Tarindrella, whose return to Teldrassil after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands hints that something is wrong. Beneath Aldrassil’s boughs, Melithar Staghelm trains novices and listens to troubling omens from the woodland spirits. Tarindrella, a dryad known as a protector of the wild, has returned to Shadowglen after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands. Dryads rarely come without cause, so Melithar fears the natural order has fallen out of balance.

quest:459.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the forest’s unrest and the furbolgs’ disappearance. Grells have grown aggressive, and Fel Moss points to dark magic in Teldrassil’s boughs. Shadowglen’s quiet woods have grown hostile. The furbolgs have left their ancestral dens and gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Feral grells and grellkin overrun the woodland paths, and Tarindrella sees the dark change spreading through Teldrassil. Tarindrella suspects corruption is stirring the forest’s creatures. You slay the grells and bring her samples of Fel Moss, proof of dark enchantments clinging to Teldrassil’s boughs. With the corruption confirmed, she sends young defenders to Dolanaar to speak with Druid Athridas Bearmantle.

quest:46.text: Bounty on Murlocs. In eastern Elwynn, murlocs are spreading, and the Stormwind Army has set a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a small nuisance now threatens eastern Elwynn, though the western roads remain comparatively secure. Guard Thomas is stationed at the eastern bridge beside the Redridge Mountains. Dangers beyond the bridge and disorder at home both call for his attention. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and bureaucracy weighs on Stormwind's military command. Town garrisons rarely receive the reinforcements they request. So Marshal Dughan and local officers offer public bounties, paying coin for murloc fins to slow the attacks along the waterways.

quest:460.text: Resting in Pieces. On Fenris Isle, Alaric's severed head calls for help from beyond the grave. He asks you to carry it across Fenris Keep to an unmarked grave near the stables, where his body lies. At Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest, Alaric served Thule Ravenclaw as chief servant and personal bodyguard. Thule was a powerful mage aligned with the Scourge. When the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, he promised his sorcery would shield Alaric. Instead, the ward trapped him in endless agony and undeath, while his awareness remained in his severed parts. Thule made the rot hide gnolls by infecting local packs with necromantic decay. Then he turned on his own bodyguard. He cut off Alaric's head and threw it to the savage gnolls as a diversion. The rot hides dragged Alaric's body to a shallow grave they had hastily dug outside the keep's stables. They kept his speaking head as a grim plaything until an outsider intervened.

quest:461.text: The Hidden Niche. In Fenris Keep, Alaric's memories guide you toward a hidden alcove. His remains point to a place of rest, and an old relic waits there. Alaric remembers Fenris Keep in its better days. Horde scouts lifted his bones from a shallow grave outside the stronghold, but he will not go quietly to the Sepulcher. He offers vital knowledge in return: a hidden niche in the keep's southwestern tower holds an item treasured by Thule Ravenclaw and his fellow mages.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks the cause of the strandings and deaths. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, leaving the night elves of Auberdine puzzled. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature on the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. Those remains will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

quest:47.text: Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet. Travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a sharp eye for profit. He repeats his words, and instead of hiring mining crews to dig raw minerals, he offers coin to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn for gold dust taken from kobolds in the region. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These rat-like tunnelers chip through the dark for candles and shiny baubles, gathering flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Driving them back serves the kingdom. Their gold dust also turns the work into a trade for coin.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore, a Beached Sea Turtle lies among the surf as murlocs scavenge its remains. Auberdine naturalists seek sound samples to send to Darnassus for study. Dead sea turtles drift ashore along Darkshore’s coast, or beach themselves in confusion. Their remains soon draw scavengers. Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame and carve away its flesh and shell. Yet bone, shell, or tissue may remain intact in the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde works in Auberdine as a field researcher, recording unusual marine life and disturbances along the coast. Night elves regard stranded beasts with reverence and scientific curiosity. Suitable remains are cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus. They seek to learn why so many giants of the open sea wash ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded as murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants wash ashore. Along Mist's Edge, enormous thresher remains have joined the shipwrecks and debris washed in by the tide. The beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows. Its size suggests it came from beyond the Veiled Sea, from waters far from the calm waters here. Murlocs swarm over the corpse, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down such a creature. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde coordinates the salvage of bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded sea giants. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope the remains will show whether illness, disturbances in the deep sea, or arcane corruption drives the giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4725.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, a broken carriage rests on the shell of a Beached Sea Turtle. Greymist murlocs gather around the great carcass. You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle carried a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach. Now the carriage lies abandoned in the tide. Greymist murlocs swarm the turtle's remains. They have made a den among the rotting meat and scavenged timber. A marked container lies among their refuse and the broken carriage frame. The turtle's former masters left it there.

quest:4727.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, a Beached Sea Turtle lies untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample goes to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge food washed up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s bones lie mostly untouched. Those who study the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoid it for some unknown reason. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples from beached sea turtles for the Temple of the Moon. The night elf priestesses study disturbances in Darkshore’s waters. Skeletal fragments may help them learn whether sickness, magic, or dangerous sea predators are killing the ancient creatures.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and travelers. On Darkshore's sand lies a giant sea mammal, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark where an orderly study began. The researchers left before they could finish. Dwarven field researchers from the Explorer's League were studying the carcass in Darkshore. Their work stopped when local murlocs swarmed the site to scavenge. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde acts for the Temple of the Moon. She accepts salvaged bone samples to help study the unnatural wash-ups along the coast.

quest:4730.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore.
