Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde says these gentle mammals live in the waters around Teldrassil's base. Unlike aggressive threshers, they have never been known to drive themselves onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is gathering bone samples to learn what corruption or threat drives them from the deep.

quest:4731.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards cling to its broad shell. It was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, not stranded by sickness or confusion. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, where scavengers feed on the remains.

quest:4732.text:
Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore, Beached Sea Turtle remains wash ashore in growing numbers. Their bones give Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine specimens to study as Kalimdor's marine life dwindles. Great sea creatures and turtles lie along Darkshore's shore. Many ancient turtles drift onto the shoals or crawl onto the sand to die. Greymist murlocs gather at the carcasses and strip away the flesh. Soon, only shell and bone remain, beside crude camps they make there. Before the Third War, sea turtles thrived in the sacred waters around Mount Hyjal and the roots of Nordrassil, the World Tree. After Nordrassil's sacrifice against the Burning Legion and Teldrassil's planting off Kalimdor's northern shore, their numbers collapsed.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde and other priestesses of Elune study the remains for the Temple of the Moon. They seek to learn whether dark magic, changing seas, or the loss of the turtles' ancient sanctuary drives them to their deaths.

quest:4733.text: Beached Sea Creature. A colossal thresher lies stranded on Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore. Its death and stranding deepen the sea troubles worrying the night elves. Along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, driftwood and sea debris wash into the inlets. In one, you find the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun to pick it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs the ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant does not belong in these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or a deeper disturbance may lie in the Veiled Sea.

quest:4740.text: WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine's council wants Murkdeep dead for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. Find the Greymist chieftain south along the coast. Greymist murlocs are usually a nuisance along Darkshore. Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine, and the wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on their leader. Murkdeep lurks off the southern coast near murloc huts clustered around a bonfire. Trespassers face an organized defense as Greymist coastrunners and shore-crawlers surge from the surf to protect their settlement. Then Murkdeep emerges with his vanguard to strike the intruders. Proof of Murkdeep's death answers the Sentinels' grim need. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea handles the council's bounty payout. With Greymist leadership broken, travelers and ships on Darkshore's foggy coast gain a reprieve from sabotage.

quest:475.text: A Troubling Breeze. Athridas Bearmantle awaits word from Starbreeze Village, where reports have gone silent. In the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren watches the sleeping Druids of the Talon, and his silence points to danger in Teldrassil. Athridas Bearmantle relies on regular word from Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden who watches over the Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The druids sleep there to keep their sacred pact with Ysera in the Emerald Dream. Their sanctuary guards the spiritual balance of the young World Tree. Now reports from the east have ceased, and unease spreads through the forest.

quest:476.text:
Gnarlpine Corruption. Near Starbreeze Village, Gnarlpine Corruption threatens Teldrassil. Wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren sends word to Dolanaar. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the village and fallen to demonic corruption. Their violence may reach the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Near the ruins of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded. His former allies, the Gnarlpine furbolgs, ambushed him. Once peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, they have turned feral.

Too badly hurt to carry warning himself, Gaerolas sends you to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar. He fears the madness will spread farther through Teldrassil.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver hears that the Blackwood furbolgs have grown hostile. Terenthis sends you with news of their growing aggression, and Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. You bring Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine after scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore. Terenthis stays in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris watches over daily life and weighs the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leaders proof that the furbolgs’ troubles reach beyond territory: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them. Thundris has heard that the forest dwellers near Auberdine have grown hostile. Yet the furbolgs are not his only concern. Corruption spreads through Darkshore’s soil, plants, and waters. Thundris believes the land cannot heal until someone finds the source of the blight. So he turns to the waterways and calls on capable allies to trace the taint upstream.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. Foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver sends Alliance investigators to collect a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. From the eastern highlands, the Cliffspring River runs to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Now its waters carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies. So he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:4763.text: The Blackwood Corrupted. In northern Darkshore, the Blackwood Corrupted are caught in a dark influence. Evidence in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River leads Thundris Windweaver to send you against it. You gather their food and purify it with moonwell water, drawing the demonic handler into the open and breaking his hold on the northern camp. In Auberdine, the night elves have long wondered why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned on their neighbors. Their search along Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion manipulate the tribe with fel magic. Insidious talismans twist the furbolgs' minds and drive them into feral aggression.

quest:477.text: Border Crossings. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends you after Dalaran's supplies and the reason the Kirin Tor support Ambermill. Their crates pass through Silverpine Forest on the way to a Dalaran camp near Pyrewood Village. Wagons bring Dalaran's supplies and arcane goods from the Hillsbrad Foothills through Silverpine Forest. They serve the outposts and staging grounds along the way. Just north of Pyrewood Village, a camp holds Dalaran personnel who watch the road. Ambermill is the main human stronghold still standing in eastern Silverpine, and Dalaran continues to support it. Shadow Priest Allister and the Forsaken leaders at the Sepulcher want to know why Dalaran gives Ambermill so much support. They suspect the Kirin Tor would not risk lives and supplies deep in Forsaken territory for a provincial town alone. Some greater strategic or magical purpose may be behind it. Intercepting the crates could show the Forsaken what Dalaran is sending west.

quest:478.text: Maps and Runes. In Silverpine, maps and runes reveal Dalaran's interest in Ambermill. Horde agents recover a hidden crate for Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher. Horde agents find a Dalaran crate hidden along the border routes near Ambermill. Detailed regional charts and a rune-inscribed pendant lie inside. Human sentries stand nearby, so the scouts retrieve the artifact carefully. Dalaran's arcane reach lies close to their borders.

quest:479.text: Ambermill Investigations. At Ambermill, Dalaran wizards weave magic that threatens the Forsaken’s hold on Silverpine Forest. From the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends agents to disrupt their work and seize the magical foci. Ambermill lies in the eastern hills of Silverpine Forest. Its human residents are wizards and defenders pledged to the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. The mages weave powerful magic in a vast ritual. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister and his companion Dalar see the danger. If the Kirin Tor channel their power unchecked, the Forsaken risk losing Silverpine entirely. As Dalar scries the forest and traces the magic, Allister sends agents against the practitioners in Ambermill. Dalaran conjurers, mages, and their protectors wear enchanted pendants that focus and coordinate their arts. Take the talismans from slain sorcerers, and the ritual falters. This buys the Sepulcher time to find the ringleader directing the arcane weave.

quest:481.text: Dalar's Analysis. In Silverpine, Allister's report sends a Dalaran relic to Dalar for study. A rune-inscribed pendant taken from a supply crate reaches Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. The relic shows that Dalaran's surviving mages are gathering great magical power for a hidden purpose. A supply crate from Dalaran is raided at a camp north of Pyrewood Village. Beneath old maps, Shadow Priest Allister finds a rune-inscribed pendant. Its enchantment is beyond his spiritual knowledge, so he sends it to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. Dalar's skill as an arcane scholar makes him better suited to read Dalaran's magical warding.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks you to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know whether the crystal is real. Moonkin were once gentle, mystical creatures bound to Kalimdor's wilds. Now aggressive packs multiply along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as danger grows. Reports point to a single spot among the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers speak of an unnatural red crystal jutting from a rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Rumors travel easily along the fogbound coast, so Glynda wants you to see the place for yourself. The crystal is real. The Sentinels still need to learn why moonkin gather there and whether it threatens the land.

quest:4812.text: As Water Cascades. At Auberdine, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water will reveal what lies beneath Darkshore's red crystal. Sacred water may pierce its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water bears divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

quest:4813.text: The Fragments Within. At the eastern cliffs, you return to the red crystal with water from a moonwell. It may reveal what lies within, and you carry the finding back to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine. Back in Auberdine, you tell Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea what you found. The discovery gives the local night elf leaders more cause for concern, but no clear answers. Glynda will present the findings to the town council. The crystal rests high on the eastern cliffs, far enough from town to bring her some comfort; it poses no immediate danger.

quest:482.text:
Dalaran's Intentions. In Silverpine Forest, Dalar Dawnweaver sends Shadow Priest Allister a warning. A pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill reveals their plan to awaken a dormant ley energy node beneath the town. At the Sepulcher, the Forsaken prepare to answer. Dalar Dawnweaver studies a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate. It recalls an old Kirin Tor survey of Ambermill. The quiet village was chosen for a reason: it sits atop a dormant ley energy node. Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap its power.

Awakening such a nexus takes immense magical reserves. The enchanted pendants the wizards wear are key to channeling and catalyzing that power. The Forsaken cannot abide a fortified Kirin Tor outpost fueled by ley energy. It would threaten the southern approaches to the Sepulcher and Tirisfal Glades. Whatever ritual the magi prepare, raw ley energy would give Dalaran an enormous strategic advantage in Lordaeron.

So Dalar urgently sends word to Shadow Priest Allister. He asks Allister to devise a way to stall the wizards before their ritual is complete.

quest:483.text: The Relics of Wakening. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, danger closes around the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the sacred mounds, while the druids' spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Four ritual relics are needed to bring the sleepers safely back to the waking world. West of Dolanaar, corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the winding corridors of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Barrow dens are secluded sanctuaries where night elf druids hibernate while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. A foul taint spreading across Teldrassil has driven these former allies mad. The furbolgs have desecrated the sanctum, while the sleepers remain unaware that danger threatens their bodies. Athridas Bearmantle needs four sacred relics for the delicate ceremony that can safely awaken the Druids of the Talon. A druid's spirit needs an anchor when returning from the Dream. Without one, sudden awakening can shatter the mind or strand the spirit. The relics lie in chests across the den: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. They are the sleepers' only hope before the Gnarlpine butcher or abduct them.

quest:486.text: Ursal the Mauler. In Teldrassil, Athridas Bearmantle seeks to rouse the Druids of the Talon from an unnatural sleep. Their kin are trapped in the Barrow Den, and Ursal the Mauler's corruption must be broken. The Druids of the Talon went to the Barrow Den of Ban'ethil to sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream. Their peaceful trance became a prison, with no path back to waking. Athridas Bearmantle traced the trouble to the gnarlpine furbolgs and their vicious leader, Ursal the Mauler. Ursal meddled with the druids' sacred rite, leaving them caught between waking and the Dream. The Relics of Wakening alone cannot carry Athridas through the spiritual fog to the druids. The source of the interference must end. Ursal the Mauler lairs in Gnarlpine Hold, home to the tribe in far southwestern Teldrassil. Slaying the furbolg warlord breaks his hold on the sleepers' minds.

quest:487.text: The Road to Darnassus. Travelers on Teldrassil’s western road face attacks from corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs. Moon Priestess Amara coordinates scouts and travelers to keep the route from Dolanaar to Darnassus clear for trade and messages. You travel west from Dolanaar toward Darnassus on Teldrassil’s main road. Goods, political messages, and travelers pass this way each day, linking the capital with the boughs of the great tree. Teldrassil is young and wild, so its kaldorei communities depend on safe roads. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have been driven mad by a sickness in the boughs of the World Tree. They attack from dens beneath the ridges. Along the road, ambushers stalk the tree line and prey on couriers and travelers, making the passage through the forest deadly. Moon Priestess Amara watches over the road outside Dolanaar. She joins the spiritual authority of Elune’s priesthood with the Sentinels’ vigilance. Amara directs capable travelers to strike at ambushers near their dens below the road. The route to Darnassus’s gates depends on keeping them at bay.

quest:488.text: Zenn's Bidding. Zenn Foulhoof draws newcomers into his schemes north of the road from Shadowglen to Dolanaar. The solitary satyr asks them to gather animal parts, counting on their trust and inexperience. Travelers on the path from Shadowglen to Dolanaar may find Zenn Foulhoof beneath the Great Tree. He offers material rewards and secrets in return for simple work. From the surrounding woods, he asks for nightsaber fangs, strigid owl feathers, and webwood spider silk. Then he whispers that their bargain should stay between them.

quest:489.text: Seek Redemption!. In Dolanaar, the Council of the Forest demands that you make amends. Adventurers were tricked into doing Zenn Foulhoof's bidding, and the council now sends you to fool him into eating corrupted fel cones. Just outside Dolanaar, the solitary satyr Zenn Foulhoof tricks passersby into doing his bidding. Adventurers who unknowingly killed nightsabers, strigid owls, and webwood spiders to satisfy his twisted appetites have drawn the Council of the Forest's sharp disapproval. The council will not accept harm to nature, least of all from its own allies. Syral Bladeleaf, Sentinel Kyra Starsong, or Sentinel Shayla Nightbreeze warns you to make amends if you wish to remain welcome in Teldrassil. Dolanaar's guardians tell you to turn Foulhoof's wicked gluttony against him instead of meeting him with steel. Gather the billowing, corrupted fel cones from the forest floor, then offer the unsuspecting satyr a taste of his own foul medicine.

quest:491.text:
Wand to Bethor. At Fenris Keep, the Woven Wand is bound for Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Three apprentice mages made it as a sign of fellowship, but Thule Ravenclaw hid it after choosing the Scourge. Its return brings a piece of Bethor's mortal youth back to the Magic Quarter. Before Lordaeron fell, three young mages joined their training wands into one: the Woven Wand. It marked their friendship and their shared hopes in the magical arts.

Then Thule Ravenclaw gave his loyalty to the Lich King and embraced the Scourge. Their fellowship was broken. He came to despise the friendship they had shared, yet could neither destroy the wand nor leave it with his former companions.

quest:492.text: A New Plague. In Brill, A New Plague faces its first test on a captive dwarf. Apothecary Johaan sends you to the cellar of Gallows' End Tavern with the brew he made from reagents gathered across Tirisfal Glades. Apothecary Johaan has brought his research to a dangerous trial. The Royal Apothecary Society serves Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, seeking a plague that kills the living while leaving undead bodies unharmed. Johaan has brewed what he calls a “special drink.” He sends you to give it to an imprisoned enemy of the Forsaken. In Brill, the Deathguard keeps captives in a damp cellar beneath Gallows' End Tavern. They await interrogation or disposal. One prisoner is a Dwarven Mountaineer, an Ironforge scout caught trespassing in Tirisfal Glades. Defiant and thirsty, he eagerly accepts the drink, unaware of what Johaan mixed into it.

quest:5041.text: Supplies for the Crossroads. Thork needs supplies back at the Crossroads after Razormane quilboar raids. The stolen crates carry provisions the outpost needs as conflict spreads across the Barrens. Thork needs provisions returned to the Crossroads after a supply caravan is ambushed. The outpost links Horde travel, trade, and defense across the Barrens. Its cargo comes from Durotar and Mulgore. Without those goods, shortages of provisions, tools, and arms threaten daily life in the harsh wilderness. Razormane quilboar have taken the crates. These swine-beasts contest Horde control across central Kalimdor. They hauled the cargo to their thorn-bush camps and keep it there. Thork sends trusted warriors into Razormane territory to recover supplies for the Horde.

quest:5061.text: Aquatic Form. You bring the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion back to Darnassus. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting binds a druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. Young night elf druids endure trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade. There, Dendrite Starblaze gives them the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion. They carry this sacred token back to Teldrassil, proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits your return in the Cenarion Enclave. Your trials along the coasts of Darkshore and Westfall have tested your endurance and attunement. Present the completed pendant to show Bearwalker that your mind and body are ready to shed their mortal skin. Then you can take the swift, breathing form of the sea lion.

quest:52.text: Protect the Frontier. At Elwynn's eastern bridge, Guard Thomas asks you to thin the wolves and bears threatening travelers and workers near Eastvale Logging Camp. The beasts have grown bold, putting roads and logging crews at risk. Goldshire and Northshire Valley have visible Stormwind garrisons. The eastern frontier has far fewer guards. Guard Thomas watches the river crossing, one of the few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep the supply roads open. Eastvale Logging Camp sends timber to Stormwind City. Woodsmen cutting trees at the forest's edge face prowlers, gray forest wolves, and young forest bears near the roads and lumber yards. Culling the beasts eases the danger to local workers for a time. Thomas suspects something deeper in the woods is driving them toward settlements.

quest:5261.text: Eagan Peltskinner. Timber wolves threaten Northshire Valley, and Eagan Peltskinner has work for recruits outside the abbey. The local furrier needs hunters to thin the packs and bring back pelts. Deputy Willem often sends abbey recruits to find Eagan Peltskinner on the nearby grounds. Northshire Valley's orchards and fields meet wild woods where timber wolves prowl. Eagan asks newcomers to hunt the aggressive packs and gather pelts for his craft. Timber wolves threaten workers, acolytes, and supplies traveling to and from Northshire. Sending young champions to Eagan helps keep nearby paths safe and leaves Stormwind's few remaining guards free for other duties. Those guards are already occupied by rising tensions across Elwynn Forest.

quest:543.text: The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell sends mercenaries into the Ruins of Alterac for a lost heirloom. The Perenolde Tiara once adorned Alterac's royal family and now rests with an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara made by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. Alterac was conquered and collapsed. When Alterac City fell, many royal treasures vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage among the Crushridge ogres, holds the tiara in the ruins. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and return the jewel to his gallery.

quest:5481.text: Gordo's Task. Along the road to Brill, Gordo gathers plants for the Royal Apothecary Society. His clumsy hands make the work too fine, so he asks travelers to gather Gloom Weed for Junior Apothecary Holland. Between Deathknell and Brill, Gordo trudges through the countryside on the Royal Apothecary Society's behalf. Abominations can fight with brute strength and carry heavy loads, but their huge, stitched hands struggle with delicate work. Sent to gather ingredients in the meadows, Gordo crushes more stems than he plucks. So he turns to passersby, bullying or bribing them to do the careful work for him.

quest:5482.text: Doom Weed. In Brill, Junior Apothecary Holland seeks doom weed for his research. The plant grows by Tirisfal's northern mass graves, where Rot Hide gnolls prowl. Junior Apothecary Holland studies alchemy in Brill for the Royal Apothecary Society. He wants doom weed for his experiments, but Gordo cannot tell one plant from another. So Holland asks capable hands to gather what he needs. Doom weed grows around the mass gravesite just north of the Brill graveyard. Death and plague have tainted the soil there. Rot Hide gnolls prowl the burial mounds, scavenging among the remains and guarding the overgrown trenches.

quest:5502.text: A Warden of the Horde. In Orgrimmar, Grunth returns to Orphan Matron Battlewail as Children's Week ends. After seeing the world with you, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After your travels together, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He recalls his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. Now he asks to return home and tell the matron about your time together. You bring Grunth back to Orphan Matron Battlewail at the orphanage in the Valley of Honor. In the new Horde, caring for the young is a solemn duty, for war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail praises your compassion as the true measure of a Horde hero. Grunth gives you a beloved pet so you will remember the bond formed on your travels.

quest:5541.text: Ammo for Rumbleshot. Outside Anvilmar, Hegnar Rumbleshot needs ammunition for the riflemen at practice. A courier fled wendigo near the Grizzled Den and left a crate behind. Loslor Rudge at Steelgrill's Depot supplies tradesmen across Dun Morogh, though wildlife often disrupts his shipments. His courier had camped near the Grizzled Den cave system when local wendigo crossed his path. He fled for his life and left the heavy wooden crate in the snow. Hegnar Rumbleshot runs a gun shop beside the main road leading away from Anvilmar. Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar squads gather in the clearing outside his forge to sight their weapons and practice with live fire. Without regular deliveries of powder and lead from suppliers like Loslor, the riflemen's marksmanship practice soon comes to a halt.

quest:5545.text: A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen races to meet a timber shipment deadline for Stormwind. Wolves and bears have driven her woodcutters from the northern woods, leaving the cut bundles behind. Eastvale's timber rebuilds towns and strengthens bridges across the kingdom, yet this vital shipment has fallen behind. The delivery deadline is drawing near, and Supervisor Raelen has little time to spare. North of the camp, wolves and bears drove the woodcutters from the bundles they cut and tied. Raelen cannot wait for guards to clear the woods, so she asks you to bring the timber back before the contract is lost.

quest:5621.text: Garments of the Moon. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight sends a young priest to aid a wounded Sentinel south of town. The duty tests an initiate's devotion and earns formal recognition in the Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune guides kaldorei in worship and helps guard Teldrassil's borders. Sentinel Shaya was wounded while patrolling the wilds south of Dolanaar, and priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot leave her post to help. So she asks a newly trained initiate to tend Shaya's wounds and strengthen her with protective magic. After restoring Sentinel Shaya's vigor, you return to Dolanaar and receive formal robes of office from Laurna Morninglight. The robes mark an acolyte's passage from lessons to practical service that can save lives. For the kaldorei, aiding the Sentinels serves Elune and helps keep Teldrassil safe.

quest:5622.text: In Favor of Elune. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests set out for guidance and training in Dolanaar. Priestess Shanda sends them along the forest path to Laurna Morninglight. Priestess Shanda trains initiates who serve Elune in Aldrassil's secluded shelter. Under her eye, they begin with simple prayers and spells of defense. Yet Shadowglen's quiet life cannot prepare them for the turmoil beyond the glade. Once an initiate shows steady faith and discipline, Shanda sends them down the forest path to Dolanaar for further teaching. In Dolanaar, a young night elf takes an important step in the service of Elune. Priestess Laurna Morninglight prepares her disciples for the trials facing Teldrassil. There, an acolyte can learn more advanced moonlit spellcraft and receive formal vestments. Those robes mark their place in the Sisterhood of Elune.

quest:5623.text: In Favor of the Light. At Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta sends you south to continue your training in Goldshire. Priestess Josetta waits at the Lion's Pride Inn to guide your next steps in the Holy Light. Your training carries you beyond Northshire Abbey's cloistered halls and into the lives of Elwynn's people. You leave secluded study for active ministry, where the Holy Light must answer everyday needs beyond the abbey's walls. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Priestess Josetta tends to Goldshire's spiritual needs and guides rising acolytes. She builds on your lessons and teaches you to offer comfort, protect the faithful, and heal the injured. Under her guidance, you learn the duties of the Church's servants across the kingdom, including caring for a wounded guard and receiving ceremonial clerical vestments.

quest:5624.text: Garments of the Light. Priestess Josetta sends you east of Goldshire to Crystal Lake, where Guard Roberts lies wounded. His recovery matters to the town, and the Church of the Holy Light will recognize your service. Josetta asks you to put divine power to use before the Church recognizes a novice priest. Guard Roberts needs healing, giving you a chance to serve someone in need. Tending him is your first step toward formal standing in the Church of the Holy Light. Close Roberts's wounds with restorative prayers, then strengthen him with a blessing of fortitude. He needs healing and resilience to return to his duties. Your care helps a town guard withstand danger, and supports the township. Josetta expects a priest to sustain defenders as well as mend them. Once Roberts has been treated, return to the Lion’s Pride Inn for your first formal robes. They mark the approval and fellowship of Stormwind's priesthood, though further training does not require them. The Church recognizes you as a servant of the Holy Light.

quest:5625.text: Garments of the Light. At Maxan Anvol’s urging, you go south of Kharanos to help a wounded mountaineer before you receive the Garments of the Light. Maxan Anvol, the priest trainer, asks for practical aid before ceremony. Acolytes usually face formal trials to prove they deserve church vestments. But Mountaineer Dolf is wounded, and he needs help now. South of Kharanos, you find Mountaineer Dolf wounded in the line of duty. Restorative prayers mend his injuries. Power Word: Fortitude strengthens him and helps keep an Ironforge defender alive. Once Dolf has received aid, Maxan Anvol presents you with formal garments. The robes give warmth against Dun Morogh’s chill and mark you as a servant of the Light. You are ready to aid wounded wanderers and local guards.

quest:5626.text: In Favor of the Light. Branstock Khalder sends a young priest from Coldridge Valley through the mountain pass to Kharanos for further study. There, Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol prepares the novice for greater duties and a chance to earn their first formal vestments. You leave Anvilmar after showing dedication and understanding of Holy magic. Branstock Khalder sends promising novices beyond the mountains, where priests meet Dun Morogh’s needs and help defend its people. The Coldridge Pass tunnel opens into central Dun Morogh, where Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol guides you beyond basic prayers. He teaches that service to the Holy Light calls for moral character, physical hardiness, and an unyielding will. Prove your resolve under his guidance, and you may receive your first formal garments of office.

quest:5627.text:
Stars of Elune. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, night elf acolytes answer the Sisterhood of Elune's summons. Their devotion has earned them sacred instruction in their faith. Night elf priests draw their holy power from Elune, their goddess. Humans and dwarves turn to the Light. When an acolyte serves the realm with steadfast devotion, the Sisterhood in Darnassus takes notice. The acolyte is summoned to the Temple of the Moon and judged ready for deeper communion.

There, the priest learns sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship. Priestess Alathea calls the initiate to learn the holy mysteries of the night elf faith, including Starshards. These spells channel the radiant wrath and grace of the White Lady. The teaching carries an acolyte beyond basic training, ready to venture beyond Teldrassil's protective canopy in Elune's name.

quest:5628.text: Returning Home. In Goldshire, a novice night elf priest hears an urgent call from Darnassus. Priestess Josetta carries the message: return to the Temple of the Moon and continue training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are rare in Elwynn Forest, and a young acolyte among its human settlements draws attention. When you reach Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets you with news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking you, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon. Your calling now leads back to Kalimdor, where your training can advance. Darnassus looks to the Temple of the Moon for night elf faith and leadership. Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversee the Sisterhood’s instruction, keeping watch over disciples even when curiosity carries them overseas. When you return, the priestesses welcome you with motherly concern. Then they begin your deeper studies of the Moon Goddess’s celestial mysteries.

quest:5629.text: Returning Home. Young night elf priests are summoned to Darnassus in Returning Home. After serving in Teldrassil’s wilds, they are called to the Temple of the Moon to meet Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Around Dolanaar, priests tend the wounded and cleanse corruption. Their service draws the Sisterhood of Elune’s notice. Trainer Laurna Morninglight brings promising initiates word that Priestess Alathea has asked to meet them. Aid to local settlements matters, yet each devotee must also deepen their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the faith’s higher calling. From Teldrassil’s boughs, the road leads to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Elune’s gentle glow fills the sanctuary above the city. It is the kaldorei’s chief house of worship and spiritual capital. An invitation into its halls marks an initiate’s recognition by the priesthood’s leaders, no longer only a young student. Priestess Alathea warmly greets the returning initiates. She says she and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind take pride when initiates venture into the uncertain world and return unharmed. This homecoming opens deeper sacred trials under Alathea’s direct guidance.

quest:5630.text: Returning Home. In Dun Morogh, a summons calls night elf priests back to Darnassus. Maxan Anvol sends them to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon. In Kharanos, Maxan Anvol sees a night elf endure Dun Morogh's bitter cold, far from Teldrassil's serene forests. The dwarven priest trainer brings urgent news. A priestess of Elune passed through seeking you with orders from Darnassus. They call you back at once. Your road leads across the sea to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, beneath Teldrassil's sacred boughs. Priestess Alathea welcomes you back to the Sisterhood of Elune, relieved that you returned safely from foreign lands. She prepares your next rites of devotion, beginning with the Stars of Elune.

quest:5631.text: Returning Home. A summons brings a night elf priest from human lands back to Teldrassil. Brother Joshua carries Priestess Alathea’s call to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where the young priest will receive advanced guidance in Elune’s mysteries. Night elf priests sometimes travel to human lands like Stormwind to share fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light. Their strongest ties remain with the Sisterhood of Elune. Brother Joshua tells you that a night elf emissary has come searching for you. Your early travels are over, and your home temple calls you back for deeper training with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind’s inner circle. Across the sea, the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus welcomes you home. Priestess Alathea greets you warmly and celebrates your safe passage through a troubled world. Your return brings joy to Alathea and Tyrande. More demanding spiritual trials await.

quest:5632.text: Returning Home. Priestess Alathea calls promising night elf priests back to Darnassus. At the Temple of the Moon, the Sisterhood of Elune will recognize them and guide their next steps. A messenger from the Sisterhood finds you while you visit Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park. You have served your people abroad, and now the order's leaders call you back to Darnassus. They have watched your spiritual growth and summon you for an evaluation and a rite of recognition. This journey marks your passage from new initiate to active servant of the Mother Moon. The summons brings you to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon, Darnassus's highest sanctuary. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversees the Sisterhood, which watches over its members wherever they serve. Your safe return honors your community and Elune. It also shows how the goddess's grace has guided and preserved you through your early trials in the wild.

quest:5633.text: Returning Home. Night elf priests in Ironforge are being summoned back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. A Sisterhood emissary seeks acolytes abroad and sends them to Priestess Alathea for further training and sacred duties. In Ironforge, night elf priests remain bound to the Sisterhood of Elune, though Teldrassil lies far away. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, bears a message from a visiting night elf priestess. The emissary sought young disciples traveling abroad and said their mentors needed them back in the capital at once. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, returning acolytes report to Priestess Alathea. Beneath the gaze of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, Alathea welcomes her student and is relieved they crossed the seas safely. Their return begins further devotion and sacred duties, including the Stars of Elune.

quest:5634.text: Desperate Prayer. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches human acolytes a prayer for when their lives are in danger. It calls on the Holy Light to heal a priest's wounds when all else fails. Priests of the Cathedral of Light use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Even the devout may be isolated, cornered, or close to death. In that moment, an acolyte can call to the Holy Light for help, with their own life at stake. High Priestess Laurena guides the clergy in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and decides when an acolyte is ready for deeper teachings. Human initiates who show devotion to the Light across the kingdom receive this lesson as protection and as a charge to keep serving the realm.

quest:5635.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, promising priests from Elwynn Forest come for deeper training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they present themselves to High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while local mentors serve Elwynn Forest's outlying settlements. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches Stormwind's senior priesthood. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks a move to deeper duties in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. At the Cathedral, acolytes come before High Priestess Laurena, a senior leader of the Church in Stormwind. She oversees their spiritual grounding and practical training as newly elevated priests. Her instruction prepares them for the Alliance's harsh trials and teaches the Light's miracles, including Desperate Prayer, a plea for salvation known among human practitioners.

quest:5636.text: Desperate Prayer. In Dolanaar, word from home calls human priests back to Stormwind for further training. A fellow priest has crossed continents to summon them to the Cathedral of Light. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight brings you a message from home. A fellow priest has crossed continents to find you, so Laurna urges you to return without delay. She offers Elune’s blessing and good wishes for your faith as you leave Teldrassil. Your road leads across the Great Sea to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. High Priestess Laurena guides the Alliance faithful in their spiritual growth. She summons promising acolytes to deepen their devotion and learn Desperate Prayer, an emergency prayer that can save a life in its darkest hour.

quest:5637.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, High Priestess Laurena calls promising dwarven acolytes to the Cathedral of Light. There they deepen their service to the Light and take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh may outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith. Ironforge keeps its holy traditions in the Mystic Ward, while Stormwind's Church of the Holy Light welcomes humans and dwarves alike. Traveling south by Deeprun Tram brings dwarven acolytes into the wider church community. The journey strengthens the spiritual bond between the allied kingdoms.

quest:5638.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides maintain ties across their traditions. So when the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not alarm. At the Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, you report to High Priestess Laurena. One of Stormwind’s senior clerical leaders, she guides young acolytes beyond their first prayers. Laurena teaches the sacred invocation called Desperate Prayer, a personal plea for divine aid. Near death, a servant of the Light can use it to mend grievous wounds in an instant.

quest:5639.text: Desperate Prayer. High Priest Rohan sends you from Ironforge to Stormwind to learn healing and survival. There, High Priestess Laurena teaches dwarven acolytes the deeper mysteries of the Church. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Rohan guides dwarven initiates devoted to the Holy Light. Seeing your discipline and faith, he sends you southwest to Stormwind. Human and dwarven clerics share close spiritual ties, and the city's grand halls hold advanced teaching. You reach Stormwind by the Deeprun Tram and climb to Cathedral Square. In the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena tests you on the Church's behalf. She teaches the desperate prayers a priest calls upon in battle, seeking divine aid when strength fails and death draws near.

quest:5640.text: Desperate Prayer. In Darnassus, young human and dwarven priests seek guidance in another faith. Priestess Alathea teaches the ways of Elune and directs followers of the Holy Light to Stormwind, where High Priestess Laurena welcomes returning acolytes to the Cathedral of Light. Alliance priests follow different sacred paths. In Darnassus, the priesthood serves Elune and channels the moon goddess's radiance and wrath. Priestess Alathea honors Elune and respects the Holy Light. Yet she cannot teach another race the deeper prayers bound to a different devotion. Human and dwarven acolytes who seek those prayers must look elsewhere. Initiates of the Holy Light return home to learn its rites, including the prayer for divine aid in a moment of peril. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena guides returning priests beneath its marble arches.

quest:5648.text: Garments of Spirituality. In Razor Hill, new priests put their healing to the test in the field. They seek Grunt Kor'ja, wounded while fighting Kul Tiras survivors, and tend her injuries. Those who succeed earn ceremonial vestments and recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. South of Razor Hill, the Horde still fights remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Tai'jin, the troll priest trainer, tests new priests in the work of battle triage. She sends them to find Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior badly wounded while repelling human infiltrators. You tend her injuries and strengthen her before she succumbs. Healing Kor'ja proves a young priest is ready to serve the Horde's spiritual tradition. Tai'jin awards the Garments of Spirituality for saving a frontline defender. To orcs and Darkspear trolls alike, the robes mark their wearer as more than an apprentice of incantations. They can be trusted to keep Horde warriors alive in battle.

quest:5649.text:
In Favor of Spirituality. In the Valley of Trials, young Darkspear priests begin their lives beyond the training grounds. Under Ken'jai's direction, they travel to Tai'jin in Razor Hill and meet Durotar's wider challenges. Their path holds both ancestral troll ways and service in the Horde. Darkspear acolytes leave the Valley of Trials after learning their basic rites from Ken'jai. The road from those secluded grounds leads to Razor Hill, a crossroads settlement in Durotar. There, a young priest steps beyond survival drills and begins to shoulder the spiritual and cultural duties of the tribe. Ken'jai speaks plainly about the Darkspear's place in Thrall's Horde. The trolls value the orcs' loyalty and lessons of honor, though some ancestral traditions sit uneasily among their allies. So Darkspear spiritual leaders teach their pupils to preserve their heritage quietly while serving the Horde.

At Razor Hill, Tai'jin welcomes the acolytes. He guides them toward self-sufficiency and strength within the community.

quest:5650.text: Garments of Darkness. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl tests fledgling Forsaken priests before they enter deeper shadow. The trial asks whether they can heal and strengthen an injured Deathguard, for their calling demands more than afflicting enemies. Forsaken priests are known for shadow and darkness, yet Dark Cleric Beryl teaches that mastering darkness also means learning light and restoration. Those who seek only ruin are urged to study arcane magic instead. A priest must strengthen and preserve comrades as well as afflict enemies. North of Brill's cemetery, Deathguard Kel holds the line against prowling gnoll packs, though he has been wounded. Beryl sends you to bind Kel's wounds with healing spells and bolster his stamina with protective enchantments. By doing so, you show you can sustain Tirisfal Glades' defenders. Beryl grants you his vestment and welcomes you into the priesthood's higher mysteries.

quest:5651.text: In Favor of Darkness. Dark Cleric Duesten sends you from Deathknell to Brill for In Favor of Darkness. There, you continue training with Dark Cleric Beryl and study the Holy Light and Shadow. Dark Cleric Duesten teaches that corruption forged the Forsaken, then cast them aside like carrion. To survive, they must understand both Light and Shadow without sentiment. You leave Deathknell's graveyard and enter the wider world beyond its walls. You follow the road northeast from Deathknell, cross a wooden covered bridge, and reach ruined Brill. Dark Cleric Beryl waits in the upper quarters of the local inn to test your resolve. He prizes ambition and cold practicality over blind devotion. A Forsaken priest must wield divine power as a weapon and a tool, never as a moral crutch.

quest:5654.text: Hex of Weakness. From Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, Hex of Weakness marks a young Darkspear priest’s next step. Tai'jin sends an initiate north to Ur'kyo, who welcomes new students into the tribe’s spiritual circle and teaches the loa’s darker arts. Tai'jin watches over young Darkspear priests as they study in Razor Hill’s barracks. When an acolyte has mastered spiritual communion and shadow magic, those first lessons come to an end. Tai'jin sends the promising priest north across Durotar’s red dirt canyons to Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. There, elder practitioners teach the tribe’s wider magical traditions. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits, the Darkspear keep a sanctuary apart from the orcs’ forges and warrior grounds. Ur'kyo, an elder priest, welcomes new initiates there. Joining his circle means honoring the loa and learning the ancestral ways of the jungle trolls. It also means mastering potent curses and hexes that sap an enemy’s strength in battle.

quest:5713.text: One Shot. One Kill.. On the road to Auberdine, Sentinel Aynasha is ambushed and cannot carry her message onward. Poisoned by Marosh the Devious and his furbolg trackers, she must mix an antidote before she can travel. Sentinel Aynasha carries important communications toward Auberdine when hostile furbolgs intercept her on a trail in northern Kalimdor. Marosh the Devious leads them. Their venom leaves the scout unsteady and unable to continue on foot. Aynasha knows how to make natural remedies, but the antidote takes time to mix and take effect. Marosh's trackers are closing in, so she needs travelers to guard her as she works. Though her strength is failing, she keeps her bow steady and fires into the brush to hold the attackers back.

quest:5722.text: Searching for the Lost Satchel. Rahauro sends you from Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise into Ragefire Chasm, where Magatha Grimtotem awaits news of her missing emissary Maur. Magatha Grimtotem learns on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise that her emissary, Maur Grimtotem, entered the cavern beneath Orgrimmar. He meant to study the troggs and try to parley with them, but never returned. Rumors say he found something unusual shortly before his death. While Warchief Thrall and his advisers attend to the Shadow Council in Ragefire Chasm, the Grimtotem clan pursues its own interests.

quest:5723.text: Testing an Enemy's Strength. At Thunder Bluff, Rahauro answers the slaughter of Magatha Grimtotem's emissaries beneath Orgrimmar. He sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to thin the troggs' ranks. Magatha Grimtotem sent tauren emissaries into the fiery depths beneath Orgrimmar to make peace with the troggs. The creatures slaughtered the delegates on arrival. Magatha took the massacre as an insult to the tauren and a growing danger to the Horde. So she resolved to answer with force. From Thunder Bluff, Rahauro carries out Magatha’s orders. He sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to find and kill trogg warriors and shamans. The Horde strikes deep into their underground home, thinning their numbers before they can pour through the tunnels into Orgrimmar.

quest:5724.text: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, you find Maur Grimtotem's satchel and carry it to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Troggs slew Maur Grimtotem in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms held fast to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grasp gives you the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

quest:5725.text: The Power to Destroy.... From the Undercity, Varimathras sends Horde adventurers beneath Orgrimmar. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks two dark tomes from the Searing Blade cult, hoping their power will aid her war against the Scourge and the Lich King. Thrall's orcs hunt the Searing Blade cult beneath their capital. The Forsaken covet the cult's occult stores. On Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Varimathras sends operatives into Ragefire Chasm to seize two demonic grimoires: Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether. The Dark Lady believes disciplined Forsaken will can use these gifts better than the lesser cultists. Once the tomes are secured, Varimathras explains their purpose. Their dark magic is meant to strengthen Sylvanas's campaign against the Scourge. The Forsaken hope to claim every scrap of forbidden power, break the Lich King's hold across Lordaeron, and free the remaining undead from his mental enslavement.

quest:5726.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall begins a covert search for the Burning Blade in Durotar. He asks a promising young adventurer to recover a Lieutenant's Insignia from Skull Rock, opening a way to uncover cultists working under the Horde's nose. In Durotar, the new Horde struggles to secure a home, and Warchief Thrall faces betrayal from within. The Burning Blade has taken root just outside Orgrimmar's gates. Its cultists prey on lingering demonic corruption and hunger for dark power. Thrall needs someone to watch and listen without drawing notice. Skull Rock lies east of Orgrimmar. Its rugged caverns hold warlocks, voidwalkers, and fanatical cultists. Thrall sends you to take a Lieutenant's Insignia from one of the Burning Blade leaders. The emblem is meant to open the cult's hidden ranks, so Thrall can learn who directs its movements.

quest:5727.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall sends you to learn what the Burning Blade knows. Cult activity at Skull Rock has brought you to Neeru Fireblade with a lieutenant's insignia, to test his loyalties. Thrall chooses cunning over a strike at the Cleft of Shadow. He knows Neeru Fireblade pretends to serve the Horde while secretly aiding the cultists. A direct attack could warn Neeru's masters and end the trail into the conspiracy. So Thrall gives you an insignia taken from the cult in Durotar and asks you to pose as an initiate, learning what Neeru knows.

quest:5728.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. You have won Neeru Fireblade's trust by pretending to share the cult's cause. Now Thrall sends you into Ragefire Chasm to strike at its leaders. Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race. Yet beneath its markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. There, remnants of the Shadow Council gather strength as the Searing Blade. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

quest:5729.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall's watch reaches into the Cleft of Shadow. After Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker die beneath the city, Thrall sends you to win Neeru Fireblade's trust. Thrall sees a chance after Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed in Ragefire Chasm. He chooses to leave Neeru Fireblade in place. Neeru has lost the lieutenants who led the local cult. So Thrall sends you back to the Cleft of Shadow, offering yourself as an ally who can fill that gap.

quest:5730.text: Hidden Enemies. In Orgrimmar, Thrall awaits your report on the Burning Blade. Neeru Fireblade trusts you, and the Warchief needs to know how far the cult's reach extends across Kalimdor.

quest:5761.text: Slaying the Beast. Neeru Fireblade sends Horde adventurers from Orgrimmar into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. He says Warchief Thrall ordered the hunt and asks for the felguard’s heart as proof the demonic cult has fallen. Ragefire Chasm runs beneath Orgrimmar’s red earthen streets. Its fiery fissure shelters troggs, beasts, and covert Searing Blade agents. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade claims to serve Thrall and cleanse the demonic rot. He points to Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard in the cavern’s heart, and calls him the mastermind behind the cult beneath the city.

quest:579.text: Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those bearing library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn funds the work, opening accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. Young King Anduin directs royal funds toward learning. They pay for copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals. In Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves these accounts and copies them for those in royal service. Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from ancient Eastern Kingdoms histories to accounts of distant lands. These books tell of conflicts beyond the capital.

quest:59.text: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker for Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. Beyond Guard Thomas's bridge, recruits seek armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. You carry his report to Goldshire, and Marshal Dughan marks your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has few stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of equipment. It is a military voucher recording your service to the crown. East of Guard Thomas's bridge lies Eastvale Logging Camp, Elwynn's main timber operation. Sara Timberlain works there under commission from the Stormwind Army, making cloth and leather gear. The kingdom's central armories are strained, so local artisans like Sara outfit troops and auxiliary scouts on the frontier.

quest:590.text: A Rogue's Deal. Calvin Montague offers newly awakened Forsaken work in Deathknell. He promises wealth for delivering a letter, but you do not know whether he will honor the bargain. Deathknell is a ruined village in southwestern Tirisfal Glades.

quest:5921.text: Moonglade. In Darnassus, young night elf druids learn a spell that carries them across the world to Moonglade. There, they meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven and begin the path toward mastering bear form. Moonglade offers an ancient sanctuary devoted to the teachings of Cenarius. Keeper Remulos watches over its groves, where druids find peace and communion with nature. Young druids learn a spell to carry themselves across the world to Moonglade. There they find wisdom beyond mortal distances. Moonglade welcomes all who follow the wild, though the Cenarion Circle knows tension. In Darnassus, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm and Keeper Remulos disagree over nature’s care and the making of Teldrassil. Their differences do not close Nighthaven to young acolytes. They are welcomed to pursue their studies. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze guides young druids in the ways of the Claw. Before an initiate takes up the bear’s mantle, the trials teach endurance, fury, and defense of the wild. Starblaze welcomes each student in reverence to Father Cenarius. Then the trials of the Great Bear Spirit begin.

quest:5922.text: Moonglade. A young tauren druid learns to reach nature’s ancient keepers in Moonglade. Guided by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, you learn to cross the waking world and commune with them directly. Beyond Kalimdor’s faction struggles, Moonglade offers a refuge to all who follow nature. Keeper Remulos, son of Cenarius, watches over the ancient valley. Night elf and tauren druids enter Nighthaven as equals beneath the Cenarion Circle’s timeless mantle. Turak Runetotem teaches you a transport spell bound to Moonglade. It aids your spiritual and martial growth, carrying you across hundreds of leagues in a heartbeat through your bond with the natural world. The valley gives you a place to study and a lasting refuge throughout your journey.

quest:5923.text: Heeding the Call. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker calls druids from Teldrassil and beyond to begin their training. An apprentice now faces the path toward mastering the bear aspect. Novice druids receive a personal summons when their instructors judge them ready for trials. Kal in Dolanaar, Denatharion in Darnassus, and Theridran in Stormwind carry Mathrengyl Bearwalker’s invitation to train. As Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm’s direct assistant, Mathrengyl is one of the night elves’ most respected and knowledgeable mentors. His guidance marks an apprentice as ready for true trials. Mathrengyl Bearwalker receives candidates on the upper level of Fandral Staghelm’s residence in the Cenarion Enclave. Druids must learn to embody nature’s living creatures, not merely watch them. He tells each candidate that the first great undertaking is to embrace the bear’s strength, endurance, and spirit. The path reaches far beyond Teldrassil, to sacred ancestral grounds.

quest:5926.text: Heeding the Call. Across Horde settlements, word reaches novice druids that Turak Runetotem wants to instruct them in person. Heeding the Call brings them to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, where the sacred trials toward the bear's form begin. Across Mulgore and Orgrimmar, you hear that Turak Runetotem has noticed your early progress. The message may come from Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Pala in Thunder Bluff, or Gennia Runetotem in Bloodhoof Village. The Cenarion Circle does not call practitioners lightly. Your work with herbs and simple spells has earned you a chance to deepen your bond with nature's wild spirits. On Elder Rise, Turak Runetotem guides young tauren in their ancestral duty. He assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem and welcomes you into the large Cenarion tent. Turak teaches that animals and plants are allies, and that these bonds carry solemn duties. His guidance opens a way beyond basic lessons, toward trials of body and heart and communion with the Great Bear Spirit.

quest:5931.text: Back to Darnassus. You leave Moonglade after meeting the Great Bear Spirit and return to Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits to guide your practical shapeshifting trials. Dendrite Starblaze sends you from Nighthaven back to Darnassus after your meeting with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. There, you leave the sanctuary where you communed with the spirit and return to the unsettled world beyond. In Darnassus, local mentors watch over Teldrassil and guide the next stage of your training. Mathrengyl Bearwalker waits for you in the Cenarion Enclave, guarding nature as its balance falters. The Great Bear Spirit's blessing is only the first step. Mathrengyl prepares you for trials of body and heart, so you can give physical form to the spirit's fierce ancestral wisdom.

quest:5932.text: Back to Thunder Bluff. At Elder Rise, Turak Runetotem awaits your return from Moonglade. Dendrite Starblaze sends you home after your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, so your training can continue among your people. In Moonglade, night elf and tauren practitioners of nature magic meet in the Cenarion Circle. There, they set aside the divides between mortal factions. After your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, Dendrite Starblaze sends you back to your people. Night elves often see tauren as fledglings in Cenarius’s formal teachings. Yet Starblaze recognizes the wisdom and balance of Turak Runetotem. You climb to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff and stand before Turak Runetotem, changed by your rite. Communion with ancient totemic spirits such as the Great Bear Spirit runs deep in tauren culture. Yet the Path of the Claw asks for serious commitment. Your spiritual bond is forged, and Turak prepares you to put your new strength and endurance into practice.

quest:6.text: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. Near Northshire Abbey, an Alliance bounty calls recruits to hunt Garrick Padfoot by the vineyards. The notorious thief and his gang threaten the valley's farmers and merchants. Northshire Valley offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. But as order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers. Stormwind's guards are stretched thin, protecting the capital and its outer borders. So local marshals and deputies rely on volunteers to keep Northshire peaceful. Deputy Willem posts a public bounty on Garrick's head, hoping to rid the valley of his gang. Padfoot's rundown shack lies east of the river. Bringing him down there strikes at the lawlessness spreading through the human heartland.

quest:60.text: Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds crowding Elwynn's mines. The alchemist has come from his Stormwind shop for their thick wax. His errand brings adventurers face to face with the creatures encroaching on the kingdom's gold veins. William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. He needs wax for the remedies, ointments, and concoctions he brews. So he turns to Elwynn's kobolds instead of buying polished candles from city merchants. They carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer to pry loose. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. They prize their candles above almost everything. The flames guide them through dark shafts as they dig for gold and shiny trinkets. Taking the candles replenishes Pestle's alchemy stocks and weakens the vermin choking off the kingdom's precious mining claims.

quest:6001.text: Body and Heart. In Darnassus, a night elf initiate stands near the end of the path of the claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends them to Darkshore, where Lunaclaw will test their body and heart before they take the form of the bear. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends night elf initiates east of Auberdine, the coastal settlement in Darkshore. There, a natural cavern shelters wild moonkin and an ancient Moonkin Stone. Anointing the stone with Cenarion Moondust awakens Lunaclaw, its ancient defender. The guardian challenges each initiate who seeks the sacred strength of the claw.

quest:6002.text: Body and Heart. At the Moonkin Stone, you face a trial of strength and heart to master Bear Form. Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids from Thunder Bluff to summon and defeat Lunaclaw near the dry frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens. Turak Runetotem tests young tauren druids who seek the path of the Druid of the Claw. You have communed with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. Now your training turns to a trial of strength. Turak, the elder druid trainer atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise, gives worthy aspirants Cenarion Lunardust. He sends you to a sacred stone near the dry frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens. West of Camp Taurajo, the Moonkin Stone marks a rare Cenarion site in southern Kalimdor. Moonkin are not native to the sun-scorched plains of central Kalimdor, and Lunaclaw guards the stone. Scatter the lunardust across the ancient monument to call Lunaclaw into battle. Defeating the guardian proves your strength and clarity of heart. Its blessing awakens the bear's inner essence.

quest:6061.text: Taming the Beast. At Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane begins a young tauren hunter’s training with Taming the Beast. The first trial leads into Mulgore, where the hunter tames an adult plainstrider and begins a bond with the Earthmother’s creatures. Tauren hunters seek more than meat and hides. Their ancestral traditions teach that meeting Mulgore’s wild creatures can bring them closer to the Earthmother. A tamed companion may once have been an adversary. Now beast and hunter join as partners in the natural balance of the plains. Yaw Sharpmane begins a hunter’s training with the plainstriders roaming Mulgore’s grasslands. Carrying an enchanted taming rod, the hunter faces an adult plainstrider and calms its wild instincts to earn its trust. This first trial tests the hunter’s resolve and prepares them to face more demanding beasts.

quest:6062.text: Taming the Beast. In Razor Hill, Taming the Beast puts young Horde hunters to their first test with a taming rod. Thotar sends them to face a fierce dire mottled boar. In Durotar, orc and Darkspear troll hunters must learn to command the wild as well as survive it. Thotar gives young hunters an enchanted taming rod and sends them against a fierce wild boar. They must subdue the beast without killing it, then make it a loyal ally. Dire mottled boars roam the dry brush around Razor Hill. Their strength and temper make them a fitting first test for young hunters. The rod can subdue a charging boar, but using it takes patience and resolve. Every Horde tracker needs those qualities.

quest:6063.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, a young night elf hunter faces the first trial of Taming the Beast with a wild Webwood Lurker. Dazalar lends an enchanted taming rod, and the hunter must earn the spider’s trust through a bond with nature. For the kaldorei, hunting asks more than skill at tracking prey or survival in the wild. It binds a hunter to nature, greater than any mortal. Animals are their own creatures, not tools to bend to a hunter’s will. Dazalar teaches novice hunters to meet them with respect. Before gaining a lifelong beast companion, a hunter must master the local wildlife through ancient techniques, never brute force. Giant arachnids infest Teldrassil’s boughs, so Dazalar gives the hunter a taming rod. In shadowed thickets, the hunter seeks a Webwood Lurker and faces the venomous spider’s attacks. To reach it, the hunter must answer with empathy. A brief mental bond proves the hunter can commune with the World Tree’s eerie, skittering predators.

quest:6064.text: Taming the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Taming the Beast sets a hunter on the first trial toward mastering companion beasts. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart guides young trackers as they calm a Large Crag Boar with an enchanted taming rod. Dwarven mountaineers and trackers depend on guns, traps, and their wits in the wild. Yet a hunter's calling is to make a lifelong bond with a wild beast. Outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Grif Wildheart oversees this rite. He tests novices against several species native to Dun Morogh before asking them to bind any beast for good. A Large Crag Boar is the first test for a young tracker. These thick-hided swine roam Dun Morogh's snowy foothills, where their bristling fur and tough flesh make them stubborn and fierce. Grif provides an enchanted Taming Rod. The hunter faces the boar's charge and tries to calm its fury until it submits to command.

quest:6065.text: The Hunter's Path. In Mulgore, The Hunter's Path sends young tauren to Bloodhoof Village for advanced training. There they seek Yaw Sharpmane and begin the trials of taming and bonding with wild beasts. Among the Shu'halo, hunting is sacred. A hunter learns nature's balance, honors the plains' spirits, and respects the animals that sustain the tribes. After young hunters prove they can survive in the wild and use a bow or gun, their elders send them to seasoned mentors. The journey marks their step beyond solitary tracking and toward adulthood in tauren culture. The road to Bloodhoof Village crosses Mulgore's grasslands and reaches the settlement beside Stonebull Lake. There, Yaw Sharpmane teaches hunters about the local beasts. Meeting him marks a hunter's readiness for the trials of beast taming. They learn to commune with predators as well as hunt them.

quest:6068.text: The Hunter's Path. In Durotar, The Hunter's Path leads young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. There, Thotar teaches them to bind wild predators. In Durotar, young hunters learn to follow prey with bow and cunning. Trails through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teach them patience. To master the Horde's way of hunting, they must also learn to bond with wild beasts. When class trainers judge a student ready, they send them to Razor Hill. At Razor Hill, Thotar teaches young hunters to subdue Durotar's fierce beasts without breaking their spirit. His lessons begin their path toward traveling the wilderness with a loyal companion.

quest:6074.text: The Hunter's Path. In Dun Morogh, the trainers send ready hunters to Kharanos to begin learning how to tame wild beasts. Grif Wildheart oversees the trials there. Novice hunters cross Dun Morogh’s snowy crags alone until they learn to bond with beasts. Olmin Burningbeard and Tristane Shadowstone watch their pupils closely. They wait until a hunter can face a savage creature calmly and spare its life. Then the trainers send the disciplined novice down the mountain roads toward Kharanos. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart oversees the final trials of dwarven huntsmanship. Taming a beast takes more than bringing it down for meat or pelt. A hunter needs patience, physical endurance, and an instinctive bond with the wild predators of the mountains. Wildheart prepares each hunter to test their will against Dun Morogh’s fiercest wildlife.

quest:6081.text: Training the Beast. In Durotar, young orc and troll hunters are sent to learn from veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. After proving themselves with the plains beasts, they travel from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There they learn to care for, feed, and train a lifelong animal companion. In Durotar's arid canyons, skill with a bow and survival in the wild are only part of a hunter's duty. Young hunters first tame the plains beasts: fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers. Once they prove their resilience, Thotar sends them from Razor Hill north through the red clay gulches to Orgrimmar's fortified gates. There, they must take responsibility for a companion. Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor is where veteran stalkers and warriors hone their craft. There, young hunters seek Ormak Grimshot, one of the Horde's revered master hunters. He looks beyond their youth to judge whether they have the patience to command a beast and care for it through famine, battle, and loss. A beast won through force remains wild until hunter and companion understand one another. Ormak teaches the traditions that keep their bond: which foods nourish each creature's spirit, how discipline teaches a beast lethal techniques, and the spiritual focus needed to revive one that falls in the line of duty.

quest:6082.text: Taming the Beast. In Durotar, a young Horde hunter faces the last trial of Taming the Beast. Thotar in Razor Hill sends the hunter to tame an armored scorpid. Success grants the power to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting companion. A hunter must first prove they can command Durotar's harsh wildlife before traveling Kalimdor with an animal companion. Thotar trains hunters in Razor Hill and sends them to subdue three kinds of creature with an enchanted taming rod. Dire boars and swift surf crawlers have already tested them. Now they face an armored scorpid, a venomous predator with heavy plates, known for its resilience and speed. Taming an armored scorpid tests focus and control under attack, not a hunter's skill at killing. Thotar urges hunters to meet the beast's quick, confident strikes. Once the scorpid is charmed, the hunter returns to Razor Hill and gives the taming rod back to Thotar. Then Thotar teaches the wild's innate techniques, so the hunter can seek out and bind a permanent companion of their choosing.

quest:6083.text: Taming the Beast. Along Durotar's coast, Taming the Beast sends young hunters to face their second trial. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, directs aspiring orc and troll hunters to tame a surf crawler near the Echo Isles and extend their bond to coastal wildlife. You have mastered a dire mottled boar, and now Thotar sends you toward the sea. Durotar's harsh shores are jagged, and shallow reefs teem with armored crustaceans. A surf crawler resists intrusion into its coastal domain. Taming one calls for patience and fortitude. Thotar teaches that a bound beast should add to a hunter's strength. With the taming rod, you subdue a surf crawler and learn to command creatures of different temperaments in different surroundings. This trial proves you are ready for permanent companions.

quest:6084.text: Taming the Beast. Grif Wildheart sends you to face a snow leopard in the second taming trial. The test reaches beyond the crag boar. Snow leopards prowl southeast of Kharanos. The crag boar tested your strength against hard blows. Now Grif expects you to face a swift, graceful predator on its own terms. Beneath its white coat lies dangerous strength, ready to strike. With an enchanted taming rod, you face a wild snow leopard and seek to turn its hunting instincts toward partnership. Its speed, agility, and sharp reflexes test you in ways the crag boar did not. Learn to work alongside a predator that strikes swiftly from the snowy crags, and you draw closer to mastering the beasts of the wild.

quest:6085.text: Taming the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Grif Wildheart tests your control of an Ice Claw Bear east of Kharanos. With an enchanted rod, you subdue the bear and learn to understand it. Then you earn the power to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting wild companion. Dun Morogh’s mountaineers and scouts depend on hardy beasts in its freezing crags. You have practiced on swift, cunning predators. Now Grif Wildheart sends you to capture an Ice Claw Bear in the snowdrifts east of Kharanos. Its strength and endurance test the control every dwarven huntsman must learn. The Taming Rod keeps the bear docile while you learn how wild instincts answer to will and calm intent. Your bond lasts only for the trial, which teaches discipline. Return the rod to Grif and the trials are complete. He then teaches you to pacify a compatible wild creature and call it throughout your life of adventure.

quest:6086.text: Training the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Grif Wildheart sends young dwarven hunters to Ironforge to learn care for a lasting animal companion. After taming the mountain’s wild predators, they learn to feed and train their beasts. Young hunters finish their trial near Kharanos under Grif Wildheart’s watch. They have tamed large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod. Then Grif sends them up the mountain pass to Ironforge. They seek the Hall of Arms in the military district. Belia Thundergranite teaches animal care in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms. Revered among the dwarven kingdom’s master animal trainers, she shows young hunters how to nourish their pets and teach them new battlefield skills. She also teaches them to call their spirits back if they fall defending their master. Her lessons turn a frightened wild beast into a loyal partner.
