Dwarven tradition asks for respect between hunter and beast, never subjugation. Belia reminds young hunters that an animal companion reflects the care it receives. Fed well, respected, and properly trained, a beast will fight loyally against troggs, frost trolls, and any threat to Khaz Modan.

quest:6087.text: Taming the Beast. In Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane sets a young tauren hunter a new trial. The hunter must master the swift prairie stalker. After mastering the adult plainstrider’s endurance, you face a new kind of hunter. Prairie stalkers rely on speed and travel in packs. They attack without fear. To tame one, you must approach without breaking stride and match the wolf’s decisive nature. Yaw Sharpmane teaches you that hunting beside a beast takes neither servitude nor brute force. You and the predator must fight as one, joined by respect and shared rhythm. Under Mulgore’s open skies, bonding with a prairie stalker teaches you to complement your companion’s attacks and move with it in battle.

quest:6088.text: Taming the Beast. In Mulgore, a young tauren hunter faces the final trial with Yaw Sharpmane in Bloodhoof Village. With an enchanted rod, you tame a wild swoop and prove you can master the sky. The trial earns you the Earthmother’s trust and lasting knowledge to tame, call, and dismiss a companion. After you subdue predators on Mulgore’s plains, Yaw Sharpmane turns your training to the open sky. A swoop is a fierce bird of prey, with a sharp beak, sweeping dives, and an intimidating air. Its talons test your reflexes and calm as you use the enchanted rod to bring its instincts into accord with your own. For the tauren, hunting and companionship with beasts are spiritual pursuits, not mere subjugation. Mastering creatures of earth and sky teaches the balance and respect needed to walk the plains without disturbing nature. Yaw Sharpmane takes back his temporary taming rod, then teaches you lasting ways to call, dismiss, and permanently tame a companion of your choosing.

quest:6089.text: Training the Beast. In Mulgore, Training the Beast brings young tauren hunters to the next step in learning beside a beast. After soothing the plains’ wild creatures, they travel to Thunder Bluff to learn the lasting bond of care and command. Tauren hunters in Mulgore have faced plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops. Now Yaw Sharpmane, their mentor in Bloodhoof Village, sends each novice to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff to take up the full mantle of the hunter. There, Holt Thunderhorn teaches them. The shu'halo honor him for communing with the wilds, and his reverence for the Earthmother is greater still. To the tauren, a beast is a partner joined through harmony with the natural world, never a weapon or thrall. Holt Thunderhorn teaches hunters how to keep that bond strong. They learn to guide a creature's combat instincts, feed it regularly, and mend its injuries. If it falls defending its companion on the plains, they can call its spirit back.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax gathered from kobolds in Elwynn Forest to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary. William Pestle gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire. His brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave the Lion's Pride Inn, so he trusts travelers bound for the city to carry his goods. William's parcel holds large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He collects them for their wax, but does not say how the brothers use it. You carry the shipment to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District.

quest:6101.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Dazalar guides you through a second trial for night elf hunters. With an enchanted taming rod, you subdue a nightsaber stalker and learn how wild beasts differ. Dazalar teaches you that the forest's creatures do not all behave alike. Each kind has its own temper, and a hunter must learn how to meet it. Beneath Teldrassil's canopy, this trial sets you against beasts more cunning and predatory than webspinners. Kaldorei revere nightsabers as sacred predators, fierce guardians, and companions of the Sentinels. With the taming rod, you face a nightsaber stalker and must keep a steady nerve and calm authority. Winning its trust proves you can handle a predator, not only the gentler creatures of the woods.

quest:6102.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the last trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, the hunter tames a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion. Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil to finish their basic beastcraft. After facing beasts of the underbrush, they meet the spirit of the skies: the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod. Taming the Strigid Screecher completes the ancient lessons in communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. The apprentice returns the spent rod to Dazalar, and the training exercises end. Then the hunter gains the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

quest:6103.text: Training the Beast. In Teldrassil, night elf hunters leave the wilds for Darnassus after taming beasts among the boughs. There, Jocaste teaches them to care for and discipline a companion. Dazalar sends you from the wilds near Dolanaar to Darnassus after you prove you can tame a beast. Before traveling Kalimdor with a loyal companion, you need more than skill with a taming rod. Subduing a wild creature tests your strength and will, but an untrained beast can still be unpredictable. In Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave, Jocaste teaches you to care for a companion. She shows you how to feed your pet, bring it back if tragedy strikes, and train it to fight. For night elves, this bond reflects reverence for nature, not simple control.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of cleansing poison. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in venom and toxins. Cenarius teaches druids and blesses them with a bond to the living world. Among his gifts is the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power comes with a burden. Before young druids wield it, they learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic. Mathrengyl Bearwalker trains druids in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. Now he sends his student beyond local practice to Moonglade. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's wider efforts. He has practical work for the novice.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, sick deer have drawn the Cenarion Circle to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to gather a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to suffer a lingering sickness, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water is tainted. He sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls. Vicious naga dwell inside Cliffspring River Cave, near the falls' headwaters. Their presence endangers anyone who comes to study the blight. The Cenarion Circle needs a sample from the cave mouth to learn what is making the wilderness sick.

quest:6123.text: Gathering the Cure. In Darkshore, sick deer need a salve, and Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine shows a young druid how to make one. The remedy calls for water and healing plants gathered nearby. Alanndarian Nightsong seeks a cure for Darkshore's sick deer. A contaminated water source has harmed the local wildlife, so sampled Cliffspring water will form the salve's base. Natural ingredients with healing power must complete the mixture. The deer cannot recover alone, and the Cenarion Circle needs a remedy soon. Earthroot and Lunar Fungus lend healing power to the salve. Earthroot grows in rocky soil, where a practiced herbalist's eye helps find it. Lunar Fungus blooms in caves east of Auberdine. The moonkin there have grown territorial and agitated, making the gathering more dangerous.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Across Darkshore, deer are falling sick, and Curing the Sick brings you a way to help them. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve for the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Deer are falling sick across Darkshore, from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat them.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. In Darnassus, Power over Poison brings a young druid back to finish the Cenarion Circle's trial. It began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong sends young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They use them to brew a salve for stricken wildlife. Before teaching the magic that purges toxins, the Cenarion Circle asks initiates to learn the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. That work shows them what common folk endure when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care. The remedy proves effective in Auberdine, and Starblaze sends the druid across the sea to Darnassus. Mathrengyl Bearwalker waits in the Cenarion Enclave. Pleased by the initiate's grace under pressure, he teaches them to cleanse toxins through nature's power. Yet virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine trouble him. They point to an unnatural blight that disturbs the land's balance.

quest:6126.text: Lessons Anew. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids to sacred Moonglade to learn the cleansing of poisons. Under Dendrite Starblaze, a night elf druid, apprentices begin that study as real poisonings call for more than practice. Cenarius granted druids an incantation to purge virulent toxins, and charged them to protect the wilds. Turak Runetotem teaches that such magic needs a firm grounding. Before using it to clear a blight, a druid must understand venom’s physical toll and learn to treat it by ordinary means. Turak sends promising acolytes north from Mulgore along sacred pathways to Moonglade. There, in the peaceful village of Nighthaven, ancient night elf mentors such as Dendrite Starblaze teach practitioners of both elf and tauren kind. Their shared study reflects the Cenarion Circle’s delicate truce, rising above the political strife between Horde and Alliance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. From Moonglade, Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a sample of water. She asks them to carry it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it may explain the poison harming wildlife. Dendrite Starblaze fears the Burning Blade has tainted Dreadmist Peak. The mountain rises northwest of the Crossroads, above the dry northern Barrens. Springs and pools crown its heights, shaping the local weather and moisture. Now a cult devoted to demons has taken hold on the crags, and its foul sorcery may poison the basin. Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and asks the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. A water sample from the peak will let him study the sickness and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem guides young tauren druids through a sacred passage. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns for a salve to treat the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs ingredients for an antidote, using the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Earthroot gives the salve its medicinal qualities, while ground kodo horn lends it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering these means relying on the earth's gifts and hunting local beasts. As Tonga Runetotem prepares the salve, he teaches the limits of physical medicine. Herbal lore and alchemy can counter certain toxins, but most poisons need their own cure. Rather than carry endless herbs and horns, druids learn to attune to nature's healing energies. That lesson leads to the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:6129.text: Curing the Sick. Sick gazelles are suffering across the northern Barrens. Tonga Runetotem sends young Horde druids to treat them with a freshly made herbal salve, then sends them before the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. An unnatural sickness is spreading among gazelles in the northern Barrens. You have gathered earthroot and kodo horns for a curative remedy, and Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads now entrusts the animals to your care. Search north of the main crossroads and tend to ten suffering gazelles. The salve brings them relief before the affliction takes deeper hold in the ecosystem. After you apply the salve, you travel to Moonglade’s tranquil druidic sanctuary. Dendrite Starblaze recognizes your compassion and vigilance there. He says the gazelles’ suffering points to a deeper corruption stalking Kalimdor’s wilderness. By tending even the lowliest beasts, tauren druids show that reverence for Cenarius reaches beyond tribal boundaries. They earn deeper secrets of poison cleansing and nature magic.

quest:6130.text: Power over Poison. At Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to claim the gift of Cure Poison. The initiate has treated poisoned gazelles near the Crossroads with herbal mixtures and now faces Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise. The Cenarion Circle asks a druid to learn how affliction feels before granting the power to cleanse venom. Dendrite Starblaze sends the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem has them gather ingredients for a salve. By treating the Barrens' poisoned gazelles by hand, without spiritual aid, the druid sees how ordinary creatures struggle against natural and unnatural toxins. After the trial, Dendrite sends the initiate to Turak Runetotem, the grand druid trainer on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Turak warns that strange, virulent poisons near the Crossroads threaten the plains' natural balance. He commends the initiate's grace under pressure and grants the spiritual art of curing poisons. The living creatures of Kalimdor are now in the initiate's care.

quest:6181.text: A Swift Message. Quartermaster Lewis needs armor for Westfall's militia, and he sends an urgent note to Stormwind by gryphon. With little help from the kingdom's forces, he asks you to take the requisition to Thor at Sentinel Hill for the flight to the capital. At Sentinel Hill, the People's Militia faces Defias outlaws and gnolls with little help from Stormwind's forces. Quartermaster Lewis relies on private contacts in the capital for weapons and armor. As the militia's supplies run low, he turns to Osric Strang, an armorer in Old Town. Lewis asks travelers to carry the urgent requisition note to Thor, Westfall's gryphon master. Gryphons carry people and messages swiftly across the Kingdom of Stormwind. Thor manages the air route to the capital from Sentinel Hill. When you give him Lewis's note, he carries the requisition to Stormwind by air. This route links Westfall's frontier garrison to the capital despite the lack of official aid.

quest:62.text: The Fargodeep Mine. South of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the kobold-held Fargodeep Mine. It lies between the Stonefield and Maclure farms, and its fall points to trouble beyond its tunnels. Kobolds have taken the Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads. It once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering echoes through its damp tunnels, where tallow candles burn. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is. When Dughan hears your report, he worries about other mineral sites, including the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. The news adds to the Stormwind Guard's strain. Its troops are already stretched thin defending against Defias bandits and gnoll incursions, leaving too few to clear the tunnels.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. At the roost in Stormwind's Trade District, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon flights for supplies bound to Westfall's defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have brought Westfall close to breaking. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia badly need provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the equipment they asked for. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier. In Stormwind's Trade District, the gryphon roost is where Dungar Longdrink coordinates courier and passenger flights. Wildhammer dwarves have long raised and handled these great beasts. Gryphons carry people and cargo across human lands when roosts at both ends know the route. Bringing Osric's heavy crate straight to Dungar shows how aerial transport works. It links the capital's stockpiles to frontier outposts such as Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note at Sentinel Hill. Thor, the local gryphon master, offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom’s trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and Elwynn Forest’s river border. Then the gryphon carries you over Stormwind City’s high white ramparts. You land at the capital’s trade roosts, then make your way into Old Town. There you find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, yet his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall’s beleaguered People’s Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. A crate of armor is bound for the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill, and Dungar Longdrink sends it from Stormwind by gryphon. The flight crosses Elwynn and Westfall to reach defenders under pressure. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, has packed a heavy crate of armor for the People's Militia volunteers at Sentinel Hill. Defias bandits, hungry gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten Westfall. A lone wagon is an easy target on those roads, so the flight master network gives the armor a safer way to the defenders. Gryphons are loyal and well trained, but they need a known destination before they carry a rider there. Dungar Longdrink explains that they instinctively return to their capital roost in Stormwind. For a remote outpost, you first meet its flight master in person. You have already checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, opening the skies over the frontier to swift travel. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis receives the crate and begins distributing its armor among the frontier defenders. He outfits Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force. Each shipment helps the militia hold its ground against the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:6321.text: Supplying the Sepulcher. At the Sepulcher, Deathguard Podrig seeks arms for a garrison worn down by the fighting. He sends an order to the Undercity as beasts, Scourge and other threats drain its stores. Deathguard Podrig says the Sepulcher has fair stores, yet fighting in Silverpine Forest steadily uses them up. Feral beasts, Scourge remnants and other local threats damage weapons and armor or leave them behind after skirmishes. Under Executor Hadrec's orders, Podrig writes a request to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer in the Undercity. Replacement arms and armor help the Forsaken hold their fragile footholds beyond Tirisfal Glades. Silverpine's roads make a slow and dangerous way to carry vital messages and supplies. So the Forsaken send them by trained vampire bats. At the Sepulcher, Karos Razok handles the bats and links its soldiers to the Undercity's aerial network. Those routes connect outlying garrisons to Sylvanas's capital.

quest:6322.text: Michael Garrett. In the Undercity, Michael Garrett waits for a crate bound for the Sepulcher. Gordon Wendham packs field supplies in the Trade Quarter, and you bring them to Garrett for the Forsaken bats to carry toward Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken send supplies from the Undercity to outposts such as the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. In the Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham packs field supplies into a crate. Ground travel through blighted forests is slow, and Scourge remnants or wild beasts may ambush the freight. The Forsaken avoid dangerous roads with captive vampire bats, bred and kept by skilled handlers. Michael Garrett tends the bats from his roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. When you bring him the cargo, he can strap it to a bat for flight over the hills toward Silverpine. The bats link the capital with its outposts.

quest:6323.text: Ride to the Undercity. From the Sepulcher, a courier carries Podrig's weapons request to the Undercity. A dread bat bears the message over Silverpine Forest to the Forsaken capital. Karos Razok handles the dread bats at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. The bats carry messengers and supplies between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts. Roads below run through danger from hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and Scourge remnants. So the bats give military requests a swift route to the capital. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, the courier brings Podrig's equipment request to Gordon Wendham. The weaponsmith prepares arms for the Dark Lady's cause. He keeps outposts such as the Sepulcher supplied with weapons ready for battle. Those outposts defend the young Forsaken nation from its surrounding enemies.

quest:6324.text: Return to Podrig. At the Undercity, you carry weapons bound for the Sepulcher after bringing a dispatch to the capital. Forsaken bats take you across Lordaeron to Deathguard Podrig. Deathguard Podrig's garrison at the Sepulcher needs weapons from the Undercity. Its sentries in Silverpine Forest face worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Fresh arms help the Forsaken hold the region and keep the outpost ready. Bat Master Michael Garrett tends the central roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Forsaken bats know the way back to the capital, but you speak with local handlers such as Karos Razok before flying to a distant outpost. Carrying Gordon's Crate across Lordaeron joins the Undercity's supplies to its scattered strongholds.

quest:6341.text: The Bounty of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong is comparing Teldrassil's fish with the mainland catch. She sends samples from Rut'theran Village to Auberdine to learn whether the island fish are larger and more plentiful. Nessa Shadowsong asks you to carry fish bones and scales to Laird in Auberdine. Fishers in Rut'theran Village bring in large, plentiful catches. Nessa wants to learn whether the mainland waters yield the same kind of fish. The samples let Laird compare the island catch with fish from the coast of Darkshore. Nessa Shadowsong sends you to Vesprystus, the hippogryph master in Rut'theran Village, with the collection for Auberdine. Give him the samples, and he arranges your passage across the water to Darkshore.

quest:6342.text: Flight to Auberdine. You carry unusual fish specimens from Teldrassil to Auberdine for Laird. Vesprystus sends you from Rut'theran Village by hippogryph. From Rut'theran Village, you fly by hippogryph toward Darkshore with fish specimens for Nessa Shadowsong. The village is a sanctuary at the edge of the wider world for young adventurers leaving Teldrassil. A ferry also crosses the strait between the island and mainland Kalimdor, while night elves travel by bonded hippogryph. At Auberdine's docks, Laird examines Nessa's findings. The scales are as large as fists, and the jawbone is nearly twice the size of mainland specimens. Waters around the base of the World Tree seem to yield altered or abnormally large life. The strange catches may be tied to Teldrassil's potent, restless nature.

quest:6343.text: Return to Nessa. Laird sends you from Auberdine to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village with his findings. This introductory errand teaches young travelers to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. Fish caught off Darkshore differ sharply from those near Teldrassil. He suspects the great World Tree changes the life in these waters. You can hire a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or take the regular ferry from Auberdine's pier to Rut'theran Village. At Rut'theran Village, Nessa Shadowsong receives Laird's reply and is fascinated by the difference in marine life. Fish near the World Tree grow so large that local fishermen benefit at once, though the Kaldorei do not know why. Nessa plans to share the findings with her fellow villagers. For now, she harvests the abundant sea life and watches for whatever forces may be responsible.

quest:6344.text: Nessa Shadowsong. Below the World Tree in Darnassus, Mydrannul sends a courier to meet Nessa Shadowsong. The delivery runs from Rut'theran Village to Darkshore, linking the city in the canopy with the shore. In Darnassus, Mydrannul watches over travelers looking for work and purpose. Fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package carried across the sea to Darkshore, so Mydrannul sends capable couriers toward the coast. Many young night elves begin their journeys among Teldrassil's boughs. This delivery takes them beyond the tree. From the Temple Gardens, the western portal in Darnassus leads down through the World Tree to Rut'theran Village. At the ocean-level roots, fishing docks and hippogryph perches connect Teldrassil with the rest of Kalimdor. Nessa Shadowsong tends her trade there and prepares shipments for Auberdine.

quest:6361.text: A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. You carry them across central Kalimdor and see how the Crossroads wind rider roost links Horde settlements. Hunters bring hides and meat to the Crossroads. There, Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot work every raw hide, so he asks you to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Its master leatherworkers can make the pelts into gear for the Horde. The trail through the Barrens and into Mulgore is rough. Quilboar and predators threaten anyone carrying cargo on foot. So Jahan sends you to Devrak, the Crossroads wind rider master. A trained wyvern can carry the goods through the air and link the Horde’s scattered settlements.

quest:6362.text: Ride to Thunder Bluff. Your wind rider carries cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff, high above the plains. The flight joins the Barrens to the Horde capital. Devrak carries travelers over the Barrens on a wind rider. For many, it is their first flight across Kalimdor. These wyverns link the young Horde’s scattered settlements and spare travelers the ground roads, where quilboar and centaur packs roam. Cured hides from the Barrens are bound for Ahanu, a craftsman at Hewa’s Armory in Thunder Bluff. He works beneath the great wind rider roost on the central mesa. Supplies from hunting outposts across the plains help him outfit local warriors and hunters.

quest:6363.text: Tal the Wind Rider Master. In Thunder Bluff, Tal the Wind Rider Master waits for Ahanu’s parcel. It is bound for Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads, where Mulgore’s leatherworkers trade with Barrens merchants. From Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, Ahanu sends finished hides to Jahan Hawkwing’s trade stall at the Crossroads. Trade between Mulgore and the Barrens matters to the young Horde. The journey down the bluffs and across the plains takes hours on foot, so winged couriers carry parcels over the divide. On Thunder Bluff’s highest central tier, Tal tends the city’s wind riders, also called wyverns. They cross Kalimdor’s rugged peaks and shifting thermal drafts. Tal arranges flights to outposts such as the Crossroads, carrying messengers and cargo between the tauren capital and its orcish allies.

quest:6364.text: Return to Jahan. You return finished leather goods to Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads. The journey begins after you bring hides to Ahanu, Thunder Bluff’s skinner, and introduces you to the Horde’s wind rider routes between Mulgore and the Barrens. Tal, Thunder Bluff’s wind rider master, arranges flights across central Kalimdor from the central mesa. For many travelers, this is their first ride on a trained wind rider. Once you have met another settlement’s wind rider master, such as Devrak at the Crossroads, a rider can carry you there. The beasts cross leagues that would otherwise make for a dangerous overland journey through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens. Jahan Hawkwing trades from the Crossroads, where hunters, scouts, and mercenaries gather each day. The flights carry goods between settlements too. Hides sent to Ahanu on Thunder Bluff’s high rises become durable armor and equipment. Then they fly back to the Barrens crossroads to supply the Horde’s growing frontier efforts.

quest:6365.text: Meats to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sends Barrens meat toward Orgrimmar. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to deliver it to Devrak, the wind rider master, and learn the route to the Horde capital. Wild game runs across the Barrens, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has cut meat for Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. He sends runners from the Crossroads to the wind rider perch instead of risking the long, dusty trek across the Southfury River into Durotar. Meeting Devrak gives a young Horde warrior a first glimpse of the wind rider routes. Wind rider masters link remote places like the Crossroads to the Horde's fortified seat in Orgrimmar. Devrak prepares you and the cargo for a swift flight over the savannah.

quest:6384.text: Ride to Orgrimmar. From the Crossroads, you fly with Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat to Orgrimmar’s Skytower. There, you deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. Their flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. High above the dusty canyon trails, wyverns carry messengers and travelers to the capital, along with dispatches and trade goods. Zargh has prepared fresh cuts of meat for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Strength. From the central Skytower, her inn is a short walk away. Gryshka accepts the parcel and fondly remarks that Zargh knows how to win a lady’s heart.

quest:6385.text: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka has thanks for Zargh at the Crossroads and needs a courier to carry them. She sends you to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar’s skytower to arrange your flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends Zargh her thanks after his shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. She has no time to travel through Durotar herself. So she trusts the aerial couriers who link Horde settlements to carry her letter across the frontier. At the flight tower in the Valley of Strength, Doras oversees Orgrimmar’s wind rider roost. Trained wyverns carry military messages and supplies between the capital and outposts such as the Crossroads. They travel far faster than anyone on foot or in a kodo cart.

quest:6386.text:
Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply travels from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider bears it across Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides your mount for the return to the Barrens.

You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and spares you the long march overland across the Southfury River. Zargh's courtship has won Gryshka's warm reply. The fine provisions pleased her, and Zargh celebrates, even musing about an impending wedding.

The delivery also brings you back to the Barrens' central hub for travel.

quest:6387.text: Honor Students. Brock Stoneseeker sends an order from Thelsamar to Ironforge for honorary mining picks. He asks you to enlist Thorgrum Borrelson to carry it there. Brock teaches new miners about rock composition and tunnel safety. He rewards the apprentices who distinguish themselves with honorary picks. Mining sustains Thelsamar, and dwarves take pride in the craft. Local supplies are limited, so the picks must come from Ironforge across Khaz Modan. Thorgrum tends the gryphon roost beside Thelsamar, linking the frontier to Ironforge through the kingdom's aerial courier network. Bring Brock's order to him, and he can arrange a swift courier run to the capital's foundries.

quest:6388.text: Gryth Thurden. In Ironforge, Gryth Thurden can send you back toward Loch Modan with a parcel. You carry the Honorary Picks from Golnir Bouldertoe for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices, and the city's gryphon roost offers a way over the mountain roads. You have traveled from Loch Modan to the Great Forge, where Golnir Bouldertoe gives you Honorary Picks for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices. He points you to Ironforge's gryphon network instead of the mountain passes on foot. Carry the bundle across the city to the master handler, who can arrange your flight back. Gryth Thurden oversees Ironforge's flight roosts in the great mountain hall. Gryphon routes link the city with dwarven settlements across Khaz Modan. After scouting the route and speaking with the local handler, you can ask Gryth to arrange transport back to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar. The picks are bound for Brock Stoneseeker's apprentices, and the route joins mountain settlements by air.

quest:6391.text: Ride to Ironforge. Brock Stoneseeker sends you from Thelsamar to Ironforge with the names of his finest mining students. You carry his list to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Great Forge. Thorgrum Borrelson carries you from Thelsamar over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges to the mountain fortress. For many young mountaineers and travelers, this is their first flight on a gryphon. At the Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe carves the students' names into ceremonial honorary picks. These honors recognize their hard work in Loch Modan's quarries and mines.

quest:6392.text: Return to Brock. You carry Brock Stoneseeker’s missive to Ironforge and receive Honorary Picks for his apprentices. Gryth Thurden can fly you back to Thelsamar. Gryth Thurden oversees Ironforge’s gryphon flights from the city’s central platform. To fly to Thelsamar, you first need to have met its handler, Thorgrum Borrelson. Then Gryth can carry you and the picks over the mountains, returning Brock’s message and tools to the Loch. Brock Stoneseeker teaches mining in Thelsamar and needs tools for his apprentices. The Honorary Picks will let young miners work the rich copper and tin veins in the hills around the Loch.

quest:6395.text: Marla's Last Wish. In Deathknell, Marla's Last Wish brings a husband and wife together in death. Novice Elreth asks you to find Samuel Fipps, still bound to the Scourge, so he may be buried beside Marla. The Forsaken honor the ties of life and set themselves apart from the Scourge. Before the Third War, Marla and Samuel Fipps were husband and wife in Lordaeron. The war devastated their home, and when the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed. He rose as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath, but Samuel killed her in his frenzy. She bore him no hatred. Novice Elreth remembers Marla's final wish: to rest beside Samuel in the Deathknell graveyard. Novice Elreth sends you northeast of Deathknell, where Samuel Fipps still wanders among a ruined campsite. Ending his torment removes a Scourge minion from the valley. Then his remains can be carried back to Marla's resting place. Elreth believes that honoring the dead and their final wishes sets the newly freed Forsaken apart from the Scourge.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, The Forgotten Heirloom is a pocket watch left behind as the Furlbrows fled their farm. Recovering it gives them a chance to reclaim something personal amid the chaos. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts from the pumpkin patches woke them in the night, leaving little time to gather what they could carry. In their flight, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. Returning for a keepsake could mean death for ordinary folk. You can take the pocket watch from the wardrobe and restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:6401.text: Kaya's Alive. Makaba Flathoof has word that Kaya Flathoof survived the Grimtotem attack in Stonetalon. He sends you to Sun Rock Retreat, where her aunt Tammra Windfield waits anxiously. The Grimtotem strike along Stonetalon's contested trails. When their village came under attack, young Kaya Flathoof was feared dead or taken by the renegades. Her rescue brings relief while tribes still fight among the crags. Makaba Flathoof sends you from Kaya to Sun Rock Retreat with news of her safety. Her aunt, Tammra Windfield, waits there anxiously for word from the trails. Your message comforts the family and keeps the remote Horde outpost connected.

quest:6421.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Kobolds dig for Resonite in the Stonetalon Mountains, while Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat fears a growing unrest in the earth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal watches the Stonetalon peaks and feels the earth stir. An unnatural agitation rises from the southeast. In Boulderslide Ravine, kobolds have abandoned their usual foraging and now dig fiercely for Resonite, a rare mineral from beneath the surface. Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts past the kobolds and into the cave's deepest reaches. He asks them to bring back raw samples and learn why the kobolds mine with such frenzy.

quest:6441.text: Satyr Horns. At Splintertree Post, Satyr Horns offer Pixel a chance to trade in Ratchet. The traveling goblin seeks them for the journey south to the port town. At Splintertree Post, Pixel sees a chance to profit while resting between travels. Satyr horns fetch a high price in Ratchet, and Pixel wants them for the journey back south to the port town. Rather than face the corrupted creatures, Pixel hires passing adventurers to bring back sixteen intact horns. Demonic satyrs haunt scattered, fel-tainted ruins across Ashenvale. They are remnants of a betrayal during the ancient sundering. You can search their strongholds at Night Run, the fortified camp of Satyrnaar, and the shadowed groves of Xavian. Pixel seeks horns from any of these places for Ratchet's merchant wharves.

quest:6442.text: Naga at the Zoram Strand. Along Ashenvale's coast, Naga threaten the Horde's hold at Zoram Strand. From Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai seeks to drive the Wrathtail away from the sunken ruins of ancient Zoram. The Horde's hold at Zoram Strand is fragile. The outpost stands amid hostile night elf territory and bitter woodland fighting, yet its coast gives the Horde a link to the sea. Now aggressive naga have crawled ashore. They could cut off that route and overwhelm the small garrison before its defenses are ready. Beneath Zoram Strand's sandy shoals lie the shattered remains of Zoram, an ancient elven city swallowed by the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Marukai and the outpost's defenders do not know why the Wrathtail have come from the deep trenches now. Their sudden interest in the sunken ruins threatens anyone walking above them. Marukai sees a simple fight for survival. With swords and tridents drawn, reason matters little. She demands twenty severed heads from the Wrathtail. She hopes force will drive the naga back into the depths and secure the shore for the Horde.

quest:6461.text: Blood Feeders. In Malaka'jin, Blood Feeders begin with butchered game drawing Deepmoss spiders toward the trolls' camps. Xen'Zilla asks the Horde to drive the predators back from the settlement. The trolls founded Malaka'jin as a frontier outpost in southeastern Stonetalon Mountains, where they could hunt. The craggy slopes offer plenty of game, but its meat draws nocturnal predators into camp. Deepmoss spiders are aggressive arachnids native to the crags and canyons to the north. Under cover of darkness, they slip in to scavenge the trolls' stores or hunt the hunters themselves. Xen'Zilla asks you to track the predators north into the mountain passes. That will help keep Malaka'jin safe and protect its supplies. Deepmoss Creepers and Venomspitters gather thickest around the rocky ravines and webs of Sishir Canyon. Thin their numbers, and the brood will retreat from the settlement. Then the hunters can rest without fearing an ambush from the shadows.

quest:6462.text: Troll Charm. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa mourns kin slain on the road and seeks their stolen sacred charms. The Thistlefur furbolgs took the talismans into their den. You are at Zoram'gar Outpost, a remote Horde refuge on Ashenvale's western coast. Woodland paths make the way dangerous. A party of Darkspear trolls never arrived after the Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed them. Mitsuwa accepts that his kin have died and will meet him in the afterlife. Yet the furbolgs stole their sacred charms, and he cannot abide the insult. Troll charms and talismans mark identity, give spiritual protection, and bind their bearers to the Loa. Mitsuwa sees a troll without her charm as hollow and worthless, like an orc without battle scars. The Thistlefur furbolgs carried the stolen charms to Thistlefur Hold, deep in the caves beyond Thistlefur Village. There they hid the talismans in chests, far from their rightful owners.

quest:6482.text: Freedom to Ruul. In northern Ashenvale, Ruul waits in a cage deep inside Thistlefur Hold. He needs a Horde ally to help him fight through the corrupted furbolg den and reach safety. Ruul Snowhoof, a druid, is trapped in Thistlefur Hold. While exploring the corrupted woods of northern Ashenvale in bear form, he strayed too close to the den. The corrupted furbolgs had lost their ancestral wisdom and, driven by feral paranoia, mistook him for an ordinary beast. They caged and starved him instead of honoring him, draining his magic until he could no longer break free alone.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends you east to Lakeshire, where a contact may know where the Defias Brotherhood hides. The People's Militia cannot find who directs the bandits. Gryan Stoutmantle needs the cartel's inner circle and its commander exposed before the thieves can be stopped. Wiley the Black waits upstairs at the Lakeshire inn. Stoutmantle trusts the rogue's underworld ties to reveal the Brotherhood's hideouts. Whether Wiley can offer a lead is still uncertain.

quest:6523.text: Protect Kaya. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaya Flathoof is held captive among hostile Grimtotem tauren. Horde adventurers guide her along dangerous trails to Camp Aparaje, then tell her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof, that she survived. Kaya Flathoof was captured deep in Grimtotem territory in the Stonetalon Mountains. The tauren clans are divided by bitter rivalries, and few face sharper hostility than the Grimtotem. Kaya has escaped captivity, but friendly ground lies beyond trails watched by enemies and predators. An armed escort gives her the best hope of getting through. Kaya aims for Camp Aparaje in the eastern Stonetalon Mountains. From there, she knows the way home and can continue on her own. You guide her along paths where ambushes threaten, helping her avoid recapture on the way to safety.

quest:6541.text: Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to Kadrak's watch tower. The orc prepares recruits for the fighting ahead near the Ashenvale border. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands. Beyond it, the Horde looks toward Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork sends fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the tower on the northern border, where Kadrak is stationed. Kadrak watches the southern approach to Ashenvale and organizes reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. Splintertree Post and an outpost along the Zoram Strand help strengthen the Horde's presence in the timber-rich woodlands. Native night elves resist them fiercely.

quest:6542.text: Report to Kadrak. At Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip sends Horde warriors north to Kadrak's watch post. The journey leads from Stonetalon's crags to Ashenvale, where the Horde holds outposts at Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand. Darn Talongrip watches the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers from Malaka'jin. The orc sends capable fighters passing through Stonetalon toward the northern Barrens watch tower. Ashenvale is the greater pressure point. There, night elf sentinels clash with Warsong lumber gatherers, and the Horde needs fighters as the struggle for the forest continues. Kadrak oversees Horde troop movements from a watch tower in the northern Barrens, where the savannah meets Ashenvale. The Horde holds outposts at the Zoram Strand in the west and Splintertree Post to the north. Kadrak coordinates supplies and troops, and sends urgent reports across the contested forest.

quest:6543.text: The Warsong Reports. Couriers from the northern Barrens carry Kadrak's orders and gather the Warsong Reports across Ashenvale. Their field observations come from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs this route because the Barrens cannot provide the timber Orgrimmar requires. So the Warsong clan has pressed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help them keep in step. Yet night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails. Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates the defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

quest:6544.text: Torek's Assault. At Silverwing Outpost, Torek leads a strike against the night elves. Sent by Splintertree Post, the orc raider means to break Sentinel resistance and kill their commander, Duriel Moonfire, in Ashenvale's border war. Across Ashenvale, the Horde's lumber camps and the native night elves are locked in a growing border war. Torek gathers raiders from Splintertree just outside Silverwing Outpost, aiming to break the Alliance's defenses. He charges before the night elves can counterattack or gather strength for a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post. Silverwing Outpost is a woodland garrison held by Silverwing Sentinels and fierce elven warriors. Torek sets his sights on their leader, Duriel Moonfire. If she falls, the local night elf command loses its head, and the raiders can report their bloody victory to Ertog Ragetusk at Splintertree Post.

quest:6545.text: Warsong Runner Update. Across Ashenvale, Warsong Runner Update warns of mounting pressure on the Warsong Clan's border. The report alerts commanders to increasingly bold naga attacks on Horde outposts. Across Ashenvale, Warsong scouts and runners watch the fighting and keep supply lines open. Night elf sentinels and the forest make their work dangerous, so frontier commanders need news quickly. Couriers carry dispatches to remote garrisons and to commanders such as Kadrak at the Mor'shan Rampart. Horde defenders expect night elves among the trees, yet outpost sentries report bolder naga attacks. The serpentine invaders strike from waterways and ancient ruins, testing barricades and drawing defenders from forest and border patrols. A dispatch to the Mor'shan Rampart warns of these coordinated assaults from the water.

quest:6548.text: Avenge My Village. Makaba Flathoof calls on Horde travelers to answer the Grimtotem assault in southeastern Stonetalon. He barely escaped, cut off from his kin and surrounded by the dead. Now he seeks vengeance at the camp of the ruffians and hired sellswords. Near the Barrens border, Makaba Flathoof is the lone survivor of a massacre in Stonetalon's red stone passes. Grimtotem raiders struck without warning and slaughtered nearly everyone in his settlement. Makaba fought back and brought down several attackers. Then they drove him into hiding with little more than his life and his wrath. The Grimtotem have long troubled the tauren tribes united under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Unlike Mulgore's peaceful nomads, their warbands use ruthless ruffians and opportunistic mercenaries to seize territory and strike isolated settlements. Makaba has no thought of diplomacy or tribal kinship now. Only blood repaid with blood can answer his grief.

quest:6608.text: You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to seek his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak teaches fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel. So he admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. Artisan fishing calls for knowledge beyond the city and the Horde. Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. Though the Horde and Alliance clash across Kalimdor, he warns you not to harm or eat Nat. Nat camps on an islet in Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

quest:6611.text: To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends seasoned Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. In the Drag, Zamja trains cooks and feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she knows, Zamja has taught all she can. She sends her pupil to Tanaris, where only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance. Gadgetzan is a steam-powered trading hub in Tanaris, run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Dirge Quikcleave works inside the town tavern. The eccentric goblin butcher has an unusual palate and no squeamishness about food. Across Kalimdor, he is known for making hearty meals from monstrous desert creatures and sometimes scraps of leather, food for hardened adventurers.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. At Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Horde Trauma calls skilled healers to the front lines. Doctor Gregory Victor needs hands ready to save lives under extreme pressure. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Arnok, the orc first aid trainer, tells proficient healers they have caught Doctor Gregory Victor's attention. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from Hammerfall in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok regards the summons as the highest step in a battlefield surgeon's career. At Hammerfall, constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and hostile local factions leave Doctor Victor flooded with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician skips the pleasantries. He sends newcomers into their scrubs to prove their worth in fast, brutal emergency triage.

quest:6625.text:
Alliance Trauma. Across the Alliance, accomplished medics are sent to Theramore Isle for service. There, you study under Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen, chief physician of the Alliance's elite medical corps. Your skill with needle, cloth, and triage has drawn Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen's notice. From Theramore Isle, he leads Alliance Trauma, caring for the wounded in Kalimdor's fiercest warzones and beyond. In Ironforge, Nissa Firestone treats VanHowzen's personal summons as a rare privilege. Theramore Isle faces regional threats, skirmishes, and harsh wilderness, so grievously wounded soldiers arrive in a steady stream.

You cross the sea to Dustwallow Marsh. There, VanHowzen tests how calmly you assess the wounded against his rigorous triage standards.

quest:6629.text: Kill Grundig Darkcloud. At Grimtotem Post, Grundig Darkcloud waits after leading the force that sacked Makaba Flathoof's home. Makaba sends you after Grundig once you have struck down the ruffians and mercenaries. Makaba Flathoof survived the Grimtotem assault on his settlement along the Stonetalon trail, but grief still weighs on him. You have proved yourself against Grimtotem foot soldiers. Now Makaba points you toward Grundig Darkcloud, who led the slaughter that leveled the village and commands a devoted band of brutes. Grundig camps at Grimtotem Post, farther up the mountain road to the west. You climb to the stronghold to avenge Makaba's kin and guard the pass from further violence. There you fight through Grundig's brutes and kill him before his raiders can descend on other vulnerable camps.

quest:6641.text:
Vorsha the Lasher. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Vorsha the Lasher's attacks threaten the Horde's foothold on Ashenvale's coast. The nearby naga honor the hydra with an offering brazier on an offshore island. Muglash means to extinguish its flame and draw Vorsha ashore. On Ashenvale's northwestern coast, Zoram Strand is one of the most dangerous stretches of shore. Zoram'gar Outpost holds a narrow strip there, facing hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Vorsha the Lasher is among the strand's worst threats. The gargantuan hydra strikes the outpost without provocation.

She surges from the surf to crush its defenses and butcher its warriors. Then she vanishes into the deep tides. The nearby naga honor Vorsha's ravenous violence. On a rocky outcrop offshore, they keep an offering brazier burning for her. Muglash, an orc set on ending the outpost's constant harassment, has found a way to draw the hydra out.

Defiling the ritual flame will enrage the naga guardians and Vorsha. In her fury, the hydra will surge to the surface, giving the defenders a chance to draw her into an ambush instead of waiting for another slaughter.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. At Smokywood Pastures' display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is tired of hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours of hearing citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. So he asks passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink. Holiday Spices from Smokywood Pastures peddlers and Small Eggs from wild birds make the cookies. Bring them together with Ice Cold Milk from a local tavern. Then the feast's organizers offer festive cheer and a small token of gratitude.

quest:6984.text: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive thanks for the stolen holiday treats you recovered. Great-father Winter waits to honor those who brought Smokywood Pastures' supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. A shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. Now the treats are recovered and the Abominable Greench is dealt with. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks. Great-father Winter waits beside the holiday tree in the Valley of Strength. The goblins have arranged for him to honor those who rescued the holiday supplies. He gives them a seasonal blessing and a Smokywood Pastures Special Gift.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. In Northshire's northern woods, kobold numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Marshal McBride needs the camps cleared, and the valley's defense depends on fresh volunteers. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey, but he has too few soldiers. So he depends on fresh volunteers like you. Each threat he cannot answer could disrupt the abbey's work or spread into the vineyards nearby. The kobold camps cannot wait. Kobolds are timid, candle-obsessed cave-dwellers who usually pick at underground seams, away from direct sunlight. Now an entire clan has reached the northern timberline. Left alone, their numbers could turn scavenging into open raids. McBride sends you to thin their vanguard and test your resolve to defend the realm.

quest:7025.text: Treats for Greatfather Winter. In Ironforge, the dwarf playing Greatfather Winter asks you for a holiday treat. Bring five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk, and he thanks you with a festive gift. Smokywood Pastures sponsors the Winter Veil festivities in Ironforge. By the holiday tree in the Commons, a performer sits dressed as Greatfather Winter. For hours, he hears holiday wishes from citizens and eager children. He wears the guise of an immortal figure from ancient titan lore and dwarven myth. After hearing requests for gifts all day, the performer grows hungry. He asks for five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. The simple meal gives the exhausted festival worker a moment of relief. Your kindness spreads goodwill through Ironforge.

quest:71.text: Report to Thomas. Guard Thomas waits at the eastern bridge between Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp. The fate of his missing men may show whether the river murlocs threaten more than scouts. With few men to spare at the crossing, Thomas had hoped Malakai and Rolf were only cut off or delayed in the riverlands. Their recovered service medallions leave no such hope. Both guards were slain near the waterways. For months, Stormwind's leaders have treated murlocs as nuisance river-dwellers, focusing instead on bandits and the kingdom's wider borders. Now two armed Stormwind guards have been slaughtered along the inland streams. The medallions show Thomas that Elwynn's eastern frontier faces an active assault, and he calls for a response before the logging routes and settlements are overwhelmed.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker needs help finding his missing crew. His appeal sends you across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met trouble along Darkshore’s wild coast. Darnassus is the grand night elven capital, and home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge who study Kalimdor’s ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to uncover ancient artifacts. Weeks have passed without word or a progress report. Greywhisker fears dangers have overtaken his field crew. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as an eccentric hobby. Discoveries in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that a terrifying ancient force threatens Azeroth from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. So the work in Darkshore’s ruins is more than scholarship. The expedition seeks to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated dangers buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:743.text: Dangers of the Windfury. Ruul Eagletalon tests your readiness against the Windfury harpies in Mulgore. Their speed and claws will challenge you on the southeastern cliffs before you leave the tauren homeland. Ruul Eagletalon watches travelers pass through Mulgore from Bloodhoof Village. He asks those coming of age or preparing to travel farther to prove their combat instincts. Beyond Mulgore's sheltered valleys, survival calls for poise against cunning foes. Ruul measures your mettle against the land's fiercest native predators. The Windfury harpies roost along Mulgore's southeastern mountain rim, far from the beaten trails. They threaten wandering wildlife and isolated travelers. They dive swiftly and strike with razor-sharp claws as they hunt for fresh flesh. Defeat them and bring back their talons to prove you can overcome a settled threat and answer an attack from the air.

quest:745.text: Sharing the Land. In Mulgore, Baine Bloodhoof asks you to stop the Palemane gnolls from killing the plains' wildlife. You help protect the herds and the tauren way of living with the Earth Mother. The tauren take only what they need from the land and honor the Earth Mother in all things. Palemane gnolls have settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west. Across the plains, they slaughter wildlife and leave carcasses behind. Their wasteful hunts harm the grasslands' balance and threaten the peaceful home the tauren are building in Mulgore. Baine Bloodhoof tried to settle the matter peacefully by speaking with the Palemane gnolls. They rejected every attempt and continued killing wildlife. Now he sends young braves to their hunting camps to stop the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer lasting harm. When you return, Baine teaches that life should never be taken out of malice, though it may be needed to keep harmony. Life and death form a circle. Every guardian of Mulgore must carry that truth.

quest:746.text: Dwarven Digging. At Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof fears the prospectors will anger Mulgore's beasts and scar its sacred earth. He asks young Horde defenders to break their picks and halt the digging. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have marked a site in Mulgore's hills. The Explorer's League searches Kalimdor for titan relics and secrets of the earthen. Often, they give little thought to the lands or customs of those who live there. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother, worthy of reverence rather than excavation for stone and metal. Baine Bloodhoof sees the dwarves' machines and blasting as a threat to the plains' fragile balance. Their noise agitates local wildlife and drives the kodos into frenzy. So the tauren mean to smash the prospectors' picks at the forges. The broken tools will warn the dwarves and halt the digging before lasting harm is done.

quest:747.text: The Hunt Begins. At Camp Narache, young hunters gather food and feathers for their people. Grull Hawkwind sends you to hunt plainstriders on Red Cloud Mesa, where the village relies on what its young can provide. Tauren hunt on Red Cloud Mesa to feed and clothe their people. They value the stalk and chase as tests of discipline and as sport. When Camp Narache's stores run low, young hunters gather plainstrider meat for cooking and feathers for tribal garments. Grull Hawkwind judges newcomers who hope to leave Red Cloud Mesa for Mulgore's wider plains. Before they can meet his father, Chief Hawkwind, he asks them to prove their ability. A successful hunt shows self-reliance and helps support the tribe.

quest:748.text: Poison Water. Tainted wells in Mulgore threaten the water that sustains the tauren and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village asks young Horde defenders to gather parts for a cleansing totem. Goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted Mulgore’s wells. The pollution threatens the water that sustains the tauren tribes and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder in Bloodhoof Village, has discovered the harm. The tauren settled here recently, and these wells are vital to life on their sacred plains. Mull turns to tauren shamanism to cleanse the Winterhoof Water Well. He needs a ritual totem made with the strength of Mulgore’s native beasts. You gather paws from prairie wolves and talons from mature plainstriders on the southwestern plains. The land’s own strength will be brought against the pollution.

quest:749.text: The Ravaged Caravan. Near Stonebull Lake, The Ravaged Caravan still draws Venture Company salvagers. Tauren warriors burned the convoy after losing companions in a skirmish. Intact crates show the scale of Venture Company operations in Mulgore. Tauren warriors burned a Venture Company convoy after an earlier skirmish cost them two companions. Morin Cloudstalker and his warriors struck swiftly, then set the wagons alight to drive out the armed intruders. They left the wreckage behind, believing the fire would consume whatever the goblins had come to haul. Venture Company salvagers have returned to the blackened wreckage, suggesting the fire failed to destroy all the cargo. Morin sends scouts to inspect the remains rather than risk more lives blindly. Intact crates among the soot-stained debris bear the Venture Company Mining Division insignia. They are packed for shipment to central processing facilities.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Orgrimmar, skilled leatherworkers learn how Onyxia's scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak teaches them a rare cloak-making technique for the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, but the black dragonflight remains a threat. Her scaled hide resists draconic flame. So Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor instead of letting them go to waste.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly honors the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft of making a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can work her hide. When a master leatherworker comes to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer sees how much that skill may matter in battles ahead.

quest:751.text: The Ravaged Caravan. In Mulgore, The Ravaged Caravan leaves the Bloodhoof Outrunners with proof of an illegal foothold in tauren territory. The Venture Company is stripping the land's mineral wealth, and the Outrunners prepare to defend their ancestral plains. East of Bloodhoof Village, a ravaged caravan lies beside the road. Inside a sealed supply crate are mined ore and minerals, along with a bound sheaf of Venture Company documents. The papers prove the company has begun mining deep in Mulgore's tranquil valleys without permission. Morin Cloudstalker and his fellow Outrunners watch Mulgore's borders with care. They fear outside factions will exploit their peaceful homeland. When Morin receives the recovered documents, they confirm his worst fears. Smoke rising over the eastern foothills signals an escalating commercial invasion. The tauren must push back against the defilers before their hills are gutted entirely.

quest:752.text: A Humble Task. On the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind asks a young adventurer to check on his mother. His pressing tribal concerns keep him at Camp Narache, so he sends you southeast to the well where Greatmother Hawkwind went for water. Every member of the tribe is expected to share in its harmony and do their part. For young tauren, duty begins with care for the community, not only prowess against quilboars or predators. Chief Hawkwind is bound to his post by the work of leading and defending the camp. So he trusts young adventurers to watch over the elders. The wells beyond the encampment provide water for the Red Cloud Mesa. Greatmother Hawkwind left Camp Narache early in the morning to fetch fresh water from a spring southeast of the encampment. Territorial wildlife and Bristleback quilboars range across the land. When an elder is away for hours, Chief Hawkwind grows concerned and sends you to make sure she is unharmed.

quest:753.text: A Humble Task. At Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren carry well water to Camp Narache at Greatmother Hawkwind's request. The work teaches humility and care for the tribe. Greatmother Hawkwind tends her duties beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa's southern edge. Age has slowed her, though she has walked many trails across the plains. When young tauren who hope to defend their people meet her, she turns their energy toward the needs of the community. Service lets them prove themselves by caring for others. You carry a filled pitcher northwest to Camp Narache and give it to Chief Hawkwind, the settlement's leader and Greatmother Hawkwind's son. Across Mulgore's dry plains, life depends on shared labor and steady supplies of fresh water. Carrying a burden for an elder shows respect for the people whose care holds the tribe together. When you bring his mother's water to Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sees more than a chore completed. Tauren custom asks those who would champion their people in distant lands to begin with humility and a ready hand. Your quiet discipline catches the chief's eye. He recommends you for the Rites of the Earthmother, spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

quest:754.text: Winterhoof Cleansing. The Winterhoof Water Well in Mulgore has been fouled. Mull Thunderhorn gives you a consecrated totem in Bloodhoof Village to cleanse it. Goblin operations have tainted the nearby springs, and clearing this well is the first step toward healing central Mulgore’s waters. Mulgore’s grassy plains rely on ancestral wells to sustain wild game and scattered tauren tribes. The Venture Company has recently brought its industrial mercenaries into the hills southeast of Bloodhoof Village. Their work has contaminated local aquifers and left the Winterhoof Water Well toxic. Wild beasts avoid its water, and nearby camps face danger if the corruption spreads through the earth. Mull Thunderhorn carves a cleansing totem and blesses it in the name of the Earth Mother. Armed Venture Company goons have claimed the spring, so you must brave them to reach the well. Set the totem at its head, and it will drive out the foul runoff. Then clean water can rise from deep within the earth.

quest:756.text: Thunderhorn Totem. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn asks young Horde champions to help shape a sacred cleansing totem. Venture Company pollution spreads through Mulgore's wells, and predator claws will bind the plains' primal strength into its wood. Mull Thunderhorn needs natural claws for a cleansing totem. The Venture Company poisons Mulgore's water as it exploits the land, and Mull works to make a remedy. Prairie stalkers and flatland cougars roam east and west of Bloodhoof Village. Their claws carry the predators' natural essence and channel their raw, uncorrupted vigor into the totem. Tauren tradition sets hunting for food or spiritual balance apart from the goblins' wholesale plunder. Mull believes native predators' pure way of hunting can help cleanse corrupted earth. Goblin machinery fouls the springs with oil and industrial waste. The beasts' natural strength can provide the spiritual force to restore the Thunderhorn Water Well.

quest:757.text: Rite of Strength. At Camp Narache, young tauren face the Rite of Strength against Bristleback quilboar. They bring belts to Chief Hawkwind to prove their courage and defend the tribe. Seer Graytongue calls young tauren to begin the Rites of the Earthmother with the Rite of Strength. To earn recognition from the tribal elders and acceptance in Thunder Bluff, each initiate must face this duty. The trial tests whether they can meet the tribe's mortal foes with courage and defend Red Cloud Mesa. East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is home to Bristleback quilboar. They trespass on ancestral lands, ambush hunting parties and raid camp supplies under cover of darkness. You are asked to slay them and bring back their belts. The belts prove your valor and help keep the settlement secure.

quest:758.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing. In Mulgore, Thunderhorn Cleansing calls you to purify the Thunderhorn Water Well. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the rite, and the Thunderhorn ancestors give their thanks when the spring is clean. Water wells sustain the tauren tribes who have settled Mulgore's grasslands. When poison taints an underground spring, the wildlife and nearby settlements suffer. The Thunderhorn Water Well lies north of Bloodhoof Village, and its waters need spiritual cleansing. Mull Thunderhorn makes a Cleansing Totem for the rite. Carry it to the poisoned spring and channel ancestral power through it to drive out the toxins. When the cleansing succeeds, the Thunderhorn ancestors visit Mull in a dream and give thanks.

quest:759.text: Wildmane Totem. At the Wildmane Well, Mull Thunderhorn seeks to heal Mulgore's last poisoned waters. He needs prairie wolf alpha teeth for a totem that can cleanse them. The Wildmane Well is the last poisoned source in central Mulgore. Mull Thunderhorn has gathered what he needs for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, yet poisoned water still harms migrating wildlife and settlements across the plains. Powerful ingredients from the land are needed to restore its balance. Prairie wolf alphas roam Mulgore's grasslands, especially beneath the high bluffs below Thunder Bluff. Mull Thunderhorn needs their teeth for a cleansing totem meant for the northern waters. Their strength and endurance will lend the totem the power of these fierce hunters. For tauren, taking from the land's creatures carries solemn weight. Mull Thunderhorn sees the alpha teeth as a necessity, not a conquest. The predators' sacrifice may help heal the Earth Mother's poisoned waters.

quest:76.text: The Jasperlode Mine. Scouts are bound for The Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn, where kobolds may have spread. Marshal Dughan needs to know how far they have reached. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora. Its stone and metal supply the kingdom. With Stormwind guards needed on town patrols, Dughan sends independent adventurers east to learn whether kobolds have taken this mine too. Scouts reaching Jasperlode's chambers find kobolds have driven out the human miners and fortified the dark passages. Marshal Dughan faces another blow as the crisis grows. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and royal troops remain withheld from outlying lands. The local garrison has too few soldiers to clear the mine. The kingdom's heart is left short of minerals and hemmed in by threats.

quest:760.text:
Wildmane Cleansing. In Mulgore, the tauren's cleansing work reaches its final well. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village sends you north with the completed Wildmane Totem to cleanse the poisoned water and protect the tauren's way of life. Mulgore's wells sustain the herds, the soil, and the tauren tribes gathered around Thunder Bluff. The Venture Company and encroaching goblins have fouled them with toxic industrial runoff. The tauren elders see the danger to their people and their land.

The Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are purified. Now the Wildmane Water Well remains, the third and final corrupted site. Its waters still need spiritual cleansing. The Wildmane Cleansing Totem is made from elements gathered across the region. It draws on the restoring power of ancestral spirits and elemental earth. Plant it beside the foul waters north of Thunder Bluff. The ritual disperses chemicals, draws out toxins, and revives the natural flow.

The cleansing guards the tauren against disease. It also makes clear they will not tolerate the despoiling of their sacred ground.

quest:761.text: Swoop Hunting. Harken Windtotem asks you to track swoops across Mulgore. Their quills test patience, cleverness, and marksmanship, and honor the trials of the Earth Mother. Across Mulgore's open grasslands, swoops test a hunter's eye. These large birds blend into sky and plain, wheeling overhead or skimming low through tall grass. They demand focus and swift feet, unlike lumbering plainstriders or grazing kodo. Young hunters pursue them to prove their skill and earn standing among the tribes. Harken Windtotem asks for trophy quills to teach discipline, not to cull wildlife. Tauren carry tokens from a hard-won stalk as signs of cleverness and perseverance. Unblemished quills presented to the elders in Bloodhoof Village show a hunter can sustain and defend the community. Swift hooves and sharp senses prepare them for the wider world.

quest:763.text: Rites of the Earthmother. At Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you beyond Red Cloud Mesa to continue the Rites of the Earthmother. After the first trials, you carry a carved totem north to Bloodhoof Village and Baine Bloodhoof. Young tauren have tested their strength at Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa for generations. The first trials teach discipline and resolve. Yet the sacred Rites of the Earthmother reach beyond surviving the mesa's wildlife. Chief Hawkwind knows when an initiate is ready to leave the sheltered hunting grounds and join the wider community. Chief Hawkwind gives you a hand-carved totem to introduce you on the road from Narache to the central settlements. Carry it down the winding path to Bloodhoof Village and present yourself to Baine Bloodhoof, the young chieftain and son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. The totem is your credential and seal of approval. It marks your readiness for the rites of spirit and wisdom ahead.

quest:764.text: The Venture Co.. In Mulgore's eastern hills, goblins dig despite the tauren's refusal. The Venture Co. brings them in force to quarry the Earth Mother's soil, and Morin Cloudstalker calls for a lethal answer. The tauren honor Mulgore as part of the Earth Mother. They value its open plains and the balance of its wildlife. When the Venture Company asks to blast and excavate the hills for ore, the tribes refuse. The company ignores them and brings machinery, laborers, and overseers into the eastern ridges to mine without permission. Morin Cloudstalker and the other tauren scouts see no use in further appeals once the mining begins. Documents from a ravaged Venture Co. caravan confirm the operation. Morin sends you against the overseers who crack the whips and the laborers who drive the drills. He means for the company to pay dearly for trespassing.

quest:765.text: Supervisor Fizsprocket. In Mulgore, Morin Cloudstalker calls for help against the Venture Company mine. Documents from a ruined caravan show a plan to drive the tauren from their homeland, and Morin needs Supervisor Fizsprocket's clipboard. A Venture Company caravan lies destroyed, and its documents reveal a plan to drive the tauren from Mulgore. The company wants the plains and the veins beneath them for itself. It means to take their resources without the tauren in its way.

quest:766.text: Mazzranache. In Bloodhoof Village, Mazzranache's bite leaves Maur Raincaller feverish and near death. A generation ago, the plainstrider haunted his grandfather's tales. Now Maur suffers delirious nightmares as the venom threatens his life. Maur Raincaller knew Mazzranache only through his grandfather's tales. The elder tauren spoke of a savage plainstrider with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite unlike that of most Mulgore wildlife. Then Maur met the beast on the open grass.
