His grandfather's warning came true, and the bite left him badly wounded as he struggled to reach safety. Mazzranache's venom brings Maur a high fever and nightmarish delirium. He needs a remedy before the infection turns fatal. Traditional tauren medicine draws on the vitality of local beasts, so Maur needs a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, a plainstrider scale, and a swoop gizzard. Together, these parts can make a brew to halt the necrotic spread and nurse him back to health.

quest:767.text: Rite of Vision. Baine Bloodhoof sends travelers across Mulgore to seek Zarlman Two-Moons before the Rite of Vision. The trial belongs to the Rites of the Earthmother, and elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff regard it as a sign of spiritual readiness. For generations, the nomadic tauren have followed the Earthmother’s guidance across Kalimdor’s plains. Now they have gathered within Mulgore’s safe borders, where spiritual traditions remain at the heart of their society. Earlier trials test an initiate’s strength and bond with the hunt. The Rite of Vision turns inward, calling young tauren and honored allies to commune with the spirits. Before seeking a vision, an initiate needs guidance in the ancient ways. In Bloodhoof Village, the revered shaman Zarlman Two-Moons offers that counsel. Baine Bloodhoof entrusts travelers to his care. Zarlman recognizes those who walk the ancestors’ path, then gives them the first rites and sacred preparations to look beyond the physical world.

quest:768.text: Gathering Leather. On Thunder Bluff, Veren Tallstrider asks hunters to bring light leather for the capital. He trades crafted goods for the hides, following the tauren way of making clothing and armor from the plains hunt. Thunder Bluff needs skilled hands to make clothing and armor for its growing population. Veren Tallstrider works skins into useful goods and asks young hunters returning from the plains to bring him their quarry. Their hunts help supply the capital and feed the tribe. Tauren hunt across the grasslands to feed, clothe, and shelter the tribe. Veren Tallstrider asks hunters who would bring honor to their clan for light leather from local wildlife. In return, he trades crafted goods for twelve well-kept hides, sustaining the ties that bind tauren society.

quest:769.text: Kodo Hide Bag. Veren Tallstrider teaches Thunder Bluff's apprentice leatherworkers a craft drawn from the plains. He asks for cured light leather and sturdy thread. Veren Tallstrider teaches leatherworking on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises. He follows the nomadic way of wasting nothing from the hunt. Bring cured light leather and sturdy thread, and he will teach you. With these basic materials, apprentices show they can make goods to carry survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses. To the tauren, the kodo is a sign of endurance, strength, and steady resolve. Its thick hide guards against brambles, biting wind, and beast claws. Making bags and garments from kodo hide is useful work, and it honors the animal that has fed and carried the Shu'halo across Mulgore's plains for generations.

quest:770.text: The Demon Scarred Cloak. In Mulgore, The Demon Scarred Cloak carries the wounds of Ghost Howl's torment. The hide came from a legendary white wolf scarred by the Burning Legion. Its arrival in Bloodhoof Village brings the beast's troubled story to a close. Ghost Howl is a legendary white wolf whose sorrowful howl carries across Mulgore. The hide left by the beast bears the scars of demonic corruption. Those marks came from desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion. The wounds lingered in Ghost Howl's flesh and spirit long after the Third War. Mulgore's tauren revere the wild beasts of their homeland as children of the Earth Mother. In Bloodhoof Village, Skorn Whitecloud receives the scarred cloak as proof that the tormented predator is dead. He recognizes the skill it took to track and defeat Ghost Howl. Somberly, he hopes the wolf's tortured spirit has found peace.

quest:771.text: Rite of Vision. Across Mulgore, young tauren gather offerings for the Rite of Vision. In Bloodhoof Village, Zarlman Two-Moons guides them as they brew the Water of the Seers and seek counsel from ancestral spirits. Zarlman Two-Moons sends you across Mulgore for well stones and ambercorn. The stones rest near sacred communal wells, while ambercorn falls beneath the roots of ancient trees. To the tauren, these are more than gifts from the land. They carry the Earth Mother's latent magic and lifeblood, ready for the rite. Zarlman combines the well stones and ambercorn to brew the Water of the Seers. You drink it beside the village's tribal flame. The draught clears your mind and summons an ethereal guide. Then you follow the guide across the plains, testing whether you can walk between the physical world and the land's spiritual whispers.

quest:772.text: Rite of Vision. At Bloodhoof Village, young tauren drink the Water of the Seers and glimpse the path before them. A spectral guide rises beside the tribal bonfire. After gathering the ritual herbs and passing the first trials of faith, you receive the Water of the Seers from Zarlman Two-Moons. You drink it before the tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. Keep your mind focused and respectful, and the sacred water opens your sight beyond the physical world. It joins the material and spiritual realms. Once you drink the brew, an ancestral ghost wolf appears in the flames. It neither speaks nor fights, but lopes northwest across Mulgore's rolling plains. Follow its quiet path away from the village and into the rocky hills. There, the hermit Seer Wiserunner waits in secluded meditation. The vision ends when you reach Seer Wiserunner at the mouth of his mountain cavern. The walk across grassy hills tests your patience, your trust in ancestral guidance, and your attunement to the Earth Mother. Pass the rite, and you earn the right to face the Rite of Wisdom, the ultimate test of adulthood.

quest:773.text: Rite of Wisdom. At Red Rocks, the Rite of Wisdom brings the Rites of the Earthmother to their final trial. After the Rite of Vision clears your sight, you travel to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and seek the dead’s blessing. After the Rite of Vision clears your sight, you travel east of Thunder Bluff to Red Rocks. Those buried here fought and died so Mulgore could know peace, and their spirits still linger. Approach their resting place with reverence and seek communion. The hills are guarded by threats as you seek counsel from the honored dead. At Red Rocks’ summit, you commune with an Ancestral Spirit. The meeting tests your spiritual readiness and your place in the generations, not your strength in battle. These spirits fought beside Cairne Bloodhoof to establish Thunder Bluff and protect the tribes. Their blessing marks you as an adult and defender. You are charged with protecting the city and may enter Thunder Bluff with pride.

quest:775.text: Journey into Thunder Bluff. The spirits send you from Mulgore to Thunder Bluff after the Rites of the Earthmother. Cairne Bloodhoof, High Chieftain of the tauren, awaits you there. Across Mulgore, the Rites of the Earthmother test your strength, vision, and wisdom. The trials lead across the plains and through the land’s ancestral sites. When the Ancestral Spirit acknowledges your final rite, you have proved yourself worthy to enter Thunder Bluff as a defender of the tauren people. From the sacred ground where spirits wander, you travel upward to Thunder Bluff. The city crowns red stone mesas, joined by rope bridges and great wooden elevators. Cairne Bloodhoof, High Chieftain of the tauren, awaits you on the High Rise, ready to greet those who have followed the ancestors’ path.

quest:776.text: Rites of the Earthmother. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sends you across Mulgore to track down the great kodo Arra'chea. Even after the old rites, he asks his people to prove their strength, tracking, and devotion anew. Arra'chea's horn shows Cairne you are ready to serve the wider Horde. In Thunder Bluff, a young tauren's childhood gives way to duty. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof asks young hunters to keep proving themselves. Reaching the high bluffs begins a life of service to the United Tauren Tribes. Cairne asks for more than a hunt for small pests: he wants proof of fieldcraft, shown by tracking and cleanly harvesting one of Mulgore's renowned wandering beasts. Arra'chea is a massive, legendary kodo whose looping path crosses the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. Bringing down this great beast takes patient stalking across the open savannah, not brute force alone. Return Arra'chea's horn to the high rise, and Cairne sends skinners and gatherers to use every part of the sacred beast for the city's provisions.

quest:7781.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head reaches Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives it as proof that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory ranks among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. His battle-scarred head is carried back to Stormwind, proof that the Alliance's greatest heroes have brought down the Lord of Blackrock. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs the kingdom from Stormwind Keep's throne room. The dragon's severed head shocks the royal court and commands reverence. The kingdom faces internal political strife and threats from beyond. This victory lifts morale and earns a place in Alliance history.

quest:7782.text: The Lord of Blackrock. At Stormwind's gates, the Alliance gathers to honor its victory over Blackrock. After you report to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon in Stormwind Keep, the heroes make for the Valley of Heroes. Field Marshal Stonebridge is ready to lead the city's public commemoration. Field Marshal Stonebridge raises Nefarian's severed head above the great arches at Stormwind's main entrance. The sight carries across the city, and the Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer inspires defenders, visiting dignitaries, and citizens. They know Deathwing's brood has suffered a crushing blow.

quest:7783.text: The Lord of Blackrock. In Orgrimmar, Nefarian's severed head is brought before Thrall as proof of victory. Its arrival marks the fall of a great enemy of the Horde. Nefarian has fallen at last. He masterminded Blackwing Lair and led the black dragon brood in the Eastern Kingdoms. His battle-scarred head proves his death. For Horde warriors, carrying this prize from the burning heights of Blackrock Mountain across the Great Sea to Durotar brings great honor. The trophy is brought before Warchief Thrall, who knows Blackrock Mountain's corruption well. He freed his people from the internment camps and led them away from the old Horde's demonic bloodlust. Now the son of Deathwing has fallen, and the Blackrock orcs are free of the dark dragon's cruel dominion.

quest:7784.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Before the Horde in Orgrimmar, Nefarian's severed head bears witness to his defeat. Thrall confirms the black dragon's death, then sends you to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength to show the trophy to all. Nefarian's head comes to Orgrimmar after the black dragon falls atop Blackwing Lair. Warchief Thrall confirms that Deathwing's son is dead, then sends you to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength. There, the remains are prepared for all to see. The trophy warns the Horde's enemies and rallies the true Horde.

quest:780.text: The Battleboars. At Camp Narache, young tauren hunt battleboars to guard their lands and feed the tribe's youth. East of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine lies in Bristleback quilboar hands. Tensions between the Shu'halo and the quilboar have grown into open war. The Bristlebacks train vicious battleboars to test tauren borders and trouble their old hunting grounds. Left unchecked, the beasts endanger game trails and Camp Narache alike. Hunting keeps the tauren safe and feeds the tribe. Grull Hawkwind asks the young hunters to bring back the battleboars' snouts and flanks. Even these beasts, trained by quilboar hands, are put to use. Their meat and gristle go into stew for the tribe's youth, turning a quilboar weapon into food for the next generation of tauren defenders.

quest:781.text: Attack on Camp Narache. At Camp Narache, you carry a warning that could give the tauren time to call for aid. The Bristleback quilboar are planning a siege, and Chief Hawkwind needs to know. In Brambleblade Ravine, you find a crude map on the cavern floor. Its dirt-stained markings reveal the Bristleback quilboar plan a long siege against Camp Narache. This is more than a string of scattered attacks. You bring the attack plans to Chief Hawkwind at Camp Narache. Few defenders guard the camp, which shelters young initiates, so Hawkwind prepares to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements. Your warning gives the camp time to prepare for the siege.

quest:783.text: A Threat Within. In Northshire Valley, volunteers answer Stormwind's call as local defenses falter. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride directs the response, and you begin serving on the threatened grounds. Northshire Valley once gave people quiet for prayer, farming, and monastic study. Now it is Elwynn Forest's first defense against unrest at home. Few guards remain nearby, so the Stormwind Guard calls on each willing volunteer who reaches the abbey. Trouble spreads across the surrounding countryside. From Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride directs the valley's defenses as danger grows. Bandits, vermin, and pests from below ground threaten the people nearby. You begin by clearing the ground around the abbey, where these threats press close to the valley's defenders and the place they protect.

quest:784.text: Vanquish the Betrayers. At Tiragarde Keep, Kul Tiran forces still hold a foothold on Durotar's coast. Gar'Thok calls the Horde to strike at Lieutenant Benedict's garrison, whose presence has broken the fragile peace with Theramore. Thrall led the Horde across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. There, he and Lady Jaina Proudmoore fought the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Peace broke when Jaina's estranged father, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, brought Kul Tiras's navy to Durotar. He blamed every orc for the Old Horde's atrocities and seized coastal strongholds, among them Tiragarde Keep. Daelin died at Theramore, but remnants of his fleet still reject any pact and keep their hatred. Tiragarde Keep fell for a time after the Grand Admiral's defeat. Then Kul Tiras reserves under Lieutenant Benedict took it back. The fortress lies between Razor Hill and Sen'jin Village. From there, sailors and marines harass travelers and threaten Durotar's eastern sea approaches. Gar'Thok sees their presence as an immediate danger to Durotar's security. So he calls on Horde warriors to strike at Benedict's command.

quest:786.text: Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Lar Prowltusk has uncovered a plan to strike Durotar's settlements and Orgrimmar. The Kolkar centaurs have divided the invasion plans among three leaders at Kolkar Crag, west of Sen'jin Village. Lar Prowltusk is a troll tracker scouting western Durotar. Under cover of night, he slipped into Kolkar Crag and found the Kolkar centaurs preparing more than scattered coastal raids. Three leaders hold the invasion plans. Their targets are the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar. The Kolkar leaders hold three attack scrolls in their camps in the dry canyons of Kolkar Crag. You are sent to destroy the scrolls before the centaurs can strike. Lar Prowltusk believes the Horde could defeat a full invasion, but burning the plans can spare Durotar's defenders costly fighting as their young nation finds its footing.

quest:787.text: The New Horde. In the Valley of Trials, Eitrigg calls the Horde's newest recruits to the Den. He sends you to Gornek for training and explains why he returned to the Horde and what Thrall hopes it can become. Under Warchief Thrall's orders, Eitrigg watches over the newest hopefuls in the Valley of Trials. After the Second War, he left the Old Horde, sickened by its corruption under the Burning Legion. He lived in quiet exile until humans captured him. Thrall rescued Eitrigg, and the veteran returned when he learned of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism and free of demonic masters. Before you leave the Valley of Trials' harsh canyons, Eitrigg sends you to the shaded cavern called the Den to speak with Gornek. Gornek speaks plainly about how rough new aspirants are. He watches over their training so only those who master discipline and survival reach the wider lands of Durotar.

quest:791.text: Carry Your Weight. Atop the watchtower overlooking Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow asks young Horde adventurers to gather canvas from human and centaur foes. Age and old injuries keep him from the front lines, so he makes supplies to help them on their way. Furl Scornbrow fought beside Warchief Thrall in Durotar and at Mount Hyjal. Age and old injuries have slowed him, and he no longer wields his axe in battle. From the watchtower above Razor Hill, Furl keeps a steady vigil and sounds the alarm when danger comes. Though he has left the front lines, he still serves the next generation of defenders from his post. As the Horde's hold on the region grows stronger, signal horn alerts come less often. Furl has more hours to make useful gear, but sturdy canvas is scarce in Durotar's dry canyons. Along the eastern shore, Kul Tiran interlopers carry canvas in abundance. So do the nomadic Kolkar centaur roaming the plains. Furl salvages canvas from these hostile forces and stitches it into utility bags for active scouts.

quest:792.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Vile Familiars pour from a nearby cavern. Zureetha Fargaze found a hidden Burning Blade coven while watching over the trials. Now recruits hunt the familiars spreading across Durotar's red earth. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls face tests of strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde in the Valley of Trials. They were meant to face scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet a cave to the northeast shelters Burning Blade agents. They have formed a secret coven beneath the valley overseers' watch. Zureetha Fargaze guides newcomers near the Den. She spotted the taint before it could overrun the canyon. Now Vile Familiars pour from the cave mouth and hurl fire at anyone who wanders too close. Before the Horde can root out the hidden masters, young recruits are sent to cut down these lesser servants and keep the valley secure.

quest:794.text: Burning Blade Medallion. Zureetha Fargaze sends young Horde initiates into the Valley of Trials cave, where the Burning Blade has gathered. They face a hidden cultist and seek the Burning Blade Medallion. Its presence points to demonic corruption near the Horde. Young orcs and trolls face trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials. A menace gathers nearby. Through divination, the warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses that the vile familiars on the northern bluffs are only the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep in a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has formed a hidden coven. Its followers practice dark arts and keep dangerous relics of demonic power.

quest:8.text: A Rogue's Deal. In Deathknell, Calvin Montague asks you to carry an unmarked message to Brill. He calls it a simple delivery and promises generous coin. Calvin Montague lounges among Deathknell's graves and ruined chapels. He says Scourge zombies and creeping spiders have worn him down, then asks you to carry an unmarked letter to Brill. He promises generous coin. For a newly awakened Forsaken, it seems a simple way to reach the region's main town.

quest:804.text: Sarkoth. On the Valley of Trials' high bluffs, Hana'zua waits for help after Sarkoth's venom leaves him stranded. You have slain the scorpid that wounded him. Now Gornek needs word at the Den so aid can reach the scout. Hana'zua, a Darkspear scout, lies stranded on the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Sarkoth's venom has left him too weak to descend the treacherous paths alone. You have avenged him by slaying the scorpid, but he still cannot cross the arid stones without help. So a passing initiate must carry word down to the training encampment. Gornek waits at the Den for your report. When he hears of Hana'zua's plight, he recognizes the danger from Sarkoth and organizes aid for the scout. Horde commanders honor those who set aside their own training to defend and rescue a fallen stranger. Such conduct proves an initiate's worth before they march into Durotar proper.

quest:805.text: Report to Sen'jin Village. Zureetha Fargaze sends young initiates from the Valley of Trials to warn the Darkspear trolls in Sen'jin Village. Burning Blade cultists have been active in the valley. Master Gadrin tells them dark magic threatens the nearby Echo Isles. After proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven, young initiates leave the Valley of Trials. Zureetha Fargaze sees that demons in the sacred proving grounds are no isolated nuisance. They point to a blight spreading across Durotar. She sends the proven fighters east past the ravine's mouth, then south toward the coast, to warn the Darkspear tribe.

quest:806.text: Dark Storms. In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists corrupt the land from Thunder Ridge. Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill has learned that Fizzle Darkstorm leads them, and asks you to end his threat. Orgnil Soulscar has learned that dark magic has taken hold in Thunder Ridge, northwest of Razor Hill. Burning Blade cultists prowl its ravine while young Horde defenders guard Durotar’s borders. The cultists bring ruin to the wildlife and land. Fizzle Darkstorm is a goblin warlock allied with the Burning Blade. He directs the cultists in Thunder Ridge and wields fel power for the cult, not for commerce or cartel interests. Slay him and bring back his twisted claw. Then Orgnil will know the ravine’s leaders have been struck down.

quest:808.text: Minshina's Skull. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin hears his dead brother Minshina's desperate cries. Zalazane slew Minshina on the Echo Isles and bound his spirit to his severed skull. You can free him from torment by reclaiming the skull from Zalazane's ritual grounds. Master Gadrin is one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village. Yet dark visions torment him. His brother Minshina fell when Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles. Minshina died in the conflict, but death brought him no peace. Troll tradition and voodoo mysticism hold that a spirit can remain bound after the body dies. Now Minshina's tormented voice reaches Gadrin in his dreams, pleading to be saved from a fate worse than death. Zalazane does more than kill his former brethren. He traps their souls to fuel his dark sorcery. He bound Minshina's spirit to his own skull, now set in a circle of power on the largest of the Echo Isles. Hexed trolls guard the circle as candles burn through the rites. The skull focuses Zalazane's twisted mojo. While it remains there, Minshina is captive to the witch doctor's will.

quest:809.text: Ak'Zeloth. Near Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade sends you into the Barrens as demonic corruption stirs. His contact waits near the border. Neeru Fireblade says the Burning Blade still threatens the Horde with demonic corruption. You have brought him a Burning Blade insignia collar from Durotar, and now he sends you into the Barrens. A cult gathers around the Demon Seed, an artifact of vile power. Neeru wants you to find his contact near the border.

quest:812.text: Need for a Cure. On Durotar’s northwestern cliffs, Rhinag is poisoned and far from the cure he needs. The Darkspear troll has little time before the venom kills him, so he sends a passing courier to Orgrimmar for Kor'ghan’s remedy. Rhinag fought venomtail scorpids near Durotar’s border when one stung him. Their venom can kill in less than an hour. The poison keeps him from walking to Orgrimmar, leaving his survival to a traveler who reaches his remote camp in time. Rhinag sends you beneath Orgrimmar to the Cleft of Shadow, where Kor'ghan knows how to counter the poisons of Durotar’s wastes. Kor'ghan can brew a cure, though he rarely helps those who have not proved themselves.

quest:813.text: Finding the Antidote. Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar races to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. You gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids beyond the city walls before their venom proves fatal. Durotar's wilds are unforgiving, and survival depends on preparing for their dangers. Rhinag, a Darkspear troll, was hunting in Durotar when venomtail scorpids struck him. Their venom acts quickly, and he needs aid at once. Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter in Orgrimmar, must brew a draught before the poison kills him. Mature venomtail scorpids outside Orgrimmar's gates carry the sacs Kor'ghan needs for an antidote. He says there will be time to chastise Rhinag for going unprepared, but each moment matters now. Bring the sacs back into the city so Kor'ghan can brew a draught for the dying hunter.

quest:816.text: Lost But Not Forgotten. Misha Tor'kren waits at her Durotar homestead for news of her son, Kron. He went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River, and she fears the worst. Misha Tor'kren lives at a farmstead northwest of Razor Hill. Days ago, her son Kron went west to hunt fierce crocolisks along the Southfury River, near the Barrens border. Misha warned him how deadly the beasts were, but pride drove him to prove his strength. No one has seen him since.

quest:817.text: Practical Prey. Vel'rin Fang calls for tiger hides from the Echo Isles to supply Sen'jin Village. The Darkspear's numbers grow, and their stores run low. Along Durotar's harsh coast, the Darkspear of Sen'jin Village make every resource last. Tiger pelts become tents, blankets and armor. Refugees arrive and scouts return, thinning the village stores. So leatherworker Vel'rin Fang sends hunters to bring back more hides. The Darkspear hunt Durotar's tigers only when the tribe needs more supplies. Their hunters cross the water to the Echo Isles and track the predators there. For the trolls, each hunt also tests patience, discipline and skill in the wild.

quest:818.text: A Solvent Spirit. In Sen'jin Village, Master Vornal tests those who seek his teaching as his sight fades. He sends them to Durotar's coast for makrura eyes and crawler mucus, measuring their patience and resolve. Master Vornal lives in Sen'jin Village, where age has dimmed his sight. Primal magic once came easily to him, but now he relies on alchemy to sharpen his perceptions and weave his arts. His body weakens, yet the stubborn troll refuses an apprentice. He says neither the Darkspear nor Durotar's orcs have produced anyone worthy of his teaching. Vornal asks for raw materials from Durotar's harsh coast: intact makrura eyes and vials of crawler mucus. Taking undamaged eyes from armored, snapping makrura calls for careful strikes. Gathering enough mucus tests whether a would-be pupil can endure tedious work. For Vornal, the hunt is less about reagents than learning who can keep their focus. For Master Vornal, time and patience measure strength. He expects brash youths to grow frustrated or abandon the work. Pristine ingredients brought back to Sen'jin Village show survival skills along the dangerous reefs of the Echo Isles channel. They also show the discipline needed to master alchemy's subtle arts.

quest:819.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In the Barrens, Chen Stormstout’s marked keg lies abandoned. Its discovery recalls the brewmaster’s old ties to Durotar. Across the dry Barrens, travelers sometimes find an abandoned wooden barrel. Razormane quilboar and Kolkar centaur leave ordinary casks behind, but this one is carefully made and bears a plaque: “Chen Stormstout - May your spirit be raised and always raise your spirits.” It is an odd relic beneath Kalimdor’s sun. To learn how it came here, you seek someone who knows brewing. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn recognizes the keg’s craft and names Chen Stormstout as its owner. Chen is a wandering Pandaren who traveled with Rexxar during the battles that secured Durotar for Thrall’s Horde. Years have passed since Chen walked Kalimdor’s red earth. Yet seasoned brewers still remember his recipes and wandering spirit.

quest:821.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn hopes to bring Chen Stormstout's potent brew back with wild Barrens ingredients. A marked keg recalls Chen Stormstout to Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet. Chen entrusted the secrets of his namesake brew to Drohn's mentor, who passed them on to Drohn. The recipe calls for raw, potent parts from the Barrens' fierce wildlife. To those outside the brewing trade, that is an unusual choice.

quest:823.text: Report to Orgnil. Master Gadrin sends a warning from Sen'jin Village to Razor Hill about the Burning Blade. Demonic corruption is spreading through Durotar. Sen'jin Village has troubles of its own, especially Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles. Yet the Burning Blade threatens more than the village. Demonic corruption has been uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and Master Gadrin knows the danger cannot be faced alone. So he sends you north along the road to Razor Hill, where orc authorities watch over Durotar. Orgnil Soulscar is at Razor Hill's military encampment, charged with rooting out evils in Durotar and guarding its central lands. When you bring Gadrin's warning, Orgnil joins the reports from Sen'jin Village and the Valley of Trials. The Burning Blade is dangerously close. He quickly gathers forces to break up the cultists before their rituals can unseat the young nation.

quest:825.text: From The Wreckage..... Gar'Thok sends Horde scouts to the Scuttle Coast wrecks to recover Gnomish Tools. The Horde hopes to study Alliance engineering and put that knowledge to use. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore brought Kul Tiras's fleet to Kalimdor. Its ships crowded the shore near Tiragarde Keep. After his defeat, broken hulls sank along the Scuttle Coast. The surviving Kul Tiran soldiers fortify the keep, while the wrecks lie scattered on the shoals beneath the tide. Alliance ingenuity can give its enemies an edge over orcish strength, iron, and blood. Gnomish technicians sailed with the expeditionary fleet and fitted its ships with complex machinery and precise tools. Gar'Thok wants the Horde to recover those tools from the wrecks. Then its craftspeople can learn how they work. Gar'Thok sends the salvaged tools by caravan from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There, Horde craftspeople and tacticians hope to study the gnomish instruments. They seek ways to counter Alliance devices in future conflicts and strengthen their own industries.

quest:826.text: Zalazane. On the Echo Isles, dark magic has driven Zalazane mad and turned him against his tribe. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village calls Horde champions to end the witch doctor's rule. Zalazane enslaved his fellow tribesmen, seized the Darkspear trolls' rightful home, and drove them into exile on Durotar's coast. After fleeing their sunken island, the Darkspear followed Thrall across the Great Sea and settled on the Echo Isles, just off Durotar's southeast coast. Zalazane was once a respected and powerful witch doctor, but he hungered for power. His hexes enslaved the minds of his kin, and violence followed. Vol'jin led those who remained free, yet they were driven from their ancestral camps and forced to build a temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village. From his hilltop stronghold on the largest Echo Isle, Zalazane still sends raiding parties across the channel. They seize more Darkspear and bring them under his control. The captured trolls become mindless voodoo and hexed thralls, lost to their tribe. Master Gadrin sees a threat to more than Darkspear land: Zalazane endangers the tribe's survival. Until his severed head is brought before the elders, no Darkspear can be safe.

quest:827.text: Skull Rock. Margoz sends you east of Orgrimmar, where Burning Blade cultists hold Skull Rock. They bind themselves to dark magic with painful demonic devices. Margoz needs the cursed artifacts to study the cult near the capital. In northeastern Durotar, Burning Blade cultists gather close to Orgrimmar's gates. Their cave lies among the hills, away from the open roads but near the Warchief's seat. The cult has long plagued orcish society, and now its followers perform rituals in the tunnels. Nearby, the Warchief's scouts keep watch. Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks. The metal bands scorch and brand their flesh. Margoz believes the pain and fel sorcery attune their wearers to demonic power. He asks you to recover the collars so he can study the spells and bindings that empower them.

quest:828.text: Margoz. In northern Durotar, Margoz keeps watch for the Burning Blade's growing threat. After the clash with fel corruption at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar sends champions to seek the shaman at his lonely camp before they strike a nearby cultist stronghold. Margoz's counsel reveals Skull Rock as the Burning Blade's concealed cavern base. After Thunder Ridge revealed the depth of fel taint, Orgnil Soulscar sees that strength alone cannot cleanse Durotar. So he sends champions to Margoz, an experienced orc shaman at a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill. Between Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz watches the northern reaches for dark omens that Orgrimmar's busy warriors often miss. Margoz knows where the Burning Blade has built its power in northern Durotar: Skull Rock, a concealed cavern system carved into the mountain cliffs outside Orgrimmar's southern gates. The cultists are closer to Thrall's capital than the Warchief's guards realize. Hidden passages there could shelter a demonic ambush, so Margoz gives counsel to those sent against the coven before they enter.

quest:829.text: Neeru Fireblade. In Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade studies dark arts he claims can guard the Horde. Margoz sends you from Durotar with a Searing Collar taken from the Burning Blade, hoping the warlock can explain its demonic power. Margoz has reached the edge of shamanic craft. The collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock bear demonic sorcery he cannot unravel. Shamans draw on the elements and ancestral spirits. So Margoz sends you to a warlock in the capital to learn what the collars do. Beneath Orgrimmar's red cliffs lies the Cleft of Shadow. Warlocks and other practitioners of forbidden magic work there beneath Thrall's wary eye. Neeru Fireblade lives in the cavern and says he studies fel power to thwart demonic threats. When you bring him the collar, his curiosity turns Durotar's investigation toward the warlock enclave.

quest:83.text: Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs linen for her tailoring. She asks you to recover bandanas from Defias bandits so she can keep making goods for travelers. Across Elwynn, Defias bandits wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire make do with cheap burlap masks. The linen gives Sara workable cloth for her tailoring. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs textiles for her trade. Taking bandanas from Defias camps scattered through the woods supplies her with cloth and helps check the bandits' encroachment.

quest:830.text: The Admiral's Orders. On Durotar’s coast, the Admiral’s Orders carry word of a threat to the young Horde. Sealed by the late Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, they show that the Kul Tiran garrison is organized and entrenched. Gar'Thok in Razor Hill needs to know what they contain. On the upper floors of Tiragarde Keep, a heavy chest holds an aged envelope under Lieutenant Benedict’s watch. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore sealed it with his crest. Its parchment gives naval commands from Kul Tiras’s bloody invasion of Durotar. Though the Grand Admiral fell at Theramore, his officers still hold their fortifications and cling to their mission against the Horde settlement.

quest:8311.text: Hallow's End Treats for Jesper!. During Hallow's End, Jesper lies sick in Stormwind and longs for treats and fun beyond the orphanage. Too ill to go out, he asks Alliance adventurers to gather sweets for him. Jesper lies sick in Stormwind's orphanage in Cathedral Square during Hallow's End. While the children gather sweets across Azeroth, he must stay inside. So he hopes passing adventurers will share the holiday spirit and bring him treats. To bring Jesper the sweets he hopes for, you travel beyond Elwynn Forest. You visit the innkeepers of Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus, then the gnome exile Talvash del Kissel. Each asks you to perform before giving you a treat. You cluck like a chicken, dance, flex, or chug like a train, and earn regional sweets such as Stormwind Nougat and Gnomeregan Gumdrops.

quest:832.text: Burning Shadows. In Skull Rock, the Eye of Burning Shadow carries warnings from the Burning Blade. Its voice threatens Gazz'uz with Neeru Fireblade's wrath. After Gazz'uz falls deep within Skull Rock, the Eye of Burning Shadow is found among his remains. The stone carries a voice into the mind of anyone who holds it. The speaker demands a report from Gazz'uz. His secret work east of Orgrimmar has been compromised.

quest:833.text: A Sacred Burial. At Red Rocks in eastern Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem calls on Horde adventurers to protect the sacred burial grounds. Bristleback quilboar have overrun the graves of tauren warriors who gave their lives founding and defending Thunder Bluff. Red Rocks is among Mulgore's most revered sanctuaries, set in the crags beneath the eastern mountains. Only the most valiant tauren are laid to rest there. These legendary warriors shed blood to protect their tribes and their chieftains, and to carve out a lasting homeland atop Thunder Bluff's mesas. To the Shu'halo, disturbing their rest insults both tradition and the Earth Mother. The nomadic Bristleback quilboar have long contested tauren control over central Kalimdor. Their recent push into Red Rocks is a grave escalation. Bands of Bristleback Interlopers have crept onto the holy grounds, ravaging the earth and disturbing the resting places. Lorekeeper Raintotem is too aged to drive them away alone, so young Horde champions must take up arms and defend the honored dead.

quest:834.text: Winds in the Desert. Rezlak waits in Durotar for a stolen supply caravan. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon and scattered the building materials among the cliffs. Rezlak came from Ratchet at Chief Engineer Gazlowe's command, to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land makes fortification work hard enough. Now shipments vanish before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with. Dustwind harpies ambushed the latest supply run in Razorwind Canyon. They roost in the high ravines beside the road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, then swoop on passing wagons. They neither eat nor destroy the freight. Instead, they hoard crates and sacks near their nests, where the supplies wait for anyone willing to fight through their territory.

quest:835.text: Securing the Lines. Near Razorwind Canyon, Rezlak needs the goblin supply routes through Durotar kept safe. Harpies in Drygulch Ravine intercept and plunder caravans, so he hires help to drive them out. Dustwind harpies make travel through Durotar’s dry valleys dangerous. Rezlak oversees regional supply operations for his boss, Gazlowe. From their roost in Drygulch Ravine, the harpies raid caravans in Razorwind Canyon and seize shipments before they reach their destinations. Rezlak believes the right price can get anything done. He hires adventurers to break the roost by eliminating Dustwind Savages and Dustwind Storm Witches, rather than entering the canyon himself. Clearing the harpies keeps trade corridors open and secures shipments of engineering gadgets. It also points helpful travelers toward greater opportunities in Ratchet.

quest:8353.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. At Hallow's End, Innkeeper Firebrew asks Ironforge visitors to cluck for a mint for Jesper, a young orphan in Stormwind. Alliance champions gather sweets from their capitals to bring him cheer. Jesper is sick, orphaned in Stormwind, and longs for Hallow's End sweets. Alliance champions gather treats for him from innkeepers in their capitals. So seasoned adventurers have reason to go door to door during the harvest-to-winter celebration. Innkeeper Firebrew keeps the Ironforge Mints at the Stonefire Tavern in Ironforge's Commons. A polite request won't do. Visitors flap their arms and cluck like chickens before he parts with one. The performance gives the tavern's patrons a laugh, and the mint helps bring holiday cheer to Jesper.

quest:8354.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. At Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a sweet to travelers helping an ailing child. Earn the Undercity Mint by setting dignity aside and flapping like a chicken. Laughter is scarce in the Undercity, built beneath Lordaeron's ruins by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End comes, even the grim folk of the Trade Quarter join the revelry. Innkeeper Norman keeps Undercity Mints for travelers gathering treats for Spoops, a sick orphan who needs holiday cheer. Innkeeper Norman will not hand a treat to seasoned adventurers without a show. He believes grown warriors and spellcasters should earn their sweets. So the petitioner must mimic a barnyard chicken right before his counter.

quest:8355.text: Incoming Gumdrop. Talvash del Kissel keeps a Gnomeregan Gumdrop in Ironforge for a sick child in Stormwind. To earn it, you must give him a convincing train impression. At Hallow’s End, trick-or-treaters visit the Alliance strongholds for treats. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel keeps the Gnomeregan Gumdrop. He feels for the young orphan who hopes to receive it. Yet Talvash asks you to bring some mischief to the holiday with a convincing train impression. Jesper is an ailing orphan in Stormwind City, hoping for four treats from across the Alliance. He wants nougat from Stormwind, a mint from Ironforge, marzipan from Darnassus, and a gumdrop from Gnomeregan. Your locomotive impression entertains Talvash and earns you the gumdrop. It brings Jesper closer to his holiday wish.

quest:8356.text: Flexing for Nougat. At the Gilded Rose, Innkeeper Allison asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. During Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for Jesper, an orphan in Stormwind. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind. The holiday marks the turn of the seasons and guards against dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers offer traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick. At the Gilded Rose in the Trade District, Innkeeper Allison asks for a show before handing out holiday candy. You are gathering sweets for Jesper, an orphaned boy. Allison playfully comments on your physique and asks you to flex your muscles. When you do, she gives you a piece of chewy Stormwind Nougat.

quest:8357.text: Dancing for Marzipan. At Hallow's End, travelers in Darnassus gather sweets for Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the trick-or-treat custom, asking for a dance before she gives her Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus takes on a lighter spirit. It is the sacred forest city of the long-lived night elves. You come seeking sweets for Jesper, a sick child recovering in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the season's custom, even for a child in need. First, she asks for a trick. Saelienne asks you to dance on the inn floor before she gives you Darnassus Marzipan. Your performance earns the sweet for the holiday care package bound for Jesper.

quest:8359.text: Flexing for Nougat. In Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka trades nougat for a little show. During Hallow's End, you flex for a sweet meant to cheer Spoops, a bedridden child. Hallow's End fills Azeroth's capitals with pranks and sweet-gathering. In Orgrimmar's inn, Innkeeper Gryshka keeps holiday sweets for those who join the custom. Your travels may bring dragons and dark sorcery, but here the bargain is plain: perform a trick or leave without a treat. Innkeeper Gryshka asks you to show Orcish strength before she gives you Orgrimmar Nougat for young Spoops. Whatever disguise or armor you wear, strike a muscular pose. Even the Horde's feared fighters can amuse the common folk for candy.

quest:8360.text: Dancing for Marzipan. During Hallow's End, Innkeeper Pala asks visitors to dance for Thunder Bluff Marzipan. The treat is meant for a sick orphan, and the custom brings holiday cheer to Mulgore's high mesas. During Hallow's End, Innkeeper Pala keeps the trick-or-treat custom in Thunder Bluff. You come seeking a sweet for an ailing child, but Pala asks for a festive dance first. Then she gives you Thunder Bluff Marzipan. For Pala, the custom is simple. Step forward and dance to earn a sweet. Once you have entertained her, she gives you the marzipan and warm wishes for the sick youth waiting for it.

quest:84.text: Back to Billy. Bernice Stonefield sends you across the road with a pork belly pie for Billy Maclure. He has information about her missing necklace, and the delivery carries on the feud between their families in central Elwynn Forest. The feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without one. She hands you the pie with plain irritation. Bernice hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

quest:840.text: Conscript of the Horde. Along Durotar’s western road, recruits head toward the Barrens under the name Conscript of the Horde. Takrin Pathseeker watches beyond Razor Hill and gives them a letter for Kargal Battlescar, whose outpost guards the crossing. You have proved your strength around Razor Hill, and now you are called west to serve the wider Horde. Takrin Pathseeker watches the road out of Durotar for his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. He gives capable travelers a recruitment letter to carry across the Southfury River. For a recruit, it marks a first formal assignment beyond the orcs’ new homeland. Kargal Battlescar holds the outpost beyond the bridge, between Durotar’s red canyons and the dry Barrens. He gathers recruits to guard the frontier, where centaur, quilboar, and Alliance expeditions test the border. Yet the Horde needs more than guards there. Raw manpower is also bound for the settlement of the Crossroads.

quest:842.text:
Crossroads Conscription. Kargal Battlescar sends recruits west from the Far Watch Post to report at Crossroads Conscription. With his signed letter, you make for Sergra Darkthorn at the Barrens’ central hub. After you prove your worth, Kargal Battlescar sends you west from the Far Watch Post. He gives you a signed letter of recruitment for the journey along the packed dirt road through the Barrens’ arid brush. The road reaches a central junction where the Crossroads links northern Kalimdor with the southern wilderness. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn receives new arrivals. Warchief Thrall chose the sharp-tongued orc shaman to oversee its operations. Kargal Battlescar grumbles that she is difficult and talks too much, though Thrall holds her in high esteem.

Sergra is fierce and unyielding. She reminds recruits, especially arrogant men, that female warriors and leaders stand as equals in Thrall’s Horde. Insolence has no place here.

quest:844.text: Plainstrider Menace. East of the Crossroads, plainstriders threaten the outpost’s food stores. Sergra Darkthorn sends new Horde arrivals to hunt them, giving the newcomers their first measure of the Barrens. The Crossroads coordinates supplies across Kalimdor. Now plainstriders east of the outpost are picking at its food crates. Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman, sends newly arrived Horde adventurers to hunt the birds before they damage the stores. The settlement depends on those provisions. Sergra Darkthorn uses the hunt to test newcomers and protect the settlement’s supplies. To her, plainstriders are simple prey, fit to teach young hunters to endure the elements and track quarry across the sun-baked plains. Bringing back their sharp beaks shows patience and the basic martial skill needed to face fiercer beasts of the Barrens.

quest:845.text: The Zhevra. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde warriors to hunt zhevra. Their trial prepares them for the Barrens' more dangerous beasts. After the plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn sets you after tougher prey. Zhevras run in herds across the northern and southern Barrens. They are swift and stubborn, though not the savanna's fiercest beasts. Their kicks can break bone. Sergra uses the hunt to test your growing skill. She asks for four intact hooves as proof of the kill. A zhevra's rear kick can knock a grown tauren onto their haunches. Pass this trial, and you draw closer to facing the plains' predatory prowlers.

quest:848.text: Fungal Spores. At the Barrens oases, Horde adventurers gather Fungal Spores for Apothecary Helbrim of the Royal Apothecary Society. Strange, mutative energies flow through the springs and alter local plants into potent reagents. Helbrim seeks the specimens to brew concoctions for his colleague in Thunder Bluff. The Barrens is dry savanna, yet the Forgotten Pools, Lushwater Oasis, and Stagnant Oasis brim with unnatural life. A curious surge of life energy flows from their waters, warping and invigorating plants and beasts that drink there. Laden mushrooms grow along the muddy banks and absorb those currents. Their spores hold rare properties that draw passing alchemists. Apothecary Helbrim works at the Crossroads, far from the Undercity, yet remains devoted to the Royal Apothecary Society's research. He gathers the altered spores because native Kalimdor reagents have strange potency, then uses them to craft powerful mixtures. The specimens are bound for Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, as part of the Forsaken's scientific work across allied lands.

quest:85.text: Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield looks for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the family across the road, and asks you to find him. The Stonefields and Maclures live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but goodwill between them is scarce. When “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield finds her cherished necklace missing, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain Billy Maclure came onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

quest:850.text: Kolkar Leaders. Regthar Deathgate moves against Kolkar leaders gathering strength in the Barrens. The nomadic centaur have plagued the tauren for generations. Now new chieftains are uniting scattered bands into a military threat, and Regthar sends Horde champions against Barak Kodobane at the Forgotten Pools before his influence spreads. Centaur have terrorized Kalimdor for countless years. Before Thrall's Horde arrived and turned the tide, they drove the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction. In the Barrens, the dominant Kolkar tribe usually roams in scattered marauding bands. Now aggressive chieftains are joining those bands together, making raiders strong enough to challenge the Horde's fortified outposts. Regthar Deathgate, an orc warrior, is stationed in an encampment west of the Crossroads. He knows boldness and brute force hold the Kolkar together. Without strong commanders, their raiders fall to infighting. So Regthar sends Horde champions against the leaders to blunt their advance. Barak Kodobane, an ambitious chieftain, is the first target. He is camped near the waters of the Forgotten Pools.

quest:851.text: Verog the Dervish. Across the southern Barrens, Verog the Dervish keeps moving while Regthar Deathgate tries to draw him out. The orc sends Horde champions to strike the Kolkar command tent at the Stagnant Oasis and bring the nomadic leader into the open. After Barak Kodobane fell, Regthar Deathgate turned to the Kolkar warlords still standing. Barak had kept near the northern waters of the Forgotten Pools, but Verog roams the sun-baked plains and seldom stays long in one camp. Horde scouts struggle to follow him across that wide country. So they must make the commander come to them. Verog works from the Kolkar command post at the Stagnant Oasis, southeast of the Crossroads. Regthar sends you against the camp to strike the Kolkar warriors near their command tent. Their alarm calls Verog back to defend the outpost. There, the Horde blades can reach him.

quest:852.text: Hezrul Bloodmark. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark directs the Kolkar incursions across the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate sends you to end his command and break the centaur's hold on the region. Barak Kodobane and Verog the Dervish have fallen. Hezrul Bloodmark remains the Kolkar's paramount chieftain in the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate calls him brutal and cunning, the spearhead of the centaur incursions across the savanna. The Horde hopes his death will sow chaos and break the Kolkar ranks beyond repair before they overwhelm Horde settlements. Hezrul commands his warbands from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. Watering holes are scarce in the Barrens, so this oasis is vital to survival. It is also a strategic hub and a staging ground for Kolkar raiders. On Hezrul's own ground, you deny the centaur their most vital stronghold and sever their hold on the southern trails.

quest:853.text: Apothecary Zamah. In Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah awaits a fragile brew from the Barrens. It must reach her laboratory beneath Spirit Rise before it loses its strength. Apothecary Helbrim has turned fungal blooms from the Barrens oases into a delicate emulsion. The brew weakens soon after it is made. Helbrim cannot reach Mulgore in time, so he entrusts the flask to a reliable runner bound for Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Zamah works in the Pools of Vision, a cavern beneath Spirit Rise's sacred heights. Forsaken mages and priests share this refuge underground. Below the tauren sanctuary, the Royal Apothecary Society quietly studies raw materials gathered across the continent.

quest:854.text: Journey to the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Kirge Sternhorn sends travelers north to aid Thork at the Crossroads. Their road leads from Mulgore into the Barrens, where the Horde’s struggles widen. At Camp Taurajo, many tauren first meet the Barrens beyond Mulgore. Just beyond the mountain pass, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches travelers descend into the dry grasslands. When Kirge sees one ready to go farther, Kirge points north along the dusty trade route to the Crossroads. The tauren of Thunder Bluff and Thrall’s new Horde now share their fortunes. Kirge says their fates are bound together, and orcs at the Crossroads need reinforcements as they struggle to establish an outpost. At the settlement, Thork welcomes travelers from even the high bluffs. He is ready to test their strength against the dangers of the savanna.

quest:855.text: Centaur Bracers. West of the Crossroads, Regthar Deathgate seeks proof against the Kolkar. Their raids threaten Horde control of the central Barrens. The young Horde is still securing its lands across Kalimdor. The Barrens stretch between Durotar and Mulgore, where Kolkar centaurs contest the watering holes and open plains. Their attacks fall on supply trains and scouting parties. From his bunker west of the Crossroads, the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate directs the defense. Regthar asks for proof that Kolkar warriors have fallen. Soldiers who enter Kolkar territory return with bracers taken from slain centaurs. These trophies support claims for Horde bounties, and Regthar hopes they will frighten the surviving raiders.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers hold Ashenvale’s southern border while commanders honor their sacrifices. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks steadfast service, even when battle brings no clear victory. Along Ashenvale’s southern border, the Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar and other capitals honor those who hold their ground against the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle. Far from the front, Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers oversee their forces. Recruiters send new fighters to Warsong Gulch, while quartermasters and tacticians account for veterans returning from hard campaigns. By honoring courage in stalemate or defeat, leaders help keep soldiers committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:858.text: Ignition. At a Venture Company camp in the northern Barrens, a trapped pilot needs the key to get free. The spy has taken a shredder without its ignition key and sends you to fetch one from the site supervisor. Sputtervalve sent a spy into a Venture Company shredder at the northern Barrens drilling grounds. The operative plans to take the machine and study its workings. Yet its steering and movement column remains locked without the ignition key. A goblin worker has spotted the idle shredder, so the hijacker claims its engine has failed. Trapped beneath the glass canopy with workers nearby, the operative points you toward the central derrick. The supervisor keeps spare ignition keys in the upper control office. One of those keys is the pilot’s only way out before the bluff fails.

quest:86.text: Pie for Billy. In Elwynn, you gather meat for Bernice's pie while Billy holds back what he knows about her necklace. Bernice agrees to bake, though she believes Billy stole her family's jewelry. Billy Maclure gives no apology when you ask about the necklace. He will neither return it nor name who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and means to enjoy the bargain. Bernice is furious at the thought of feeding the boy she believes stole her family's jewelry. Still, she agrees to bake before you gather the meat. You bring her meat from wild boars roaming nearby pastures. She sets aside her pride, hoping to get her prized necklace back.

quest:860.text:
Sergra Darkthorn. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits tauren hunters leaving Mulgore behind. Melor Stonehoof sends them north into the Barrens, where danger grows harsher and the Horde's lands reach beyond their home. When their first trials are done, Melor Stonehoof sends young tauren hunters east from Mulgore. Bloodhoof Village and its valleys are familiar ground, where patient tracking has prepared them for what comes next. Now he tells them to pack their gear and cross the mountain pass into the Barrens, leaving their homeland's safety for harsher country. The road winds through red rock canyons before opening onto the Barrens' broad, sun-scorched savanna. There, where Kalimdor's central trade routes meet, the Crossroads is a fortified settlement shared by orcs, trolls, and tauren.

Sergra Darkthorn waits on its eastern side. The experienced orc shaman demands much of the hunters she guides. She teaches those who come to stalk the Barrens' fierce wildlife, testing their eagerness against the discipline the wilderness requires.

quest:861.text: The Hunter's Way. In Mulgore, young adventurers follow The Hunter's Way under Skorn Whitecloud's guidance. You hunt flatland prowlers and take their claws to Melor Stonehoof on Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise, proving your skill and respect for the wild. Among the tauren, hunting is one of the highest honors. It asks for patience, care for the Earth Mother's balance, and respect for the beasts of the plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud tracked across Kalimdor for decades before coming to rest in Mulgore. Seeing young adventurers eager to roam, he gives them a traditional trial to turn ambition into discipline. Flatland prowlers test a candidate's tracking skill. Great cats, they move swiftly and quietly through Mulgore's high grass, then ambush their prey. Bring four sets of claws to show you can find a predator before it finds you. Then turn its own ferocity against it. With the claws gathered, you climb the wooden towers and bridges to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. Melor Stonehoof receives the trophies there. A master tracker, Melor values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom. He accepts the claws as proof that you have the spirit to learn more of Kalimdor's hunting ways.

quest:863.text: The Escape. At the Sludge Fen in northern Barrens, Wizzlecrank fights his way out of a Venture Company drill site. Trapped in a stolen prototype shredder, the goblin pilot needs your protection from company mercenaries. Then you carry word to his contact, Sputtervalve, in Ratchet. At the Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank struggles to control the stolen shredder. He lit the prototype deep inside the Venture Company drill site, but knows little of its levers and switches. The heavy machine lurches across the muddy quarry floor. Its erratic driving and roaring joints alert nearby laborers and armed guards, turning a stealthy escape into a running battle up the excavation pit’s western ramp. Venture Company mercenaries move to stop the stolen prototype. As the machine claws up the slope toward open ground, squads try to intercept and disable it. The shredder lashes out, but cannot withstand their sabotage without your protection. It clears the rim and staggers from the main drilling depression. Soon, the machine suffers a critical failure.

quest:8642.text: Silvervein the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers find Silvervein the Elder on the hills above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. They honor him and the ancient ties among Azeroth’s elder peoples, and he grants them an ancestral blessing. Above Thelsamar, Silvervein keeps watch as travelers honor him. He holds memories from ages past. Though trogg invasions and local disputes trouble Loch Modan, the elder spirit remains peaceful on his overlook. Silvervein welcomes travelers who honor Azeroth’s olden races. His greeting carries ancestral appreciation. To those who pay homage, he offers a commemorative token.

quest:8646.text: Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, you meet Hammershout the Elder in Stormwind's Park and honor the old races with a ceremonial token. Ancestor spirits walk Azeroth for the festival, offering wisdom and blessings to travelers who pay their respects. In Stormwind's Park, Hammershout the Elder recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose. Hammershout the Elder asks only that you acknowledge the past. He is relieved and grateful when people still honor the old races. In return, he gives you a ceremonial token, binding the living to the spirits who came before.

quest:8648.text: Darkcore the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers find Darkcore the Elder in the Undercity and honor Azeroth's ancient spirits. In return, they receive a Coin of Ancestry. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear across the continents. They offer wisdom and blessings to those who seek them. Elder Darkcore dwells in the Undercity's shadowed halls, watching the world as it is now and remembering those who sought its roots. Approaching Elder Darkcore honors an ancient custom. It shows respect for the venerable dead and Azeroth's timeless wardens. In return for the pilgrimage, the spirit gives travelers a Coin of Ancestry, a token of goodwill and enduring memory.

quest:8649.text: Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder greets travelers during the Lunar Festival. They honor Azeroth’s ancient traditions and olden races, and receive a commemorative coin in return. Behind Goldshire’s smithy, a quiet pond lies beneath the forest canopy. There Stormbrow the Elder appears as an honored spirit. Guards, tradesfolk, and travelers pass through the town as visitors come to honor the realm’s long history. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Stormbrow commends travelers who remember those who came before. For honoring the elder peoples’ wisdom and legacy, visitors receive a blessing and a commemorative coin.

quest:865.text: Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix seeks intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. He believes the Barrens raptors owe their cunning to their horns, and pays travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix chases fortune in Ratchet, where goblins are forever trying one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with more craft and coordination than beasts elsewhere. So Mebok decided their intelligence must lie in their horns. He seeks no formal inquiry. He means to turn the idea to profit. Mebok wants undamaged horns from Sunscale Scytheclaws, among the Barrens' deadliest predators. They prowl the southern stretches of the Barrens and the northern borders near Ashenvale. These raptors hunt in packs and defend their territory fiercely. Bringing one down and taking its horns intact calls for skill in battle.

quest:8652.text: Graveborn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Graveborn the Elder waits outside Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Travelers find him among its blighted groves to honor Azeroth’s ancient forebears and receive his blessing and a holiday token. In Tirisfal Glades, the Forsaken make their homes among ruined manors and grave sites. During the Lunar Festival, an ancient spirit appears just outside Brill. Elder Graveborn welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the old ways, even in a land shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead. During the Lunar Festival, spirits from long ago return with wisdom and gratitude. When you approach Elder Graveborn, he says it heartens him that Tirisfal’s people still honor their ancestors despite the land’s decay. He gives you a Coin of Ancestry when you greet him.

quest:8653.text: Goldwell the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Goldwell welcomes travelers in Kharanos and invites them to honor the ancestors. Your visit keeps their memory alive across the snowy dwarven lands. Beside the Thunderbrew Distillery, Elder Goldwell greets those who follow the trade path to Ironforge's gates. Weary travelers, adventurers, and locals all pass before him. He remembers the ancient days when the first mortals walked beneath Azeroth's stars. Goldwell is glad that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds. He thanks you for pausing to honor them. Then he gives you a Coin of Ancestry as a sign of his blessing.

quest:867.text: Harpy Raiders. Across the northwestern Barrens, Witchwing harpies prey on supply caravans. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads sends you after their raiders and roguefeathers, whose talons will prove each kill. Witchwing harpies make the northwestern Barrens dangerous for every caravan. From rocky crags, they swoop on merchant trains and supply wagons. They kill pack animals and seize goods bound for orcish outposts. Darsok Swiftdagger, an orc rogue, has watched the flock's habits and ranks for days. He believes an unfocused attack on their mountain roosts would scatter them. So he means to break the Witchwing from the lowest rank upward, beginning with raiders before turning to their commanders.

quest:8670.text: Runetotem the Elder. In Razor Hill, travelers can honor Runetotem the Elder during the Lunar Festival. This ancestral spirit waits beneath a beam of heavenly light and offers blessings and festival tokens to those who remember the past. During the Lunar Festival, ancient elders appear across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem waits just inside Razor Hill's southern entrance. Starlight falls on her as she watches over the orcish settlement. Travelers may pause to honor the wisdom of those who came before. Pay Elder Runetotem homage and she gives you a festival token of fortune. She also tells you where other spirits can be found. Her directions lead to Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain elsewhere across the continent.

quest:8673.text: Bloodhoof the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder near the bridge north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit offers them a Coin of Ancestry. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears near the bridge north of Bloodhoof Village. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching him. He offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry. On Mulgore’s ancestral lands, Elder Bloodhoof joins the living tauren tribes to the memory of their forebears. Honoring the dead is central to tauren spiritual life. It keeps the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those walking the plains in harmony.

quest:8675.text: Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder watches over Westfall from Sentinel Tower. Travelers climb to honor her as an ancestral spirit, and she recognizes the living with a blessing. Sentinel Hill is Westfall's lone fortified redoubt. Below, weary soldiers and settlers face threats from Defias raiders and roving scavengers across the scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower, watching from above the dust and wind. Anyone may climb and pay her respect. Across Azeroth, the Lunar Festival honors wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits. When you approach, Elder Skychaser recognizes the living spark within you and accepts your homage. She gives you a token of her favor, binding the living to the honored dead.

quest:8677.text: Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder welcomes travelers within Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she carries age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts and watches the young warrior city. Approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or enter as an Alliance traveler. Travelers greet Elder Darkhorn and pay her reverence, and she recognizes the spark of life in them. For honoring the old ways, you receive a Coin of Ancestry and her blessing. The tokens celebrate victory over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength passed down through unbroken bloodlines.

quest:8678.text: Proudhorn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder welcomes visitors on Thunder Bluff's high mesas. Tauren honor him as an ancestral spirit and seek the wisdom of those who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder appears on Thunder Bluff's windblown mesas. Tauren hold their ancestors' voices in the highest regard. They believe ancient leaders and sages remain as spirits, offering guidance and strength to the living. Travelers who climb Thunder Bluff's heights to honor Elder Proudhorn are welcomed as vital flames of life. In return, he gives them a Coin of Ancestry. The coin marks a bond between the enduring past and the living champions who fight for the world's future.

quest:86784.text: Sticks and Bones. Deathguard Bartholomew asks travelers to bring dry branches to Eleanor Shackleton in the western hills of Tirisfal Glades. She camps far from the settlements and knows how to live in the wilds. Between patrols in Tirisfal Glades, Deathguard Bartholomew looks out for Eleanor Shackleton. Deathguards guard against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, yet Bartholomew also cares for his acquaintance. Eleanor spends her unlife in the harsh elements, so he asks you to bring dry branches for her campfire. Eleanor Shackleton survives alone in Tirisfal's blighted wilderness. The Forsaken are undead, yet they still feel the damp, bitter chill rolling off the northern moors. Eleanor's rule is simple: when you think you have enough firewood, gather five times more. Grateful for the extra timber, she lets you keep Bartholomew's basket and shares the warmth of her fire.

quest:8680.text: Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers find Windtotem the Elder on a bluff above Ratchet. She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to elders across Kalimdor. From a grassy hill northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches the goblin docks and the open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below. Above it all, the Barrens winds blow quietly beneath a shaft of celestial light. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder guides wandering mortals, as do the other ancestral spirits. Those who seek her receive her blessing and a token of her favor. She also whispers the way to nearby elders across the continent, including Elder Runetotem and Elder Bloodhoof.

quest:869.text: Raptor Thieves. At the Crossroads, a raptor has stolen the guards' pay, and Gazrog fears another strike. The defenders are left without coin and with no clear answer. The Crossroads relies on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay keeps morale and discipline firm. When silver vanished from the guard tower, the leaders suspected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night. The settlement was stunned, and short of coin. Gazrog cannot fathom why wild beasts would hoard shiny coins, and has no wish to study their ways. The guards are restless without their pay, so he calls for blood to deter another attack. He sends hunters after a dozen raptors across the savannah. He hopes to curb their boldness before the search for the silver begins.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Billy Maclure's careless play has set the Stonefield and Maclure families against each other. His trail leads you to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt. He says he found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and fled to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Yet Goldtooth lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold returns Bernice's necklace and settles the families' dispute. Bernice also gives you an old campaign keepsake left by her late husband.

quest:870.text: The Forgotten Pools. At the Forgotten Pools, life rises in the Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads asks Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids feel unseen forces stirring below the earth. Long ago, the Barrens flourished as fertile land. Ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent and left this region a sun-baked scrubland. Now lush oases are taking root in its dry basin. The Cenarion Circle’s druids find this sudden growth unnatural. They feel powers below the earth pressing upward and stirring plants and wildlife to life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

quest:871.text: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have stopped caravans from Durotar, leaving the outpost short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans carry food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks. Thork sends you to the quilboar bramble dens northeast of the settlement, before they can assault the town walls. Striking their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Hunters weakens the Razormane scouting perimeter and deprives raiding parties of magical and logistical support. These skirmishes buy time while Horde trackers search the brush for the one organizing the raids.

quest:8717.text: Moonwarden the Elder. At the Crossroads, Moonwarden the Elder receives travelers beneath a beam of light. During the Lunar Festival, people honor ancestral spirits and seek his wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. At the Crossroads, a column of light falls around Elder Moonwarden. He is among the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival. Mortals set aside their conflicts then and seek the wisdom of generations past. Elder Moonwarden looks to the stars for answers to earthly mysteries. He offers ancestral blessings and directs seekers to other elders across Kalimdor, including Elder Bloodhoof, Elder High Mountain, Elder Morningdew, and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8718.text: Bladeswift the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Bladeswift the Elder is honored beneath the boughs of Darnassus. Travelers seek his wisdom in the Cenarion Enclave and receive a blessing rooted in night elf tradition. During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth to share wisdom and bless travelers. In Darnassus, Bladeswift the Elder appears among the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave. He looks to the night sky and its mysteries while the living face the trials of the present. Night elves have long read the heavens as reflections of Elune and signs of deeper truths. Bladeswift urges the wise and fortunate to seek answers among the stars. Those who honor him receive a Coin of Ancestry and join a ceremony linking the living with spirits of the past.

quest:872.text: The Disruption Ends. Along the Horde road, Thork orders a strike to end the Razormane raids. Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks from the northern Barrens, and his death is meant to break the warband's hold on the route between Durotar and the Crossroads. The road between Durotar and the Crossroads carries provisions and reinforcements through the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar ambushes threaten that passage. Scout reports name Kreenig Snarlsnout as their leader. His raiding party organizes the attacks, so Thork orders a strike against him to break the warband's unity and secure the road. Kreenig's war party holds craggy hills northeast of the Crossroads. Hardy Razormane Defenders and geomancers who manipulate the arid earth shield his position. Thork orders a breach through their guard and a strike against Kreenig in his redoubt. His tusk will prove the leader's death and warn the plains that the Horde will not accept attacks on its lifelines.

quest:8721.text: Starweave the Elder. In Auberdine, Elder Starweave welcomes visitors during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor Kalimdor's ancestral spirits and seek her wisdom and blessing.
