During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth beneath pillars of celestial light. Elder Starweave joins the night elves in Auberdine, a harbor on Darkshore's coast. Travelers come to honor her and seek guidance from ages past. Elder Starweave looks to the heavens above Kalimdor. She tells visitors that the stars hold answers to mortal doubts and worldly riddles. Those who seek her counsel are urged to look skyward for truth and receive ancestral favor, along with tidings of other wandering spirits across the wild frontier.

quest:8725.text: Riversong the Elder. Beneath a shrine in Astranaar, Riversong the Elder receives pilgrims during the Lunar Festival. The night elf spirit offers wisdom and points them toward honored ancestors across Kalimdor. In Astranaar, an open night elf shrine shelters Riversong the Elder. Light falls through the Ashenvale canopy onto her spirit. During the Lunar Festival, pilgrims gather there to honor those who came before. Riversong the Elder recalls how night elves seek truth and mystery among the stars. She urges patience and contemplation, then guides pilgrims toward other spirits, including Elder Starweave.

quest:875.text: Harpy Lieutenants. In the northern Barrens, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Horde champions against the Witchwing coven. In the Dry Hills, they target the flock’s officers to break its command. After the first clashes with Witchwing raiders, Darsok Swiftdagger turns the Horde’s attack toward the harpies in the Dry Hills. Scouts seek out the Witchwing Slayers who lead the flock. These officers keep lesser harpies in line and direct raids on Horde supply paths. Their deaths are vital to securing the Barrens’ northern approaches. Witchwing Slayers rule through strength, and the most vicious among them wear ornate rings to mark their authority in the matriarchy. Taking the rings proves the lieutenants are dead and disrupts the roost’s coordination. It also warns the coven that attacks on Horde territory will meet decisive retribution.

quest:877.text: The Stagnant Oasis. From the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast to search the Stagnant Oasis. He wants to know whether its murky waters hide a fissure like the one beneath the Forgotten Pools. Tonga Runetotem sends you to search the Stagnant Oasis after a strange fissure is found beneath the Forgotten Pools. He suspects the sudden patches of lush growth across the Barrens have a cause beneath the earth. You search the murky shallows for another opening while predators haunt the water.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield asks you to kill Princess before the sow ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning pig from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, putting the family’s crops at risk. The sow belongs to the Brackwells. She grew enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots. Ma has had enough of Princess eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants the pig put down before the season’s yield is lost. Princess stays at Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead. Protective boars surround her. Get past her guards and bring Ma the distinctive brass collar from Princess’s neck. It will prove the sow can trouble the Stonefield fields no more.

quest:880.text:
Altered Beings. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem investigates strange changes in the Barrens' oasis waters. Fissures beneath the pools may be changing the creatures there, so he asks you to bring him shells from altered snapjaws. Tonga Runetotem seeks the cause of strange changes in the Barrens' oases. Though the savanna is dry, a handful of pools keep fertile ground alive. Beneath the waters, Tonga found peculiar fissures that send out potent energies. He cannot tell whether that force came from outside or rose from deep within the earth.

Now Tonga studies the creatures that drink from and live in the pools. He hopes they will show what the fissures are doing to them. You are sent to the Lushwater Oasis and the Stagnant Oasis to gather altered snapjaw shells. Snapjaws live in the shallows, taking in the strange essence through food and exposure. Their changed carapaces may show Tonga how the fissures affect local wildlife. He hopes the shells will help him understand the disturbance before it spreads farther across Kalimdor.

quest:881.text:
Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, hunters prepare to summon Echeyakee, the white lion of the northern Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde hunters to test their strength against him. Across the central plains, a white-maned lion rules the savannah cats. Taur-ahe speakers call him Whitemist, or Echeyakee. Legend says he moves without a sound, like morning mist over red earth. His strikes are swift, and prey knows neither fear nor suffering. Local hunters honor him as a sign of mercy and swift death. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn trains fledgling warriors. The experienced orc shaman sends them against the king of beasts once they have proven themselves against lesser savannah prowlers.

With a special horn, you travel northeast past the mountain ridges to a graveyard of massive kodo bones. Sound it to challenge Echeyakee and draw the elusive predator from hiding. There, your strength and cunning face their trial.

quest:882.text: Ishamuhale. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you after Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators. Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs. Yet none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. Facing him tests whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity. Ishamuhale will not be found resting in a nest. To draw him out, follow the plains' natural rhythm. Jorn tells you to kill a fresh zhevra and carry its carcass to a lone, withered dead tree on the plains northwest of Ratchet. The scent of blood on the arid wind brings Ishamuhale swiftly to claim his prey. When you bring Ishamuhale's fang back to Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sees a profound spiritual milestone, not merely a victory. Tauren belief holds that overcoming such a fierce predator lets you absorb some of its raw strength. Then the test turns inward. You must bear that might with temperance, honor, and restraint, rather than surrender to blind bloodlust.

quest:8827.text: Winter's Presents. In Ironforge, revelers gather for the Feast of Winter Veil. They direct travelers to Greatfather Winter beside the Smokywood Pastures stalls, where gifts wait beneath the holiday tree. Winter settles over Khaz Modan, and Ironforge fills with cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Revelers and holiday enthusiasts point passersby toward the decorated tree near the Smokywood Pastures vendors. Smokywood Pastures, a goblin enterprise, shares the season with Greatfather Winter. He greets visitors as goblin merchants remind gift recipients that festive treats and seasonal wares make gifts for friends and family.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. The Feast of Winter Veil brings gifts beneath Orgrimmar’s festive tree. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders send Horde heroes to Great-father Winter to receive them. Late-year winds sweep across Durotar as Orgrimmar pauses for the Feast of Winter Veil. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are invited to share in the season’s generosity. Great-father Winter sits near the Smokywood Pastures market among holiday ribbons and packaged cartons. The ancient figure marks the season’s renewal. Nearby, goblin merchants offer seasonal wares and festive treats to visitors.

quest:8846.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. In Ironforge, Field Marshal Snowfall trades commendation signets for supplies bound for the Grand Alliance’s war effort. You can exchange them for field rations, bandages, and combat gear to keep those serving on the home front equipped for the conflicts ahead. Couriers and heroes bring Snowfall commendation signets earned through civic service. He trades them for survival rations and tactical gear bound for the fronts. Armies there need steady supplies as much as courage. Royal heralds offer public honor and civic standing for commendation signets. Snowfall offers another choice: five signets buy field gear, without pomp, glory, or official recognition. These goods help soldiers and volunteers stay alive as they march into hostile lands.

quest:8851.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers what its campaign needs. Workers earn commendation signets for their contributions, and Warlord Gorchuk trades them for supplies to equip the fighters. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers raw goods, weapons, and provisions for a vast campaign. Gatherers and tradesfolk bring bandages, metals, and herbs into the cities. There, military overseers award commendation signets for their work. Each token marks a contribution to the stockpile growing along Orgrimmar's central avenues. Warlord Gorchuk knows the wider war effort needs supplies. Each warrior also needs gear and provisions to survive the march into battle. Fighters can trade their commendation signets back to the Horde's stores for field supplies and surplus materiel. They give up personal recognition for what they need on the front.

quest:886.text: The Barrens Oases. Beneath the Barrens, strange power stirs, and Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem takes heed from Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. He sends travelers east through Mulgore to meet Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads and investigate the new waters. For generations, the Barrens have known drought while Mulgore flourishes under the Earth Mother's care. Now tauren druids on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise feel strange currents waking beneath the plains. Life stirs where it should not, and the Cenarion Circle fears the power behind it may endanger the land and its creatures. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem sends Tonga Runetotem to investigate the strange stirrings. The wilderness is too dangerous for one investigator, so Hamuul asks travelers leaving Mulgore to follow. Go east past Bloodhoof Village and through the mountain passes to the Crossroads, where Tonga waits for news. There, in the Barrens, stands the Horde's busy heart.

quest:8866.text: Bronzebeard the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bronzebeard the Elder beneath Ironforge. His greeting offers wisdom and a token of esteem. Across Khaz Modan, people revere their forebears and their long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with travelers who honor the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard carries the Bronzebeard clan’s stalwart resilience. He is quietly pleased when travelers come to pay their respects and the people honor the lineage of the old races. No great trial or perilous journey is needed. Travelers pause to greet Elder Bronzebeard and offer their good wishes. He returns the greeting with a Coin of Ancestry, a festival token recalling the living bond between the present and the generations who forged Khaz Modan from stone and fire.

quest:887.text: Southsea Freebooters. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, pirates strike goblin trading vessels. Gazlowe hires adventurers to attack the Southsea Freebooters' camp and curb the raids. Pirates on the Merchant Coast are hurting Ratchet's trade. The port lies in central Kalimdor, along the route merchant vessels take between Kalimdor and the eastern continents. South of town, the Southsea Freebooters hold a fortified beach camp. From there, they attack goblin cargo ships coming and going, cutting profits and disrupting local shipping lanes. Gazlowe blames the pirates and the Steamwheedle Cartel's naval leaders. The Trade Princes have spent immense sums on defensive fleets, yet Vice Admiral Grezzlik has failed to patrol the waters effectively. Frustrated by Undermine's slow response, Gazlowe hires independent mercenaries to thin the pirate brigands and cannoneers.

quest:888.text: Stolen Booty. Along Ratchet’s coast, Gazlowe weighs two stolen goods against the rest of the cargo. Boots for local laborers and a delicate lens are needed to finish his observatory. For years, Southsea Freebooters have troubled merchant lanes across the Great Sea. Their fortified camp just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. Pirates intercepted merchant vessels bound for the port and seized valuable supplies from the Steamwheedle Cartel. Some cargo could be counted as a shipping loss. Other goods mattered enough for Gazlowe to hire mercenaries to break into the pirate stronghold. Gazlowe has two practical priorities. Drizzlik sent a needed shipment of boots from Booty Bay for local laborers. The other item is a ground telescopic lens made for the observatory tower overlooking Ratchet. Its twin came safely by caravan through Durotar, but pirates seized this lens at sea. Until it is recovered, the observatory remains an empty frame.

quest:890.text:
The Missing Shipment. In Ratchet, Gazlowe waits for goods sent from Booty Bay across the Great Sea. He sends couriers to Wharfmaster Dizzywig to check the dock records, while the Southsea Freebooters remain a possible cause of the delay. Ratchet is the Steamwheedle Cartel's trading port on Kalimdor. Ships cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay, bringing manufactured goods, exotic supplies, and heavy freight for building and trade. When cargo goes missing, business suffers. Chief Engineer Gazlowe tracks every crate brought into port. The Southsea Freebooters haunt the coast south of Ratchet and often intercept merchant ships. Gazlowe checks his records before accusing the pirates or sending anyone into a fight. He sends his inventory ledger to Wharfmaster Dizzywig at the docks.

Dizzywig oversees the unloading and storage of ship cargo. He can check whether goods were lost at sea or misplaced in a warehouse.

quest:892.text: The Missing Shipment. At Ratchet’s docks, Gazlowe is searching for a shipment that never arrived. Dizzywig’s ledger points away from the harbor and toward the Southsea Freebooters, while Gazlowe prepares to reclaim his cargo. Ratchet’s trade keeps its docks busy and its accounts difficult to manage. When a shipment goes missing, Gazlowe suspects bad harbor accounts or foul play on the piers. Wharfmaster Dizzywig checks the manifest and says his books are clean. The intake records account for everything. The missing goods never reached the dock.

quest:894.text: Samophlange. At a Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve seeks a device called a samophlange. He sends you southwest of the Sludge Fen to find it. In the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve cannot say what the Venture Company is building. The goblin engineer and tinker works in Ratchet, while the rival company experiments southwest of the Sludge Fen. Its workers call one device a samophlange. Sputtervalve knows neither its purpose nor its value, but wants to study its design before his competitors profit from it. Armed overseers, deforesters, and machinery guard the Venture Company research site. Sputtervalve gives you an intercepted operating manual to help shut down the rig safely. At the central control station, you find a locked console fitted with levers, lights, and gauges. Three control valves keep the rig's pressure in order.

quest:895.text: WANTED: Baron Longshore. On Ratchet's docks, Chief Engineer Gazlowe posts a bounty for the pirate Baron Longshore. From Gilneas, Longshore commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. His raids along the Merchant Coast threaten goblin shipping across the region. South of Ratchet, the Southsea Freebooters keep fortified camps along the Merchant Coast. Their pirates harass merchant vessels and disrupt the sea lanes the Steamwheedle Cartel relies on between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and points beyond. Under captains such as Baron Longshore, the raids drain the local goblin administration and threaten trade along the coast. Baron Longshore comes from Gilneas, the isolated human kingdom across the sea. On Kalimdor, he commands the pirate vessel Heedless and leads crews ashore just north of Northwatch Hold. Chief Engineer Gazlowe answers with a bounty and calls for Longshore's identifiable head.

quest:896.text: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has word of a great emerald at Boulder Lode Mine. He wants you to take it from the Venture Company's overseers and share the proceeds. Merchants sailing between Ratchet and Booty Bay bring news to Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Now word has reached him of a huge gem found deep in Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Company strips the northern Barrens for its own gain, so few are likely to ask questions if its finest recent find vanishes. Northeast of the Sludge Fen, laborers work the rocky shaft of Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Co. Overseers and Enforcers hold the Cats Eye Emerald, and an ordinary digger cannot claim so rare a prize. Face the armed managers, take the stone, and bring it to Dizzywig. He can weigh its worth against the market in Undermine.

quest:9.text: The Killing Fields. In Westfall, The Killing Fields begins with Farmer Saldean's crops under threat. Rogue Harvest Watchers overrun his fields and neighboring farms, while the Defias Brotherhood's disruption has left local agriculture in ruin. Many Westfall farmers abandoned their land when bandits and outlaws swept through. Farmer Saldean and his family chose to stay. Thieves are not the only danger on their farm. Harvest Watchers built to tend and guard the grain have run wild, pacing the furrows and attacking anyone who comes near. Farmer Saldean asks passing travelers to dismantle twenty hostile Harvest Watchers across his fields and the adjoining plots. Clearing them gives his harvest a little relief. For now, his farm remains one stubborn hope that Westfall's breadbasket can be reclaimed.

quest:900.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery keeps the Venture Company's digging rig running. Seal its three valves before the central apparatus can be shut down safely. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company's machinery is complex and dangerous. The central console shows that one switch cannot stop its core. First, the feed lines must be handled by hand. Otherwise, the apparatus could fail or explode. Three valves feed the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be sealed by hand against high pressure. As they close, the console's green indicators fade to yellow. Then the central shutoff is safe to engage.

quest:901.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery sits idle, its pressure relieved and valves shut. Tinkerer Sniggles holds the key to open the control unit and free the samophlange within. You have turned the auxiliary valves and relieved the pressure. The dials and gauges have settled, but the housing remains locked against tampering. The goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site holds its key. Tinkerer Sniggles oversees the Venture Company’s equipment at the Sludge Fen. His hut lies just northeast of the main rig, and he keeps the console key there. You need it to open the housing and reach the samophlange.

quest:902.text: Samophlange. At the Venture Company console, you uncover the samophlange and bring it to Ratchet. Its controls and defenses are shut down, and Sputtervalve is ready to examine the delicate device. You find strange engineering behind the Venture Company console's faceplate. Wiring and purposeless tubing crowd the space. Deep inside lies the samophlange, a core component that has baffled engineers across the region. With a firm tug, you free it from its housing and carry it back to the goblin who began the recovery effort.

quest:903.text: Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you to hunt prowlers of the Barrens. Their claws will show whether you can face the land’s greatest beasts. Hunters who have faced plainstriders and zhevras now face Sergra Darkthorn’s test. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the scrub of the central Barrens. Unlike the herds, these great cats hunt. They wait in tall grass and ambush their prey, so unwary travelers can fall to them. Sergra warns you that prowlers know how to hunt. Read the grasses and strike before a cat leaps. Bring Sergra seven prowler claws to prove you have the cunning and quick reflexes to survive Kalimdor’s deadliest wildlife.

quest:905.text: The Angry Scytheclaws. South of the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends hunters against the scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. Carry sunscale raptor feathers to their nests, and show you can face these beasts without fear. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters against the Barrens' beasts. After lesser trials, she sends you south of the Crossroads to hunt vicious sunscale raptors and gather their feathers. Then you carry them southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, deep into raptor territory. Place the feathers in the nests, and prove you can face the scytheclaws without fear. Southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, three raptor nests lie near the Gold Road. Red, blue, and yellow eggs mark the separate clutches. Scytheclaws fiercely defend their nests from anything that draws near. Place feathers from fallen raptors among the eggs, and the challenge is plain to the beasts. After entering the nests, return to the Crossroads. Sergra can see you faced the danger and lived. Walking out of a raptor den takes raw courage. The Barrens test every hunter; each fight may harden you or leave your bones among the kodo ribs scattered across the dirt.

quest:907.text: Enraged Thunder Lizards. In the southern Barrens, thunder lizards roam the plains around Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer calls hunters to face the great beasts and bring back their blood for a wider rite of passage. After defeating the raptor Ishamuhale, you return to Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer, the tauren elder, now tests your strength against the land's largest grazers. Stormsnouts and Thunderheads roam the southern Barrens. Their heavy strides can crush an unwary hunter beneath them. Tauren and orc hunters prize poise, position, and strength against a thunder lizard. Jorn asks you to bring back samples of their potent blood. They prove you stood before the rumbling beasts and survived with your bones unbroken. That trophy opens the way to Jorn's final quarry in the skies.

quest:90902.text: Rediscovering the Light. In Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken paladins learn that the Light still answers them, though it burns. The Holy Light still answers newly risen Forsaken paladins, but it burns their withered bodies. Many once served as champions of the Silver Hand or knights of Lordaeron. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them that powers they once used without thought now bring fierce pain. The Light clashes with the foul magic that sustains undeath, so calling on it takes resolve and endurance. Deathguards in Deathknell suffer grievous wounds fighting mindless zombies, and Forsaken paladins are called to heal them. Aramis teaches that enduring the burning pain is like exercising an atrophied muscle. The paladins bear that agony as a badge of honor and proof that the Light has not forsaken them.

quest:91208.text: Coming to Terms. A frightened former paladin has fled into the hills west of the chapel. Aramis Hammerhand asks a newly risen knight to reach her with compassion. The Silver Hand's former paladins wake among the Forsaken in shock. In life, they served the Holy Light and fought the undead. Now their souls are bound to decomposing flesh. Aramis Hammerhand guides some through this change, while others flee into the Tirisfal wilderness, unable to face their new existence.

quest:91209.text: Continue Your Training. In Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken paladins begin their training before setting out for Brill. Aramis Hammerhand sends them east through Tirisfal Glades, where danger and distrust greet those who wield the Holy Light. After learning martial combat and channeling holy power in Deathknell's graveyard, you travel east through Tirisfal Glades to Brill. The town is the regional outpost and administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the training of those who follow the paladin's path in undeath. Aramis warns that an undead paladin's calling is perilous. Lordaeron still needs defenders against threats from beyond, yet wielding the Holy Light under Sylvanas Windrunner's banner invites suspicion. Many Forsaken suffered agony or death at the hands of holy zealots. Among their undead kin, the Light's presence breeds distrust.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves for venom sacs to learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. So he asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed. Webwood spiders live in and around Shadowthread Cave, where they threaten young night elves in the glen. Gathering their venom can help thin their numbers. It also gives Darnassian researchers evidence of Teldrassil's effect on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks a Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. Venom samples are in hand, but he needs a living specimen to study the unnatural aggression in the forest’s creatures. An egg can be examined safely, without capturing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs living subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have gathered venom from the aggressive spiders, but taking a thrashing giant from the depths could prove deadly for a novice. So Gilshalan asks you to bring an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave. Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a subject they can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to send it to Darnassus with his venom samples for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks Timberling Seeds to test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work joins the quiet efforts of night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, bound closely to the health of the surrounding flora. Usually they reflect the forest's balance in peaceful form. Their recent hostility alarms the local night elves, though no cause is known. Botanist Denalan seeks to learn what stirred them before choosing to cull them. Denalan suspects the blemish lies deep in the ground. He hopes to raise a gentler generation of timberlings in enriched, carefully treated loam. By gathering seeds from wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he will test whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:919.text: Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts spread along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly become aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting them helps protect the grove. Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil. Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

quest:92.text: Redridge Goulash. In Lakeshire, Redridge Goulash feeds a town under strain. During the recent Blackrock orc uprising, Chef Breanna fed the Stormwind garrison until her pantry was bare, and now seeks hearty ingredients in the mountains. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and fierce wild beasts still besiege Lakeshire. When the recent orc uprising began along the ridges, Chef Breanna took charge of feeding the Stormwind brigade stationed in town. The active garrison soon emptied her cupboards, while many hungry mouths remained. With her cupboards bare, Chef Breanna turns to the dangerous wilderness beyond Lakeshire's gates. Her signature goulash calls for tough mountain condor meat, seasoned snouts from Great Goretusks, and crisp leg meat from giant tarantulas prowling the hills.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker sends you to meet Tenaron Stormgrip in Aldrassil. Your work against dangers in the woods has brought the elder's attention. Your fight against venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder wants to see you. Even night elves know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil. Tenaron waits in Aldrassil's highest chamber and looks across Shadowglen's boughs. His concerns reach beyond the glen, to Teldrassil's moonwells and the corruption spreading through the young World Tree's ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip prepares young night elves for their departure from Shadowglen. They draw sacred water in a rite that recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people surrendered there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast took their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history through a rite, so the novices leave with humility and purpose in a changing world. You draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters bear remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary of arcane sorcery, which is forbidden. The wellspring sustains their land, yet recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs help finding missing books. He sends young adventurers to Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, to count the library's archives. But Daniel's thoughts turn to local tradeskills, making a clear answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey keeps scholarly works, spiritual writings, and records of Stormwind's history that survived the First War. Brother Paxton, a careful monk, takes pride in the collection. Now books are missing from the shelves, and he needs a clear count to learn how many are gone. He has little patience for chasing his daydreaming helper. Daniel assists Brother Paxton in the abbey library, but his thoughts stray from parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades and professions of Elwynn Forest, including smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. So when Paxton asks him to count the books, Daniel rambles about local crafters instead of looking for lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan’s retreat by Lake Al’Ameth, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings word of trouble spreading through Teldrassil’s boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al’Ameth. After you gather seeds from nearby timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with one for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave’s terraces. He has taken an interest in Denalan’s research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle works to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. A strange affliction is twisting Teldrassil’s native plants and animals. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood and pulse with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause. Timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point of the outbreak. Its timberlings are among the most tainted on the World Tree. Rellian Greenspyre asks you to kill these corrupted guardians and cut away their tumors. Bring the growths to the druids in Darnassus, where they can be burned safely. The night elves hope this will slow the contagion while they search for the disease’s source.

quest:924.text: The Demon Seed. Neeru Fireblade's orders reach Ak'Zeloth, and the orc sends Horde travelers against the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. A Flawed Power Stone can break the Burning Legion's conduit before its influence spreads farther through the Barrens. You carry an unstable Flawed Power Stone to a cave high on Dreadmist Peak. There, the Demon Seed hangs above an altar of fire. The artifact anchors the Burning Legion's demonic power in the heart of the Barrens. Ak'Zeloth prepared the stone to break its link to the Nether, but its energy will not last long.

quest:92460.text: Coming of Age. In Thendal Village, young Skyborne begin the rite that welcomes them into service to the shen'dorei. Ailee Farheart leads them to Rorian the Dayseeker, who gives each initiate an ancestral relic and hears their pledge to aid their people. Ailee Farheart guides young Skyborne from Thendal Village toward adulthood. They travel just west to the greatfather tree, where the village elder waits. For the shen'dorei, the rite marks a passage into adulthood and a pledge to serve their community. Local troubles are rising. At the entrance to the greatfather tree, Rorian the Dayseeker leads the ceremony. He gives each initiate an ancestral relic, an heirloom passed through generations of shen'dorei. The relic is a token of the winds of home. It stays with its bearer until their ashes are scattered to the breeze.

quest:92461.text: Harmony in Balance. On Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker gives fledgling adventurers an early rite of duty. You thin the vuldren in Thendal Grove to protect the island’s natural balance, for its beasts feel magic shifting in the winds. In Thendal Grove, vuldren have grown too numerous for the island to sustain. Their numbers threaten the environmental harmony that supports Zephras Isle’s wildlife. Rorian the Dayseeker gives young protectors the duty of thinning the herd before it strains the grove and the life around it. Vuldren are usually docile, yet the beasts of Zephras Isle are sensitive to the island’s atmosphere. When magic carried on the winds falls out of balance, they respond sharply. Keeping their numbers in check helps prevent them from becoming unpredictable and dangerous pests.

quest:92462.text: Infestation Investigation. In Thendal Grove, cirrusflies swarm the eastern woods. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight sends young defenders to thin their growing numbers before nearby settlements are at risk. Local rangers report a sudden rise in cirrusflies along Thendal Grove’s eastern edge. One is a minor pest, but a swarm grows aggressive and destructive. So Ranger Elatrell Featherlight sends capable youths to cull the insects before they overwhelm the grove. After coming of age, young defenders help keep Zephras Isle safe. Clearing pests protects nearby settlements from outbreaks in the woods. Yet entrails and insects clinging to returning hunters show the swarm is far larger than first feared.

quest:92463.text: The Cirrusfly Queen. In Thendal Grove, cirrusflies threaten the rangers of Zephras Isle. Their swarm has spread far, so Elatrell Featherlight sends you to hunt its queen and thin the flies at their source. You have seen that killing worker cirrusflies does little to curb the swarm spreading through Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight sends you to the grove’s southeastern reaches, where the main hive lies. The queen directs the colony and heavier soldier drones guard her. From afar, cirrusflies may seem like petty pests. Yet the larger breeds threaten anyone who passes beneath Zephras’s boughs. Hunt down the matriarch and withstand her guards, and you prove your skill in battle. Featherlight’s rangers will give you praise and respect.

quest:92464.text: Elemental Unrest. Near the Thendal Standing Stones, lesser wind spirits have grown restless. Their sentient elemental benefactors have departed Zephras Isle, and Rorian the Dayseeker sends you into Thendal Grove to find his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and learn what troubles the breeze. For generations, powerful wind spirits lived beside the people of Zephras. They were sentient, and they guided and protected the islanders. Now those elemental benefactors have departed, leaving Zephras in lasting imbalance. Without them to tend the air, simple sprites reflect the volatile feelings and forces that linger across the land. Northeast of Rorian's post, the air near the ancient Thendal Standing Stones has turned hostile. The lesser wind spirits lack true self-awareness, so they act in reaction, not malice. Rorian sent his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, to watch their erratic behavior from the grove's edge. She is to discover what unseen tension disturbs them.

quest:92465.text:
Agitators. On Zephras Isle, unrest in Thendal Grove draws Yala Windwatcher's concern. The Al'Aketh cult has stirred peaceful wind sprites into hostile elementals, and its converts now threaten the grove. Cultists of Al'Aketh have pushed into Thendal Grove and stirred the wind spirits who dwell there. Once peaceful, the sprites now rage as roiling winds, threatening anyone who passes through. Yala Windwatcher asks you to subdue the enraged elementals and the Al'Aketh converts behind the unrest. Quieting the wind creatures may restore a fragile calm to the grove.

Yala grieves at the thought of shen'dorei blood shed among her own people. Yet while the cult remains, she sees little choice.

quest:92469.text: Return to Rorian. Yala Windwatcher sends you to Thendal Grove with urgent news from the field. After you help drive back the agitators on Zephras Isle, she reports that the Al'Aketh have disturbed the local wind spirits. Yala Windwatcher remains on Zephras Isle to face the hostiles still there. She sends you to Thendal Grove with word that the Al'Aketh are no longer working only in the shadows.

quest:92470.text: Foul Matriarch. In the caves south of Thendal Village, Aetheen of the Gales tests new initiates against the ursera. They must thin the packs and slay their den mother, Urs'anah, to prove they can face greater perils across Zephras Isle. Around Thendal Village, Aetheen of the Gales watches newcomers find their footing. When an initiate shows early skill, Aetheen sends them into the southern caves for a dangerous rite of passage. There, they thin the local ursera packs and face the broodmother who threatens the village's edge. Local rangers know the ursera are fierce, but Urs'anah is the greatest threat to the haven. Deep in Thendal Cave, the formidable matriarch directs her scavengers and guards her lair. Her severed head proves an adventurer can face ferocious beasts and is ready to venture beyond the starting grove.

quest:92471.text: Aetheen of the Gales. On Zephras Isle, young adventurers who pass their first trials go to meet Aetheen of the Gales at Thendal Grove. There, the next generation faces her judgment. Young novices on Zephras Isle take on early duties that test their grit and spirit. The island's mentors watch for those ready to help defend their home. Rorian the Dayseeker notices youths prepared for greater responsibility. At Thendal Grove, Aetheen of the Gales reads the currents of the air. She belongs to the Council of Elders, which governs Zephras Isle, and assesses young shen'dorei as they come of age. Reporting to her takes you beyond minor duties along the island's perimeter and toward threats facing the community.

quest:92472.text: The Next Step. Elder Aetheen turns south after the beasts near Thendal Village are dealt with. The Al'Aketh Cult's zealots threaten Shen'dar Village. Elder Aetheen of the Gales sees danger growing across Zephras Isle. The predators and matriarchs of the northern wilderness have been dealt with, but that was only the lesser trouble. Outlying settlements still need defenders. The Al'Aketh Cult is the chief danger in southern Zephras. Its ruthless zealots worship Al'Akir the Windlord, ruler of Skywall in the elemental realm. Their growing power threatens Shen'dar Village. Aetheen sends travelers south along the road, past ambushers in the highlands, to aid Constable Aonda's local guard.

quest:92473.text: Aggressive Encroachment. At the village, starving ursera now threaten the settlement. Valreaa Valewind calls for a cull after one beast nearly attacked a child at the elder tree. Ursera from dens southwest of the village have become dangerous to its people. A hungry adolescent reached the base of the central elder tree and nearly mauled a child at play. The settlement's rangers killed the beast before anyone was hurt. The rangers believe hunger is driving ursera toward settled ground. They have ordered a cull of the scrawniest beasts prowling outside their dens in Thendal Grove. The Rangers of the Grove hope this will stop further incursions while they seek the cause of the wildlife's distress.

quest:92474.text: Falling With Style. At Thendal Village, Myriaal Mistwake sends young Skyborne from a watchtower to test their falling skill. They glide down to Rorian the Dayseeker below. High above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage with a daring leap. She urges newcomers to step from the watchtower ledge and trust their gift for slowing a fall. The practice is playful, yet it prepares them to walk on air when danger comes beyond the grove. Myriaal delights in sudden descents that startle onlookers, while Rorian the Dayseeker favors caution. As novices glide down to land before him, he warns that careless use of their magic may leave travelers helpless in danger. Still, he accepts that controlled practice within the village has its place.

quest:92481.text: A Student of the Arcane. On Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker calls novice spellcasters to A Student of the Arcane. After newcomers prove their mettle, they review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to Dorii Brightwhisper, the local mentor. After helping with the troublesome vuldren near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages receive a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Dorii Brightwhisper, the island’s arcane instructor, left it behind. Its recorded message tests an initiate’s aptitude and welcomes them into deeper study of magic. Dorii Brightwhisper says arcane mastery has slowly faded among their people. For millennia, they lived secluded high in the clouds. So Dorii sees each new practitioner as a pioneer who can recover lost knowledge and restore their people’s once-mighty magical heritage.

quest:92482.text: The Way of the Hunter. Young hunters in Thendal Grove begin training after driving back the local vuldren. Now Rorian the Dayseeker summons them to meet Tai'ree Farsight and begin formal tutelage. After thinning the disruptive vuldren on Thendal Grove's outskirts, young hunters return to find their practical skills have drawn attention. Rorian the Dayseeker gives them a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers preparing to explore Zephras Isle, the meeting turns their work from defending the island to learning martial skills and survival. Near the center of the village, Tai'ree Farsight welcomes promising pupils with stern realism. Thriving in untamed nature demands sharp senses and lightning reflexes. Her guidance comes from her long years of experience, giving island trackers a foundation for honing their marksmanship and survival skills.

quest:92483.text: At Home in the Shadows. Rorian sends you to meet Akeri Duskblade in Thendal Grove, where rogue training begins. The summons marks a change from village chores to stealth and combat. Akeri Duskblade has noticed young rogues dealing with threats around Thendal Grove. The grove's rogue trainer avoids an open meeting in the settlement, so he sends a note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Though Akeri keeps his reasons close, Rorian sees that he knows the skills a rogue needs beyond the grove's sheltered bounds. Akeri Duskblade waits in the Thendal Grove village watchtower. He judges each newcomer’s footing and awareness, then warns that careless steps beyond the grove can lead to an early grave. Passing his scrutiny begins formal training in stealth, precision, and survival on Zephras Isle.

quest:92484.text: Embracing the Elements. In Thendal Grove, Rorian the Dayseeker calls young shamans to begin their elemental training. Windshaper Boro’s message speaks of a silence between the people and the spirits of the winds. Rorian the Dayseeker comes to you after you help with the vuldren around the village. Windshaper Boro left a humming recall crystal while you were away. Its message calls you to the center of the grove, where formal elemental instruction begins. Windshaper Boro tells you the spirits of the four winds ended all communication years ago. They left behind the communion they once shared with the people. Now the shamans of Zephras study the natural world and train hard, hoping to bridge the silence and speak with the spirits again.

quest:92485.text: A Student of Nature. On Zephras Isle, A Student of Nature begins with a summons to novice druids. After they help restore local harmony, Xyton Silverwind calls them beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove to learn the isle's natural balance. After local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife are resolved, Rorian the Dayseeker brings a personal summons to young initiates. The folded parchment was left by Xyton Silverwind. It invites aspiring druids to step forward and study the deeper mysteries of the wild, for their natural talents have caught the grove elders' attention. Meeting Xyton Silverwind on the lower level of the great tree in Thendal Grove marks a novice's first step in their calling. To Silverwind, Zephras Isle's plants and animals form an intricate living whole that needs constant care and watchful balance. The path of fang, claw, feather, and branch calls for lasting mentorship, and this meeting begins a lifetime of stewardship.

quest:92532.text:
The Warrior's Path. Rorian the Dayseeker sends you to Blademaster Ren in Thendal Village. She offers young warriors instruction and discipline to defend their people. After restoring balance nearby, you return to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village. The village blademaster has noticed you, and Rorian gives you a crumpled note written by Ren herself. She asks you to come to her directly.

Ren waits in the village watchtower, high above the settlement. From there, she watches the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them. Inside the watchtower, Blademaster Ren teaches you that combat takes more than brute strength. A warrior must lead, endure, and protect as the world grows more uncertain. Ren pledges to guide you as you hone your skills. Her rigorous training prepares you for the greater dangers threatening your home.

quest:92544.text: Al'Aketh Thugs. At the temple ruins near Thendal Grove, Al'Aketh cultists threaten travelers. Sent from the Shrine of Akir under High Priestess Lorthuna's orders, they harass wayfarers and force recruits into their ranks. Hanaa Nightwind asks you to break their hold and slay their commander. Just southwest of Thendal Grove, ancient temple ruins have become dangerous for travelers. The Al'Aketh have seized the grounds and prey on people near the grove. Rangers stationed nearby suspect High Priestess Lorthuna sent the ruffians from the Shrine of Akir. They bully the people and force them to submit to the cult. At the ruins, Malduko Cloudcrush rules through violence and fear. Brutes and newly indoctrinated neophytes obey him, making the temple an aggressive outpost at Thendal Grove's doorstep. Hanaa Nightwind hopes that striking down Cloudcrush and scattering his followers will break the cult's confidence. It will warn them that coercion will not be tolerated in these lands.

quest:92597.text: Reading the Ley Lines. On Zephras Isle, young Skyborne seek the arcane currents beneath their feet. Falorne Fallwind sends them to Thendal Grove to feel power rising through the elemental plane. Ley lines run beneath Zephras Isle, even through the elemental plane. Strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh cross the island as these buried currents rise toward the surface. For those with the bloodline and knowledge to channel them, the exposed lines open a path to raw arcane power. Falorne Fallwind urges initiates to claim their Highborne ancestry instead of seeking favor from wind spirits. The local Windshapers and the Al'Aketh both look to such spirits. Fallwind believes survival amid the elemental plane's harsh powers depends on mastering the arcane force beneath the ground, rather than asking foreign creatures for mercy. Northeast of the settlement, Thendal Grove's ancient standing stones mark a powerful meeting of ley lines. Roiling winds and Al'Aketh converts surround this exposed place. There, initiates can attune their senses to the ley line's pulse and unleash the full potential of their natural racial abilities.

quest:92598.text: The Gift of Skysight. On Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish guides young Windshapers toward Skysight. At an Elemental Convergence, they awaken their perception and listen to the spirits. Windshapers are born with a bond to the elemental forces that shape their world. They call its sacred faculty Skysight. This gift attunes mortal senses to the spiritual realm and reaches across the divide between the living and the unseen. In the wilds, a Windshaper can call on this inner vision. Near concentrated power, the bond grows stronger, bringing boons and wisdom whispered by the spirits. Northeast of the settlement, ancient standing stones mark an Elemental Convergence in Thendal Grove. Raw energies gather at such places, where spirits linger. Ventaari Brightwish sends novices there to test their spiritual strength. Skysight grows with practice, like a faculty of body or mind. Windshapers must learn to read the elements' changing omens, for their people's survival depends on it.

quest:926.text: Flawed Power Stone. Across the Barrens, flawed stones sit charged with arcane energy on ritual tables. Their makers left them unstable, and they consume their power soon after they are moved. Across the Barrens, flawed power stones hold arcane essence in compromised structures. Their makers left them unstable, so they decay into inert matter moments after someone handles them. A stone starts consuming its power as soon as it leaves the ritual table where it rests. Its energy burns away too quickly for anyone to carry it far.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Lieutenant Orrin calls Stormwind's defenders to drive back Scourge forces pressing against the city. Necropolises loom beyond its walls, and he asks them to gather Necrotic Stones and study the runes around enemy camps. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital. Glowing runes mark the dirt around Scourge camps, but their purpose remains unclear. The circles crackle with magic like that of the necropolises and carry eerie whispers. Lieutenant Orrin can only guess who, if anyone, hears those unnatural voices.

quest:9261.text: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. The Scourge presses against Ironforge’s gates, and Lieutenant Nevell calls for defenders. Undead troops gather beneath a hovering necropolis while glowing runic circles mark their camps. Lieutenant Nevell and the Argent Dawn watch the undead at Ironforge’s mountain entrance. Necropolises hover above Dun Morogh’s frigid heights, far from Lordaeron and the plagued lands of the north. They mean to stop the Scourge before it reaches the Bronzebeard fortress.

quest:9262.text: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. At Darnassus, Lieutenant Beitha calls for help as Scourge encampments press close. The Argent Dawn needs defenders to strike the undead and learn what the runes outside the gates are for. The Scourge has reached Teldrassil. Floating necropolises loom over invasion camps near Darnassus, and ghouls, skeletons, and other undead horrors spill from them. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn coordinates the city's defense. She calls on volunteers to slow the attack and gather information before the undead overwhelm the night elven homeland.

quest:9263.text: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. Outside Orgrimmar, the Scourge presses its attack beneath a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel calls on defenders to repel the undead, recover necrotic stones, and examine runic circles charged with necromantic energy. The assault brings the Lich King's reach to Durotar. The Scourge now threatens lands far from Lordaeron and the northern ice. Its floating necropolises cast shadows across Azeroth, even over Durotar. Undead forces have gathered at Orgrimmar's threshold and raised camps that threaten the Horde capital. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn coordinate the defense, calling on local champions to drive the invaders back before they can secure a siege.

quest:927.text:
The Moss-twined Heart. Near Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies a heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid. Dark, oily moss covers the core, yet it keeps beating after it is cut from the timberling. Blackmoss the Fetid's heart still beats after it is cut from the timberling. Dark, oily moss hides nearly all of the core, but a slow rhythm continues within. That pulse points to a corruption beyond ordinary rot in Teldrassil's wild plants. Denalan studies local flora near Lake Al'Ameth, and the heart commands his keen interest. He recognizes its troubling corruption. Timberlings should be gentle beings tied to the boughs of the World Tree, yet this core bears a virulent blight.

Troubled by what he sees and eager to understand it, Denalan plans to plant and study the organ. He hopes to learn how foul moss takes root in the island's soil.

quest:92742.text: Testing the Wells. Across Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends you to test the farm wells. Their samples may show what is poisoning the soil and groundwater. Alba Fairmoon asks you to test the water beneath Westfall. Neglect and banditry have already harmed the open plains. Now poison below the earth threatens the farmland that remains. You gather samples from farm wells so Alba can learn what is tainting the soil and water. You gather samples from the wells at Jansen Stead and Molsen Farm. These homesteads lie among scattered farms, exposed to Defias outlaws and feral wildlife. Their water may show whether the blight rises from the ground, comes from magic, or was put there deliberately.

quest:92744.text: Murloc Gills. At Westfall's Longshore, Alba Fairmoon seeks murloc gills to test the sea. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could show whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is close to ruin. Crops fail, farmers leave their homes, and bandits roam the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may drain from inland fields into the Great Sea. If it taints the coast, fish that feed Westfall's poor and fill Stormwind City's tables could vanish. Then an already strained kingdom may face famine. Murlocs are stubborn and violent, but their amphibious bodies can reveal the water's condition. As they breathe, their gills filter seawater and readily take in poisons, blight, and unnatural pollutants. Alba Fairmoon hopes fresh gills from murlocs prowling the Longshore will show how far the contamination has spread.

quest:92745.text: The State of the Mines. Toxic metals are turning up in Westfall's wells, and Alba Fairmoon fears for the farmland. She suspects the Defias mines and warns that the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the Defias Brotherhood is poisoning the water through the mines it seized. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades. The Defias put local creatures to work alongside their highwaymen, stripping Westfall of its resources. Riverpaw gnolls dig for stone and minerals at Gold Coast Quarry, while kobold diggers tunnel through Jangolode Mine. Disrupting their labor weakens the Defias' ability to process and distribute contaminated minerals.

quest:92747.text: Moonbrook Espionage. In Moonbrook, Alba Fairmoon follows signs of industry trouble in Westfall. The poison found across the region does not seem to come from the smaller mines, so the Deadmines beneath the town draw her attention. The mines already searched across Westfall have yielded no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation seems to be its source. One great site remains unexplored: the Deadmines, whose vast shafts lie beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

quest:92748.text: Explosive Consultation. Alba Fairmoon sends you to find a way to stop the poison spreading from the Deadmines into Westfall's fields. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, you seek an engineer who can make the heavy explosives the work requires. Westfall's poisoned fields lead back to caustic toxins and industrial refuse in the Deadmines. Reinforced machinery guards the underground works, and ordinary weapons cannot disable it. Heavy explosives could break through that machinery and halt the poisoning. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, you seek Sprite Jumpsprocket, an engineer able to devise the needed explosives. Roaring forges, tinkerers, and merchants selling blasting powder fill the district. Its craftsmen may know how to stop the Deadmines operation.

quest:92749.text: A Dynamite Plan. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to begin a plan sparked by talk of industrial sabotage. She wants ten sticks of coarse dynamite. Sprite Jumpsprocket is a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. She welcomes talk of industrial sabotage and asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite. You can make coarse dynamite at an engineering workbench or trade with the city's craftsmen. Sprite asks for ten sticks, enough to disrupt industrial schemes unfolding in the surrounding territories. Her plan shows the practical, perilous methods gnomes favor when facing mechanical and political disruptions.

quest:92750.text: Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Volatile chemicals are handled recklessly by goblins and gnomes, though some blasts call for care. A standard fuse can put you in danger. Ordinary tinkerers do not keep the special trigger Sprite needs for a controlled explosion. Sprite sends you to Stormwind Intelligence in Old Town, rather than to local dwarven blasters or ordinary engineering suppliers. Its agents, known as SI:7, work in sabotage, stealth, and targeted demolitions. Jasper Fel serves among them in the capital and can provide discreet, dangerous equipment.

quest:92751.text: Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, blasts beneath Westfall have drawn SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to let you handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

quest:92752.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. In wartime Westfall, the road is already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts. Carrying a live charge makes the journey more dangerous. Sprite Jumpsprocket warns you to guard the detonator. The explosives are meant to destroy the hidden industrial operation in the Deadmines, which is poisoning Westfall's farmland. Alba Fairmoon needs the explosives intact before she can use them.

quest:92753.text: Destruction in Deadmines. In the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry blights the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hold a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes the forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. She wants it destroyed.

quest:928.text: Crown of the Earth. In Shadowglen, you carry moonwell water south to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. The journey takes you from sheltered training into the wider work of protecting Teldrassil. You have tasted the enchanted water of Shadowglen's moonwell. At the crown of Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip seals the gathered water in a larger vessel and sends you beyond the sheltered glade. The road runs south to Dolanaar, through woods where danger has grown harder to predict. Dolanaar is the first major village beyond Shadowglen, along the cobblestone paths through central Teldrassil. Its moonwell lies at the village's heart. Corithras Moonrage, an elder who oversees preservation across the boughs, waits there. The vessel you carry joins you to the wider effort to protect the World Tree.

quest:92819.text: Destruction in Deadmines. Alba Fairmoon sends you against the Defias forge beneath Westfall. The explosives are planted, and she waits in the hills behind Moonbrook with the detonator. Beneath Westfall, the Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength. Alba Fairmoon sends you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are planted beside it. You return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook, where you can set them off from a safe distance. She hopes the blast will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal. Deep in the Deadmines, the charge waits beside the forge. After you rejoin Alba Fairmoon in the hills behind Moonbrook, a remote detonator lets you set it off from outside the caves. She hopes the destroyed forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal.

quest:929.text:
Crown of the Earth. Near Starbreeze Village, you draw sacred water for Darnassus. Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar sends young night elves to replenish the city's moonwell and teaches them why their people tend Teldrassil's great boughs. Druids have made you a jade phial for the journey to Starbreeze Village. There, a lesser moonwell holds sanctified water. The phial's refined craft lets you draw the luminous water and carry it without disturbing its purity.

Darnassus's central moonwell depends on scattered fonts like this one. Elders send initiates on foot to keep the city's fountains full of Elune's grace. The journey teaches the young what it takes to nourish Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tells you of the sorrow that followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The night elves sacrificed Nordrassil, their ancestral World Tree, and lost their immortality. Illidan Stormrage was unleashed amid the ruin, while Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared.

Grief and isolation marked the days that followed. The kaldorei turned to Teldrassil.

quest:930.text: The Glowing Fruit. A strange fruit shines among Teldrassil's trees, and its growth troubles those who find it. You carry it to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, where the herbalist can study the unfamiliar plant. In Teldrassil's misty boughs, you may find plants bearing large, round fruit that shine with their own light. The World Tree's balance is delicate, and its wildlife has behaved strangely of late. So unusual plants call for care. You gather the glowing fruit to bring it to someone who knows the wild flora.

quest:931.text: The Shimmering Frond. A curious plant shimmers among Teldrassil's roots and canopy. Travelers carry a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain where it came from. A strange plant catches the light in Teldrassil's boughs. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye among the young forest's plants.

quest:932.text: Twisted Hatred. Near Teldrassil’s settlements, Lord Melenas has rallied the grell at Fel Rock. Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions to stop the satyr before he threatens the night elves. Satyrs carry an ancient betrayal in kaldorei history. During the War of the Ancients, they were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion. Now one has taken hold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant as a sanctuary. For Tallonkai Swiftroot and the defenders who stand with him, that presence is a bitter disgrace. North of the nearby paths, Fel Rock’s corrupted caverns crawl with feral grell. Lord Melenas has gathered the chaotic creatures into a hostile force under his will. Tallonkai fears what the satyr may unleash upon the World Tree’s boughs, and demands a swift, quiet end. He wants Melenas slain and his severed head brought back.

quest:933.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Pools of Arlithrien, Corithras Moonrage asks you to fetch water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War. Corithras Moonrage gives you a tourmaline phial and sends you to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were once peaceful, but now they lash out without warning. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. These skirmishes have become a threat to the night elves' new home. When you return with the filled phial, Corithras tells you how Teldrassil began. After the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids without a leader and divided. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took the mantle of leadership in his absence. He urged the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore to set aside their mourning. The night elves, he argued, had to regain their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a vast new World Tree.

quest:934.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Oracle Glade, Corithras Moonrage sends you to gather water from Teldrassil’s sacred moonwell. The journey begins to reveal why the World Tree’s creation went awry. Corithras Moonrage sends you northwest across Teldrassil to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the Oracle Tree’s great boughs lies the island’s first and most powerful moonwell. You draw water from its sacred pool into an Amethyst Phial. Druids and the tree itself watch over their new homeland’s health from this sanctuary.

quest:935.text: Crown of the Earth. In Teldrassil, moonwell waters are gathered to ease the World Tree’s sickness. The rites carry the samples to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, where worry grows over a tree raised without blessings. Teldrassil rose after the Third War to give the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. Yet the Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings and would not sanction its making. Without their protection, sickness spreads through the tree. Strange creatures emerge from its boughs, and furbolg tribes once at peace fall into madness.

quest:93552.text: Harvesting Windstones. At Thendal Grove, Dalia the Collector asks you to gather raw windstones before their power fades. The ancient elemental energies of Zephras Isle are slowly dwindling. Zephras Isle still draws on wind magic, but its natural defenses are failing. Centuries ago, the wind elementals who shared the island with its elves vanished. Since then, the magic that sustains the land and its great anchor pylons has weakened. So Thendal Grove’s residents need every reserve of raw energy they can secure. Blue crystalline windstones lie scattered through Thendal Grove. Their brittle shells hold dense wind magic from ages past. They cannot sustain the island forever, yet they give its elves a dependable source of arcane power. Gathering raw clusters remains vital to daily life.

quest:937.text: The Enchanted Glade. In northwestern Teldrassil, Bloodfeather harpies threaten the Oracle Glade and its ancient Oracle Tree. After they kill a runner bound for Darnassus, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak calls for their nests to be thinned and their belts brought back as proof. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak guards the Oracle Glade with an escort of warriors. At its heart stands the colossal Oracle Tree, an ancient rooted among Teldrassil's boughs. Bloodfeather harpies have spread through the surrounding canopy. They nest in its hollows and threaten anyone who comes near. A runner carrying an urgent report from the Oracle Tree never reaches Darnassus. Bloodfeather harpies ambush and kill the messenger before the runner can leave the glade. Arynia calls on you to thin their flock and bring back Bloodfeather belts as proof that their nests have been weakened.

quest:93746.text: A Firm Response. Ayessa Dawnsinger answers the High Order’s intrusion on Zephras Isle with force. She sends you after Belathaan Brightwish on the road north to the Shrine of Akir, to make the Windshapers’ boundaries clear. The Windshapers of Zephras Isle will not accept the High Order’s secretive scrutiny. Their warnings have gone unheeded, so Ayessa Dawnsinger escalates the dispute. She sends you to intercept Belathaan Brightwish on the lonely road north to the Shrine of Akir, away from prying eyes in town.

quest:938.text: Mist. In Teldrassil's shaded boughs, Mist lies wounded and apart from her companion. She needs a safe path to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. Mist lies wounded in Teldrassil's undergrowth, her gray coat marked by deep slashes across her back and belly. Her blue eyes remain bright, and she stays calm instead of acting like a feral beast. She looks to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

quest:93963.text: Exploring the Alliance. In Stormwind Keep, you begin a journey to meet the rulers of Ironforge and Darnassus. Their lands show you the breadth of the Alliance before you turn toward Westfall. Randal Emerson, an attendant in Stormwind Keep’s southern antechamber, sends you beyond the human capital. Newly arrived on Azeroth, you are invited to see the Alliance’s allied peoples firsthand. The journey takes you beyond the keep to learn the distinct cultures, traditions, and strength of those who stand with Stormwind. Your travels cross land and sea to the leaders of the Alliance. In Ironforge, you meet King Magni Bronzebeard in the mountain halls and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, leader of the displaced gnomes. In Darnassus atop Teldrassil, you meet High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Their cities and peoples reveal the ties among humans, dwarves, gnomes, and night elves. After the long journey, you return to Stormwind. Knowing more of Azeroth helps you aid your own people, while your order prepares to establish itself in Dalaran. For now, the troubled territories near the capital need help, beginning with Westfall’s struggling farmlands.

quest:940.text: Teldrassil. After the harpies are driven back, Arynia Cloudsbreak sends you to Darnassus with news for the kaldorei leadership. The inscribed bark tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm what troubles Teldrassil's boughs. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak gives you a piece of inscribed bark after you clear the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade. The Oracle Tree watches over the forest, and now Arynia can send word to the kaldorei leadership. You carry her report through the wilderness to Darnassus, the great forest of stone, and deliver it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Fandral Staghelm receives the report with gratitude and frustration. The harpies have been pushed back, yet one threat gives way to another across Teldrassil. Staghelm championed the planting of the new World Tree to reclaim the night elves' lost immortality. The afflictions in its boughs remind him that his work is far from finished.

quest:941.text: Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan care for a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. He clears away its moss, then asks you to place it in his planter and see if it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. So the herbalist trusts his years of tending plants and soil. He asks you to bury the heart in his personal planter, hoping his enriched soil can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

quest:944.text: The Master's Glaive. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu fears the Twilight's Hammer cult has reached the fallen ancient horror. He sends Alliance scouts to investigate. Onu sees corruption linger along Darkshore, driving wildlife from its homes. The naga on the coast trouble him, but signs of the Twilight's Hammer trouble him more. Its followers worship primal lords who ruled the world before their overthrow in ages past. South of Onu, a grim excavation surrounds a colossal creature pierced by a great stone weapon. Onu gives you a Phial of Scrying and asks you to enter the pit and learn whether cultists have gathered there. The behemoth has been dead for eons, yet corruptive power still clings to its bones. The Twilight's Hammer may seek to claim it.

quest:94414.text: The Anchors of Zephras. On Zephras Isle, Halaan Hawk-Eye asks you to watch the ancient anchor pylons that hold the island aloft. Their magic has begun to waver, and the wind spirits' blessing may no longer be steady. Wind spirits gave Zephras's ancient anchor pylons the power to bind and sustain the floating island. Their magic keeps the land steady amid the churning skies. From afar, the towering monoliths look untouched. Yet the island depends on the wind spirits' continuing blessing. The anchor pylons look proud and undamaged, yet their magic has grown erratic. Halaan Hawk-Eye says the harmony that sustains them has become unstable and uncertain. No clear sign of physical harm appears. Those who watch over the groves have reason to fear what threatens the isle. Halaan Hawk-Eye cannot use skysight to peer between worlds, nor can he tap Zephras's deep ley lines. His gift is natural vision sharp enough to reach immense distances. He lends that sight to newcomers, so they can study the distant pylons and watch for changes in their homeland's fate.

quest:945.text: Therylune's Escape. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Therylune needs help reaching safety. She wandered into the dig sites, and her sister Therysil waits at the Shrine of Aessina, worried for her. At the Master's Glaive, Twilight's Hammer cultists have pinned Therylune down. An ancient monstrosity's skull dominates the ravine, pierced by a huge stone blade. Despite the dread around it, Therylune wandered into the valley's heart. She survives by reacting quickly and hiding among the rough terrain. Therysil waits far to the south at the Shrine of Aessina. Her adventurous sister Therylune rarely minds getting dirt on her clothes, but even Therysil was shocked to hear she had ventured into the unwholesome excavations at the Master's Glaive. Tell her Therylune is safe, and her worry will ease. Therysil knows the dark forces digging through Darkshore's ancient earth.

quest:947.text: Cave Mushrooms. In Darkshore, Cave Mushrooms are needed for a potion Barithras Moonshade prepares in Auberdine. He asks you to gather rare fungi behind Cliffspring Falls and investigate warnings from the Grove of the Ancients. Barithras Moonshade needs scaber stalks and a death cap for a potent mixture. Both grow in a damp cavern behind Cliffspring Falls in northeastern Darkshore. Gathering them is more dangerous than picking ordinary woodland herbs.

quest:948.text: Onu. Barithras Moonshade sends you south from Auberdine to consult Onu. Your findings at Cliffspring Falls have caught the notice of one of Darkshore’s oldest guardians. Barithras Moonshade sees more than strange fungi in the samples you brought to Auberdine. The caves beneath Cliffspring Falls are tainted, and word of them has reached Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients south of town. Darkshore’s waterways may be corrupted beyond anything a naturalist can explain. Onu seeks counsel, and even an Ancient’s patience cannot hide the weight of his summons. The road south from Auberdine turns inland, away from the coastal ruins and toward the mountain slopes. The Grove of the Ancients shelters an old refuge of nature, apart from the decay along the shore. Onu waits among stone barrows and kindred spirits. He is ready to guide allies toward the blights stirring at the edge of the wilderness.

quest:949.text: The Twilight Camp. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, cultists gather while Alliance scouts seek their purpose. A scrying bowl has revealed their ritual site. Now you enter the excavation to learn what the Twilight's Hammer seeks beneath the earth. The Twilight's Hammer has made the Master's Glaive a threat. A scrying bowl revealed the cultists' fortifications. You enter their camp to learn their designs before the Alliance can prepare its defenses.

quest:950.text: Return to Onu. You bring a torn page from the Twilight Tome to Onu in Darkshore. The cultists' writing is all you could bear to take from their book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

quest:95041.text: Data Hoarders. Outside Gnomeregan, Jemma Quikswitch searches the snow for lost punch cards. The exiled gnome lives in Ironforge, and the cards hold her family's archives, from submarine designs to family recipes. Without them, the records she still has remain unreadable.
