When troggs invaded Gnomeregan and radiation struck, thousands of gnomes fled with what they could carry. A damaged satchel spilled several of Jemma's cards into the snow around the fallen city. Without them, her surviving records read as gibberish, and her family's knowledge risks being lost. The Quikswitch archives hold arcanotechnical field equations and submarine hull blueprints from the Second War. They also preserve Grandma Quikswitch's secret chili recipe. For refugees in Ironforge, the comforts of home matter as much as engineering marvels.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray keeps to his fishing line while the fish are biting. His supplies run low, so he asks passersby to fetch nightcrawlers and a shiny bauble from a shop along the city canals. Gilbert Gray watches his bobber dance on the water. The elderly angler will not leave his prized perch while the fish are biting. His supplies have run out, and he needs help so he can stay at his line instead of returning to the city. Catherine Leland runs a tackle shop beside Stormwind's stone canals, just west of the Trade District. Fishermen across the city come to her for lures and bait. Her shop can replenish what Gilbert Gray needs to keep fishing.

quest:952.text: Grove of the Ancients. An urgent dispatch takes you from Darnassus to Darkshore, where Onu waits in the Grove of the Ancients. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm sends you across the sea with a message for the Ancient of Lore, who lives south of Auberdine. After you help at the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm calls you to another duty. He sends you across the sea to Darkshore with an urgent dispatch for Onu. From Darnassus, you can take a hippogryph flight. South of Auberdine, you reach the Grove of the Ancients and deliver the message to Onu. The towering Ancient of Lore accepts it quietly and remarks on Staghelm's impatience. Onu and the forest's ancient keepers believe all things unfold in their proper time. Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage embodied that patient wisdom, while Staghelm lacks it.

quest:953.text:
The Fall of Ameth'Aran. At Ameth'Aran in Darkshore, you search the ruins and read their ancient stone tablets for Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Their words tell how the Highborne city fell in the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine. Ameth'Aran was home to Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who wielded powerful arcane magic. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city fell to broken marble and cracked pillars. The Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins as restless, anguished spirits. Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact. The War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival, and much of their history was lost. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed Ameth'Aran and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran.

Ghostly Highborne specters drove Tysha from the ruins. Their readings can carry the disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

quest:95314.text:
That Shadowvale Green Elixir. In Brill, That Shadowvale Green Elixir draws buyers despite the old ban. Shadowvale's secluded villagers once brewed Whispering Elixir from local herbs, and the Scourge left the village in ruins. Before the Scourge came, Shadowvale's villagers brewed Whispering Elixir from rare herbs found only in Tirisfal Glades. The draught grew known across northern Lordaeron. The Capital City outlawed it, yet mystics, poisoners, and apothecaries still sought its unusual properties, defying royal decrees. Shadowvale lies deep in the Whispering Forest of western Tirisfal. Its people were insular and distrustful, and rarely welcomed outsiders. The Scourge invasion left the settlement in ruins, though forgotten stores of aged green elixir remain among the wreckage.

Carolai Anise works from Brill. The underworld still wants the brew, so she pays adventurers willing to brave the forest's unsettling silence.

quest:954.text: Bashal'Aran. An eerie blue aura burns above a shrine in Bashal'Aran, where satyrs and grells will not go. Thundris Windweaver, Auberdine's elder, asks you to find its source. Bashal'Aran once flourished under the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Now demonic taint fills its broken marble halls and overgrown arches. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed on the ruins' lingering magic, growing more malicious by the day. Yet Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine has noticed a mystery: atop a western bluff, a blue aura shines above a shrine that no demon will approach.

quest:955.text: Bashal'Aran. Magic still binds Asterion beneath Bashal'Aran's broken stones. The ancient night elf seeks release from his ghostly form and suspects the grells have touched the seal that holds him. He asks travelers to gather their earrings and trace its lingering magic. For centuries, Asterion has waited among Bashal'Aran's shattered marble. The ancient night elf spirit remains caught between life and true death beneath Darkshore's canopy. Arcane craft binds him to the ruined settlement, and he cannot break free alone. Solitude and despair have worn down his mind. Asterion believes an ancient seal hidden in the ruins may hold the key to his release. He cannot search the brush and fallen stones himself. The feral grells of Bashal'Aran forage there and steal small baubles, so he asks travelers to gather their earrings. He hopes the trinkets' lingering magic will lead him to the seal that torments his soul.

quest:956.text:
Bashal'Aran. Among the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran, Asterion seeks release from his prison. He has traced the binding magic to the satyrs who command the grells. Now he asks travelers to recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For more than a thousand years, Asterion has been bound within the ruins of Bashal'Aran. The marble pillars mark the bounds of his prison. His strength and ancient magic cannot carry him beyond them. A cursed relic holds him there.

Through the centuries, Asterion has watched Darkshore's canopy. He wonders if the worn stone around him might ever set him free. Nearby grells bore traces of the magic binding Asterion. From them, he reasoned that the Ancient Moonstone Seal was the enchantment's source. The satyrs who command the grells hold the seal now. These demonic night elves roam the ancient groves and keep watch over the relic. Asterion needs travelers to recover the seal so its binding power can be broken.

quest:957.text: Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion's spirit remains bound by an ancient seal. You carry the seal south to Ameth'Aran, where an old flame may break his bonds. The Ancient Moonstone Seal was forged by Highborne sorcerers before the Great Sundering, and no ordinary strength can break its power. Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister settlements of the kaldorei under Queen Azshara, when the Well of Eternity anchored their empire. Now both are overgrown, haunted ruins, where ghosts linger and arcane power remains volatile. At Ameth'Aran, a mystical brazier burns with cyan fire in a stone gazebo; that is the sole flame able to consume the Ancient Moonstone Seal.

quest:959.text: Trouble at the Docks. In Ratchet, a stolen bottle puts Bigglefuzz's job at risk. Mad Magglish fled inland with a 99-Year-Old Port, a gift from Baron Revilgaz to Gazlowe, and now hides in the Wailing Caverns. Ratchet's docks carry sea trade with Booty Bay across the Great Sea. One morning, a huge shipment arrived, and Crane Operator Bigglefuzz overloaded his crane to unload it faster. The crane dropped the whole load across the docks. In the confusion, Mad Magglish, a local nuisance, snatched a valuable bottle of liquor and fled inland. The bottle is a 99-Year-Old Port, a personal diplomatic gift from Baron Revilgaz, Booty Bay's ruler, to Gazlowe, Ratchet's chief engineer and overseer. Its loss could humiliate Bigglefuzz and anger both trade leaders. Fearing for his job or worse, Bigglefuzz followed the thief to the mouth of the Wailing Caverns. But fear stopped him from going inside. Mad Magglish hides in damp natural tunnels outside the Wailing Caverns' inner gateway, not deep in the corrupted dreamscape. The thief relies on clumsy stealth and dark alcoves, hoping pursuers will give up. Find Magglish in the outer caverns before the port is uncorked or destroyed.

quest:960.text:
Onu is meditating. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu enters a deep trance as a threat grows. The ancient of lore weighs the alliance and motives of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the naga. If you lose your scrying phial, speak to him for another. In the Grove of the Ancients, Onu holds Kalimdor's history in his ancient memory. Ominous reports of dark excavations at the Master's Glaive draw his vast consciousness inward. He considers what brings the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cultists and the naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. As you carry out his reconnaissance, Onu remains within reach and can replace a scrying phial misplaced in the wild. Onu uses nature-attuned divination to watch the ruins without risking his physical presence. He entrusts you with a scrying phial, which conjures a scrying bowl at the excavation site and lets him commune from afar. The journey south through Darkshore is perilous, with hostile wildlife and cultist patrols, so mishaps can happen.

Onu's trance is an attentive vigil, not unbroken slumber. He readily offers another vial of sacred waters so you can continue the investigation of the Master's Glaive.

quest:96047.text: Camping 101: First Aid. In Kharanos, Thamner Pol teaches you to prepare First Aid Kits for camps in Dun Morogh. With these supplies, travelers can stay alive in the field. You can build on your basic bandaging skills by learning to prepare supplies for a resting site. Thamner Pol shows you how raw medical supplies become complete kits, ready for use at camp when travelers need care far from shelter. Thamner Pol teaches you practical ways to outfit expedition sites with emergency supplies. A proper field kit lets a group bind wounds and regain strength together by the hearth before heading back into the cold.

quest:96139.text: The Valor Family. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi seeks records of Raven Hill's lost people. The village remembers their courage, but her library holds little of Raven Hill's history. Sirra Von'Indi says brave people helped Darkshire endure. Lady Althea was among them, as were those who died at Raven Hill. You are asked to search for anything that might preserve their memory.

quest:962.text: Serpentbloom. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Serpentbloom draws Apothecary Zamah’s attention. She seeks more specimens for the Royal Apothecary Society’s research and the Forsaken. Apothecary Zamah watches the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff’s Spirit Rise. She came from the Undercity as an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society. Her tauren hosts tend to spiritual balance and the wounded land, while Zamah studies rare and virulent materials. She has isolated a sample of Serpentbloom and seeks more for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken’s research. Serpentbloom grows in the damp, twisting grottos of the Wailing Caverns, far from the Barrens’ open sun. The corrupted druids of the Fang have twisted these humid depths, where serpentine denizens guard the plant. Many scouts sent by Zamah failed to return. Now she seeks hardy adventurers to gather more.

quest:963.text: For Love Eternal. In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to ease Anaya Dawnrunner's torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has lasted since the city fell. Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. Ameth'Aran fell, and Anaya Dawnrunner was lost to Cerellean Whiteclaw. Grief-stricken, Cerellean joined Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage in the druids' long hibernation. He hoped the ages spent walking the Emerald Dream would quiet his heart, but his sorrow endured. When he awoke, Cerellean wandered Darkshore in a stupor. At last he came to the melancholy ruins of Ameth'Aran, where he saw Anaya's tortured ghost. He cannot raise a weapon against the woman he loved. So he asks passing travelers to destroy her tormented form, retrieve her pendant, and bring peace to her troubled soul.

quest:96390.text: Nip 'Em in the Bud. Dark Iron spies move through Dun Morogh, and Earthseer Farsen calls for help. Near Ironband's Compound, their presence threatens the Bronzebeard homeland. Dark Iron spies have crossed Dun Morogh's high passes and snowy crags. They hide near settlements and excavations, where even a few watchers may signal a strike. Earthseer Farsen sees the danger and calls on Alliance defenders to find them before their plans advance.

quest:96391.text: Underground Map. Near Ironband's Compound, the Underground Map points toward chambers beneath Ironforge. Recovered from Dark Iron spies, its runes trace a hidden route piercing toward ancient halls beneath the mountain. You bring it to Earthseer Farsen to begin learning what lies below. You find the parchment near Ironband's Compound after dealing with Dark Iron spies. Its diagrams lay out an intricate maze of roads beneath the earth. Harsh, jagged runes mark passages that run deep underground and converge beneath Ironforge. Their course suggests a possible threat beneath the Bronzebeard capital, though the Dark Iron notes remain uncertain.

quest:96392.text: Farsen's Watch. Near Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen watches for Dark Iron movement close to Ironforge. The Wildhammer shaman lends you his farsight, revealing a threat that calls for swift action. From his post above Gol'Bolar Quarry, Farsen watches the lower reaches of Dun Morogh. He came south from the crags of Aerie Peak, bringing a Wildhammer's spiritual awareness with him. His clan's old arts let him sense tremors underground and watch for sudden movement along the hillsides. Farsen lends you his farsight, a shamanic gift that carries sight across great distances. Through it, you see danger beyond troggs and wild beasts. Dark Iron dwarves have drawn close to Ironforge's industrial center and are digging in. Their foothold must be confronted before it takes root.

quest:96393.text: Old Ironforge Incursion. Beneath Ironforge, Earthseer Farsen sends you to the Hall of Thanes for the last part of the investigation. There, you face the Dark Iron threat and report to King Magni Bronzebeard. The underground map reveals Dark Iron movements, and Earthseer Farsen identifies the mastermind behind the intrusion. The entrance to the Hall of Thanes lies deep within Old Ironforge's ancient stone halls. While the upper city tends to matters on the surface, Dark Iron forces slip into caverns that lie dormant beneath the kingdom.

quest:96395.text: An Ancient Grudge. Within the Hall of Thanes, Faldrim Anvilmar's spirit remains troubled by an old grievance. His ghostly attendant asks travelers to bring him peace. A ghostly attendant remains in the Hall of Thanes, where Faldrim Anvilmar once ruled. The spirit can barely speak across the veil between the living and the dead. It asks you to quiet its master's restless spirit. It seeks peace for him, not freedom for itself.

quest:96408.text: A Visitor to Dun Morogh. Beldin Steelgrill sends you to learn who has lit a fire above Gol'Bolar Quarry. The camp overlooks the excavation, and the dwarves fear its visitor may mean them harm. High on the snowy ridges east of Kharanos, a stranger's campfire burns above the quarry. The unfamiliar fire has worried the folk of Kharanos. There, the Mountaineers watch the heights for danger.

quest:965.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. North of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze fears trouble at an ancient ruin. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, but his report has not come. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze keeps watch for danger around Auberdine. Suspicious activity near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore caught her attention, so she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word. Elissa asks you to travel north, find Balthule, and make sure he has not met an untimely end.

quest:966.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Warlocks gather at the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, drawing Balthule Shadowstrike's watchful eye. He asks travelers to recover scraps of parchment from the fanatics camped outside the ruins, hoping to learn who they are and what they seek. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the misty shore of northern Darkshore and keeps the ancient Tower of Althalaxx in sight. Auberdine sent him to watch the ruin and warn Delgren the Purifier if danger grows. Yet leaving his post to report might let the dark spellcasters among the stones slip from view. So Balthule asks passing travelers to scout the camps around the tower.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. Beyond city walls, The Great Outdoors teaches you to meet the wild with care. Seasoned travelers begin with a campfire and the habits that make each journey safer. A sharp blade or potent magic will not save you if you neglect the basics. Near roadside clearings, seasoned wanderers teach travelers leaving their home valleys to rest by a campfire. Its warmth eases sore boots, settles the mind, and prepares you for the harsh road ahead. Rest and preparation improve your chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory. Your instructors also send you to town tradesfolk, because a field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear beneath the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. From Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends you toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have proved your skill defending the abbey, and now he wants you to look into a newcomer. With the Defias and vermin threats easing, McBride turns his attention to the road beyond the valley. His garrison needs promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods. Marshal McBride asks you to check on Sam Sarsaparilla, who was spotted near Goldshire. This is neither a military order nor a hunt for a bounty. The newcomer draws you from Northshire’s secluded valley into Elwynn’s wider wilds.

quest:96628.text: The Adventurer. At Dun Morogh’s southern gate, The Adventurer carries supplies toward Kharanos. Mountaineer Thalos asks travelers to bring provisions to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Mountaineer Thalos keeps watch at Dun Morogh’s southern gate, where the trail leaves Coldridge Valley. Guarding the high passes and tunnels keeps the Mountaineers busy. Thalos also watches for dangers and travelers on the road. When a lone adventurer arrives near Kharanos, he asks trusted passersby to carry supplies onward. The bundle is meant to help newcomers venturing into the frozen crags. The road from the southern pass winds down to Kharanos, a center of dwarven craft and travel in central Dun Morogh. Eric Brighthammer has recently made camp just outside the village. Carrying the Mountaineers’ provisions to him links the sentries on the ridge with those walking the wilderness.

quest:96630.text: The Adventurer. In Teldrassil, you find a lost journal meant for Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Its pages follow an unknown traveler's quiet journeys and camping outings. Among Teldrassil's boughs and roots, you find a journal left behind. Its nameless writer tells of modest wanderings and the simple pleasure of camping beneath the twilight canopy. You can carry the journal toward Dolanaar instead of leaving it in the wilderness. Lyreena Duskblade waits near the night elf settlement to receive its lost pages.

quest:96638.text: The Adventurer. On Zephras Isle, The Adventurer leaves Thendal Grove for the road to Shen'dar Village. Aetheen of the Gales sends newly seasoned wanderers southwest to meet Raan Wildwind, a veteran camper who knows the wilds. Thendal Grove offers shelter, but Zephras Isle beyond it remains wild and perilous. Aetheen of the Gales watches over the initiates and knows when a traveler is ready to leave familiar ground. Those seeking fame, fortune or purpose have outgrown the grove's sheltered bounds. Raan Wildwind has made camp southwest of Thendal Grove, along the road to Shen'dar Village. He has spent time facing the dangers beyond the safe haven. For wanderers setting out from the grove, Raan offers practical counsel on surviving the open roads.

quest:96652.text: The Adventurer. On Durotar’s red wastes, The Adventurer finds a lost journal meant for Brakk near Razor Hill. Its pages remember quiet travels and nights beneath the stars. A lost journal lies in Durotar’s red dirt, far from the battles and campaigns that mark the land. An unknown traveler fills its pages with daily journeys and the pleasure of making camp beneath the open sky. The journal offers a quiet glimpse of life on the road through harsh country. The journal is meant for Brakk, an adventurer camped near Razor Hill. Its pages link an unknown traveler to someone watching the dusty roads. Carrying it to Brakk may keep the writer’s travels remembered.

quest:96656.text: The Adventurer. Near Deathknell, The Adventurer is sent to investigate a stranger on the road to Brill. Scarlet Crusaders threaten the region, but the stranger is Eleanor Shackleton, a Forsaken traveler who can teach wilderness skills. Executor Arren watches Deathknell and the roads around it. Scarlet Crusaders spy on the region and infiltrate northern Lordaeron, so an unfamiliar figure near Brill draws his suspicion. You have proved your dedication by striking at Crusader threats along the border. Now Arren asks you to investigate the stranger quietly and learn whether she threatens the Forsaken. By the roadside near Brill, you find Eleanor Shackleton. She is a Forsaken traveler, pausing before another journey into the wilds. She has no Crusader plot or Scourge necromancy in mind. Seeing a fellow adventurer in those sent to check on her, Eleanor offers to teach you how to survive in open country and make camp.

quest:96658.text: Camping 101: Cooking. As you learn to cook, a basic campfire gives you a hearth for camping beyond fortified walls. Across Alliance and Horde lands, cooking trainers show new adventurers how to kindle one and prepare for life in the wild. Beyond fortified walls, a campfire boils water and roasts meat. Its flames give you a hearth when you travel through unfamiliar country and make camp. Apprentice cooks kindle small fires with few surroundings. As your cooking grows, you can light larger fires for more elaborate campsites. Other practical trades teach you to make useful furnishings.

quest:96659.text: The Adventurer. From Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind sends young travelers with supplies for Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. She aided him long ago, and he means to repay her kindness. Chief Hawkwind asks you to carry provisions to Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. Long ago, she helped him when he was in need, and he remembers her kindness. Now she has made camp outside the village. So Hawkwind entrusts young travelers leaving the mesa with supplies for his old benefactor. The trail runs from Red Cloud Mesa toward Bloodhoof Village, across the plains of Mulgore. With Hawkwind's bundle, you travel beyond Camp Narache, where young tauren have trained. The path leads into the wider lands of the United Tauren Tribes.

quest:967.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Dark Strand cultists gather, and Balthule Shadowstrike needs help. He sends a warning with an Alliance courier to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale for his mentor, Delgren the Purifier. Balthule Shadowstrike sees that one scout cannot face the Dark Strand threat alone. After clashing with cultists near the Tower of Althalaxx, he writes a report for his master, Delgren the Purifier, and gives it to an Alliance messenger. The cult's summoners grow bolder. Balthule needs seasoned leaders to direct a response. Balthule's dispatch sends you south along Darkshore's coastal road, then across the wooded border into Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier is stationed at Maestra's Post beside the western road. The human paladin works to cleanse demons and undead from the woodland. Night elven customs once seemed strange to him, but he has earned the Sentinels' deep respect as an indispensable ally.

quest:968.text:
Tools of the Highborne. Thundris Windweaver sends you from Auberdine to Ameth'Aran. Highborne spirits still haunt the ruins with enchanted relics in their hands, and he wants them taken away. Ameth'Aran lies south of Auberdine and east of the coastal highway. Its stone foundations are overgrown. Ten thousand years ago, it was a stronghold of the Highborne, the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire.

Their unchecked arcane magic helped bring about the Sundering, which shattered the settlement. Yet its inhabitants never truly left. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report Highborne ghosts in the sunken plazas, still clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they held in life. For the kaldorei, arcane magic recalls a danger that nearly destroyed life on Azeroth. Thundris Windweaver fears that the Highborne implements could invite corruption if they remain in ghostly hands. So he sends you to wrest the relics from the restless spirits. He intends to have them destroyed before their tainted magic can fuel another disaster.

quest:97279.text: Wayward Weapons. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends fresh arrivals to recover weapons for the encampment. Young warriors keep coming to serve the Horde, and Kzan Thornslash needs old arms returned to use. Young recruits face harsh trials in Durotar's red wastes. Many arrive ready to pledge their blades to the warchief, leaving the encampment short of weapons. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to meet demand. Early lessons can end in death or humiliation for those unready. Overseer Gornek turns the shortage into a practical trial. He sends fresh arrivals to recover abandoned blades and blunt training weapons left by recruits who fell or fled. Kzan can repair and temper the recovered arms for the next wave. The recruits learn that survival in the Horde calls for scavenging as well as swinging steel.

quest:97558.text: Hides for the Forsaken. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken gather hides to keep their bodies intact. Shelene Rhobart asks you to bring darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin. Forsaken flesh cannot mend itself. When they are wounded, the gap rots and stays open. So they stitch living tissue over their injuries to hold their forms together and keep their corpses working. Each kind of material mends a different part of the body. Thick darkhound hide holds firm over broad wounds. Duskbat wing membranes are thin and pliable, so they cover faces and fingers without stiffening them. Vile Fin murloc skin lines inner membranes and sensitive places such as cheeks and mouths.

quest:97894.text: Business in Auberdine. In Stormwind, Borgus Steelhand waits for news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. You can reach Gorbold by sailing west from Stormwind Harbor to northern Kalimdor. Gorbold crossed the Great Sea to keep a merchant stall in auberdine. He hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without word, and Borgus worries for his brother so far from Ironforge and Stormwind. The passage to Kalimdor once led through Menethil Harbor or neutral goblin ports such as Booty Bay. Borgus sends you to the vessel at stormwind harbor's southern-most dock. Its direct sailing ends at Auberdine's long wooden piers.

quest:97914.text: Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine to Stormwind. He wants the settlement's work and its home known beyond Darkshore. Auberdine's sea passage now joins Darkshore directly to Stormwind. Its leaders want the shipping route kept safe and the coastal settlement linked to the wider Alliance. Nearby, the ruined cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran have long drawn more notice than Auberdine and its living people. Baros Alexston oversees Stormwind's construction and infrastructure. His duties include public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver's letter crosses the Great Sea to the official charged with the human capital's building needs.

quest:97919.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle shows you how to prepare First Aid Kits for camping. You need enough First Aid skill to learn how to ready these supplies for the road ahead. Travel through Elwynn can leave you wounded, far from a town healer or inn. First Aid lets you tend your own injuries without relying on anyone else. Bandages help with bleeding and trauma, without arcane rites or holy prayers. At Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle teaches skilled practitioners to assemble First Aid Kits. Keep medical supplies at camp so a weary party can treat injuries and regain strength before facing the dangers ahead.

quest:97920.text: Camping 101: Fishing. Lee Brown teaches novice anglers near Goldshire how to use their fishing skill around camp. With simple catches and basic materials, they can make useful additions for a campsite. Fishing can feed you on the road and add comfort to camp. A fish bowl lifts the spirits of weary travelers between excursions. A sound mind and high spirits help make formidable fighters. Lee Brown waits beside the waters outside Goldshire for fishermen ready to broaden their craft. Show him your skill with rod and line, and he can teach you to make useful additions for camp.

quest:97926.text: Making Do. Auberdine waits for word from Stormwind, but no aid is coming. Making Do carries Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver. You carry Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. The letter brings no troops or relief. Stormwind's representative explains that the kingdom's treasury is nearly empty. What wealth remains must stretch across its own struggling territories.

quest:97957.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Tirisfal, Eleanor Shackleton sends new herbalists to Faruza in Brill to learn a useful craft. Incense Candles help spellcasters rest at camps in the wild. Herbalism gives alchemists their first materials. Travelers also rely on gathered roots and blossoms. Across the regions, master herbalists teach foragers to prepare Incense Candles. In Tirisfal Glades, Eleanor Shackleton sends promising foragers to Faruza in Brill once they show basic skill. Long journeys wear on spellcasters and spiritualists. Incense Candles release restorative fragrances that lift spirits and soothe tired minds. Gatherers infuse dried plants into the candles, helping healers and mages whose magical reserves falter on the road.

quest:97960.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Tirisfal Glades, Camping 101: Skinning sends new skinners to learn a useful craft. They learn to make a camp chair from harvested hides and where to find teachers across Azeroth. A sharp blade alone will not carry you through the wilds. You also need a way to rest between trials. In the field, skinners can learn the basics and use treated skins to make a chair for camp. It gives weary travelers a place to recover before danger calls again. Young Forsaken skinners in Tirisfal Glades are sent to Rand Rhobart once they reach their first measure of skill. He works along the road between Brill and the Capital ruins of the Undercity. Rhobart teaches practical ways to turn rough leather into a seat for camp. Skinning masters across the lands of the Horde and Alliance teach the same craft.

quest:982.text: Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, two night elf vessels lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as they sailed into port, and the surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as they neared Auberdine. Both ships sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the vessels and their captains still weighs on the port. Gorbold Steelhand, a dwarf in Auberdine, seeks to honor the fallen night elf captains. Murlocs now occupy the underwater wrecks, though the captains' lockboxes remain in the flooded holds. Their logs and personal effects could help the surviving sailors mourn their commanders and lay their spirits to rest.

quest:98219.text: The Shamed Lieutenant. A Stormwind guard asks you to check on Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore. His reassignment is meant to teach him a lesson, but the guard hopes he can still succeed. You've safely delivered the statuette. Now your contact asks you to speak with Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, a city guard sent to Southshore in Hillsbrad Foothills. Farren's father was a friend of the guard, who believes he could benefit from help. If you are passing through, a boat bound for Southshore leaves from Menethil Harbor.

quest:98247.text: Shipping Label. A damaged Shipping Label leads you to the Azeroth Commerce Authority's trade hub at Three Corners in the Redridge Mountains. It marks a supply crate as the authority's property and shows where to report it. A damaged label marks a stocked supply crate as freight belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. The destination and recipient are torn away. Anyone who finds the cargo can return it or report it to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rough map shows the roads toward the Three Corners intersection. At Three Corners, representatives of the Azeroth Commerce Authority enlist travelers as independent couriers. The authority asks no strict merchant contracts of its haulers. Instead, it runs an informal network and gives Merchant's Favor to couriers who recover missing cargo or complete abandoned deliveries along the highway.

quest:983.text: Buzzbox 827. Along Darkshore's coast, repairs are needed at Buzzbox 827. Wizbang Cranktoggle built it as the first link in a chain of voice relays, each made to use parts from local wildlife. Restoring it lets Wizbang test his network from Auberdine. In Auberdine, gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle is linking Darkshore's wild coast with a chain of voice relays called Buzzboxes. Their levers and gears carry speech across great distances, a sharp contrast with the ancient ruins and somber forests around them. The machines break down often, so each needs constant care to keep working. Buzzbox 827 lies on the shore just south of Auberdine. Wizbang built each relay to use parts from nearby wildlife, so repairs do not depend on carrying refined iron gears and copper pins through the wilderness. This unit takes the sturdy, jointed legs of local tide and reef crawlers. Put the legs in its receiver hopper, and the machine assembles itself and carries Wizbang's voice through its speakers.

quest:98386.text: Alther's Mill. At Alther's Mill, giant spiders have stopped the timber shipments Lakeshire needs for its bridge. Foreman Oslow is waiting for the lumber so the work can continue. Foreman Oslow is trying to keep Lakeshire's bridge repairs on schedule. Blackrock orcs, gnoll packs, and murlocs along Lake Everstill already strain his workforce. Now giant tarantulas have overrun Alther's Mill to the east, stopping the timber shipments the bridge needs. Greater tarantulas lurk among the timber stacks, leaving Alther's Mill useless. Foreman Oslow cannot risk sending laborers into their nest, so he hires capable adventurers to clear the spiders and destroy their egg clutches. He is irritated that Alther let the mill fall into disarray, but Lakeshire needs the lumber before the bridge work can continue.

quest:98389.text: A Light in the Darkness. In Deathknell, Aramis Hammerhand asks you to save newly raised Forsaken from Night's Web Hollow. Your aid may prove that those who wield the Holy Light stay loyal to Sylvanas and their people. Some Forsaken still wield the Holy Light they knew in life, though it pains their undead flesh. In Deathknell, Aramis Hammerhand and others hope to prove their faith has not set them against their own people. They use their gifts to protect the Forsaken and ease fears that they see their kin as monsters. Northwest of Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken wander into Night's Web Hollow, a dank cavern crawling with vicious spiders. Disoriented and unable to defend themselves, they become trapped in sticky webs. Saving them brings new recruits to the Dark Lady and may convince Executor Arren that wielders of the Light serve the Forsaken faithfully.

quest:984.text: How Big a Threat?. In Auberdine, Terenthis asks scouts to learn whether furbolg corruption has reached Darkshore. Madness has taken hold among furbolgs in Teldrassil, and the night elf druid now sends them to inspect mainland settlements across the sea. Night elves across northern Kalimdor have long lived peacefully with the furbolg tribes. Since the Third War, strange corruption has unhinged furbolg minds in Teldrassil. They have kidnapped and attacked their former allies. Terenthis, the druid in Auberdine, fears the affliction has spread to mainland tribes along Darkshore’s coast.

quest:98407.text: Show of Force. Deputy Feldon sends you against gnoll packs closing on Lakeshire. The town's guards need proof that the thrashers have been beaten. Gnoll packs have grown bolder in the Redridge Mountains. Their camps now lie close to Lakeshire and the human homesteads beyond. Stormwind has too few soldiers for the borderlands, so local folk rely on travelers to hold the perimeter. The gnolls have not struck the town, but their camps bring them within reach of its homes. Deputy Feldon knows the gnolls respect strength above all. He sends you after their fiercest fighters, the gnoll thrashers, and asks you to bring back their spiked collars as proof. Lakeshire's defenders hope that breaking the front line and showing these trophies will frighten the surviving packs into retreating to the highlands.

quest:985.text: How Big a Threat?. In Darkshore, Terenthis sends you against the Blackwood furbolgs south of Auberdine. Their corrupted camp threatens the settlement, and the Sentinels seek to cull its pathfinders and windtalkers. The Sentinels see the Blackwood furbolgs as an immediate danger to Darkshore’s refugees and defenders. After you scout south of Auberdine, Terenthis sends you to strike their camp. Kill Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers to hinder their attack before it reaches the settlement. Night elves have long counted furbolgs as spiritual kin and allies of the wilderness. Fel moss and demonic taint have spread across northern Kalimdor, driving the Blackwood tribe mad. No known remedy can restore their minds. So Auberdine’s defenders face a grim choice: stop the furbolgs before innocent people die.

quest:98576.text: Glyphic Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends young mages to Mai'ah for their first lessons. A runed notice points them to the mage near the Den, where their study of the arcane begins. New recruits face Durotar's local pests, but those drawn to magic need more than strength. Gornek gives them a notice marked with runes. It directs novice spellcasters to Mai'ah, who guides the Horde's newest recruits through their first lessons in magic. Just outside the Den, Mai'ah teaches young spellweavers to temper ambition with patience and thought. She urges them to choose their moment instead of casting raw sorcery without care. Her novices learn to weave delicate strands of the cosmos rather than unleash an unruly tempest.

quest:98601.text: A Difficult Path. In Deathknell, a newly awakened Forsaken paladin begins training with the Light. After the undead outside the crypt are cleared, you go to the village church to meet Aramis Hammerhand and learn what holy power demands of the Forsaken. After you clear the feral undead outside the crypt, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives you an unexpected delivery. The Consecrated Scroll shines with holy energy, and Sarvis recoils before asking you to step aside. To one devoted to shadow and decay, the Holy Light burns like an open flame. Aramis Hammerhand waits in Deathknell’s desecrated church to train Forsaken paladins. Other races may wield the Light with ease and joy, but the undead endure searing agony when they call upon it. Aramis speaks plainly: channeling holy power through a rotting body is torment. He expects his disciples to face that pain instead of shrinking from it, and let it temper their resolve.

quest:99.text: Arugal's Folly. In Pyrewood Village, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the magic binding its people to a curse. He needs their enchanted shackles to study Archmage Arugal's work and understand their transformation into worgen. South of the Sepulcher, Pyrewood Village lives two lives. By day, its fearful and insular residents seem like ordinary human peasants. At twilight, their human forms break apart and become savage Moonrage worgen. Then they roam the streets under Arugal's sway. Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the arcane bindings behind this horror.

quest:990.text: Trek to Ashenvale. Sentinel Selarin sends travelers south from Auberdine into Ashenvale. In Astranaar, you report to Raene Wolfrunner as the Sentinels face spreading corruption. From Auberdine on Darkshore's somber gray coast, Sentinel Selarin calls you south to aid the night elf lands. Selarin trusts capable fighters and scouts to journey into Ashenvale's heart. With local threats in Darkshore handled, greater perils now demand attention. An ancient night elf road winds south beneath Ashenvale's dense canopy. Raene Wolfrunner leads the Sentinels in Astranaar and has urgently called for reinforcements. Demonic taints, rampant wildlife, and incursions from beyond ancestral lands have stretched the defenders thin. They need outside aid to hold the sacred forest.

quest:991.text: Raene's Cleansing. In Ashenvale, Raene Wolfrunner asks you to find Teronis in Raene's Cleansing. He set out toward Lake Falathim to recover a magic gemstone and find a way to halt the furbolgs' growing aggression. Raene Wolfrunner serves with the Sentinels in Astranaar, defending Ashenvale from mounting threats. Teronis was among her closest companions. He set out to find a strong defense against the furbolg tribes as they grew more violent. Days passed without his return, and Raene feared the worst while duty kept her at her post. Teronis followed rumors of a powerful rod forged by a wicked wizard who had died. He believed its magic could calm the furbolg fury. To restore the rod, he needed an enchanted gem hidden in an elven shrine at Lake Falathim, near the mountains to the west. Yet aggressive murloc tribes had recently taken the lake's once-tranquil waters.

quest:99134.text: Discipline. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand calls on outsiders to keep the Deathguard alert. He trusts his garrison little and orders punishment for sentries who slacken. The Deathguard guard the Forsaken across Lordaeron. Freedom from the Lich King's control has brought apathy, fatigue, and neglect. Yet the Scarlet Crusade and Scourge prowl Tirisfal's borders, so the garrison must stay ready. Executor Zygand has little patience for sentries who let their discipline slip. The officers use force and close oversight to keep their troops alert. Executor Zygand chooses outsiders to punish negligent Deathguards instead of using soldiers from his own garrison. With the Executor's Motivator, you remind the sentries that service to the Dark Lady demands constant vigilance. Even in undeath, they face the consequences of neglecting their duties.

quest:99141.text: Patience. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand waits for field reports that have not arrived. He sends you to find Deathguards near Brill and a sentry by Stillwater Pond. Executor Zygand commands security in Tirisfal Glades and permits no lapse in vigilance. He serves Lady Sylvanas and expects every duty to be done. When scheduled field reports fail to reach his post, he counts the delay as a breach of duty. He holds his place and sends Forsaken agents to find the tardy subordinates and keep the borders secure. Zygand's sentries around Brill owe him their reports. Deathguard Dillinger watches the graveyard west of town, where rogue undead and Scourge remnants stir. East of Brill, Deathguard Kristof guards a waystation on the approaches to the Capital City and the eastern roads. Gordo is the strangest sentry: a hulking abomination who wanders near Stillwater Pond, where military record-keeping seems beyond his simple mind.

quest:99142.text: Tomb Weed. At Balnir Farmstead, Holland's altered doom weed has drawn the Scourge. The crop now bears the name tomb weed, and Holland wants it for his experiments. Junior Apothecary Holland seeks more than a place in the Royal Apothecary Society. He gathers doom weed, alters it through alchemy, then plants it again in Balnir Farmstead's soil. From that work comes a new strain: tomb weed. Holland sees it as the heart of his experiments and a path to the future he wants for himself. Holland expected his altered plants to grow stronger in alchemical use. Instead, the Scourge wandering Balnir Farmstead have taken an interest in them. Now he relies on travelers to get past the undead and gather the mature crop, so his experiments can go on.

quest:99156.text: Rear Guard Patrol. In Tirisfal Glades, Deathguard Linnea calls the patrollers to defend the border. She sends them after Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have passed the Bulwark. The Bulwark is the only fortified barrier between Tirisfal Glades and the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Forsaken strategy depends on holding one front. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, they can choke the supply routes that feed it. Spirits and ghouls sometimes get past the barricades, but an abomination roaming the glades means containment has failed badly.

quest:997.text:
Denalan's Earth. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf seeks a courier for rare earth bound south to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. The night elf researcher studies Teldrassil's young plants. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf has a shipment of rare earth for Denalan. The soil came from Darnassus to aid his botanical studies, but delays held it back. Now Syral seeks a courier to carry it south along the forest trail to Denalan's campsite by Lake Al'Ameth. At a station on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, Denalan works alone and watches Teldrassil's young ecosystem take root. The tree grew quickly after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and its plants behave in unexpected ways.

Denalan tests the vitality and behavior of timberlings and native plants with unique soil mixtures and specimens. The rare earth shipment will support those experiments.

quest:cutting-teeth.text: Cutting Teeth. In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face their first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends warriors and spellcasters to thin the herds around the cactus dirt farms and prove they can fight for the Horde. Young recruits may dream of hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield. Overseer Gornek starts them at the farms instead. Thinning the mottled boars tests their first skill with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and survive their first skirmish. Feral swine roam the dirt farms north and northeast of camp. They root through cactus patches and threaten the few supplies grown in Durotar’s harsh soil. Clearing them keeps local pests in check. It also shapes young orcs and trolls into defenders of their new nation.

quest:galgar-s-cactus-apple-surprise.text: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise. In the Valley of Trials, Galgar sends new recruits to gather cactus apples for a cooling treat. Foraging helps them learn to live in Durotar's dry land. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their work as defenders of the Horde in the Valley of Trials. Combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts leave them tired and thirsty. Learning to live off the land matters as much as learning to swing an axe. Across the valley, cacti bear ripe apples rich with water, a welcome relief from the desert sun. Galgar cooks in the training grounds and knows how to forage. His Cactus Apple Surprise is said to cool a person faster than a plunge into river water. He sends eager recruits to gather prickly fruit from nearby cacti. That keeps his kitchen stocked and ensures new wanderers do not set out into Durotar hungry.

quest:lazy-peons.text: Lazy Peons. Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to rouse sleeping peons. Their labor keeps timber moving to Durotar's settlements. Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons have little skill in battle, so they carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, heat and grueling work drive Foreman Thazz'ril's crews beneath the trees for unauthorized naps. Foreman Thazz'ril gives new Horde recruits his blackjack and sends them across the valley to wake the sleeping workers. Startled, the peons return to chopping wood. Their labor keeps lumber flowing for Durotar's survival.

quest:sarkoth.text: Sarkoth. On a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth has left a young Darkspear hunter near death. Beneath a tree, Hana'zua asks a passing warrior to kill the scorpid and bring back its mangled claw, so his last strike will count for something. The Valley of Trials puts aspiring Horde warriors against Durotar's harsh desert. While hunting its venomous creatures, young troll scout Hana'zua met a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. He struck hard enough to mangle one pincer. Then Sarkoth drove its tail into his chest. Now Hana'zua bleeds in the red dirt and fears his life is near its end. He wants the beast dead before it outlives him. Sarkoth roams a high mesa above the southern Valley of Trials. Hana'zua shattered one claw, but the scorpid still rules the ridge and attacks anyone climbing the rocky path. Bring the scarred claw back to the wounded scout. Then he will know his last strike weakened the monster enough for someone to bring it down.

quest:your-place-in-the-world.text: Your Place In The World. Kaltunk sends new recruits in the Valley of Trials to Gornek for training. There, young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their service to the Horde and learn what honor and survival demand in Durotar. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove their worth in Durotar's arid Valley of Trials before they enter the wider world. Under Warchief Thrall, life demands strength, vigilance, and discipline. Kaltunk tests each eager recruit and turns their dreams of wrestling demons and dragons toward the practical duties ahead. In the canyon, training begins with humility before glory. Gornek waits beside the camp fire, only steps from Kaltunk. The gruff veteran regards fresh arrivals with a skeptical eye and grumbles about the meager stock reaching camp. He hardens young fighters through trials, beginning with the vermin that threaten the encampment's supplies.
